review_text:
At last, now we can get the delicious food from Russ & Daughters in a nice, comfortable sit-down restaurant without the endless, cramped, tourist-ridden waits that plague the original location.

The leisurely meal I had tonight in the only semi-busy restaurant might not last long though, as not only is the food here great, but it is also opening at the perfect time to capitalize on the current exploding popularity of bagels. We did try a bagel as part of one of the dishes, but knowing that they aren't the strong suit of Russ & Daughter's, we ordered a ton of other stuff instead:

- Bread Basket ($6)
This was really great, and worth the purchase. They give you a ton of bread, with 3 hearty slices each of rye and pumpernickel. They were nice and warm and tasted really great with some butter. They also have a Bagel & Bialy Basket for the same price.

- Potato Latkes with Salmon Roe and Creme Fraiche ($9 for 3)
These were really great, and especially incredible when eaten with the generous portion of salty salmon roe. Don't tell my mom, but I think these might beat hers.

- Russ & Daughters Knishes ($8 for 2)
These were minuscule, and not particularly good. The skin wasn't flaky enough and the potatoes weren't buttery enough on the inside. If you haven't had a really exemplary knish to compare it to though, it tastes pretty good when paired with the mustard.

- Matzo Brei ($12)
Listed under the "Eggs" section of the menu, this was pretty good. It was probably a little lacking in flavor since it is after all made mostly of matzo. Most of the other egg dishes look better, like the Benedict, but we went with this smaller one since we had so much other food.

- Pastrami Russ ($10)
This is a little sandwich on a tiny pretzel roll with a ton of flavor. Along with the great pastrami-cured salmon, there is muenster cheese, sauerkraut, mustard and pickled, making for a really delicious starter-sized sandwich.

- The Classic Board ($16)
This is pretty much a create-your-own-bagel-with-lox. Rather than ordering a sandwich, this is all of the ingredients of the classic bagel sandwich laid out on a board. As mentioned above, the bagels here aren't really great, but they're passable and are perfectly fine as a vehicle for the incredible gaspe nova smoked salmon. You can also add capers, tomatoes, onions and cream cheese for a really satisfying sandwich.

- Chocolate Egg Cream ($7)
I just don't get egg creams. This one was better than some I've had, but I can't get behind the fizziness with my chocolate. You can also get Buxar and Vanilla flavors, but I would prefer a shake.

- Babka French Toast ($10)
On to the Sweet section of the menu, which was the best part. This was incredible - made from chocolate babka, this dessert came out piping hot. It was so soft and fluffy and packed with chocolate. It came with some strawberries on the side, but to really enjoy it, you must order it with:

- Halvah Ice Cream ($8)
Wow! Sure, $8 for a scoop of ice cream is shocking, but not as shocking as how amazing it tasted. Seriously, you must get a scoop of this for dessert. Be smart and get it with the Babka French Toast too, for the ultimate hot and cold combination.

The service was ok, but perhaps the opposite of Jewish waiters, as we often waited a bit for service. However, everything felt much smoother than you would expect from a restaurant on opening night, and they already felt like pros that have been open for awhile. The food was mostly really great, and I would definitely love to return to try some more of the extensive menu of noshed and delicious smoked fish boards. Oh, and the Challah Bread Pudding sounds ridiculously good. With a scoop of Halvah Ice Cream of course.

Russ and Daughters Cafe opened yesterday (May 7, 2014) and I imagine it will quickly achieve the popularity of its legendary space a few blocks away. This outpost is a real, sit-down restaurant that manages to be both retro and modern: diner-style seating with a white-tiled, vintage photo walled, hip-typeface atmosphere. 

Many people have complained that Russ and Daughters and become much too expensive, and this cafe certainly doesn't do anything to disprove that. There's a $180 caviar omelette on the menu, and most of the egg/fish based dishes are in the $15-25 range, which, to me, is a lot for breakfast food. However, you are getting expertly cured fishes and thoughtfully planned combinations. Lots of bagels and bialys, a nice selection of sandwiches, platters, and brunch standbys like eggs Benedict, challah French toast, bread puddings, etc. all of these dishes have a little Jewish-American comfort food twist. I had a small dish that highlighted some of their fish salad and schmear, and it was delicious. 

A big plus here is that there is an extensive drinks menu with wine, beer, shrubs, breakfast beverages, and some top notch Bloody Marys. I can really see this cafe becoming a brunch hotspot soon. 

I think they're still working out service and operations, but the staff was friendly and attentive. The space is pretty big, and the menu has options for everyone, whether you're a carb-loader or gluten abstainer. 

This cafe, once a twinkle in the LES' eye, is another sign of the hipsterification of Orchard Street. But, it was about time that Russ and Daughters expanded to accommodate their growing fanbase.

Great space, the food was awesome, and the service was excellent.  We tried both kinds of potato latkes, the chopped liver, a few of the soups and the original bagel with lox-- all delicious.  We followed it up with the bread pudding, halvah ice cream, and the blintz-- which were all so good.  The martini was great and they make house made sodas which I really enjoyed.  We came with an infant and had plenty of room to move around with her when she became a little fussy and they actually had a changing table in one of the bathrooms which I really appreciated.  The design is one that gives you that modern old diner feel.  We were excited when we heard the restaurant was opening and it definitely exceeded our expectations.

This place has an amazing menu. You can get all your favorites from the original Russ and Daughters or some classic comfort food. The soups are incredible; the fish is as wonderful as you expect; plus, there are Jewish classics (matzo brei!) that remind of childhood.

We were so happy that R&D were opening a cafe, but couldn't imagine it would be as amazing as it is.  It looks and feels like the store, and somehow even more fabulous, because you get to linger longer.  Really good cocktails, METAL straws (I love them for this, thank you for not wasting plastic!), delicious food, lovely bar staff (we sat at the bar), great jazz was playing.... I was smiling the whole time I was there, felt welcomed and comfortable.  Loved the artwork on the walls - ink sketches of the store staff and other iconic Russ and Daughters "stuff" AND the bathrooms - even those are so tasteful.  The wallpaper made me think of a Mast Brothers chocolate bar wrapper - and that's classy!  I will be back, again and again.... I think this one's gonna be here a while.  
Congrats Niki and Josh....

As a fan of the original, I went last week to give this place a try, here are my thoughts:

The space is nice, but I think I will stick to the original and the street bench in front.  I don't mind paying top dollar for quality smoked fish, but it really is obscene, or more aptly put, a lot of chutzpah, to charge $7 for an egg cream!  Let's think about this for a second, there are only 3 ingredients in an egg cream: cold milk, Fox's U-Bet syrup, and seltzer...being generous, assuming they use organic milk (which they don't) I would say these ingredients cost them fifty cents at most.  Yes, the nova was great, but as I ate, I could not help but feel like I was being taken advantage of with our $7 egg cream and $5 soda.  

After my experience here, based on their prices, it is my impression that R&Ds, a treasure from the past, is now primarily catering to the 1% or at least not the folks being priced out of the neighborhood.  Sad.  I don't think I will be back.

It's a great-looking restaurant, and pleasant to sit in (no horrible loud music). The chopped salad and the smoked trout and potato salad were both wildly tasty. But the serving sizes for both salads were also skimpy, and at $14 each! We went away still hungry. Would it kill them to add more salad greens or cucumbers? Charging $7 for a bread "basket," too, rather than including a roll or slice of pumpernickel with the salads also struck us as grasping. And we were almost finished with our salads by the time the bread arrived, since it had to be toasted, the waiter said. R & D should review its menus and pricing, and emulate restaurants with a more generous spirit, like Chez Oskar in Brooklyn, for one. One doesn't long to return to a restaurant that makes it so clear that it's all about offering the bare minimum while extracting maximum profit.

It felt as if Doc Brown and I had stepped out of the Delorean, and into 1955. This place has been set dressed to invoke a much earlier era, and it was meticulously done. 

Service was excellent, food was exquisite.

Started with the pastrami russ, amazing I think I could eat 5 of them. 

Then I had the Lower Sunny, yum perfect amount of food, and was a nice sampler. My boyfriend got the eggs benedict, with challah it was amazing. 

All around I can find no downside, this was one of the most enjoyable dining experiences I have had in a while.

Put your name down, take a walk they will text you when your table is read.

Very disappointed! We walked by only days after they opened and got very excited about having yet another great place on LES. We normally go several times a month to the original Russ & Daughters and Pravda to fulfill our cravings for pickled herring and caviar so obviously we were very excited. But after dining at the Russ & Daughters Restaurant I can only say, Never Again.. This place is overpriced and you basically get deli sliced smoked fish for $90 without anything else. Don't go!!!!!

The Russ family has done a masterful job recreating the old world feel of the store with modern levels of comfort and service. From the shape of the water jugs to the white coated staff, surfaces, menu items, font styles etc. there was clearly a lot of effort put into the details and I can't imagine a much better job. I sat at the bar and found the wait staff charming and efficient. I get the complaints about small portions and high prices, but this is NYC people, and its top quality stuff. Had the nova eggs and onions and an order of latkes. Loved both. Will be back often.

Bottom line: I can see this place being a LES staple for decades to come, like the store is. In fact, I wouldn't be surprised if they opened more of these. I know if owned this place, I would.
Awesome new addition to the LES. Beet Shrub is outstanding! I only wish I could order some of the selected fish from the shop such as the smoked herring, lox, and loin cut salmon. Great place.

Walking in felt like walking into what an old NY cafeteria might have felt like. Lots of shiny chrome details, very white, tables well spaced...it's a perfect mirror to its Houston St. shop. 

Sitting up at the bar I got to watch the staff mix up delicious cocktails,egg-creams, and homemade sodas. I put my order in and sat back with a caraway infused vodka Bloody Mary. I was a little heartbroken that it was promised to come with pickles and had two little pickle shavings tucked onto a toothpick instead. I have a pickle problem. The drink was heavily iced but the tomato blend was solid.

For lunch I ordered the Borscht and the Super Heebster. The soup was well balanced and hit the spot...for the first half of the bowl. The second half I spent slogging through the creaminess. Texturally it was entirely one note. It came with a tiny piece of pumpernickel toast so then I took my rye crouton off the toothpick (the meat in  my pickle sliver Bloody Mary garnish) and used it to dip through a little more. Did the bartender look at me oddly? Yup. It's cool- I come from a long line of dippers. 

The Super Heebster was banging in taste and presentation but unfortunately tiny. Yeah, it's under the Nosh column so I didn't expect anything huge but it definitely wasn't $10 big. 

Nice place.
Great vibe.
Some quality menu choices. 
Friendly team.
Overpriced.

3.5/5

The meal couldn't have been better if Louis CK himself showed up to dangle a fish in my mouth. My companion was running behind, so the bartender (in a lab coat, obvs) and very nice hostess kept me company for 20 minutes as I sipped an my new favorite sparkling wine (from Hungary). 

And the food was perfection. I make pretty good latkes. Russ & Daughters makes them better. I could have eaten them for days. The knishes? Also great. My date loved her sturgeon, caviar, and chicken soup. 

We closed down the place (kitchen's done at 10), so I didn't get to try any desserts this visit. I'll be back, chocolate babke french toast.

This spot is just as delightful, but more refined than the original space just up the street. I came on a busy Sunday with a friend and instead of waiting for a table, we sat at the bar, which is way more fun anyway. We ordered coffee sodas, which is basically coffee concentrate and a sweet-ish bubbly water. It's unusual, but delicious. We shared a classic board of a bagel, lox, tomatoes/capers/onions, and cream cheese. It was delicious, but you already knew that. We also shared the house pickles, which included a few that seemed to be classic, spicy, curry, and red wine cured. I'm not really sure if that's what they are, but just get them, they're good. 

I actually recommend sitting at the bar so you can get a first-hand experience at the elaborate drinks they mix. That and chatting with the bartenders is fun.

Waited two hours on a Saturday afternoon, but it was worth it. I love the vibe of the place-- goes well with the deep history of the store. Their menu is very well crafted and so are their dishes.

First, we had the herring plate and the classic board. Also had latkes which were paired beautifully with the ikura salmon roe. Big ups there. Never thought myself to eat ikura with potato but it worked harmoniously. The classic board in my opinion is something you can get anywhere. Same with eggs benny. The smoked salmon is great, but not so hard to come by and I would have liked to see a bigger portion. However, the herring plate was fabulous. Three types of herring and choices of dipping sauces with wonderfully pickled onions. Absolutely delish. A smaller portioned pickled herring is also available served on pumpernickel bread.

The Bloody Mary was great and I am particular about my bloody Mary's. Smoked pepper infused vodka an smoked salt. Paired nicely with smoked salmon of course. Would have liked to taste my horseradish though.

Last but certainly not least was the CAVIAR. Part of me wants to try their $1970 osetra haha maybe some other time. Kept looking at their caviar selections and decided to try their hackleback. Recommended over pickleback by the waiter. It was delicately and classically served with blinis and creme fraiche and some chives and choice of diced mini egg whites and egg yolk. Little bits of heaven in your mouth. Great for sharing so your wallet won't be hurt. But I love caviar. And fish. And everything related.

Will come back when I have time to wait again. Thanks!

Best Bite(s): Smoked Whitefish Chowder!, Pickled Herring with Onion, Bloody Mary with Caraway-Vodka (I know, it's a sip more than a bite), and despite not even ordering it, the Classic Sandwich Board

MAY 25, 2014 - We walked on over and put our names down for brunch on a Saturday. 45 minutes later a text arrived, and we made a beeline for the door to get our brunch on. Here's how that went down...

I have to say right off the bat that I love how this place is designed. It feels a bit like going back in time, but the little modern touches are excellent, specifically the menu. I liked it so much I made it the title picture for the review. The choices are a bit overwhelming, but only because you get the distinct feeling you're missing out no matter what you order. We began with a couple drinks, including the excellent bloody mary with caraway-vodka and pickles and a 'lower east side' (very fresh gin drink with lime, cucumber and dill). Both hit the spot.

When scanning the menu, the smoked whitefish chowder jumped out at me, as if by divine intervention. I say this because the chowder was heavenly. Crumbling up the matzo into the creamy (but not overly so) soup and getting nice chunks of whitefish with each bite was very rewarding and an exceptional way to start brunch.

Next up we sampled the pickled herring trio, a selection of three bites each on pumpernickel with various treatments on top: onion, mustard and dill and apple. Each had good balance, with our favorites being the onion and mustard versions. As someone who doesn't adore pickled herring on its own, I think this dish works rather nicely as a taster.

Continuing our fish frenzy, we ordered the smoked trout and potato salad with watercress and a caper-mustard dressing. In contrast to most potato salads, this was a very clean, savory version with a good balance of acid, salt and brininess. It's the kind of thing you wish someone in your family would bring to a potluck.

We finished brunch with a yum kippered sandwich board, complete with lightly toasted bagel, tomatoes, onion, capers, cream cheese and a piece of baked salmon. This is a twist on the R&D standard, but to be honest, I missed the smoked salmon and probably would stick to the tried and true classic version of this in future. Don't get me wrong, this all makes for a delicious sandwich, but the baked salmon got lost for me and I found my sense memory wishing for its colder, fleshier smoked cousin.

Wrapping Up...

I really do like this place and am so glad the family decided to branch out in this direction. Brunch in this city is an institution, and it was almost sad that R&D couldn't be enjoyed this way previously. I'll certainly be returning to taste more of this great menu, and would encourage you to brave the wait while it's short so that you too can enjoy this unique LES gem.

Let's keep this simple. 

1) If you want some really good smoked fish (with or without a bagel), are in possession of a moderate amount of wealth and need to work on Friday mornings, then go to the original Russ & Daughters on Houston - take your food to go and eat it at home or in a grungy/charming Lower East Side park. 

2) If you want some really good smoked fish (no bagels or cream cheese) and are broke/adventurous/don't need to work on Friday mornings/like buying in bulk, then schlep out to Greenpoint and buy directly from the source, ACME Fish Market. It's only open to the public from 8am to 1pm on Fridays though.

3) Finally, if you want some really good smoked fish (attractively sliced and laid out on a plate accompanied by slices of tomatoes, capers and baked goods) and want to eat it in a clean, retro diner with air conditioning and cute waitresses, then go to Russ & Daughters Café (on Orchard). However, be prepared to pay a 30% premium to the original Russ & Daughters on Houston and a 600% premium to ACME Fish Market.

You must have a lot of beitsem to 1) charge for a bagel and lox 2) bring a stale, soft and bland bagel 3) ignore customers sitting at a counter and then charge $45 for a breakfast. I know now that we should've just left when we saw the $180 omelet, but we were already there. We thought"this bagel with lox must be the best one in a city full of bagel shops. A city which is known for bagels. Right?" Wrong-o! I've had Lenders better than this. How dare you charge this much for a sub- par meal? Those poor wealthy tourists were getting fleeced and didn't know. Keep the old timey music and corny white jackets. Just get the basics right. The only reason I didn't give it one star is because I didn't vomit after. Stay away from this place. There are dozens of better places to eat, including the corner bodega. Yuck.

Some of the best smoked fish in the city. Seltzer on tap. And the most amazing scoop of halva ice cream I've ever tasted. If I lived closer to this place, I'd be in some serious trouble. (Read: broke and fat.)

RUN DONT WALK!
Everything is perfect, the food, the service the decor. Now of course we went @530 on Friday so didn't have to wait but Russ & Daughters is a MUST do. And go hungry, there are too many sublime choices to hold back.

One of our favorite places to visit while in New York is Russ and Daughters.  So the new Russ and Daughters Café was a must do on our most recent visit to the city.  We went on a Sunday morning, along with a number of other pilgrims, and by the time we arrived at 10:20, the wait was 45 minutes, not long after that, the wait had expanded for later arrivals to 1 hour and 45 minutes.  A beautiful day, we were undaunted by this, and not a bit tempted to walk back down to Houston and just get our sandwiches to go.

While they were very accommodating to us as we increased our party size from 2 to 3, the disappointment started with a glimpse of the menu, and most of our favorites were omitted in favor of caviar servings for amazing amounts of money.  While this may seem flashy on a menu/placemat, and instagram worthy, I wonder how many takers at breakfast/brunch there are for this.  Often over time, restaurants learn where the hits are as well as the misses - I hope that Russ and Daughters, that is new and trying to differentiate itself from its original location will do the same.

The place is very retro-chic, beautifully appointed, and with the most uncomfortable seats (tall bar-stool type) that we have experienced in a while.  Even the stools at the counter had a bit of a back to them which might have been nice as we waited overly long for our food to be served.

The food that was served was good, but not memorable, and the portion size for the price relatively paltry.  If this is one's initial experience with Russ and Daughters, my concern is that people will not understand what all the fuss is about.  While most of us understand that you have to charge more for food that is prepared and delivered to your table vs. carry-out, then our recommendation is to charge more, rather than shrinking the size and trying to get by with a cuter name for the same tinier option.

We love you, Russ and Daughters, and look forward to our return in a couple of months.  But we will go to Houston, take our sandwiches to go, and replace the current memories with much better ones - Fancy Delancy - here I come!

(ZERO STARS)
whether you're a real new Yorker or not, if you're looking for an authentic Jewish deli for bagel and lox, try their original location, or shlep uptown to Barney Greengrass,  Zabar's, Tap Bagels, or Ess-A-Bagel.
we expected a long wait when we planned a visit on Sunday of memorial day weekend and as such didn't go there starving.  upon arrival the young hostess told us it'd be an hour wait for our party of four.
in the meantime, we discovered a great craft beer place called Top Hops. right down the street.
one hour later, my least favorite game commenced: the wait continually extended "another 15 minutes" for a whole nother hour.  
at some point, we probably should've given up, but we were trying to exercise patience. 
 As we were finally seated my wife casually suggested to the hostess that maybe they could send us some pickles or something for our troubles.
15 minutes go by, no sign of a server, water, nothing. finally a rough-shaven fellow. in a black ballcap  crouched down next to our booth and coldly says,"I hear you guys have a problem."  we calmly explained how our wait time was mismanaged, we still hadn't received any service, and that it'd be courteous of them to throw a little something our way to make up for it. "you waited a long time and you want something for free now. we don't offer any amuse bushe."  this was his response? still no "I'm sorry" he glared at our wives and generally dooshed up another opportunity to make good. 
after he sulked away the four of us decided: pizza! and quietly walked out of there.

a later look at the Russ and daughters website (albeit the one for their main store) showed that this manager, was Joshua Russ Tupper, a 4th generation Russ. is this the values the legacy should be displaying?  what he presents on the site that what the store means to him is "quality, service" sure as heck does not show in person.
At t least with Barney green grass the attitude is expected and part of the charm.  this joint tries to dress itself up as something it isn't with the standard white tile and "jarred things" look, unfortunately helmed by clueless vacant inexperienced hostesses. 
I am SO GLAD that we didn't give them two zizem of our monies, especially when looking at the menu it's ridiculously overpriced too!
never again.

Similar experience to Corey W.  After waiting for almost two hours, my wife ordered a drink at the bar and then was rudely chased away from the bar by the manager who said he needed the seat for another customer. Turns out he is the same guy who was rude to Corey. R&W made their reputation by offering quality products and customer service. The generation running the cafe needs to remember that. That said, once seated, the service was fine and the food was better.

Russ and Daughters cafe is dishonoring a classic New York establishment. Fancy tiles and bathrooms trump the tiny portions, and you will find significantly higher prices and fewer choices. 

It's sad to see yet another chi chi manhattan gimmick that is more about the interior finishes then the product they are selling.

This is the first time we are here and I have to say...Deeeelish! I had the east side sunny and my husband had the classic board. We both agree that this was the best smoked salmon we've ever had and that's a lot coming from two New York Jews :-). The halva sundae was amazing. We will def come here again!

I love their original spot, but now that the cafe has opened I'm so excited to try everything on the menu! Came here saturday morning and had the classic salmon bagel. That is always a favorite, instead of building it for you as a sandwich it's on a board so you'll have to make your own. We also ordered the Heebster and that was very good!! It's small so good to share, along with the pickled Terring trio. This comes with 6 mini pieces, all very fresh and topped with 3 different toppings. I have to come back to try other items and dessert!

Would give this place 5 stars IF they had stuff on the menu for "real" people too.

The foo foo offerings are creative and certainly yummy! But they need to give us some regular deli pickles (where are the half sours???) and good old fashioned comfort food. This place could be the best and I hope to see the menu evolve. Definitely my fav Deli in the world, this cafe is a great concept and it is done ALMOST right!!


Yes, I will be back. Despite my pet peeves.

So sorry to have to write this review...but doing it so in the hopes that the powers that be at R&D might have a chance to rectify the problems we experienced this past Monday afternoon.  

Based on our location, we tried to get into Clinton St. Bakery first. There was a 90 min. wait so we decided to take a walk over to Russ & Daughters Cafe.  We thought there would be an equally long wait but, alas, we were able to walk right in.  We have been huge fans of R & D for many years and have mail ordered from there many times a year.  

The decor is great and a fun throw back in time.  We sat at the counter which was comfortable. We shared all of the following:
The Super Heebster - an appetizer sized "bagel toast" with white fist salad for $10. Delicious but very small.

The Heebster - a bialy or bagel with sturgeon, butter, tomatoes, onion, capers for $22.  The bialy was not fresh, 3 paper think slices of sturgeon.  Very disappointed with this dish. Such a stingy portion and why would the bialy be stale??

Still hungry after spending $32 so far so we then ordered the eggs benedict on challah. This dish was done well with perfectly poached eggs.  

We were so hoping to be able to rave about R & D Cafe. Unless things change drastically, next time we are craving this comfort food we'll be going back to Kutchers instead.

This Cafe has little or no similarities to highest quality of appetizing and the warmth of the "hamish" ambience at the original store on Houston Street: food at the Cafe is just fair and the prices are ridiculously high for ridiculously small portions. Disappointing would be an understatement. Perhaps the only thing that was positive was the lack of lines at 3:00 on a Thursday afternoon. Servers were pleasant, but service was terribly slow. And to run out of borscht by mid-afternoon was unacceptable. Two tiny knishes for $8.00 borders on the obscene.
I had to plead to have the SUPER HEEBSTER on a bagel, instead of on the bagel toasts, and was ultimately charged $6.00 extra for a tiny bagel. To make it even more insulting, it didn't come close to the size of the bagel, the heaping portion of the whitefish and the fabulous taste of the wasabi when it's made at the store.
I'll stick to the appetizing store, and let those who want to be ripped off to come to the Cafe.

I shared a bagel with lox, latkes with salmon roe and crème fraiche, and bread pudding. All was excellent. Nice ambience with lots of carrara marble and brightish blue. Nice balance of tradition and trend in the decor and menu.

This is a place for people who love the best quality smoked salmon.  For the first time, they decided to open a cafe.  It's a sit down version of their take out order and more.

For me, I regularly go to their store to bring home smoked salmon and other smoked fish and pickled herring.  This time, it's making them prepare those things they sell. I'm very familiar with the food so I like it.

The borscht which they don't have at the store is delightful! The salad is clean tasting and very fresh.  Next time I'll try the smoked white fish chowder.  These are items not in their store and must order in this cafe.

Looking forward to going back in the future.

And if you've never tried their smoked salmon, you won't regret it. It's excellent quality.

And if you don't know what excellent smoked salmon is compared to packaged ones in the grocery, don't come. You won't appreciate it.  Can't get any better than this!

I feel compelled to write this review because R&D appears to be so polarizing! 

Our server at R&D was hands-down the best we've had in NYC - friendly, exceptionally knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the food. Her recommendations were fantastic and she made the meal fun without intruding on our evening. 

The food was also brilliant - we shared the sours, super heebster, pastrami russ and the latkes with apple sauce. All lovely. Not huge servings sure, but satisfied this hungry couple. We finished the night sharing the challah bread pudding and had a couple of cocktails (the smoked martini and the schmoozer). 

Finally, the decor (so reviled on here!) was delightful - tasteful, nostalgic and comfortable. Particularly the grey-blue leather booths and backlit shelving signs. 

TL:DR If you're broke or a longterm fan of the deli on Houston, head straight back there and eat take away in the park. But if you appreciate a lovely meal, exceptional service and beautiful design, don't hesitate.

I'm the kind of person that doesn't order appetizers or dessert at a restaurant because it's too much food for me. I like reasonable, even smallish portions. Still, I found the portions at this cafe to be very stingy. Paid $112 for lunch for four, including tip, with no alcohol, and left hungry. It feels like a tourist trap, so I won't be going there again. There is a 99 cent pizza place down the street, you may need to hit that before, or after R&D Cafe.

As a long time, fairly frequent customer of R&D on Houston St., I was totally disappointed with the cafe.I look forward to going to Houston St., I would never look forward to going to the cafe - once was more than enough.

I ordered the basic lox on a bagel, something I usually buy at the original store, and if I didn't know the quality of the food on Houston, I would wonder what all the fuss was about.  The food at the cafe was just not good.  Very little lox for $17 and a horrid, stale, bland bagel with a tiny portion of cream cheese, tomato and onions - just not what I would even call a good lox sandwich.  Also ordered the kasha varnishkas, something I normally love, and the bow tie noodles had a sweet flavor which I've never experienced anywhere else before and do not want to ever again.

The decor is cute but we found the booths uncomfortable and very tight.  Waitress was pleasant but front reception people almost seemed to glare at us when we came in.  Will definitely stick to Houston Street -  as for the cafe, never again will be too soon.

I like Russ and Daughter's appetizing very much.  It's cramped, but it has a good vibe, and lovely smoked fish and cream cheese.

Their new cafe on Orchard St?  Meh.  

I had a "board" -- their term for an individual serving that includes a bagel, a modest amount of smoked fish, a small container of cream cheese, and some onions and capers -- with sturgeon.  It was delicious.  I know it's a restaurant, and I don't expect them to charge the same price as they do by the pound at the appetizing shop on Houston St; however, for $22, I think they could have been a bit more generous than 3 slices of sturgeon...  

Also, why is an appetizing place as spectacular as Russ and daughter not offering a VARIETY of different salmons at its cafe?  When I go into R+D, I don't say "Give me smoked salmon," I say "May I please have the New Zealand smoked salmon" or the Scottish or whatever.  Offering that kind of variety would make the Cafe a far more interesting and appealing place.  Even an average place that serves oysters on the half shell typically offers the diner the choice of several types...

In addition, its crowded at lunch.  They should take reservations.  I waited there quite a while, first for the rest of my party (not the Cafe's fault) then for a table (which was the Cafe's fault).  Waiting patrons = patrons who don't return...

I should note that It is nice and bright and clean.  And our waiter was very nice.

Still, only three stars, and almost two.

F'ing brilliant.  

Admit it If you can put a little slice of raw mackerel on rice and charge 3 dollars for it (hey I love sushi don't get me wrong) how much better a filet of pickled herring on a slice of black bread?    Damnit  people eat lox and rice with cream cheese and dare to call it sushi wtf?  We have all eaten smoked salmon eggs Benedict for brunch and loved it.  Admit it, you did it and you liked it!   Word.  This is a Renaissance, a rebirth a beautiful thing!   Un- clench  your fists and embrace the future! 

PS.  Whitefish salad tacos  would be a crime against God and nature. Juss sayin :)

Like many people who have written reviews of the Cafe, I've been a customer at Russ & Daughters' shop on East Houston forever. My dad and I used to make the trek there from the Bronx on a fairly regular basis when i was a kid. In any event, you're all correct: the restaurant is NOT the store. That said, my husband and I enjoyed our meal there immensely. We thought the decor was totally in the spirit of the store, and the service we received couldn't have been better. The food was fantastic (and yes, the portions aren't huge, but I generally find portions at restaurants to be too big, and I'm amazed at how much good food goes to waste, because people can't finish their gargantuan portions). We had a Shtetl (sable on a bialy w/tomato, cream cheese, capers, and onions), latkes, matzoh ball soup, and a DIVINE challah bread pudding & coffee. It was a bit spendy, but for the quality of the food, the atmosphere, and the service, I'll happily go back for more. In fact, I'm already looking ahead to our next meal there!

Even knowing what you're in for, the prices vs portions at Russ & Daughters Cafe are a bit of a shock. You either accept, wholeheartedly and whole-wallet-ly, that you are paying a premium to sit indoors in a charming cafe--and, if you're lucky, talk to a waiter who is channeling Woody Allen to add to the atmosphere--or go elsewhere.

And, as in clear in other reviews and using basic math, don't get the bagel board when you can get the same thing at the nearby Russ & Daughters deli for so much less. Instead, try a dish that is more than an overthought, DIY bagel sandwich.

We went on a Monday around 1pm, and waltzed right in and to a table. Seeing how not crowded it was then, if you have the choice, I wouldn't bother waiting in a line on a weekend.

First, you must to take the "Noshes" category title seriously. Despite their meal-like pricing, these are tiny bites, not meant on their own to be a meal. My partner and I shared the Pastrami Russ, which was really pleasant with it's warm pretzel roll, tart pickle, Muenster cheese, mustard, and best of all, pastrami'd salmon. The ingredients in concept struck the right balance, but there was not enough salmon compared to the other ingredients by a long shot, especially for a $12 nosh, and especially for how tasty the salmon was.

We shared a special herring plate with apple, pickled beets, and pickles, adding a challah bun for $1. More flavorful than filling, it was also nosh sized . One piece of herring, creamy textured and briny bright, and a tablespoon each of meticulously microcubed fruit and vegetable. It absolutely worked for taste and presentation, but we savored each bite slowly to try to get the most out of our money (I think it was around $10).

I skipped right past the vanilla and chocolate egg creams--why get those typical flavors when they can be had in any NY diner for $2? Instead I got the buxar (carob) egg cream, which was unlike any egg cream I've had before, malty and luscious. The cucumber soda ($5) tasted like...cucumbers and, was not unique enough to be worth it.

We loved the blintzes with jam and sour cream ($8). I've made blintzes myself, and what a pain in the toches--so they're highly worth ordering when you're at a restaurant. The plate came with two fat blintzes, the crepe crispy on top, perfectly doughy elsewhere, stuffed thick with whipped barely sweet farmers cheese. The blueberry jam was almost entirely comprised of whole, fresh blueberries. Really fantastic, classically done dish.

If we were having a regular lunch, instead of a nosh stop, that would not have been enough food. I would have added on a whitefish chowder, which looked outstanding, and a scale up to the full herring platter. Those additions would have taken lunch well over $30 each, which is not a lunch I could justify often.

One problem I had was we sat at one of the high tables with stools. If you are short like me, don't sit at these high tables. The stools were built for taller people, fixed to the table and unmovable with a foot rest that I could barely touch with my toes, and so were really uncomfortable and awkward.

The rub is, if you can ignore the pricing you could love Russ & Daughters Cafe, like I did. Having moved away from NY over a decade ago, it gave me a dose of a lot of what I miss, all in one meal. Eating there could never become an affordable habit, but as an occasional treat, it's worth it.

Loved this modern trendy take on Russ & Daughters traditional fourth generation appetizing store. I had the Lower East Side Sunny. Food looks beautiful and tastes great. The only thing that kept me from giving the full 5 stars was service was just a bit off on the very busy day we were there. In one case a utensil came after the food and milk for coffee arrived late. They did provide a little applesauce for my latkas when I asked. This made the already great latkas even better.  Longer review on my blog here:  http://thestarryeye.typepad.com/explorenyc/2014/06/-russ-daughters-and-.html

This place ain't cheap. You won't get huge, heaping portions of food. But what you will get is real tasty food that you savor with every bite. I had the Shtetl and split a Holland herring. The herring was buttery, but firm, briny, and could eaten by itself. The accompanying onions and cornichons should be used sparingly to enjoy the clean flavors of the fish.

The sable in the Shtetl is pretty damn amazing and went well w/ the red, ripe tomatoes, red onions, capers and goat cheese. The only misfire was the bagel that had been sitting around all day. Then again, that should've been expected since the bagels are made once and delivered in the morning. I saw some breakfast stuff I wanted to try so I'll be back for sure. And if the prices give you pause, you can always get the heebster, shtetl and mensch at the original store to go for a little less.
Really poor customer service
So happy they finally have a sit down cafe to enjoy the deliciousness stress-free!!!!
Like your grandmother's kosher dairy restaurant only with better coffee , more refined food, friendlier service and quadruple the price.

Slow service for a not-too-crowded early lunch - but the food was delicious!  Highly recommend the matzo ball soup and the kasha varnishkes.  Bread basket was good too, though it came with butter and not cream cheese (for shame!).

A cool, modern version of a traditional Jewish Deli.  Great, creative presentation.  We share a nova platter (skimpy on the fish) but great quality, and the herring platter which was awesome.
Great decor and efficient service.
On the pricey side but very good.

Being a fan of the original, I just had an obligation as a New Yorker to give this a try right?  I did just that, inside is a new clean modern look with a nice bar counter to plop down on if you don't want to wait for a table.

I went with the sturgeon, eggs, and onions plate.  Thought I'd fancy it up today and everything was done very well.  My only complaint about this place is the price...$20 for that??  Ouch, clearly not a spot to get breakfast at every morning...

First, no, it is not Barney Greengrass, but then Orchard Street is not the Upper West Side.
Second, it does not have to be as The Cafe enjoys its own wonderful and unique pedigree.  

In a word, I  was very Happy there, sitting in a booth and thrilled with the options presented before me. I settled for a lox platter, served with too very toasted, scooped out bagels. The bagels arrived perfectly toasted and scooped out as if by a surgeon who left his/her profession.

The lox was creamy and smooth, but, the truth was that I wanted belly lox. When I requested it, I was told, they don't serve it; there simply isn't the demand. I was more than a little disappointed, but told I could stop at the shop up the street, and buy the belly lox, and would be served without a "corking" fee.  I also ate a Holland Herring fillet, which was everything and more than advertised. Worth a year's wait? Yes.

Of special note, the Babka French toast was almost too good. I had to be physically restrained by my friend, Boym, from ordering a second slice. On my next visit I will go with a friend who is less health conscious. 

A bright, cheery  and unaffected place, I plan to return at least once a week, and therefore recommend it unreservedly.

PS Having read a number of reviews that mention "This place ain't cheap," I will simply say: Eat there and skip your next meal or two. In the end, it all works out.

What a beautiful place to have delicious fish at a premium price!  Yes, the lox and sable were absolutely wonderful.  However, three THIN slices weren't enough for my small appetite.  There were more than amble tomatoes, onions and capers - but for the price, how about 4 slices - at least then you'll have two very thin slices on each side of your also small bagel.

So glad they opened an actual restaurant offshoot of the famous Houston St. Location. This place has without a doubt the best smoked salmon if ever had. Friendly staff, fast service. If coming on a weekend, come early, it gets pretty packed. The Lower Sunny Side and the Hot Smoke/Cold Smoke dishes are a must!

Food is great, but the portions are way too small for the prices. I feel confident saying that because if you go to the original counter on Houston, you get an XXXL serving of lox on your bagel for the same or a cheaper price. Whitefish salad with wasabi roe was good but not great and not worth the price. The guy next to me ordered the usual bagel with lox and actually was moved to complain about the laughably small portion. No one is there to pay $20 to be served one measly flaky piece of lox draped unceremoniously on a cutting board. I felt like we were getting punked. 

Moral of story: just stick to Houston, unless you want to pay significantly more (plus tax, tip, the drink you'll need) to sit at a shiny white bar and be irritated.

So incredibly delicious. Perfect crispy potato latkes with roe and creme fraiche and I believe a smoked salmon dip of some kind with their house made chips. Plenty for two. Lovely location, too. Go go go!

Ehhh kinda too pricey and the wait on the weekends isn't worth it probably but damn does Russ and Daughters (Russ and his Daughters, her daughters? Oh, the ambiguity) still does fish the best.

I had the shtetl plate which came with rye, goat cheese, onion/caper/tomato, and sable. And lord that sable. So delicate, buttery and rich. Honestly put a tear in my eye thinking how much my grandad would have liked it.

fantastic service, superb food and drink, and the ambience is a perfect measure of openness and moderate lighting combined with a feeling of intimacy

it's like being at the most refined, elegant diner you've ever gone to, and instead of burgers and fries-type fare, they serve exquisitely cooked fish, egg dishes, and a few unusual treats

if you think the portions are small, perhaps you're used to eating the gigantic portions that are so much a part of American dining culture (and arguably contribute to obesity); if you are European, of European leaning, vegan, athletic, and/or very healthy, you will like think the portions are perfect

prices high? well, maybe compared to the cheapest diner below 14th St (whatever that might be)

I now go to this place EVERY week; it is my new fave restaurant in the City; and that's after dining pretty regularly in Manhattan since 1996

One of my good friends has been introducing me to some great places with Jewish fare. After about a 45 min wait, we were able to try out this newish hot spot for brunch.

We both had one thing on our minds when going here: the babka French toast! It totally lived up to its hype. It was one of the most delicious things I've ever eaten. It sounds exactly like how it will be: babka used instead of bread and prepared like French toast. Do yourself a favor and come here for this. It comes with chocolate babka but I think they should consider cinnamon as an option as well. This was more of a dessert to me so I could only eat a little bit in the morning. I got the eggs, lox and onions as my meal, which was quite standard but very flavorful. We both shared the potato latkes with salmon roe and creme fraiche. This was my first time having them but they were delicious and my friend (who grew up on this food) thought they were excellent.

The rest of the menu here looks so good. I would have to say the dessert list is what will bring me back here (challah bread pudding, havlah ice cream, kugel, etc). They are open till 10pm and offer a nice cocktail list, which gives me the perfect opportunity to come back for dessert and drinks and also avoid the brunch crowd wait.

Today's NYT runs a review I generally agree with... save for the omission of three salient points. First, if you are a Jewish specialty place and cannot serve a bagel that isn't as hard as concrete, call it a day. (Not just our experience... we observed several customers banging their bagels on the table like gavels -- DO NOT risk losing a tooth... take a pass!). Second, a latke should be bigger than a flattened tater-tot. Third, if you have to wait 45-minutes for your scrambled eggs with lox to be served you are not running an efficient kitchen. Sadly, I have to say that not since Bernie Madoff have Jews been so mistreated by one of their own.

Hands down BEST smoked salon of my life. It's sliced thin and melts in your mouth. The coffee is rich and perfection. Also if you enjoy a good knish, the outside is light and flaky. The knish is delish!!! Every time I come to NYC, this is where you'll find me.

Love the decor in this place! Came here for brunch and after a 2 hr wait and suppressing our hanger..our service was pretty prompt and attentive. We had ordered the pastrami Russ which wasn't bad if you like mustard, the super heebster which was really good but really small, and the lower sunny side which seemed kind of disjointed but yummy. The drinks are wonderful - cucumber soda and shrubs were yummy. I wish the food and drinks lasted longer since they were pretty delish. Eat here with plans to eat elsewhere.

Couldn't wait to try the new cafe at Russ & Daughters! The restaurant is beautiful and you feel like you have been transported back to an old fashioned ice cream parlor or apothecary. Names of classic Jewish foods line the ceiling and made me smile.

Our waiter was funny and a real character, making the meal memorable.

Food was ok but not great. I may not have ordered properly (I've heard the babka french toast is out of this world). We started with a salmon dip appetizer that was really nice but then both had the classic bagel board for mains. The lox was outstanding (so unbelievably soft) but the bagels were not impressive at all. They were small and hard, making it difficult to bite through. The boards were also absurdly expensive ($16 each)!! Not worth it in my opinion. He egg cream on the other hand was excellent.

If only they could bring in bagels from Ess-a-bagel...perfection would be had!

Delicious sodas, sumptuous salmon and fish in the most ridiculously undersized portions (or disproportionately priced). The service leaves a lot to be desired, but the décor and the menu are exquisitely designed.

we were so excited to come here after the article in the New York Times and a tad disappointed. YES, the decor was fresh and loved the staff in pharmacist style jackets and they were VERY kind and helpful, no attitude here at all, but 40 minutes to wait? Come on, then the food was good but not as good as what you can buy at Zabar's and take out! The rye was stale and few seeds and too chewy, the smoked salmon was top notch, the potato pancakes were good but think and not as good as my Jewish mom's handgrated latkes...the herring trio was cute, bites, but....we are so glad we came but will think twice abotu a return. And then we walked around the corner to the store and bougt a rye--really mediocre, ruggelach that were ok but not as fab as can be when again homemade, and so-so gefilte fish. We so wanted to LOVE this place and don't understand the Times' writer's hyperbolic fabulous article, oh well. the prices were not outrageous, however, though portions were too small. It is fun to walk around the LES, see other food stores, including Essex Market, and there's a  restaurant with lobster rolls and more we will try next time.

This is a tough one. I am passionately in love with Russ & Daughters as the pre-eminent standard for smoked fish, caviiar, lox in NYC (it's been the measuring stick for 100 years). Can't mention how many times I've been there and had nothing but great food for takeout and thought it was always reasonably priced and worthy. So I was eagerly looking to try the new Cafe a few blocks away on the LES. Really pricey. $7 for an egg cream (you need to try one if you haven't) but seriously? Food was yummy but expensive. $16 for a lox bagel? The lox is exquisite, tastes like butter and is dreamy smooth. But they serve it on rubber bagels. Bagels actually are sub-par, reminded me of Lender's a little. They won't do takeout here, it's only table service. My advice? walk a few blocks and get the real deal and take it home.

We waited 10 minutes for a table at lunch on a Monday, which didn't seem bad at all.  The friendly hostess even went back a couple of times to keep us updated on how long the wait would be.

The dining room is very nice, comfy booths, and the service is friendly and efficient.  The smoked fish was wonderful.  But...my toasted bialy was cold and barely toasted, and the portion of smoked salmon was very small.  For $16, they should serve enough to cover the bialy.  

We wanted to order a few tastes of different smoked fish, but at $80 for a sharing plate, it was out of the question.

The café is a nice treat, but for regular fare I'll buy fresh smoked fish at Russ & Daughters, and eat at home (with better bagels and bialys, toasted).

The ONLY place for any of your bagel/shmear needs in the city. I came here on my last trip and waited almost an hour, but dear god...was it worth the wait. The service is amazing. But be prepared to wait!

The smoked salmon board was delicious.  I liked the fact that the bagel was not the size of my head.  There was just enough of everything to satisfy.  

We also had an order of the Latkes.  While not my favorite, the were good.  (It must be difficult to serve food this steeped in family tradition.  You're not going to compete with grandma's recipe)

The servers were very friendly.  Overall, I was very happy and will  be back.

Was entertaining friends a few weekends ago and came here for brunch. Our server was really great, knowledgeable and attentive. She even gave me some tips for dying my hair blonde, as she was in the process of doing the same. What I can only assume was the manager was stomping around, very frantic, and being very rude to employees...a few tables noticed and it made us a little uncomfortable but maybe it was just a bad day for him. Anyway, food was really great, salmon obviously amazing,  atmosphere very charming. Overall a nice experience. If I am in the area I will come back again.

As a LES resident, I get the pleasure of witnessing the insane lines that the original Russ and Daughters pulls. I've battled through the crowd a couple times for their lox bagels but otherwise just pass by. 

At the opening of their new cafe, I was surprised, and intrigued. Since they open at 8am, I was able to get a quick breakfast in with an out of town guest before going to work. I was surprised to see the difference in the set up to the original location (but I had no idea what to expect). I must say, they did an awesome job on this place. It makes you want to take all kinds of pictures for your instagram. 

I ordered the french toast. absolutely no regret to be had, it was AMAZING. it had chocolate baked into it. no syrup served, no syrup needed. The strawberries they paired with with took it to the next level. It was hands down the best. Also really great coffee with outstanding service so your cup is never even half empty. The food came out really fast (keep in mind we were 1 of 3 tables in there at the time,not sure what its like during a busier hour). My boyfriend had the eggs benny. it looked great and he seemed to like it. 

You have to try it out!

OH PS...its a pricey breakfast. eggs benny, french toast and 2 coffees came to $37 before tip

Dang, prices are steep - but they haven't stopped me from coming here three out of the last five times I've gone out to eat. I enthusiastically recommend Russ & Daughters to my friends because I just cannot get enough of the Hot Smoke/Cold Smoke (though I'm not sure where the hot part is). 

The first time I came here, I split the Hot Smoke/Cold Smoke (HSCS from now on) and potato latkes with salmon roe with a friend. We were both pleasantly full, though we found that there was a lot more salmon spread leftover, even when we piled it generously on top of our waffle chips. That spread is ridiculously addicting, and I would buy some if I could. In quarts, preferably. I'd put it on everything. The latkes were good, as was the salmon roe, but I don't think I'd go out of my way to order them again because I've had comparable latkes. 

The second time I came here, my friend and I opted to get a bread basket to accompany the HSCS. It was an excellent idea, but it was waaay too much bread for the two of us. The HSCS is definitely an appetizer, but the bread basket transformed it into a carby, filling lunch. I think the bread basket's meant for 4+ people. 

The third time I came here, I got the babka French toast. My friend got the potato latkes and I convinced her to get the HSCS to split. The appetizer and our two entrées were more than enough for the two of us, and I left feeling both mildly guilty for stuffing my face and unrepentent because both the French toast and the HSCS were so decadently delicious. It's hard to venture off these favorites, but I'm confident that the other salmon dishes will be good. I'll just have to make sure to come early and get a lot of people so I can finally share a board. 

4 stars for now because it appears that the Russ & Daughters bagel place offers much more salmon for much less. Hmmmm ... I'll have to check that.

We (party of three) had a great time here tonight. 

The service was awesome!

I had the matzo ball soup and potato latkes with salmon roe and creme fraiche. Absolutely delicious!

Definitely planning to come here again soon!
Great latkes, great matzo ball, great creme fraiche, great roe, great salmon, great atmosphere, great bathroom, great service

Timing is everything. 

We stopped the day before for a late Sunday lunch (around 1:30 p.m.) and the crowd outside suggested that the wait was long (and must be worth it). So, Monday (Labor Day) we tried a late breakfast around 10:30....and walked right in. Man! Worth the wait.

First off, the place is clever, tight and  designed. Fun interior with a lot of personality which translates to the people that work there to the attitude of the food, the graphics, the descriptions, the presentation. Pitch perfect. We were charmed immediately by it all. Sublime, perfect, funny, amusing.

My son and I had the "classic" smoked salmon with bialys and were amazed by the sheer perfection of the fish....and the crispy snap of the bread (no doughy mess here). We split an appetizer with whitefish and wasabi infused caviar (OMG....beyond sublime..mixing classic deli with tastes that are part of their wheelhouse but takes it to another place. Creative/delicious/ outrageous. We all had bottomless cups of coffee but were tempted by the shrubs, the egg creams and other drinks we saw on crowded trays going to other tables.

Love doesnt even begin to describe our feelings for Russ and Daughters Cafe. We want to get married...or at least return, as soon as possible.

Dinner with Mom, Dad, Auntie, and Spouse. Arrived at 7:30 on a Saturday night and were seated immediately ("brunch rush ended at 4:30," the hostess said). Though every table was soon occupied, the restaurant remained quiet throughout the evening--in downtown Manhattan on a weekend evening, that's worth its wait in gold. The bread arrived. The bread was superb. The rye is as good as they say--it has a wonderful malted taste--and the meal fell in line beautifully from there. Velvety smoked sable, whitefish, and herring salad; for the non-pescatarians, mushroom barley soup and borscht (the latter perhaps the better of the two, with wonderful clean flavors). Dessert--halva ice cream--was ingeniously delicious. A ribbon of halva running through the icea cream. The service was very good, and the decor--from the lighting on the bar to, I kid you not, the paper towel dispenser in the bathroom--was thrillingly perfect. I look forward to going back!

Stopped by here for a Saturday brunch. I'm not even a huge smoked fish fan, but wanted to give it a try and I can always find SOMETHING I like. I was debating between the trout and the sturgeon, so they offered me the chance to sample them both, which was great. I ended up loving the sturgeon and not the trout, which is the opposite of what I expected. Had the sturgeon board, with an everything bagel. We had a sweet, funny older man as our waiter - he was great. My only complaints are the ridiculous prices (definitely not worth it, but had to do it once) and the awkward high table we sat at, where my feet couldn't even rest on the floor or my chair. They just dangled there... haha.

We loved it. Came for dinner on a Saturday evening-they were busy, but we didn't have to wait. The hot smoke/cold smoke dip was definitely the favorite of the evening. The Pastrami Russ was really good-maybe a bit too strong with the mustard and sauerkraut. The Classic Board, was classic and perfect.

I decided to amble in here for a late afternoon snack around 3pm. As a solo diner, I had a wait time of ~20 minutes until I was seated at the bar. Parties of two were quoted an hour though, even so late in the day!

I decided on the super heebster since I had already ate. Even though I was warned by the bartender that it was a small portion size, surely a combo of fish salad, cream cheese and toast would be filling enough? I was proven so wrong.

The heebster was an open faced sandwich and half of it could fit my palm easily. I was very disappointed that a $10 sandwich turned out to be so small. I felt almost tricked like this was the cafe's ploy to get diners to order more.

I also got the pineapple vinegar drink which was good but not great. In the end, I spent $20 for a tiny snack and a drink. Not worth my time or money. The woman next to me had the classic salmon board and thought it was worth the wait though, so who knows.

We went to New York for the San Gennaro festival so our intent was to eat Italian all day. We walked by Russ and Daughters and figured a non-Italian breakfast could be interesting. WOW, I have had traditional Jewish food before but the food here is outstanding. The chicken liver is the best I've ever had, the herring selections are amazing and very fresh and the chocolate babka French toast should be illegal in 49 states. 

We ended up having breakfast there all three days of our trip and I'm having withdrawals already.

Shared the Ida platter with three others. We were definitely full and there were four slices of each fish, so that worked out.

Skip the latkes, they were over fried and bland. I also didn't care for the knishes.

The wait is pretty long because the space is small. I would rather go to the deli location and just grab a bagel prepared by the expert staff.

I love Russ and Daughters Cafe for the fine quality and perfect portion size.  One does not leave stuffed and one does not leave starved. The price is right for the delectable cuisine. 
The decor is a nod to those who came before. It's like stepping a back into time, with subtle current additions. 

I have had the Heebster (perfect breakfast choice!), the laktes (delicious), several of the bagels and fish and cannot wait to continue through the rest of the menu.

I am quite surprised by the negative reviews. 

Then again, I guess there are those who cannot be not satisfied with a meal until they are filled to the gills, judging everything based on how little they can spend in their gluttonous pursuits. Russ and Daughters is not for them.  They should go to canal street near church and get a table at Tribeca Bagels, which may be more their speed.

But for those of you who love quality, good decor and fantastic food, I highly recommend Russ and Daughters.

Came here for weekend brunch. Got a couple of the egg dishes, knishes, blitzes, and the pastrami salmon sandwich. Had high hopes for this place but the food, frankly, just wasn't that good. Perhaps eggs and brunch fare isn't their core competency. Plus, it's quite a wait, prices are steep, and portions are small, so I say stick with the old Russ and Daughters for now.

Went for a late-night dinner on a Friday night. Portions were laughably small for ridiculously high prices. This place seems to be running on pure hype. The food tasted good, but honestly, it was not worth it. At least we didn't have to wait at all. I recommend going to the original Russ & Daughters to get food to go.

It's 2014 and Bubbe wears Prada.

One must make peace with the fact that the simple, common and unsophisticated appetizing delights of the early to mid 1900s are no long on every other block but the few that are left are pretty fantastic, the Russ & Daughters outposts being at the top.

Like it's clinic-white parent shop this restaurant also boasts many of the same food items and white jacket motif that makes the shop so charming while flying somewhere between casual and upscale depending on where you sit and what you order. An eight dollar matzo ball soup can be found a column over from a $500 serving of caviar. I stuck with the soup on this trip and it stuck to my ribs for the next several hours. It's pricey but also very well made and won't leave your face grimacing from an overdose of sodium and schmaltz common in other matzo ball soups.

Combine the soup with the chicken liver plate and you got yourself a hearty lunch that won't put you to sleep. The perfectly-spiced pate has a good, somewhat chunky consistency that spreads firm on the matzo and contrasts so nicely with the side of pickled onions. I'd eat this stuff every other day.

Order an egg cream too and play some stickball with your pals after.

IN LOVE with Russ & Daughters Cafe.  I always loved the original Russ & Daughters, but struggled with where to eat my bagel and lox after picking it up.  The cafe is the answer to that question and so much more.  

The space is impeccably designed and nods to it's 100 year old heritage but also feels fresh and modern.  The menu is perfect - with the right balance of options that leave you wanting to come back, but also few enough that each dish is thought through and perfectly executed.  Of course the fish is incredible, but they also have lots of other wonderful things to try, such as chocolate babka french toast, potato latkes, and egg dishes.

If only it didn't constantly have hour+ waits on weekend mornings, I would be here constantly.  I guess I may be reverting back to the LES stoop to eat my take-out bagel from the shop on Houston.
Don't be a putz, complaining about NY prices. Eat your fish.

Stopped by for lunch on a Thursday.  Service and ambiance were great. Call me old fashion, but my issue is with their Matzo Ball soup.  The broth tasted like Lipton's Instant Chicken Noodle soup and the Matzo Ball, whose consistency was soft and could be cut with a spoon, was almost tasteless.  The chopped liver needed salt and the pickled red onions just didn't go with it; I would have preferred fresh raw onions.
The Baked Farmer Cheese was tasty and went well with the pumpernickel.  All in all, my mother, may she rest in peace, made better Matzo Ball soup and chopped liver. Fortunately she left me her recipes.

so amazing - I had seen this place on TV and had to check it out. the food was out of this world - plenty of smoked and pickled fish and roe, some fine drinks as well. the staff was polite and professional, the whole place was clean. I wish I had more money and time to spend there and will definitely be going back next time I go into town!

This was a great choice for a late afternoon snack. The portions were just right, a little pricey but the quality, ambiance and service were terrific! A plus was having Niki Tuss Federman welcome us at HHS door. So great to experience ongoing history...four generations!

Looking for the market, we stumbled upon the cafe version and stopped to eat because we were starving. During lunch on Monday, Columbus Day, the wait was about an hour. We were seated a little quicker because we were willing to sit at the bar. We pondered over the menu for a while before deciding on a bowl of the smoked whitefish chowder and the Classic bagel board on an everything bagel.

The chowder was good with a decent amount of whitefish with every scoop. The board was a cool idea, everything presented and you putting it together. The bagel itself was delicious. Add on the cream cheese, smoked salmon, and tomato? That all made for a delicious sandwich. I also got the Concord Grape House soda which was okay. All that being said, I'm not sure I could justify the prices for all the things (chowder - $10, board - $16, and soda - $5).

Next time I'm in NYC, I'll have to stop by the original location instead!

Lovely as you'd expect. That said, how did our bagels and lox come with two slices of salmon each. Two? 
Two?
For real? 
We were visiting here a day after I had returned from a trip to Scotland where I basically had to push salmon away. Salmon literally was jumping in my mouth in Scotland and then here at Russ & Daughters... two slices.
That's crazy.
C'mon tourists!

Gotta say I was disappointed. I've been wanting to go for a while and after a 30 minute wait, we ordered a bunch of options - all of which were good, but nothing more than the average bagel/lox. There are plenty of other options besides this - for one, try Baz bagel down the block, it has a better menu, higher quality food and has way better service.

Arrived at Russ & Daughters early in the morning after a long flight from Israel. There was a pile-up of luggage (including ours) at the entrance to the restaurant. Clearly, we were not the only travelers who made this their first stop in NYC before heading to their hotels. The smoked sable on bialy was super delicious -- the best I've ever had. Bravo!
Scrambled eggs with sturgeon is great.  Also eggs with salmon.  Very long wait on Sunday morning.
The business has been around since 1914 I think, but they just opened up this cafe, and their menu features every possible iteration of delicious smoked fish imaginable.

As a Native New Yorker who was raised on and loves smoked fish and caviar I decided to visit the Russ and Daughters cafe that opened about a year ago on Orchard Street in lower manhattan. 

The service was sub standard, the Bagels were below average, the potato Latkes over cooked and the smoked fish dry.

This restaurant itself is very narrow with limited seating and with no atmosphere whatsoever. 

In  addition to subpar food the place is run by rude and arrogant people who in my opinion know nothing about running a restaurant moreover customer service.

If your in the Big Apple and want excellent appetizing and caviar without all the hoopla and arogance visit following places:

1. Barney Greengrass / 542 Amsterdam Avenue NYC /  212-724-4707 / www.barneygreengrass.com

2. Sables / 1489 Second Avenue NYC / 212-249-6177 / www.sables.com

3. Zabar's / 2245 Broadway NYC /  212-787-2000 / www.zabars.com

4. Shelsky's Smoked Fish / 141 Court Street Brooklyn New York / 718-855- 8817  / www.shelskys.com

5. Zucker's / 146 Chambers Street Tribeca NYC / 212-608-5844 / www.zuckersbagelsnewyork.com

6. Kossar's (Just for Bagels and Bialys) 367 Grand Street NYC /  212 473-4810 / www.kossars.com

There are many others, the above just happen to be my favorites.

If Caviar is your thing then I would pay a visit to:

1. Caviar Russe / 538 Madison Avenue NYC / 212-980-5908 / www.caviarrusse.com

2. Petrossian / 212-245-2214 / www.Petrossian.com

3. Zabars / 2245 Broadway NYC /  212-787-2000 / www.zabars.com

4. Browne Trading company Caviar / http://www.brownetrading.com/

I used to love the fish from russ and daughters.  What happened when the new generation took over did they start buying cheaper fish and charging more for it?  I guess the new family members forgot what their parents and grandparents built through high quality and great customer service can be destroyed in ten seconds through low quality and rudeness. Guess I'll be buying my fish at a place where they thank you for spending a few hundred dollars on breakfast.

Interesting.

Being neither Jewish nor New Yorker this was a totally different culinary experience for me.

Needless to say I had no idea what to expect nor was this my choice but I'm glad I went.  For those of you already in the cab, on the way (as I was) this is not your average diner.  Your not getting a pastrami sandwhich or flapjacks.  No, your getting something smoked (not meat), something cured, something pickled and something schmeared!  

My coworkers had borscht and matzo ball soup.  They enjoyed it.  We all shared an order of the sours and latkes.  They were very good.  Especially the sours.  And the sours complimented everything else.  The latkes were crisp and tasty.  Mind you I have not had them all that often (much like everything else here) so my barometer might not be the same as yours.  

For my main dish I had the Pastrami Russ.  Pastrami cured salmon (I didn't even know that was a thing) on a pretzle roll with sauerkraut, Munster cheese, mustard and a pickle.  Well, that's what it tasted like!  It wasn't bad!  But it also was not my cup of tea.  Between the texture and the very bitter flavors this was a very unique dish.  It came with thin (fresh) waffle chip.  This was actually an appetizer so the servings were small and just right.  

Here is the thing, this type of food is not really my wheelhouse but i was glad I tried it and I would recommend others to try it as well.  It's not bad but no doubt it is an acquired taste.  I have not acquired it as of yet.

Excellent New York breakfast food like bagels and lox in an old fashioned ice cream parlor like atmosphere. The Jewish comfort food menu is good but pricey. The bagels are good though a bit small and the fish is out of this world, but $16 for a bagel with lox and creme cheese is harsh. The cocktails were very testy as well and they have a superb bloody Mary selection.

This place is amazing. Almost shocked at how every dish we ordered was amazing. Solid.

The Classic board: Of course is a must, as you can tell from all the photos and reviews on it. The lox is delicious and no foul seafood smell, which is important to me. They could have given a little more lox than two slices. Love the capers, which gives the dish the much needed seasoning. The bagel was a little dry and dull, but definitely recommend this dish. 

Super Heebster: Easily my favorite dish from here. Can't put into words of my experience. Highly recommend.

Farm Omelette: The fluffiest omelette I've ever seen. The filling was a little bit watery, but nevertheless delicious.

I already look forward to going back here.

Love it here. Whenever I go I get put in the best mood and feel so satisfied. I usually get the classic board and it's amazing and everything so so fresh and delicious. One thing to keep in mind.  The class board is about $16 and I usually get about 3 slices of lox (I know it's measured by weight but..) and at the Russ and Daughters deli for a classic sand which its about $10 and I noticed that I receive a lot more lox for my money. They do up charge at the cafe but the sit down service is great. 

ALSO you must try the babka French toast.... It's literally the most amazing melt in your mouth treat you will ever try....!

While we were sitting in the window waiting for a table, the man sitting next to us - also waiting for a table - started chatting with my kids. He turned out to be none other than Mark Russ, the grandson of the founder of the original Russ & Daughters store. 

Russ & Daughters isn't your typical diner-looking Jewish deli. They have meticulously replicated particular details of the the original Russ & Daughters store, from the signs around the restaurant to the servers dressed in white lab coats.

We got two small knishes in our order. They were excellent. The matzoh ball soup was very good (did the balls have extra schmaltz?), but I still prefer Second Avenue Deli's. The latkes were outstanding and we almost ordered another whole plate of them. We couldn't resist ordering the chocolate babka french toast. It was yummy and very chocolately but only consisted of one slice for $10.

I didn't know what to expect with the pastrami salmon (I had never heard of such a thing), but it was not at all fishy and was wonderfully tender. It came with beautifully latticed housemade potato chips (wish there were more), and I wondered if the mustard was homemade. I loved this dish. It also showed how the restaurant was different from other Jewish delis - it truly is a cafe. The portions aren't ridiculously huge and they don't focus on super meaty sandwiches. And since the portions are smaller you can try more things. These are both pluses for me since I prefer to nosh on things like knishes, latkes, and matzoh ball soup anyway. Additionally, the menu listed so many things I wanted to try I was really disappointed when we weren't able to come back for a second time before we left. It's at the very top of my list for my next New York visit.

Two things I would like to see them change: 1) I SO wish they let people place to-go orders. We stayed in an apartment across the street and wanted to bring in dinner one night while our kids were sleeping (nope). Another day when there was a 1 1/2 hour wait (beware going there on weekend mornings!) we would have gladly just picked up our order. 2) I wish they would change their voicemail so I wouldn't have to listen to a message that's over a minute long just to talk to a person and ask if our table was ready.

They open at 10am, but there's a line by 9:30 on the weekends made up of mostly larger parties, so if you're just one or two you should be able to grab a seat. I love the Pastrami Russ but its a 3-4 bite thing, so I recommend getting the chocolate french toast as well. If you're in the mood for eggs I like the Lower Sunny Side so you get to enjoy the latkes + their celebrated smoked salmon versus the Eggs Benny which you can get anywhere.

Okay.  So the main reason this gets anything less than five stars: there's a better selection of lox in a deli setting at there other location.  Their deli is a deli, a good, high-end, well-stocked deli.  And you get more for your money at the deli.

It shouldn't be a compromise.  But alas.  One is a superb deli with no seating, one is a nice, sleek cafe with bar tables, a bar with short stools, and tables in the back.  Seating galore!  I want to look at the selections before I order, I also want to sit and relax while I eat my well-chosen food.  I want to get more than two thin slices of lox for my bagel, I also wouldn't mind constructing my bagel with lox myself via a wood cutting board spread.  Oh the dilemma!

I got a cutting board with my bagel and lox set up.  I also got a beet shrub, although it was poured over ice.  Wow.  The cost was worth going once, but not again.  I also kept having issues sitting on the bar stool at my little table.  Cute setup with a hook for my bag, even, but the foot rest was ::just:: out of comfortable foot range.  I could reach it with my toes.

So...the four stars?  You're not going to get much better quality than Russ & Daughters.  That's it really.  In a giant nut shell.

Just had a Lower Sunny Sid as the restaurant and a delight daughters at the houston's deli. All I would say is that they still fresh, delicious and with a service warm and friendly. I had the potato latkes for the first time and it was perfect. Definitely Russ & daughter is a must go destination in NYC.
