Wow! Only been there once, and already in love! We've been longtime fans of the century-old store, so were curious about the new cafe. We knew they don't take reservations, so on a cold and dismal night we went, and were seated immediately. Even though the cafe only opened this year, they've patterned it after the store, so it looks old.  There are booths in the back, a couple of tall tables in the front, and seats at the full bar. 

We tried a signature drink, the "Shmoozer," kind of bitter but in a good way, and some nice beer on tap. How about the food? OK, the matzoh ball soup and the borscht both great, the borscht a thick puree unlike any I've had before; really tasty. 

Of course we got some smoked fish, sable, and it was so melt-in-your-mouth good, you could plotz. They're NOT kosher, so there were meat specials. I got some nice chicken paprikash that was a little spicy, in a good way. 

We were feeling so convivial that we ordered a dessert, challah bread pudding (with apricots and caramel syrup) and a cup of their delicious signature coffee. 

We had a wonderful dinner experience all around, but I bet for brunch, this place would be really crowded. Can't wait to go back.

Ohmygod...I had no idea what to expect with the herring, but man...I want some more. 

My boyfriend showed me the video with Louis CK eating some fish straight in the Russ & Daughters deli store. I didn't think much of it. So when we were picking dinner on our first night in NYC, we thought we should give the Russ & Daughters diner a try since we wanted a place to sit down. You would've thought we were crazy for ordering 3 things to share and then ordering the eggs benedict, but here's the verdict:

Assorted Herring Platter: I think there were about 4 different types of sliced herring on here. We finished it all. I wish I knew what each of them were, but it was so good. Some were a bit on the salty side so it's good to eat on top of a slice of bread. My favorite one was the one that was a bit pickled and sweet. 

Potato Latkes: We got these with the fish roe and creme fraiche. Even though I'm not much of a potato person, I love latkes. These were quite possibly the best ones I've ever had, but honestly, my word probably means nothing since I've never had too many of these. So much good flavor, and still kind of crunch. Like hashbrowns or imagine them as flat tater tots.

Shtetl Board: This is one of those boards where you can make kind of an open faced sandwich. This comes with smoked sable, cream cheese, onions and capers, and we chose the rye bread. Mmm, so good. 

Eggs Benedict: I thought we'd be full, but since we don't know when we'd be back, my boyfriend wanted the eggs benedict. I'm not a huge eggs benedict fan, but you know what sets this apart from others? Not only were the eggs perfectly poached but the hollandaise sauce was surprisingly light. The sauteed spinach is a nice touch on these. 

Chocolate Egg Cream: I had this for dessert. To me, it tastes like chocolate milk with sparkling water. I've never had it before so I don't know what to compare it to, but I probably wouldn't get it again.

There's nothing not to like about this place. I would LOVE to come back and even go to the deli/market store since it sounds like they have a wider selection.

This is a great way to experience the famous Russ & Daughters for a traveler.  The deli counter up the street is great, but if you're visiting the city, you may not be able to accommodate buying amazing items to go.  If you'd prefer to have the same great stuff with table service, get to the cafe.  If you go, you must at least step into the deli to check it out.  It's an icon.

Knew beforehand that some of the servings are small and that it is expensive, but we are BIG fans of the E. Houston home and wanted to give it a try (plus the halvah ice cream was the subject of my dreams for several nights). Oh, lordy, was this stuff great! We went on an off hour (11:00 on a Thursday), so wasn't crowded. The waitress was extremely pleasant. I ordered the smoked sable plate and my husband ordered scrambled eggs/lox/potato latkes. We had the herring sampler for an appetizer. I was really happy that my sable wasn't too big so that I could fit desert (and I love their small dense bagels). Both of us loved the food: it's just the best, no other competitors. Of course, if you go to the mother ship you can choose a variety and get exactly what you want (and probably cheaper in the long run), but here you get to sit and enjoy (and did I mention ice cream?). Everything looked great---babka french toast, noodle kugel, sturgeon, herring, lox. Gotta go back 20 times.

This place was PHENOMENAL! At first I was a bit taken back by the prices--wanting a cheap brunch to curb the hunger for the day--but it ended up being more than worth it. The food was so great and the service was punctual and friendly. 

It may not be my go to cheap brunch spot, but it's definitely on my list of restaurants to go back to!

The vibe was very true to it's roots and I appreciated the decor. I'm glad they didn't divorce itself from it's originally located (which I've visited but funny enough never purchased anything).

Had some latkes which were on the burnt side but were good. Hey they're fried fucking potatoes, of course they'll be good. I got the board with sable and my GF got the original. I thought there would be more fish but comboing it with red onion, tomato and cheese is always good. The one upsetting part was the choice of bagels. I'd expect a better quality bagel from a NY legend like R&D but again this is the cafe. 

I wouldn't revisit the cafe but this definitely makes me want to go to the original where they're apparently a little more heavy handed with the CC and salmon. Daddy likes pescado with his queso ;)

I wanted to try something on the menu other than the heebster but then I remembered: HEEBSTER! How could I get anything else? Visually the place is a wonder. It's like being transported back to another era. They nailed it. Spot on. The only thing missing is the butcher paper from the location around the block. Opening up a sandwhi he from there was like unwrapping a present. One last thing: our 8 year old tried the heebster, loved it, and asked if we could come back for dinner. That says it all.

Don't waste your time!  We were so disappointed.  The waiter was so bad. 
When we overheard him tell the table next to our the specials and then asked
him why he didn't tell us they had specials his answer was that we were seated five minutes before they started serving them.  Really !!!

He forgot to bring the cocktail we ordered and had to remind him to remove it from the bill.  No apology and totally ignored us. This waiter was awful!!

The food was bland.  The matzah soup was tasteless and the board platter portion was  a nouveau riche serving.  

All in all a totally disappointing evening!!!  I could of stayed in our midtown neighborhood instead of traveling downtown.

Had in mind a fun day with my daughter, who is home on Christmas break from college, so we planned to have brunch at the new Russ & Daughters Cafe.  We arrived at about 1:45 on a Sunday, only to find that a lot of other people also had the same idea. The woman who took our names was very sweet, as she told us that we were in a for a 90 minute wait, but since she offered to text us when a table was ready, we decided to actually wait it out.  So we walked all over the Lower East Side, and eventually got the text.  When we arrived, we were seated at a cute-but-uncomfortable table for two, with backless-stools, and footrests that were too far away for my 5'2" frame.  Having already had plenty of time to memorize the menu, we ordered quickly.  Pleasantly, our meal was delivered quickly, too.  I ordered one of their sandwich "boards," which consisted of a toasted bagel, cream cheese, lox, tomatoes, capers and sliced onion served on a wooden cutting board, that you assemble yourself.  While the lox looked beautiful, and was sliced paper-thin, there were a scant two slices, which did not make for a very filling meal.  My daughter had the eggs Benedict, which had lox under the eggs, and it was delicious.  However, for the price-- $16 for the bagel and lox, and $18 for the eggs Benedict-- I really expected more generous portions.  I also had planned to order an egg cream (an old-time favorite of mine), but $7 for an egg cream, which is essentially a little chocolate syrup and milk mixed with a lot of seltzer, just seemed extreme.  So, though I had high hopes for this place, unless they get more generous with their portions, I don't plan to return.

Upon seeing that Russ and Daughters was rated the number 2 new restaurant by The New York Times, I decided to go see what the hype was about, and ventured down to the lower east side for lunch. As soon as we walked into the restaurant, we were greeted by a sea of people as well as a warm smile on the hostess' face. After being told there was an hour's wait, we joined the large crowd of others waiting for their seats and had plenty of time to soak up the Art Deco influenced atmosphere. Russ and Daughters has a certain old fashioned pharmacy type feel to it, with its variety of jars and boxes lining the top shelves on the walls and the white "pharmaceutical" coats worn by the wait staff. When the wait was over, we were taken to a pleasant booth towards the back of the restaurant, where we had a clear view of the kitchen. 

We ordered our food, but despite the accommodating staff, the service was a tad bit slow. The first to be delivered to our table was the egg cream; I ordered a mix of the chocolate and malt one. It was perfect. Creamy, authentic, and absolutely delicious, the egg cream was frothy on the top and smooth at the bottom. The borscht soup came next. It was bursting with both color and flavor, and had a perfect consistency and balance of flavor. The bread basket, knishes, and latkes came soon after, and all at once we were greeted with an abundance of deliciousness. The bread basket was filled to the brim with an assortment of fresh breads, of which my favorite was by far the rye. The knishes were possibly the best I have had, not at all heavy, but rather light and airy. However, the best part of lunch were the latkes. Crispy on the outside and warm and soft on the inside, these latkes were thick and filled with flavor. After stuffing our faces, we decided to get some dessert, despite the fact that we were ready to burst. It was definitely a good decision. We went with the halvah ice cream and it was gone within seconds of its arrival. The ice cream was creamy, and the salty halvah and sesame seeds along with the sweet caramel sauce created the perfect balance. Overall, it is clear why Russ and Daughters was at the top of the list, and I am already eager to go back.

The food is quite good, but the atmosphere is phony.  It's a hipster hangout.  You know the old-time deli-style eatery is dead and buried when a place like Russ & Daughters can be taken seriously.  No doubt it will open up a satellite in Times Square.
But I should emphasize... the food is good, if pricey.

Crazy cold outside and the wait was 30 min. No problem! They text you when ready. Tiny front interior, not room to stand.
Once seated, no rush - the staff allows you to peruse the menu / ask questions. 
Not cheap, but a fun treat. 
Goods- waiter and service are excellent.  The coffee is wonderful, latkes and lox are fab. Even the tomato on lox board was lush in December.  Pickled fennel a hit.
Loved the seltzer water too. Cute menu placemats.
Not as goods - wooden bar stools aren't too comfy, the crowds/strollers make it hard to wait indoors, grapefruit was not broiled hot as listed.

Shocked that this place doesn't have a perfect score. Other than it being a little pricey, everything was perfect. First of all, whoever decorated this restaurant is a genius and an inspiration. The sesame seed wall paper, the booths, the seating at the bar, the stamped paper bags, the menus, the plates, everything! Now the food: everything we ate was amazing. Latkes with sour cream and applesauce were awesome - very thick but held together well and very crispy on the outside. The schtetl plate was incredible - goat cheese cream cheese is awesome. The salmon pastrami on a pretzel roll was a total dream - the salmon really does taste like traditional pastrami and the pretzel roll has such good flavor! And last but certainly not least, the noodle koogle is what I've been dreaming about since I left. The perfect amount of sweetness, cinnamon, and raisin. The noodles were nice and soft and I could eat it every day the rest of my life. I'm serious. Needless to say I left very happy and very full.

Wanted to try this homage to the Russ and Daughters appetizing.  Nice place, lovely jazz music playing.  I ordered the classic board and coffee.  Bartender forgot I ordered the coffee so I waited longer than I would have liked for it.  All in all, the lox was delicious yet it thought portions were skimpy.  Glad I tried it but there are better places in the city for a true "Jewish appetizing experience".

This is the place of my brunch dreams.
I had been going downtown to see what the wait was like at Russ & Daughters a handful of weekends. Everytime the hostess said over two hours and I was always too hangry (hungry/angry) to wait it out. But last weekend I was more than determined. I had a plan! 
I sent my boyfriend down ahead of my mother and me to put our names down. He reported that it would be about an hour and 45 minutes. While I got dressed, he shopped around and by the time I was in a cab he was texting me that our table was ready! So, they were about an hour ahead of schedule!!

Once we were seated it was extremely difficult to choose what to get. I literally would have closed my eyes and pointed to anything on the menu and been happy.
Our waiter was lovely and patient with us, urging us to think of it as "Jewish tapas" (ha!) and to order a bunch of plates for everyone to share. 

The three of us got:
Super Heebster Bagel Toast - whitefish and baked salmon salad with wasabi infused fish roe, horseradish dill cream cheese on a toasted bagel
Pastrami Russ - pastrami-cured salmon, muenster cheese, sauerkraut, mustard, pickles, on a pretzel roll ***MY FAV***
Sturgeon, Eggs & Onions - with toasted pumpernickel
Blintzes - fruit compote, sour cream
Babka French Toast - chocolate babka, sour cream, strawberries 

I also got one of four different types of bloody mary's (it was amazing in case you couldn't guess) and my mom treated herself to a chocolate egg cream to indulge her inner child!
We left in the best mood! 
I need to go back a MILLION more times

this place is overrated and I was a little disappointed..

as most brunch places on the weekend, you can expect a wait.. especially for Russ and daughters ranging from 10am-2pm. I tried to come here 2 times and both times the wait was 45 minutes, and my bf and I didn't want to wait, especially since there are so many brunch places nearby.  

We arrived on a cold and rainy day on a saturday at 10:30am and scored seats right away. We were put on a table with stools- and it was so uncomfortable. There were no hooks to hang my jacket and I had to sit on top of my poofy winter jacket. My feet also didn't reach the end of the floor so they were just dangling and I could feel my sciatica kicking in. 

now to review the food-- I tried the Latkes and I wasn't impressed. I got the original platter, and yes the salmon was very fresh and went well with the onions and capers, but the bagel was stale. The portions were tiny and it was pretty pricey. We tried the bread pudding and it looked amazing, but it was a bit on the dry side and fell short on expectations.

3 1/2 stars. Last Sunday we came to Russ and daughters for the first time with a group of 4. We knew we were in for a wait (hour and a half to be exact) so we posted up at lucky jacks next store for a bloody or two. Our table was ready in due time and the hosting staff was prompt, friendly, kind. We were seated at a comfy booth in the back of the restaurant which makes you feel like you're at an old fashioned high class diner in the best of ways. We instantly felt at home and we were ready to chow.

Brooklyn roasting coffee, ginger sodas, cocktails, all fantastic. The coffee was strong, hot, fresh. The cocktails smooth and well balanced. Couldn't wait for the food. It did. Not. Disappoint. 5 stars for the truly PERFECT eggs Benedict on challah with lovely smoked salmon and spinach. Additionally we ordered the pastrami Russ--pastrami smoked salmon with a salty pretzel bread? The combination is something you didn't know you needed.  And finally the whitefish salad with wasabi roe was innnnnspired. 

Here's what soured our meal and ultimately my review. 2 stars for service at the table. Russ and Daughters, when we wait patiently for an hour and a half DO NOT try and push us out the door the minute we sit down. We had barely received our food before being asked if we wanted our bill. It's rude, and it spoiled an otherwise flawless brunch experience.

Sunday brunch was excellent, poached eggs, matzah ball soup, and potato knishes were superb! Light, fresh, and good portions.

Decor was warm, transformative, and appropriate. I felt like I was transported to the past. Felt like the movie Pleasantville. 

Service was mediocre however. Hostess was friendly and accommodating. Our wait was not long for 2 people. Arrived at 10am, seated by 10:30. Our server ALON was awful. We waited 20 minutes and had to request from another server that they take our order. He talked to customers as he's walking away. Never checked in on us. Overall poor service experience - the bus boys did make up for some. They were all so friendly and helpful. 

Definitely recommend to friends, but if I get ALON again I'll ask to be moved to another servers area.
The Schtetl board with smoked Sable was nice.  The potato latkes were crunchy and the salmon roe added an interesting touch.  Plus, I love crème fraîche.  The bagel was just ok- wasn't wowed by it.

Went during lunch on a Friday and it was perfect. Got seated pretty quickly and our waiter was great. Ordered the smoked white fish chowder, heebster nosh and the eggs benny. All so good and def recommend trying.

After my meal last week, my feeling was that i could eat here everyday.  The hot and cold smoke was wonderful.  Flavorful yet not overly salted and very fresh.  The cocktails were interesting.  We had a wonderful server.  The menu is deep.  I could have pointed at something randomly and would probably have enjoyed it.  I can't wait to return.

Fantastic food, fantastic service. Fun, nostalgic, with a twist.  This isn't your grandmother's Russ & Daughters...  Everything is familiar, just "amped up".  Unexpectedly great chopped liver.  Bagels and lox--phenomenal. Kasha with a poached egg on top. (Are you kidding me--a poached egg? Ridiculously delicious!) Attention to every detail, decor that transports you back to the restaurant's origins but thoroughly modern takes on Jewish comfort food. Worth the wait for brunch!

Honestly, I only came to this place because Black Tree (??) next door had no availability for dinner. It was Friday night around 7. But what a blessing in disguise! The ambiance has a very clean look, which I loved. Sat down at the bar with a friend. Bartender was very friendly and talked us through the cocktail menu. I ordered the potato latkes (unbelievably delicious!!!) and the beet salad. So fresh and wholesome, simple and flavorful. But the real star of the meal was the challah bread pudding.... Oy!!! Will definitely come back here.

P.s. It looks like it would be a great brunch spot. And as far as I saw, no meat on the menu; just fish/seafood.
Pastrami-cured salmon on the pretzel roll is delectable. I was left wanting MORE (but in a good way). Friendly servers and cute decor.

Vegan/dairy free tofu spread. YASS. Now this is what I'm talking about. I came here on a raining and moody Sunday morning for breakfast and they had jazz/blues on. I had my tea, lox, bagel, and cream cheese. Honestly, what could be better. Great service and staff. Everyone just knows what's up here. Also, great ambience and graphic design. What an amazing amazing place. Long live R&D!!!

So this is the best food I've ever eaten anywhere.  Chopped liver- perfect.  Smoked fishes all perfection.  Halvah ice cream?  Who else does that?  Babka French toast?  Best restaurant in the universe.

Great place for brunch with a twist (ie with fish).  We cam with a group of 5 at 10-30am and waited 15 mins for a table, not bad.  The seating hostess was polite and kept us informed of our wait time.   They don't take reservations, so you have to be prepared to wait, in what is quite a small waiting area.  They have an eclectic menu based on fish (smoked/pickled etc) - plus some brunch classics.  Service was good and prices reasonable.

Institution!!! 
Awesome locks variety, awesome cream cheese selections, plenty of pickeled stuff, several bagels type, bialys, excellent liver mousse, fish eggs, whole dried fish, this place absolutely rocks. Try it especially on an early morning when you will be amazed to see how awake the staff is. They are always wearing white blouse, bow ties, and can really help you make a decision. My fav is a salmon, salmon cream cheese bialys with capers.

Dropped in for lunch as I aimlessly wandered around LES. Kept it simple and went with the smoked whitefish chowder and the pastrami russ. Chowder was creamy and rich, with nice chunks of fish in most spoonfuls and the pastrami cured salmon with the muenster cheese and pretzel bread was great!

This place is dope especially when you can beat the line. Try to go off hours. 

-Classic board was great. 
-I'd get the French toast (which I loved) over the blintz next time. 
-The homemade sodas were dope. 
-The white fish chowder was a little pricey but good. Probably will try something else next time. 
-Potato latkes were pretty good.

Had a late dinner here with friends and everything we ordered was fresh and delicious.  Matzoh ball soup...with chunks of chicken and no noodles (yay!) a big fluffy light matzoh in amazingly rich chicken broth and fresh crunchy celery, with soft onions and carrots.

The beet salad...also delicious. Fresh, sweet beets, light dressing, yummy greens...the Pastrami Russ...oh so tiny but oh so tasty on a tiny torpedo shaped pretzel roll, with amazingly fresh cucumber pickles and crispy waffle fries. I tasted the Heebster bagel toast...also fresh, with a large portion of whitefish salad and topped with crispy wasabi caviar.

We ended with the Challah bread pudding with apricots and caramel sauce...piping hot, fluffy, not too sweet but light and...yes, delicious.

Go. Now.

The first time I went to Russ was about 2 years ago and I have been loyal to the overcrowded experience on East Houston street, but now with a big restaurant you still get the crowded experience, with a lot more comfort once you get a table. The key to Russ is the awesome ingredients, combined with friendly staff I love the experience. We had the Super Heepster and it was awesome!!! Have it! It's boombastic! The pastrami russ was nice but not exceptional. I always used to order the classic in the bold place and found it strange that it was not prepared for you, but still a great taste! Potato latkes were awesome! I like the place even though it feels "commercialised" compared to the old place...we will be back!!!

3 of us waited with great anticipation, based on history of R&D and type of food.  The wait wasn't too bad, everyone friendly, especially the employee at reception.  The decor is wonderful, reminiscent of old-time NY Jewish delis, but modern, very clean and bright, very comfortable seating. Food quality is excellent. Jazz music is unobtrusive and sets a good mood.

That said, the actual dining left us not satisfied:
Haphazard waiter service--much left out and had to be reminded--more than once, more than twice
Portion sizes are, in good part, not what one expects in a Lower East Side experience
You pay extra for this and that and this.  So prices are elevated at checkout.  

Given the choices for this type menu on the Lower East Side, we feel R&D Cafe is not where we will return.  The original store:  YES!  Of course.
The food was bomb. More expensive than the store, but we enjoyed caviar, latkes with salmon roe, and a platter of smoked salmon (with capers, red onion, tomato, and a bagel).

I made the pilgrimage and am sad to report this is not the temple to Jewish brunch gastronomy. 
Had the "classic" nova platter. Very good. My complaints: too little cream cheese and too little fish. What Jew eats a bagel without a good sized schmear?  They need to serve almost twice as much fish to cover two half bagels. And what's with the bagel selection? Surely they can source a classic NY bagel and offer in addition to the Black Seed -- which the menu is silent about. But come on! 
I ordered a side of scrambled eggs. The cook must have been channeling my father because they came to me virtually liquid. Yuck! I asked for eggs cooked more and out came browned eggs. Egads! Surely there is room between liquid and hard.
A disappointment, especially for the high price.

It's one of those places which makes you happy. Just a cool vibe, and cute little decor. Food is good, portion is slightly small but all the carb... you won't be hungry. Wish they served little more fish and cream cheese. Love the design and art work on the wall. Very clean bathroom.

The wait was worth it, we popped into a cafe down the street after giving the hostess our phone number.  Exactly an hour later we were seated.  Plan to wait.  Food was delicious, I highly recommend their egg and locks scramble.  Free sparkling water was a great touch, and it was shockingly affordable. Highly recommend!

Classic Jewish deli, they don't make 'em like this anymore. Everything is wonderful, especially he smoke fish, sable, salmon- all high quality with fresh but classic fee inside 
And don't miss the halava ice cream, it's amazing
Got 6 bagels and one hand the wrong cheese (goat rather than scallion). Bagels are super stiff and overloaded with cream cheese. Salmon is decent but not worth the price and wait.
Tasty, but there's a negative correlation between the price and the portions. Must try: the latkes, and the pastrami-cured salmon. The ambience is great, and the service is stellar.

It was over an hour wait but they took my number and texted me when the table was ready so I could walk around, which I appreciated! I was keeping passover and ordered matzoh brei and potato latkes, both delicious. I'll need to go back when I can eat bread though so I can get one of the bagel platters and/or noodle pudding! Definitely a great brunch spot for all of your favorite jewish foods!

Wow.  We are native New Yorkers who have relocated to California.  It's been hard finding decent deli food, let alone, bagels and chopped liver.  We came in for dinner and instantly knew what we were going to get.  My son and I ordered the Board - which consisted of bagel, lox, cream cheese, tomato, capers and thinly sliced red onion.  My son also ordered the matzo ball soup.  My husband needed his potato knishes, chopped liver and bread basket.  We loved everything and wished there was a Russ & Daughters by where we live.  Chopped liver, bread basket, matzo ball soup, knish and two orders of the board, were completely devoured and we left the place....extremely happy!  Trying to plan a trip again before we leave to return to San Francisco.

I will always be coming here on my NYC trips! Everything was amazing. Everything! Of course, we had to have the bagel and lox. We did the herring 3-ways. The heebster  bagel toast was one of the best things I've ever had. The latkes, something I would have never ordered but it came with high reviews from the waiter, and it was fantastic. Get all of these things and don't miss out on the cocktails. I had them make me a fantastic Moscow mule with their ginger/lavender beer.

The place is super cute, they were super nice and accommodating of our baby and stroller, and the food was great- hard to decide what to order!  

The only negative was that I saw quite a few small flies there :(

Hosts are supposed to greet you, not vice versa. We said hello to them, we asked if there was a wait. They responded with "yes", then we had to ask how long... "They told us an hour and 45 minutes" followed by a giggle.  We left. They annoyed my girlfriend and I, and the manager should know.

The reason why I gave 1 star is because my friend's credit card got copied, information got stolen and used in somewhere else!!!!! This is so unexpected as this restaurant looks decent. So disappointed. BE CAREFUL everyone.  

My friends and I went to this place on a Sat morning. It was crowded, we waited for about 30 mins. The food was good, expect they dont have a special menu for brunch, so it is kind of disappointed. Fish is def their specialty. The service was bad. Waiter was slow and not paying attention.
Got the bagel with the ikura and smoked salmon.  Fresh and great for the experience of eating it.  But I think I prefer my smoked salmon on toast and ikura on rice.  Especially for $20.  Sorry.

The hype is legitimate, this is a very cool place and concept.  The backstory what with the grandchildren of the original shops owners opening a super trendy revisionist Jewish deli style restaurant.  The design surreally summons together the aesthetics and vibes of new and old LES, which I guess this place actually is simultaneously.  Just thinking about it makes your head spin.
  The smoked fish is excellent, not surprisingly considering the heritage.  It is presented in varying forms and styles in presentations that lean on influences like Japanese and New Nordic cuisine just as much as old-school Jewish Deli.  Thin slices of wonderfully salty smoked salmon lined the interior of  a perfectly crispy/chewy skinny pretzel roll sandwich.  Smoke fish chowder brought out the musky flavors of said fishes wonderfully.  My personal favorite dish hands down however, are the knishes.  Pretty much the polar opposite of the leaden gut bombs I often encountered in Long Island childhood, these small wonders are both sturdy and light as air, with such deep flavors that my dining companion was convinced they had meat in them.  Jewish delis are often times fairly expensive, and this one is no exception, however its worth it for a singularly NY experience.

I was really happy to stop in here for a late breakfast on a weekday when it wasn't crowded at all. I enjoyed counter service with very friendly and helpful service from the staff - they offered to help me make any selections, since I hadn't been there before. I got to try a few different things, including an egg cream that came with a metal straw. I tried the pickled fish assortment which, honestly, was a bit too much for me but still fun to try. The noodle kugel was truly exceptional, though!

The food is good but you have to like smoked fish and salmon. I am not crazy about this type of food so I did not enjoy it as much as my friend. I ordered the chocolate French toast and it was crispy on the outside and warm on the inside. It wasn't loaded with chocolate but more of like encrusted with a dusting of chocolate. It was tasty. My friend had the eggs Benedict. I had a bite without the salmon and it was just okay for me. The egg was slightly under cooked for a poached egg. I probably won't come back since I am not into this style of food but my friend said he would definitely come back. Also, dill Bloody Mary was tasty but after a few sips it stopped tasting as good.

FINALLY ate here. I gave up getting in for brunch, so we came here for an early dinner and walked right in. It was everything I dreamed it would be. Service - very good. Atmosphere - like a high class, hip, diner. Food - the BEST. Loved the smoked fish platter, the herring, the bread basket, chocolate babka. Drink - I got the ginger soda, spiked with vodka. Heaven!

Ok, sorry LA but this place stands above everyone!  Hostesses are sweethearts, the waiters are so friendly and quick and helpful!  Coffees great!  The heebster was great and tasty!  Bagel lox and the works was perfect!  Lox is amazing!  We also had lox eggs and onions which was the best and the eggs benny with lox and spinach!  A must is the chopped liver soo flavorful and fresh!!

Have eaten there three times and would move nearby if I could afford it. It's just the best best best place. Granted, the portions are not huge (but the platter was very hefty for four people), but I was happy about it because we could order a variety of dishes and not burst. I've had their sturgeon (oh, lordie), potato latkes are fabulous---the thick but crispy kind, several herring appetizers, gravlax, pastrami cut lox, more lox, goat cheese spread, and I almost fainted with joy at the halvah ice cream, the apricot challah pudding, and the cookie/candy plate. Been going to the Russ & Daughters mothership for some 25 years, and thats great, too---AND you an choose exactly what you want there and whatever amount you can fit in your gut. But the cafe is a great space to sit and shmooze and feed your face.

Came here for dinner, jetlagged & craving bagels / breakfast at 7pm. We were ushered to the back booth by the lovely hostess and were served by several wait staff. I had a Schmoozer cocktail which was beautiful and my friend had a glass of red.

I started with the matzo ball soup, it was delicious. The matzo ball was light, definitely a floater haha! I also had the classic board with an everything bagel -  it really hit the spot, only wish there was more of that delicious salmon. My friend had the soup of the day and a chop salad, both of which she rated highly too.

Would definitely come back again on my next NY trip

Looked forward to trying this restaurant.  Ate there yesterday.  Meeting friends at 1, I was early by half an hour but was able to put down my name and was told then there was a 30 minute wait.  We were seated 10 minutes after the the rest of our party arrived.  They don't take reservations.  

Had potato pancakes with apple sauce and sour cream.  The potato pancakes were almost as good as my mothers were.  Also had the Classic which was the thinnest lox served on a board with cream cheese, tomatoes, onions, bagel and capers.  Didn't think the bagel was that good and the wait staff made a couple of mistakes.  Unfortunately they removed our plates before we were all finished which I detest but these days it's done more and more.were finished it this seems to me what is done today.  All and all a good 4 star restaurant and we will hope to return.

The only reason not a 5 star is the wait- why not take reservations? We waited 1 1/2 hours for a table for 4.
The food was great and my mother in law, turning 90, absolutely loved it. Everything was top quality and the presentation was lovely however $7 for an egg cream was crazy.

Russ and Daughters Cafe was my favorite restaurant in Summer 2014. 

The presentation of the sturgeon was on point. It was served on a carving board with butter, capers, tomatoes, and rye bread. Rye bread and sturgeon are a ridiculously delicious pair.  I buttered the bread then laid one piece of sturgeon on top and finished by topping it with tomatoes, onions and capers. The only disappointing part of this meal were the pickles. I prefer sour pickles and these were on the sweeter side of the pickling spectrum. However, they made up for the hiccup with their their limeade. Bottom line is that Russ & Daughters should be on any fish lover's list.

The atmosphere is great...was a ride in the Delorian back to 1965. Clean, very minimalistic white and the cooks had old school paper hats that you'd see at a drive thru burger joint. 
I started with a cucumber soda which was exquisite.  Not too sweet and really creative ingredients as was the case for all the soda options (ie. You won't find a plain ol coke).
All down here fro here.
Waiter comes up and says..."thoughts?" I was thinking,  come again...?
I think the dining experience should always be creative from the kitchen to the atmosphere but waiting on a table...please keep it simple and courteous. He never came back until the check was due.
It was obvious he didn't need our business and so fine.. i knew from that point on I wouldn't be back.

So pressing forward we ordered the pastrami salmon on pretzel roll, whitefish chowder, knish w.carmalized onions and spicy mustard and the classic- salmon cream cheese and rye.
See the picture...the knishes were a total let down. I didn't mind paying 8 dollars as they sounded mouth watering but as you can see for the size it was highway robbery. As for the taste, I'd been better off at my corner street cart and 7 dollars richer. Let me stop there but you see where the rest of this is going. 
Enjoy tourists....

It's aight. Not worth the price... certainly not worth the hour-plus wait time. Portions are small.

Good for tourists who want to see some celebs.

The best bagel spot ever.. Love their lox, cream cheese and capers with a bagel is to die for!!! Truth my favorite most expensive bagel place ever.. Not a everyday place but a day to break a diet and treat yourself to an amazing  bagel and lox!!

We heard about their Lox so decided to take the subway down for a late breakfast. We were lucky because we later found out there could be a long wait. We were seated immediately, I had  the regular lox and bagels. The lox is cut paper thin, it's see- through. It melted in my mouth! It was memorable. Worth the trip. I gave it one star less because they made a gourmet pickle . Just stick to the good old dill. I also felt a bit of attitude but it didn't take away from the wonderful lox!

I have a serious obsession with bagel and lox and knew Russ & Daughters would be a must-stop during my NYC vacay. Our experience here totally surpassed expectations! Our group of 4 rolled in during peak Saturday brunch hours to a 90-minute wait but after exploring nearby neighborhoods to kill time, R&D called us 1 hour later and voilà, our table was ready.

DRINKY-DRINKS
-Bloody Marys: tried two kinds 1. Caraway vodka with rye croutons soaked in vodka 2. Pepper vodka with smoked salt (I liked the second one more)
-Cucumber Soda with vodka: incredibly refreshing!

NOMS
-Knishes: 2 baked dough pockets filled with potato; flavor was okay and they're really small at the price of $8 but the grainy mustard makes this item shine
-Classic Fish Board: lox is seriously delicious and on point.
-Shtetl Fish Board: smoked sable served with a goat cream cheese. If smoked fish isn't your thing, I highly recommend you try this because the flavor is so delicate and mild. Loved this!
-Eggs, Lox, and Onions: luscious scrambled eggs folded with lox and served with rye bread and yummy salad greens. Best scrambled eggs ever!
-Red & Golden Beets: lovely salad of colorful beets, pumpernickel croutons, grapefruit segments, and walnuts all on a bed of watercress.
-Blintzes: perfect "dessert" to end the meal! Two plump blintzes filled with the perfect amount of ricotta, sour cream, and blueberry sauce?! Yes, please!

Portions aren't huge, it's a little overpriced, and employees could be a little friendlier, but service was prompt, food arrived quickly, and the café vibe and décor is just what you need to kick off the weekend. Thanks for the fun experience, R&D!

P.S. This is my 200th Yelp review = woo-hoo!

Refreshing cucumber soda but what an odd taste.  Beautiful new clean looking retro decor but my, they are PRICEY! So pricey, I was afraid to eat. What I wanted most was an old authentic experience and I didn't think I got it because the drinks and menu seemed new and not from the days of NY's past however, the people in the white coats were very pleasant. And the room temperature was cold enough that they could be the igloo cafe of NY.

Wow. And more wow.

There was a long wait, but it was well worth it. I went with two friends and we shared cherry & mango shrubs (I liked the cherry best, $6), chocolate malt egg cream $7, sours (pickled carrots, cucumbers, onions, etc) $7, mixed greens with kippered (baked, kind of mushy, probably my least favorite) salmon $14, the "shtetl" (smoked sable, goat cream cheese, tomato, red onion, capers, delicious) $18, and the "lower sunny side" (sunny side up eggs, smoked salmon, potato latkes) $16. The lower sunny side was my favorite; the salmon was incredible. But, having some greens and the smoked sable was great, too, so I'd suggest sharing a few plates to get the right mix.

Love the drinks, food, and decor. Service was friendly, too. A new favorite!!

Russ & Daughters never disappoints. I took another seafood loving, new NYC transplant and they too enjoyed their meal. Having dined on multiple occasions at both the Cafe and Delicatessen, I urge those unaquainted with the franchise to firstly try a dish or two with one of the establishment's specialty loxs. I think it is their strong suit. I have tried all of their pickled herring and I must say, the pickling/brine is not my favorite - I like it less sweet such as that often encountered in the Netherlands.

Holy chocolate babka - get yourself to Russ & Daughters and order this french toast immediately! It's the perfect portion and brought me back to my love of chocolate croissants and Nutella crepes in France. The coffee and atmosphere are great as well. I arrived just when it opened on Sunday morning so that I could eat here before catching a flight home. I want to come back and try the potato latkes! There just isn't enough time in the day. :)
Excellent brunch, excellent service, authentic cuisine. Their Bloody Marys and Shrubs aren't too shabby either! I will be back soon.

I owe the best bagel I've had in my life to this place. Russ & Daughters has been around for over a century, and their relatively new cafe down the street promises the same excellent bagels/cream cheese, in a hip 50s-diner-esque setting as opposed to take out. If you avoid their bagel/lox specials (pricey), this place is actually quite affordable. We came here and had a bagel with cream cheese each, along with their bread pudding and some of their soda water. The total came out to a little over $20. Pretty awesome.

I recommend their goat cheese cream cheese on an everything bagel, toasted. Their goat cheese cream cheese is as good as it sounds.

Service was excellent, the atmosphere and decor were beautiful, and above all the food was very good - from the bagels to the delicious bread pudding.

If you find yourself on the lower east side, this place is worthy of your time - it may be the best bagel you ever have.
Very delicious and quality smoked fish and bagels, a must try when you visit NYC! They are a bit pricey however worth the experience.

I liked double water.   Fizzy and flat.   Fish platters for 5 adults with couple egg dishes was very very good.   Plenty of bread choices in basket.  A bialy bagel basket would be nice addition to menu.  Smoked fish was generous size and for area priced fairly.    Tables were big diner size booths and sat down in ~15 minutes.    Good word of mouth earned.

Finally, Russ & Daughters appetizer store, opened up a Cafe! 

PLACE
The ambiance is perfect. The attention to detail from the moment you walk in to the back of the room is simply divine! From the marble floor decor, white doctor jackets the employees where, the black and white photos, the bagel and fish sculpture, the light fixtures, the salmon station, everything was great. 

FOOD
- The classic ($16) ... bagel, lox, cream cheese, tomatoes, onions, capers. ($12 in the store).  You can't go wrong with this, but if you're hungry order another plate. 
- The latkas small plate comes with 3 latkas. The apple sauce was delicious too.
- The chocolate caviar ... chocolate mousse, dark chocolate chips on top ($12) 
- This place should be listed as $$$, not $$!

Heads up.  Don't expect this place to be  an extension of their famous retail store; it's not.
Bagles were very dry with no elasticity in the dough, potato pancakes were not golden brown and slightly over-done. Egg Cream needed to be sweeter with more chocolate.
Creamed Herring was very liquidy, saturated with vinegar, without a good ratio of sour cream.

If you're trying to just order a bagel with cream cheese, you've got the wrong place--walk a block up the street and there's the famous "Appetizer Store," that's probably what you're looking for. While you can get the bagel of your dreams, it's going to cost more in the Cafe than it would at the Appetizer Store--consider The Classic (a bagel with generous lox, cream cheese and capers), $16 in the Cafe, $12 in the Store. If you're wanting to try some of the other taste treats (latkas, eggs, bloody marys)--then perhaps suck up the price hike.

No reservations, so plan smart. After a little wait, we were treated to a lovely experience. The waitstaff are friendly and offer great guidance and recommendations when asked. We were steered toward the Super Heebster which was amazing. The decor and ambiance are equally enjoyable. A strong recommendation for this place.

After living in New York for a couple years I finally made it down here. I went on a Saturday in the middle of the day and it was packed. There was a little bit of a wait, but it was worth it. I got an everything bagel, with Norwegian smoked salmon, capers and caviar cream cheese. The combination of everything together made the best bagel lox I've ever had. The smoked salmon had just the right amount of flavor.

The only reason that I am giving this 3 stars is because I think the bagels they use are just okay and not over the top great. I wish i could say i loved this place, but i did not. And being a Jew and growing up with this food and loving it and even making it, this place falls short in some departments. Any of you just wanting a bagel, lox , red onion, cream cheese capers, save yourself the trip and you can find some other great neighborhood bagel joints with such better bagels. Of course you might not get the same quality of Lox, but Id much rather have  really great everything bagel with some decent Nova. I mean after all, once you put all the stuff on the bagel, the thing for me that stands out the most is the toasted everything bagel. Russ and Daughters was mediocre at best. Which translates into, that this everything bagel didn't have nearly enough everything. And Lou Reeds wife, Laurie Anderson wrote about this being their fav place before Lou died and how the Horseradish dill cream cheese is amazing. I can make this recipe a hundred times better with much more flavor. So why should I go out and spend a fortune on the basics when I can cook this stuff so much better than these guys. I think you're better off at their take out joint on Houston and take the fish home and get the bagels and all the trimming elsewhere. I should open my own freaking joint and blows these guys out of the water. But the biz is just to much of a pain in the ass and I no longer have an ego..

Simply fantastic.. I got the shtetl (smoked sable with goat cream cheese, tomatoes, onions and capers on a gluten free bagel). Great flavor, texture, mouth feel... Heavenly.. also got the eggs Benny on a gluten free bagel... Very delicious. My new favorite breakfast place in the LES.
Really good, really expensive. I don't know, not sure classic Jewish food and hipsters mix

Best lox I have ever had!!! It was just perfect - dense but soft bagel, smooth cream cheese, and seriously silky, melt-in-you're-mouth smoked salmon! To be honest, I wasn't a fan of the popular latkes but I most certainly will be back for those lox!! The wait can be bad but they text you when the table is ready so you can explore nearby areas!

It was my first time here.  Decided to go here as my friend was craving a bagel and as the original shop on Houston Street was closed as it was evening time, went here instead. 

The place has a very nice decorum, lighting and setup.  The service at the bar was decent but their menu for what you get is simple ridiculous!!!!  

We decided on just a bagel and the matzah ball soup.  I was a virgin for the soup until but nothing to write home about.  

As it's overpriced and nothing I cannot buy at a market and whip up myself, I say pass on this place as the prices are simply not justified for the portions you get here.  I obviously looked around while I was there and checked out yelp photos. Nah, greed of a price to charge!

Finally visited R&D after a year of swooning over photos on Instagram from the other side of the country. 

Everything was delicious and thought-out. Their menu is aesthetically pleasing and they had an elevated fish stick special that was out of this world. 

Would definitely go back and highly recommend!
So good, the food are unique and delicious. The interior is so nice I wish I can stay there forever. It give me a 60s feel. Love it!

Went here on a Sunday morning so was not able to imbibe in one of their creative cocktails which are not served before noon on Sundays.  I was able to enjoy their classic, Gaspe Nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers on a toasted plain bagel.  The best!  Freshed squeezed orange juice with lots of pulp did an admirable job substituting for a cocktail.  Such a great move for this Lower East Side institution to open a sit down cafe.

went for second time with 4 others. food all very good and authentic. share the large salmon platter which was excellent. borscht was historic. latkes and herrings excellent. 
no reservations are drag, waited 30 minutes as told for a sunday brunch. friendly and attentive waitress.
negatives where several pesky flys that seemed to also be fans of smoked fish. also the 'busboy' who when i asked for a plate so that i didn't have to eat my salmon platter off the table replied 'you want a extra plate?'..i said, as i pointed to my placemat, no, i want A plate.
clearly he doesn't know he is in the front of the restaurant. truly annoying and a non customer friendly style.

I had a fantastically satisfying meal here today. Went with the Shtetl, the heebster toast and an order of blintzes. Every item was perfect. Service was excellent, and the decor inside is really great. It was all pretty much perfect.
Spectacular! Gorgeous interior, splendid service, and downright terrific food. I got the chopped salad with a sesame bagel and it was divine.

This is the best restaurant in the LES. 
Make sure you get their pastrami salmon sandwich with pretzel roll. 
This will blow your mind. Every bite of it is perfect. 

Also, if you are a pickles person, get the pickles. 
Cucumbers are on the salty/crunchy side, not like sweet dill pickle, and that's how I like them.
Pickled fennel (i don't think it was celery root, an I right?) is delightful. The sweetness of it perfectly compliments the rest of the meal. 

On another note, it's a perfect place to take your out-towner parents! 
(Clean, not too hip/loud, etc)

It might be expensive, but it is to DIE for!! Russ and Daughters Cafe is somewhere I highly recommend going.  The lox is so fresh and the bagels are great.  Plus, I'm gluten free and they had some amazing options for me (including a gluten free bagel).  Thrilled to have been able to go here and can't wait to go back!

I'd heard legends about Russ & Daughters having some of the best bagels and lox in New York, and it was one of the few restaurants on my NYC bucket list.  I finally got around to going for Saturday brunch, and for my wallet's sake, I'm so so so so glad that I didn't know about this place a couple of years ago.  

The food was incredible.  I got "The Classic" sandwich, which was your standard everything bagel with cream cheese, smoked salmon, onions, tomato, and capers.  We also split an order of the latkes with applesauce as an appetizer.  I'm not going to say that, by itself, it was the best bagel I'd had in NYC (that honor still goes to Tompkin's Square Bagels), but it was hands down the best bagel and lox and toppings combination I'd had.

The cafe was very clean (I'll almost say sterile) and even though there was a long 45-50 minute wait, they'd invested in one of those computer systems that texts you when your table is ready, so we were free to...well...start drinking early even though it wasn't noon yet.  Black Tree is right next door, which is an awesome bar for beer or picklebacks while you're waiting.

The damage here is going to be $30-40 per person, which is pretty hefty for a breakfast/brunch that doesn't include a self-refilling pitcher of mimosas, so like I said, for my wallet's sake, I'm glad I won't be able to make R&D a regular event.  That being said, it's an excellent choice if you have family or friends coming in from out of town, and you want to give them a taste of NY.

Food: 5/5
Value: 3/5
Service: 4/5
Atmosphere: 4/5

Great brunch last Sunday morning. I got the pickled herring and eggs Benedict. Amazing! My girlfriend got the beat salad and leaks bagel board... Again phenomenal! We were happy with the entire experience

Admittedly, I was visiting from DC so I might have the out-of-towner bias, but this place hit the spot for a nice breakfast before heading back home. I had the Classic Board, with a lightly toasted everything bagel and it was amazing. Besides the amazingly tender, thinly sliced gaspe nova smoked salmon, I was super impressed by the flavorful, ruby red tomato slices they served along with the rest of the standard accoutrements (cream cheese, onions, and capers). 

My dining partner literally moaned with pleasure when he tasted his first bite of the Lox, Eggs, & Onions. Not only were the eggs fluffy and peppered generously with bits of tasty lox and thinly sliced sautéed onion, they were served alongside a tastefully dressed (champagne vinaigrette, in my estimation) mixed greens salad, a piece of toasted shissel rye, and a nice fat pat of house butter.  

The cocktails were also impressive. The fenugreek-infused vodka Bloody Mary was on point and the smokey martini was just what the doctor ordered. I desperately wished I could ball out and get some caviar plates, but that will have to wait until my next visit! 

As far as ambiance, the place exudes old school charm and serious NY deli/market heritage. I have to say I was enchanted. Can't wait to go back during my next trip to NYC.

, but the hostes  girl , is very bad :((( they not do professional work . For waiting table you need to be ready for 45 minutes or hours  , and after they propose sit on a bar , where people who waiting will push you all time . This is not place  to have a nice lunch with your second part .  And if you want table for two is take longer then people with more :((( or sit on a bar :((((

First visit. Thoroughly enjoyed sharing the Anne platter & Chocolate Babka French toast with my wife, two kids & parents. During the 80-min wait we walked to the original shop and bought choc-covered grahams and jelly grahams to tide us over. Smoked fish in the case made my mouth water in anticipation of the real meal. Favorite fish on the platter were trout and nova lox. Pumpernickel slices in the bread basket were perfect. Coffee was rich, just right. I realized, though, that I prefer picking from chunks of smoked fish, getting way more flavor per bite than from slices of, say, sable or sturgeon. Other menu items looked tremendous, eg. Chopped salad, Pastrami Russ and Smoked whitefish chowder.

My husband and I were in town this weekend and decided to take a walk up to Russ and Daughters Cafe for Sunday breakfast. 

Immediately I'm struck by the decor and ambience. It's inviting and has a purity about it that reminds me of crisp, high thread count, white linen. The service is friendly, welcoming and appropriately attentive.

We opted for the complementary seltzer water. It was crisp, cold and refreshing. Such a nice touch. We ordered the chopped liver, the classic open faced sandwich with a bagel and the eggs Benny.

I convinced the hubby to try the chopped liver, which is served with pickled onions and matzah. It was creamy and delicious with a great balance of acid provided by the onions. My husband who hates liver is now a convert.

The eggs Benny was amazing. Perfectly poached eggs, delicate lox, dense challah, with silky hollandaise and nicely prepared greens.

The lox sandwich was presented on a wooden block in a "build your own" style. I actually prefer this. Cream cheese, beautiful slices of lox, sliced tomato, red onion and capers. The bagel size was just perfect, not overly large as they can sometimes be. Clearly great attention has been given to proportions. I really enjoyed this version of my favorite.

We have already decided that Russ and Daughters will be our breakfast MUST when we are in town from now on.
What a fabulous place! Jazz in the background, fabulous selection of all my favourite fish dishes. I can't wait to bring my dad here

I've been to this cafe twice and it has become one of my favorite eateries. First is the great retro diner look. Fantastic service. Let's talk menu. Do you have to be Jewish to kvell over the lox, assorted herrings, sable, bialys, challah bread pudding or noodle pudding? Don't think so. If you fee like being a big spender go for the varied assortment of cavier. Good coffee to boot. Great little eatery any time of the day.

A great place for lunch, but on the pricey side.  The smoked fish is wonderful and comes from the main store on Delancy. The serve egg creams which was a real treat and seltzer is complimentary.  My wife had a bowl of soup which was great and the knish appetizer.  Two small but tasty knishes four eight bucks?  Not even in New York!

A great place to eat.  The service was probably the best service I've ever had.  But really, it's not that hard to have great service there. The place is spotless, the drinks are refreshing and the food is good.    There are a ton of things to try on the menu.  I only took away one star because the food is mostly appetizer portions. For the price, I don't want to be hungry an hour or two after eating.

The restaurant is lovely, and sitting at the table alone makes me feel sophisticated. The staff's uniforms are also a nice touch, and presentation impeccable.

For me, it is not the type of food that I will crave, and that's why the low star rating. The matzo soup was too salty for me. My friend really liked it though.

This cafe, run by the younger generation of the Russ appetizing dynasty, was a pleasant oasis on a hot and muggy NYC afternoon. The staff was friendly and prompt, and unlike so many new places it was not overwhelmingly noisy. As to the food, we only had a few dishes, but it's not quite the old-style Lower East Side Jewish cuisine. I had the noodle/cheese kugel, too dense and dry--I had to ask for sour cream to accompany. The prices are a bit high, for what is essentially working class food ($8 for a knish is ridiculous), and offering $250 portions of caviar seems a bit pretentious. Needs work, but a nice place, really 3.5 stars.

We came in around 9AM on a Sunday and were seated right away. I got the Shtetl board, coffee, and Halvah ice cream. The goat cream cheese with the smoked sable was so good that I didn't mind the disappointing size of the bagel (it was a teeny bit small). The coffee was good (free refills!); the Halvah ice cream was great too. It wasn't too sweet, and had a really nice texture. They also didn't judge me for ordering ice cream at 9AM. I also loved the decor - it was very retro and crisp. I would come again to try something else and totally recommend this place if you want a chill breakfast.

Public service announcement: the cafe does *NOT* accept Russ & Daughters giftcards. There is no indication on the giftcards themselves, which I find to be a bit of a scam. My family gifted me what they thought would be a nice meal (at a place I cannot otherwise afford), and I ended up having to foot a bill that was way beyond my budget. The manager told me that this is a common mistake. If this is true (and I believe her), it seems a bit insidious that they would have chosen to not correct this issue - or at least figure out a way to let folks know what the limitations are when they purchase Russ & Daughters giftcards. The fact that the card comes with no such distinction, and that they offer no assistance when you "mistakenly" attempt to use it, tells me just how much they care about their customers.

I ordered the lower sunny side and Omg the Gaspe nova smoked salmon was so flavorful.
Perfect portions and great service.

I had been wanting to go to Russ and Daughters for years and the cafe did not disappoint.  The five of us got a sampler plate which was so much food. It had 4 different types of fish with different toppings and flavors of cream cheese as well as breads and bagels. Very good!

Don't come here... unless, of course, you're prepared for the best brunch of your life. Obviously Russ & Daughters wasn't going to disappoint us. I only recently heard that they opened this cafe and I was very excited to come in. The decor was adorable. I loved the retro diner aesthetic, it was kitschy without feeling dated. The service was friendly, and the cute server outfits added to the atmosphere as a whole.

We came in on a Monday morning which was perfect, because we didn't have to wait even though we were a party of 8. I can't even imagine what this place must look like on a Saturday or Sunday morning, but I still would have braved the crowd.

Most of us tried their homemade sodas. I had a sip of my friend's blueberry soda and it was perfect. It really tasted like fresh blueberries. I had a cherry shrub which was also great. For the virgins, a shrub is sort of like sweet vinegar to drink. Think somewhere in between Maraschino cherry juice and pickle juice. It may sound odd, but it's a must-try. They also gave us large bottles of seltzer water for the table, which was crisp and refreshing.

4 of us shared the Ida platter, which was the perfect amount of food. It came with a bread basket, cream cheese, potato salad, red onion, caper, the most beautiful ruby red tomato I've ever seen, and, of course, 4 types of their smoked salmon (Scottish, Gaspe, Pastrami, and Grav Lox). All of us that shared the platter were die-hard smoked fish fans, and each type we tasted was better than the previous (though looking back I think my favorite was the Grav Lox). The bread and bagels were fresh, and the potato salad was surprisingly able to stand up to the salmon. For $70 this platter was very fairly priced and well-worth it. We also got an order of herring fillet which came with pumpernickel bread and cream sauce on a bed of onions. This served us as a wonderful amuse-bouche, but no need to go out of your way for it.

Our other friends ordered the Shtetl board, the chocolate babka french toast, the classic board, and an omelette (for the vegetarian). We were all incredibly satisfied. Some reviews say that the food is overpriced, but I thought prices were very fair. None of us were disappointed when the bill came out.

Russ & Daughters, you nailed it. You're known for your smoked fish, and you've successfully created a menu that truly showcases your talent. Oh, sure, I'm sure your caviar scrambled eggs are good too, but that'll have to wait 'til I can spend $150 on eggs. In the mean time, I'll stick to your heavenly smoked salmon.

Delicious food and great service!! Had the nova platter, the pickled herring and the caviar plus two bloody marys. Rye bread was INSANE and food was genuinely worth every penny. Cannot wait to come back

Went in for brunch with the lady, who was immensely excited to check it out. I have heard about the spot from a top 15 restaurants to try in New York. Being that i've lived here for 23 years, I definitely had to  test it out. Decor is stunning. Its a clean and polished look. The waiters are all dressed alike and also have a polished look. The menu's were simple yet beautiful( as you can tell from the pictures. Follow my lady on Instagram: @i_cunningham) food was amazing. Went for the salmon with a Bagel and Cream cheese. The Salmon was so fresh! I can see myself coming back. Especially with the amazing Waitresses/Waiters they have on staff. All informative and relatable. Stellar restaurant!

I had high hopes. I love bagel and lox. This has been touted as one of the best in the city and I have to disagree. For $16 I expect an awesome bagel and ample lox. The bagel was tough and difficult to chew and the lox was stringy and tissue paper thin. I won't be repeating. Lindy's diner has a much better platter!

I really really wanted to like this place, but I didn't.  It had a bad start to begin with.  I came for meal at 12:50 pm and was told there would be a 30-45 min wait, and they would text me when it's ready- ok I expected to wait that long.    But I waited and waited, people who came after me got a seat and finished their meal!  Every time i checked on my table the hostess assured me that it will be ready soon.  At 2:38 I got a text saying my table would be ready in 5 mins.  Yes I stood outside for almost 2 HOURS.  After I got the text I went inside and I still had to wait about 20 minutes.  If the table was not ready, why would you text me that it is?  I wasnt even mad about the waiy because i was just catching up with some friends and was expecting to have some kick ass food. This would have all been worth it if the food was amazing- it wasn't.
The food was average.  I got the lower sunny side, it was nothing special- tasted like any brunch place.  The salmon tasted like regular salmon.  The only part that made it good was the latkes.  I also got the egg creme, idgi why did people rave about it...  I did like my friends coffee soda a lot tho.  They give you bottled water so you can refill your own water, which I liked.  But that was the trade off for having no one to ever check up to see if you need anything.
Overall no one should every wait 2 hours for average food.  Wouldn't come again.

Food:
1- Matzo Ball Soup
Tasty, lots of flavors going on here. 
2- The Hattie Platter
Wow, this is the real deal. Each piece of fish was very flavorful and fresh. Even the tomatoes and onions were fresh.The cream cheeses and breads were perfect.  

Drinks:
1- Caraway Bloody Mary
Can a Bloody Mary be smooth? Well, this one is. Top 3 Bloody in NYC. 
2- Chocolate Egg Cream
Delicious! Order this!
3- Lower East Side
Refreshing yet strong, quite the paradox.
I wish I didn't have to travel across the country to visit Russ & Daughters -- Oh, wait, they ship cross country! Now I can get the best smoked fish ever for every birthday - and maybe every weekend?

Wait was long, but totally worth it! Brunch was amazing and everything I'd hoped for. My husband has a severe allergy that they were more than willing to accomodate. The potato latkes were crispy and tasty and the whitefish salad was to die for! Although we didn't have drinks from the bar they looked interesting. Next time we would love to sit at the bar!

It's a fine cafe to eat good Jewish and American food following the traditional bagels, lox, latkes and knishes from their deli around the corner.
Very nice ambiance and stuff. Everything is decor like the 50's again, following the old school vibe from their business.
The food is good but anything out of this world and the portions are quite small so it gets a little pricey. 
The lox is awesome and the knishes and latkes not so much. I prefer barney's greengrass.

I came here for lunch; However, I'm not a fish eater, so the salmon on almost every dish eliminated almost everything for me. 

RESTAURANT OVERVIEW:
-Trendy diner vibe.

FOOD:
-Potato Latke with sour cream and applesauce: these were good, but a bit too fried for me. Came with 3 big latkes. Very very filling and heavy. 
-Matzo Ball Soup: This was good! no complaints

SERVICE:
-Good, no complaints.

Came here for brunch with a friend. The wait on Sunday was only 30 minutes for two people. The cafe has a retro diner vibe (and was heavily air conditioned, thank god, on a hot August day). My friend and I split the hot and cold smoked salmon dip, which was phenomenal. I got the classic bagel with lox. I agree with some others that the portions are small, but I actually appreciated that, as a HUGE bagel with lox would have been a lot (especially after the salmon dip). My friend had the babka french toast, which was quite rich - I don't know if I could have eaten it as an entree, but it was great just to have a taste. Would love to come back and try more of the different smoked fishes.

My husband and I each had one of the bagel boards-  mine with baked salmon and his with lox. Probably the most delicious fish we ever had. We also had unique mixed drinks with the meal and a fantastic halvah ice cream. The only slight disappointment were the bagels themselves as we expected them to be bigger and chewier but the food overall was fantastic. A bit overpriced but worth it!
Delicious.  Yummy. This is the MUST GO TO restaurant in Manhattan! The staff are also wonderful.  Did I mention the ambience-lovely!

Super classy old school New York
Vibes. 

I had the classic bagel with smoked salmon, cream cheese, onions capers and tomato it was awesome. Their bagels are excellent. 

Everyone else shared the chopped liver, herring, smoked sable (I tried this, delicious), and fish sticks. We loved it and everything is really well presented. I will definitely take anyone that visits NYC here for an authentic NYC institution.

I loved this place so much! I got a blueberry soda, The Classic, and our table shared blintzes, chocolate babka French toast, and knishes. Everything was super tasty. Grab lunch here and then check out a tour at the Tenement museum! The service was fantastic and I loved the decor.

Love, love, love it here.

Must try items are the smoked salmon and anything involving their whitefish salad. The drinks are also great, especially the shrubs!

I really like the clean, open feeling of the dining area- and that the design hearkens back to the history of the shop without being too hackneyed. 

If you can, come on a weekday afternoon to avoid the lines.

This has to be the best breakfast I've ever had... anywhere.  If you are in NYC and you like bagels with smoked fish, definitely get to Russ & Daughters.  You won't be disappointed.  
We arrived with a party of 6 at 10am on Sunday and were told we had a 45 minute wait.  We walked around nearby and were sent a text about 20 minutes later that our table was ready.  I loved that they send you a text, so you don't have to wait right there.  
The restaurant was very clean, including the restrooms.  I like the servers uniforms, also... clean, casual and professional.   I liked everything about this restaurant.  
Our server was friendly and helpful.  She gave us suggestions and even let us switch the fish on one classic board from nova to the smoked whitefish.  I believe her name was Alesandra or Alexandra.  We also had the classic nova board, a Shtetl Fish Board and a Matzo Brei.  We shared a few knishes.  I tried the chocolate egg cream and it was great.  Child got the grape soda and loved it.  
Breakfast/brunch here will be a definite any time I'm in NYC.  I wish I could ship some to my house right now, as my mouth is watering writing this review.

Really a classy place to eat breakfast.  The atmosphere is delightful and the food was great.  i had the Lower Sunny Side and it was delicious.  The salmon might be a little salty to some but it was fine for me and the potatoes latkes were really good.

We got the Anne Board because it has a little bit of everything.  The food is good, if a little pricey.  The bread was a little bit stale.  The roe was amazing.

Couldn't finish it all, so we asked for it to be wrapped up.  They didn't pack up most of the leftovers and only gave us the bread.  What?  Pack up the fish items, potato salad, roe, and not stale bread, duh!

A lot of these yelp restaurant reviews make me laugh.  The people who write these yelp reviews that make me laugh, make me laugh more.  Sigh.  One thing though that don't make me laugh is this place.  Glorious!!!  Tried going to Sadelle's where we were told the wait was 2-3 hours.  HA!  Bah ha!!  Walked over here and the wait was 45mins but they txt us in 30 mins.  We are so glad we decided to eat here today and patronize a long standing family business with so much history and not another corporate restaurant caricature/bastardization of a culture's cuisine.  Russ and Daughters is the REAL DEAL.  Always enjoy shopping at the store, too.  Everything was great:  service, food, decor.  I'm not gonna tell you what we ordered cuz everybody likes different things so what does it matter.  What matters is we all enjoyed our meal.  Good portions.  Everybody was nice, friendly and knowledgable.  YUM.  Thank you for opening up this cafe.  Will be back for more!!  p.s. - Please take reservations.  Please.

Yum yum! Delicious, crispy yet tender latkes and the Classic board were politely gobbled up by my family at the bar. Beautiful space, consistent design, and very nice and calm climate in there.

If you're a tourist, stop by the cafe before you leave the Lower East Side. Buy one of their black & white cookies for me! Is it delicious?!?

Are you friggin' kidding me?

In a city where a decent knish can be had off of a corner cart and almost any luncheonette can make you a decent egg cream this overhyped expensive tourist trap has the balls to charge you offensive amounts for absolutely shitty examples of both.

The smoked fish is great - get it from the original store and take it home to enjoy.

PS - when your server picks something up off the floor and then DOESN'T WASH THEIR HANDS before handing you food and drink, that is a DEALBREAKER.

VERY DISAPPOINTED - go elsewhere - second ave deli is a thousand times better.

My first experience at Russ and Daughters and what a success. First I have to say service was extremely welcoming. We walked in on Sunday night at 9:35, with closing at 10, and they seated has in their best booth with smiles on their face. 

We shared the matzoh ball soup which they graciously separated into two bowls. It was delicious despite all the celery (hate celery!). Could have used some more carrots but very good size portion.

We both had the classic, one with poppy and another with everything bagel. I was blown away by how delicious this was. I'm not the biggest lox fan but I couldn't stop eating this meal!!! I thought the bagel was on the small size and maybe there is a reason for that but come on, we're New Yorkers and we like our bagels a certain size, thankyouverymuch. The lox and cream cheese combination though - wow!!! It's a must!

One star off as always because $16 is steep, but I suppose you have to look at this as a very fancy (and filling!) sandwich. I am curious if the shop has the same prices because I noticed it was $8 for a knish which seems unheard of. In any case I will be back!!!

My new favorite breakfast/lunch spot in NYC. The food is amazingly fresh, tasty and authentic, while still incorporating new elements of dining. The service is impeccable and the ambiance is clean and cozy.

My kind of place. They really cover all the bases, but hit a homerun on the smoked fish front. I had the Classic (lox, everything bagel). We also ordered some latkes which were great, but the lox was outstanding. Just melts in your mouth without being too smokey. Got the "pickles" too, which had an array of pickled vegetables; sour and dill pickles, tomatoes, carrots, onions. The pickles were my favorite, but the tomatoes followed very closely behind. Oh yeah, the challah is delicious too :)

I got the french toast and although its not what I'm used to (fluffy vanilla flavored please!) I love their take on it. The whip cream on the side is addictive, and the chocolate gooey-ness inside is A+. Can't wait to go back to try the rest of the menu!
Very good menu. Friendly service. I recommend the herring with pickled onions as an appetizer.

The best of the best!  Wait times can be up to two hours so come early.  Ordered the classic with a everything bagel and a side of latkes.  Everything tasted amazing, the atmosphere is very old ny and the service was good. I now understand why this place is so popular.

Love the vibe, food and service at Russ & Daughters. The cafe is pristine, white and airy. I honestly could have sat there all day, coffee in hand.

The potato latkes were some of the best I've ever eaten, so do yourself a favor and order these. The classic board was also tasty. Definitely an affordable brunch option and if you get there early you won't have to wait for a table. I can't wait to go back.

I've been waiting for this place to open all year and was thrilled when we got to try it last Christmas. Yes! They're open on Christmas Day and with a line too! I love everything about the R&D shop on Houston, but now there's even more to love with the Cafe. The service was friendly and I needed them to be because it was not fun waiting outside on a cold NY winter morning. Once inside, it's smells of yummy breads and fried eggs. I got the Kasha Varnishkas (I'm a sucker for anything with kasha!) and the Hubs had the Pastrami Russ. Both were delicious and perfectly presented. This place is wonderful and I look forward to our next visit.

The wait on a Sunday was extremely long, but that's expected, especially when you don't make a reservation (shame on us). After waiting over an hour, we were finally seated. We ordered the classic board and Bloody Mary's. The smoked salmon was soooo Delicious. I love my smoked salmon cut very thin, and their's was perfect! Didn't care much for the Bloody Mary, but the board was worth the wait. Will definitely be back again

Delicious brunch. Extensive smoked fish selection (pricey, but isn't all good fish?). Shrubs are really refreshing in the summer. No reservations means a long line -- we waited an hour. Otherwise, would come again!

I've been wanting to try Russ & Daughters ever since I saw a special on Sturgeon Queens, a movie about their shop.  We went back and forth on whether we wanted to try the café, or try the original store, but decided we wanted to sit down, sample, and take our time.  

We absolutely pigged out.  Ordered the Classic Board, Hot smoke/Cold smoke, Pickled Herring Trio, Smoked Whitefish chowder, and a plate of sours.  The lox on the classic was incredible.  Best I've ever had.  I'm used to lox being stringy and fatty and hard to chew.  Not the case here.  It was perfectly smooth and not the least bit chewy.  The smoked salmon spread in the hot smoke was my favorite and my fiancé loved the Herring.  

The entire place is very cute.  I wish I could return for more meals here.

The Russ & Daughters menu is simple and delicious! The wait was a bit long, but the host was determined to get us seated quickly. We were seated in a large booth that could seat 6. My boyfriend and I then realized after browsing the menu and restaurant decor, that this was a cafe that served Jewish comfort food. Cool! I went with the Classic Board and it was fantastic. I would definitely like to go back soon for brunch. I highly recommend this cafe if you're wanting to try something new.
