I had been dreaming about this place for a few weeks when I first read about it in the NY Times.  We flew from San Diego to NYC to spend a week and knew we had to make this Jewish deli a priority. 

We purchased tickets to tour the Lower East Side Tenement Museum, which was across the street, and schedule it so we could have a nice lunch here first. 

It did not disappoint!  I had the lox and bagel , but with goat cheese cream cheese, which was different, but nice. The lox was so perfect!  Hubby had smoked salmon eggs Benedict, which was great. 

Then we added a side of the pastrami curd smoked salmon...OMG just out of this world!  

Loved the counter, seats, cleanliness, and the history - it's been there for 101 years!   

Great service. Large menu. Fun mix of patrons hanging out for lunch. 

I HIGHLY HIGHLY HIGHLY recommend Russ and Daughters if you're into smoked fish and Jewish delis in a great walking neighborhood on the lower east side.

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this place!   The BEST smoked salmon ever...I am a complete loss for words because you have to try it yourself.  The quality is exceptional, the taste is divine and it keeps you wanting for more.  So one brisk and chilly winter morning, we walked all the way from Chinatown to Russ & Daughters Cafe.  I just wanted to try something different since my husband has a tendency not to try anything new unless someone else tells him about it.  So what better way to discover new foods is to bring your beloved teen daughter whose palate is pretty eclectic.  I ordered the smoked salmon with eggs sunny side up and my daughter opted for the eggs benedict.  We make a best efforts basis to go back here for this luscious breakfast.

I've been wanting to come here ever since they were featured on Louie C.K's show a while back. This place is all about smoked and cured fish with a couple of smaller dishes if you're opting out of the whole fish thing. The herring is hands down incredible and the prices are fair. 
Also the chocolate babka french toast was really good.

Went for dinner on a Thus night. Not your typical dinner foods, but not a problem for us. We ordered 2 main dishes which were both excellent. Upscale, diner-like atmosphere and seltzer water, standard. Reasonable prices and portions (i.e. NOT huge). We look forward to heading back here.

i ordered the LES - it was sunnyside eggs, 2 latkes and smoked salmon - and it was goood!!! the guy next to me ordered a classic board - i have to remember to order that next time - that looked good too!  very cool looking restaurant, and the bartender lady was super awesome!!!  great service, and atmosphere and food of course!  highly recommend!

Beside the wait of 1.5hr for a table on a Saturday for brunch this place is incredible! My girlfriend and I met there for brunch. We each got the salmon board to start.  Ending our meal off with halva ice ream, and challah bread pudding, all fantastic. Also if you're into a cocktail or two, I recommend the smoked martini & the heads and tails.

Nothing less than expected with quality tasty traditional food and great service; wish it's just a tiny closer to my home on the west side lol.  Thank you for providing yummy food and treats all these years.

we at at noon yesterday and sat at the bar. The bar tender was quite helpful. She answered my many questions. I had western lox and herring on one of their house salads. The quality was excellent. My daughter had noodle sweet dish and a lox and bialy. The meal as quite expensive and the wait was long but the food and service were worth it. They text us when our table was bar seats were ready. Orchard and Rivington street have some cute art galleries like Chelsea had 30 ago. On a nice day the wait is fine in bad weather, make another plan because they don't take reservations. If you are locals buy their stuff at their store it's worth it.

Me and my friend went for saturday brunch and waited 1.5 hours to sit which wasn't too bad. Staff and hostesses were friendly for the most part. Our waitress barely gave us attention which bothers me a lot- could have gotten in and out a lot quicker if she did. We started out with the chocolate babka French toast which was very good. I got the   My friend got the super heebster which was amazing. Pretty small for $12 but to describe what it tastes most like is tuna sal

This place is great! I've been wanting to go here forever and it was everything I expected and more. My friend and I went here on a Saturday morning at 9am and there was about a half hour wait for two people. Once seated, the server was quick to take our drink orders and bring them out -- both the margarita and bloody mary were strong and delicious. We ordered latkes with sour cream and salmon roe, the heebster, the salmon pastrami, and the chocolate babka. The latkes were crispy on the outside and just the right texture on the inside. The heebster was a little difficult to eat since they did not skimp out on the whitefish salad or roe. However, the whitefish salad, which usually plays second fiddle to lox in the breakfast arena, tasted very luxurious and not at all like the whitefish salad from a regular deli. The pastrami was phenomenal but we did wish it came in a bigger portion. I'm not usually a fan of chocolate but the babka was the perfect ending to a great meal. We stopped by the Russ & Daughters main bagel store afterwards to pick up bagels and they did not disappoint either. Overall, a great experience and I totally understand why this is a NY classic. Can't wait to go back and order the rest of the menu!
Food very good. Service/management of seating quite poor. Waited almost 2h after being told wait was around 45 minutes.

Tip: Grab a ticket number right when you enter! 

Everything bagel with king salmon, scallion cream cheese, tomato, and onions.

For my first time having a NYC bagel I really didn't notice anything different. Maybe it's just me. Anyways the bagel I had was super tough to chew, and made my jaws hurt. Regardless the salmon and cream cheese was delicious, I would definitely come back.
I went here for breakfast and got the classic board and the latkes, both AMAZING. Love the jewishness as well. Will definitely recommend and I hope to come back!

The food is good, but it's really the decor and plating that pulls this place together.  The space is so sleek and clean that you don't mind waiting an hour and paying $16 for a smoked salmon and cream cheese bagel (it's just displayed so beautifully!).  The challah bread pudding and potato latkes are equally comforting, although probably not the absolute best of the city.  Definitely a cute place to take out-of-towners who've come for ambiance and would rather not go to the original store and eat on the sidewalk.

Always my best deli stop in NYC! They have classic delicacies and unique smoked fish/caviar options. The baked salmon and whitefish salad is absolutely amazing! This trip to the cafe I ordered that on a bialy with horseradish cream cheese and caviar. Mouth is watering now just thinking about it. 

Make sure to also stop over to the Russ and Daughter's store for some items to take home, including dried apricots!

Have been for breakfast two times this week - both amazing. First time ordered the latkes with salmon and it was fantastic. Second time had the eggs Benny which was also good... But I ended up ordering a side of latkes to make it perfect!

The food was good. Uneven but mostly very good. Latkes were delicious but arrived just barely warm. Caviar and blinis were good - nice presentation. Matzoh ball soup was delicious! The borscht...enough for a week! The Anne Platter was good, but surprisingly we found the salmon wasn't the best nor were the bagels. The sable didn't compare to what I've had at Barney Greengrass. The house made sodas were a treat. 

We were seated just across from the server station so one would imagine we'd get lots of attentive service. Not so much. Our server was either brand new and poorly trained or having the worst day ever. He spilled soup AND coffee on one of my dining companions. He rarely checked in with us and poorly bussed our table through courses. He was not communicative. And just plain unfriendly.

We found ourselves wondering if the food would've tasted better if we'd felt more comfortable. Which reminds me that the booths are not at all comfortable (how weird is that?).
Really good Potato latkes and a buzzing atmosphere - staff are very friendly. Be prepared for long wait times for Sunday brunch (1.5 hours plus) - it's worth the wait!!

I mean, Russ and Daughters. You just can't go wrong. Whether it's this newer cafe or their original deli location on Houston, it's 100% worth the wait. Get the white fish salad, goat cheese cream cheese and always, always the chocolate babka.

Way overrated. The bialys are sub par as was the kippered salmon (my favorite food ) and the sturgeon was also very blah. Scrambled eggs were excellent as was the service. The place with the blue and white striped awning is far superior .

Not bad, not bad. Came around on a Sunday afternoon at 1:15pm, quoted a 1.5 hr wait. Put our name down, they will text us when table is ready.

Table was ready around 2:45pm. Promptly seated when we showed up. People were still walking in at this time, so I suspect the long wait is going to happen throughout the entire day. 

Had the Heebster (it was good), Eggs Benny (Awesome) and the Classic Board (It was a-okay). 

All in all, I'd say if you want to come here, come early, put your name down, and plan to grab a cup of coffee nearby or walk around for a bit - 'cause you'll be waiting anyway. Food is alright. Good to try once or twice - but it's definitely not a place where I'd ever go "Salmon / Eggs Benedict / XXX food? We HAAAVEEEEEE to go to Russ & Daughters!!!!!"

Gotta get the LOX!

This great little old school cafe based off the Russ and Daughters Appetizers deli on E.houston street makes you feel like you are going back in time to a diner.

When I got here it was a short wait only 30 minutes which is lucky for a Saturday. The table we got was directly across from the bar which was very cool the bar area. I knew what I wanted right away something with LOX! 

We got the Lower Sunny Side which was sunny side up eggs, gaspe nova smoked salmon, potato latkes and the Eggs Benny - poached eggs, scottish smoked salmon, sauteed spinach, hollandaise over challah bread. Both dishes were amazing the latkes were so crispy yet moist and the lox was the best I have ever had it was so smooth,salty, and straight up delicious. 

After eating all that it was time to split a desert which we decided on the Babka French toast which taste exactly like it sounds. The sweetness of the syrup with a mix the chocolate was delectable.

In short the food here was amazing and the service was superb. I will be back here many times over.

In short:
- Great for Brunch
- Great Service
- Best Lox I have ever had
- No reservations

What is there to not love about Russ & Daughters Cafe? It's history from their first store incorporated in every detail of the restaurant. Amazing. 

So, yes, I'm a vegetarian and this is the Mecca of smoked fish. There is so much more to love! 

We started with the bread basket because we all know NYC has these scrumptious carbs on point. There was no exception here, all the Jewish varieties were included like rye, bagel, bialy, pumpernickel, and challah. Perfect way to start while waiting for your entrees. 

The potato pancakes were insanely fresh, crunchy on the outside and delicate and soft in the inside. Served with sour cream and apple sauce to counterbalance the salty bites. So good!

Do not leave without trying the bobka french toast. It's a relatively small portion, and due to the decadence, it was appreciated. It was chocolately and flakey and warm. The fresh strawberries went perfectly with the sweet flavor of the main attraction. 

We arrived shortly after they opened on a Saturday morning and were seated right away. If you are impatient with the long, well deserved wait times for a table, get there early!

Had a late lunch here on Saturday. Delicious food and extremely attentive service. Really nice presentation as well. I ordered "The Classic," which is a platter of lox, onions, tomatoes, capers, cream cheese and your choice of bread. I chose the bialy. The lox was great, chewy, not too salty and subtly sweet. To go with it I had the caraway infused vodka bloody mary. That, too, was delicious and refreshing. A satisfying, yummy lunch for about $35.00 including tip. I will definitely be going back.

Delicious latkes, I also got a cranberry soda and my friend got a ginger soda and both were excellent. You should definitely try a soda, they are specially made here. The service was great and the vibe in the restaurant was great. I'm definitely going to come back.
This is probably one those LES spots you need to put on your go to list. Would give it 5 stars if prices were a little bit more reasonable.

Oh man. This deli really took me over the top. Caviar and creme fraiche before our bagel and lox plate? YES PLEASE. They even custom made me a plate of matzo brie, my favorite food in the world. I wish I lived in New York just so I could come here on a regular basis.

I may be a Sephardic Jew but Russ and Daughters makes me feel at at home and wanna do the hora! Great Marzoh Ball soup - light and fluffy and flavorful. And the whitefish salad is to die for! Only issue is the wait. So come at 2 o'clock-ish and you'll be fine! Tell em Yankeleh sent you!

If the fish is meant to be the star of the show here, don't make me pay $18 for one tiny almost see through slither of tastless salmon with your Eggs Benny. I came for your salmon, not an inch of gritty spinach.

Poached eggs were cooked well, though why do you try and fit the whole thing on just one small peice of challah?

Please pick-up your game.
Weekday morning was about a 45 minute wait, which was well worth it. Potato latkes were awesome but the best part is the smoked fish! The boards are the stars of the show!

We were really stuck after another nearby restaurant was unable to honor our reservation (the kitchen didn't open for an hour after our OpenTable seating time).
Luckily, after a moment of scrambling, there was an open table here, at Russ & Daughters, and they did a terrific job of feeding us full of delicious food, treating us great, and getting us out in time for our off-Broadway show.
A little bit pricey, it's true - and what the NY Times said about the caviar markup being ridiculous is definitely on the money - but the soups, eggs, latkes, and obviously the salmon were all first-rate, the service was top-notch, and honestly, considering how we were put in a bit of a jam by our original restaurant, Russ & Daughters Cafe saved our entire evening.

I have been a few times this year but was really disappointed during my visit yesterday. There was hair on one of my plates of food. I really hoped they addressed it with the kitchen staff. I was shocked.

OH MAN. This place is the best. So happy they finally opened a sit-down cafe. The food, the decor, the service, it's all top notch. I recommend the smoked whitefish chowder to start and the Shtetl was the shitl. It's clear that throughout all of their years of business, R&D continue to care about the quality of their food. You won't regret it.

Let's keep this brief.  If you appreciate fine food and want the have the pinnacle of the Jewish deli/lox/bagel experience then eat here. It is perfection. Every ingredient is the best, and the bagels are made in house. 10/10. Fantastic!!!
Make sure you get "the classic" with the bread pudding as a breakfast dessert (that's right, you know you do it too). Other than that, expect great food from this awesome spot!

I really wanted to dislike this place and have tried to avoid it for the last five years. I'm generally negatively disposed towards places encircled with unseemly amounts of hype--the types of places lauded by the masses and despised by the discerning. The high expectations surrounding this place actually lowered my own expectations, which may have contributed to me walking out very satisfied. Obviously, expect a wait. We went a little later in the day and still had to wait over an hour. If you expect to walk right in and be seated, you're in the wrong city. Despite the wait and casually paced service, the caviar (w/ blinis and creme fraiche) was wonderful and the bagels and lox were enjoyable. I won't be raving about the experience like some do, but it certainly doesn't merit opprobrium.

A truly great breakfast / lunch spot (also known as brunch). 

A huge plus is that they have gluten free bagels as well as gluten free bread!

However, as a gluten eater, I was not blow away by their bagels. They were not up to my expectations, and I almost preferred my mom's gluten free bagel. 

Luckily, regardless of taste, this is a very instagramable meal. The likes on my photo make up for the lackluster bagel.

frindly service!
excellent smoked fish platters!
delicous barley soup!
nice design!

highly recommend this place....

Had a wonderful dinner here.  Loved the bread, salmon, and drinks.  A very fun spot and with attentive service.  The only thing that I did not like is having to use the 'Reserve' app to get a dinner reservation.  Stay away from that app!

I've been wanting to try this New York classic since forever. My friend from out of town was visiting, and we were both craving lox so this was the perfect opportunity. We arrived around 2pm, and were given an hours wait time. We weren't starving and grabbed bubble tea down the street so it wasn't too terrible a wait time. But they do underestimate the wait because we waited for an hour and a half. By that time, we were thinking that this better be the best lox bagel I will have in my life! 

We both ordered the classic board ($16), which included smoked nova salmon, cream cheese, tomatoes, onions, capers and a bagel of your choice. The lox bagel was so good! The everything bagel was the best I've ever had. It was so nicely flavored and toasted perfectly. The salmon was so fresh! It didn't have that fishy taste that a lot of smoked salmons have, which immediately made me rate this as one of the best and top notch salmons. The tomatoes were kind of tasteless and sandy, so that kind of chipped away from the overall taste. But overall, this is a quality plate! You must try this at least once!

Expensive prices aside ($17 for a gluten free bagel w/ trimmings), I really enjoyed what we ate at R&D cafe. I ordered the Super Heebster twice because the first one didn't really fill me up and our server didn't charge me $20 (it's $10 per order) but instead charged me $17 for the two half-bagels. Still pricey but at least I got $3 off. My bf had the cold smoked Yum Kippered and a bowl of the chilled borscht both of which he found tasty and filling. To wash it all down, we shared a refreshing homemade lime and basil soda. 

We waited roughly ten minutes for a table on Friday evening (at around 6:30) without a reservation. The place was already packed when we got there so plan accordingly. Overall, it was a good dining experience but will probably come back only when I'm feeling rich enough to pay $17 for a bagel.

First time visiting NY and the atmosphere here was very unique! We loved it. We got the classic board and it was the best bagel and lox I've ever had. We also tries the egg benny- lox eggs Benedict-which was also amazing!!!! They also have 4 diff types of bloody Mary's they make right there with fresh ingredients for only 10bucks! They have a caviar menu that ranges from 70 bucks to 900! Caviar is not our thing but def cool to see on the menu listed by diff types and grams.

Sissy and I ventured out the day after #jonas2016 and we were still quoted an hour wait although we arrived a few minutes after opening. Nothing keeps New Yorkers from flocking for their bagels! We ended up waiting about 45 minutes before getting a text that our table was ready.

The cafe is warm and bright with a very old school charm.  Service was pretty shoddy but whatever. We ordered a classic board each and some latkes and babka french toast to share. The food came out quick enough. 

The classic board is DIY with the bagel, onions, tomatoes, cream cheese and 3 slices of nova smoked salmon. The bagel is really nothing special -- I've had better at many other spots. The salmon, however, is so, so good. A solid sandwich but very expensive at that. 

The latkes, three per order, were incredible. Definitely some of the best I've ever had. These patties were thick and crunchy on the outside while encompassing a piping hot, soft and flavorful inside. I cut it up into small pieces to make it last as long as possible. 

The babka french toast was the most disappointing dish of all. I was expecting fluffy and soft but it was more like dry and sad. Very chocolatey, yes, but dry, dry, dry. 

Overall, I had a good meal and would come back to try some of their other items.
The food is amazing, the service is terrible. If you don't mind to suffer for a good breakfast/brunch/dinner it is your place. If you expect to be treated as a guest, you better go somewhere else

DO come here and DO eat everything! This place serves the delicious goods from Russ & Daughters but in a nice sit down environment. I am head over heels in love with the decor - feels like an escape back in time!

Started the meal with matzo ball soup, which is perfect on a cold day (or any day actually). I had the lower sunny side which includes eggs, lox and potato latkes. The lox is very good and the potato latkes are out of this world - probably some of the best latkes I have ever tried! Also tried their cucumber soda which I highly recommend - it's house made and very refreshing!

Service is good, a little slow but overall friendly and accommodating. Be warned - this place is really popular and there is a guaranteed wait if you come during peak times. Luckily, they will text you when your table is ready so you can wander around to kill the time (or empty your wallet at economy candy just two blocks away). Definitely worth the wait!

What better way to say goodbye to NYC than with a classic breakfast at Russ and Daughters. With a decor out of the 1920's, soft jazz vocals piped out if the speaker, soft lighting equals a romantic breakfast. Then there is the hand carved nova with bagel, cream cheese, capers, onion marrying beautifully into an elegant bite. And don't forget the potato latke. Crunchy on the outside, with a potato oniony center. Pair it with applesauce and sour cream and prepare to be transcended. Make this your final memory of NYC and prepare to leave with a smile.

The ambiance is great, if you're going for lunch, get there early because it fills up quickly. My boyfriend and I got there around 10:05 AM, and by 10:15- it was PACKED.
Once we were seated we ordered the classic plate (bagel and lox), and the eggs benedict with challah, both were bland, and the fish tasted overly smoked- kinda like it was out of the grocery store. The eggs benedict didn't have much flavor, and to my taste- were a little bitter.
On the other hand, the service was great. The waiters were attentive and friendly, it definately gives an extra star to the resturant. 
I would come back again for the ambiance, maybe order something else, but it really is overhyped- as most brunch places are in NYC.

Usually, when a place is as hyped up as Russ & Daughters, it fails to deliver. You go there and you think, "yeah, this is good...but is it so much better than three other places I can think of?" Russ & Daughters represents one of the rare instances where a restaurant actually lives up to the hype. Their fish in particular is just in a different league. Your first time, you have to get The Classic board. Until you do, you've never really had a bagel with lox. 

Oh yeah, and the Bloody Mary's are excellent also.

(But be prepared to wait a long time on the weekends. We went on a Sunday at 12:30 and it was an estimated 2 - 2:15 hour wait for two people, although it ended up being a little under two hours in actuality.)

All tiny portions. I know smoked fish is expensive but this is crazy.  lunch menu was very limited. Maybe 8-10 choices. Everything sounded delicious & when I looked at other tables, the food looked just as good. I had a pastrami lox sandwich, served on pretzel bread. I'm not Kidding, it was 4 bites. Served with a pickle and delicious potato chips. Chips have to be home made. Very thin and with waffled holes. A tasty lunch but I was still hungry so I decided to try the egg cream. Just the right mixture of syrup, Selzer & milk but $5 for an egg cream? Seriously. Maybe they depend on hipsters or tourists but gouging is gouging. I give 4 stars despite my grievances because of the food quality, fine service and presentation. I'll come back but not as often as I ordinarily would and only when I want to spend more than I usually do. (Not often lol)

We accidentally showed up to the cafe side vs. the to go side.. but I wasn't mad about it. Ordered the Yum Kippered and I was not disappointed. On the pricer side ($60 Breakfast) but it was delicious nonetheless.

This spot is a must for me every time I am in the city. My boyfriend and I have gone twice for dinner and there was absolutely no wait, in fact the restaurant was rather slow on both occasions- which we rather prefer, anyway. On both occasions we ordered the exact same thing-I started with matzo ball soup, he began with the cold borscht, and we split knishes and latkes (with sour cream an applesauce), with honey cake and apple ice cream to finish. Everything is so very wonderful, I crave it constantly. The atmosphere is super charming, puts you in the mind of an old school soda counter with a modern twist (also I am in dire need of the wallpaper in the women's restroom, love it). The staff is extremely attentive, you will never have an empty water carafe. I would highly recommend this spot to anyone and everyone. It is extremely close to the tenement museum- hit up both and make a date night out of it like we did!

I have been begging my friends for months now to go to this place for brunch. "Eh, I don't feel like waiting in line for 3 hours," many of them joked. But what if we go early? "Brunch before noon? Are you insane?"

Which led me to try this spot solo, post-workout one Saturday morning. I'd worked up an appetite at class and was stoked to try something savory. Or sweet. It really didn't matter, as long as it was scrumptious. 

First impression: The place is cute, and if you can score a table you've won the jackpot. I grabbed a seat at the counter, forgoing the 1.5-hour wait for parties of two or more (yes, even at 10:30 on a Saturday, which is dawn by LES standards). Hosts and servers are very sweet, though, and will tell you to hang tight with a smile on their face.

The girl behind the counter recommended the Lower East Side dish, which consisted of two sunny side up eggs, two potato latkes, and lox. It ended up being a sliver of salmon, some smaller latkes and, admittedly, perfect eggs. But the latkes were relatively bland, and the fish portion so small, I couldn't really gauge how good it was. Let's just say, I was still hungry after finishing my plate.

Coffee plus the dish cost about $20. A bit much? Maybe, though comparable to other brunch spots in the area. I'd just rather go somewhere with less of a wait, with more flavor.

Great food, love the selections of smoked fish.  I highly recommend the super heebster. We also got the Ida platter with a side of caviar. The food came out quick, the waitress was very nice and sweet, the only reason I'm not giving this four stars was the hour and half wait... Which was worth it by the way, but most of all the extremely rude hostess who tried to seat us at the counter by the entrance when there were two open tables in the back? Why? Especially with such a long wait time... Holding things up for the hype? She gave us an attitude when I asked if we could sit at the table in the back. Thankfully an unpleasant experience was quickly turned around.

A family friend now lives in New York City and we wanted to grab brunch together so he suggested this place. Totally down since I've seen so many pictures and looks good. 

I ordered the eggs benedict (poached eggs, smoked salmon, sauteed spinach, hollandaise, and challah). The challah was an interesting twist on a normal benedict. The smoked salmon (which I normally don't love) was definitely a little bit cooked by the time I got to it, but it was pretty good.  

My friend ended up getting some other things, but he was sick so I didn't try any of it. Last meal in New York was delicious! 

Protip: get there early - like when it opens to not have to wait for seats!

A must visit when I'm in NY. I always get the classic board and Bloody Mary. The combination is just too good. Usually there is a long wait so plan to get there early and put a name down then walk around the neighborhood. Worth the wait.

I went there for lunch with a friend, we waited 1 hour for a table but i am glad we did it because it was AMAZING! Omg, sometimes when you get into a restaurant in nyc you have many chances to get bad quality food, here, you can say that all the products are super super good quality, the fish was soo goood, same for the cream cheese, same for the bread (which I suppose was made there) and I get the french toast for the desert which was amazing too !
But for this kind of food you have to pay a little more, for sure, so it's to me a little bit expensive but it's totally justify for the food you get :)
In plus, the service was great, I love the ambience and the decoration you feel you're on the seaside

Found this place on yelp and turns out EVERYONE I know (and their mothers) have been to this place. So I had to check it out on Valentine's day weekend with the Beau. We arrived at around 10am and had a 40 minute wait - they don't take reservations but we were prepared to wait. We were able to give them our number for them to text us when our reservation was ready (we went to Chinatown for a quick snack). ANYWAY, when we arrived back, we had 2 seats at the bar waiting for us. The bar is very cute and the drinks are VERY strong.

I had a Smoked Martini which was very good and VERY strong even though it was a small glass. I definitely didn't need more than one. My beau got a Bloody Mary which, despite me disliking every other one I've tried, this was not terrible. The Break-Fast Martini looked really good as well (definitely trying that next time)

As for food, we split the Potato Latkes - wild salmon roe & creme fraiche, Lower Sunny Side, & Eggs Benny. All of which was very good - although I the Eggs benny were a bit over done and not as runny as I would have preferred. I ate very slowly so I could savor every bite. 

This place is relatively expensive, so be prepared to spend a bit but it is worth it with the ambiance, service, and food.

Service:
We sat at the bar - the staff was very nice and attentive to us. The water glasses were very small but were never empty. The food came out very quickly.

I would definitely come here again - potentially thinking about bringing my parents here!

When we left around 12pm, the line seemed to have cleared out.
I'm powerless against the force. They do it all, and do it right. Pretentious,sure. Overpriced, absolutely. Crazy delish,certainly. Throw a dart at the menu; it is that good.

The wait will be long, especially for brunch. When the hostess tells you 1.5-2 hrs, she meant it. No joke!

After a long wait, my best friend & I finally got seated at the bar. Food was on point & our waiter was very helpful w/ suggestions.

I loved my eggs benny! Yum yum yum! Perfect poached eggs on top of smoked salmon, spinach & a nice fluffy piece of challah bread?! Hell yeah, dericious!!!

Feed me more, please!! :D

During the polar vortex I thought that maybe Russ & Daughters famous 90 minute wait time for Saturday brunch would be a touch reduced. It wasn't, but it was totally worth said wait. I strongly recommend going next door to Lucky Jacks and warming up with a hot rum and cinnamon butter concoction, it's a great bar with great music. 

Despite the long wait and sometimes demanding crowds, the customer service was impeccable. Everyone greeted us with a smile, and once we sat down our waitress never rushed us despite the growing wait times. In fact, she took the time to answer some of my questions about the menu and make recommendations. I love that! 

Me and my friend split the bissel of caviar ($30). It comes with blinis and creme fraiche, and is a perfect way to get a little luxury while also being somewhat budget conscious. It was delicious, obviously.

My friend had the whitefish soup- creamy and sweet with a slight kick, I had no idea I even liked whitefish. Admittedly it was my first time having it. And I actually liked it even more than the matzo ball soup I ordered, even though that was also really good.

For my entree I got the Lower Sunny Side: latkes, smoked salmon, and sunny side up eggs. Hell yes to all of this! The smoked salmon was some of the best I've ever had. I piled it on top of the latkes and then piled the eggs on top of that. The portion looks small but don't be fooled, it's actually quite filling. After having the soup we felt ready to be wheeled out of there.

Nice beer list, absolutely phenomenal bloody mary's (I recommend the smoked pepper version). They definitely lived up to the hype :)

I don't really believe you should sit down and have a bagel. That's not brunch food in my mind.  But I will change that tune for this place!  We had the smoked sampler and it was amazing.  The knish was fab and the bloody marys were really excellent.  Didn't hurt that Jake Gyllenhaal was at the table next to us either.

3.5 stars. Extra half star visually for the fairly efficient texting system/service. 

Overall I am not as impressed as I hoped to be with this place. Yes the salmon was delicious. But there were literally 3 pieces of it on my small plate, which had 2 eggs, a meager slice of challah (which was originally supposed to be latke but they ran out), and a small salad. When I'm paying $16 for brunch I'm expecting to be pretty full by the end but I definitely felt like portions were on the smaller side here. 

Next time I'm craving some of this amazing fish I think the best bet is just to go to the shop instead of the cafe. That way I can also skip the 90-minute wait on Saturday/Sunday mornings. Really sad I didn't get to try the latkes and really sad they didn't make a better, more value-worthy substitution!

The wait took a while even though it was 4pm on a Saturday, but it was worth it. You can get a drink at the retro/diner bar while you wait. The Bloody Mary is bloody good. The one we got was the spicy one. It had a great kick to it and would definitely have it again.

The smoked fish chowder was light, slightly creamy and perfectly seasoned.  They even split it into two bowls to share without us asking. 

You can't visit Russ & Daughters without trying the Classic board with deliciously smoked salmon, capers, tomatoes and onions, cream cheese and a bagel. I asked for a toasted everything bagel. My friend got an eggs benedict and it looked and tasted fantastic.

We were too full to try any of the desserts, but the lady next to us had the Havlah Ice cream and by her enthusiasm while ordering it, it must be really great.

They are extremely accommodating here and are willing to exclude/include according to your preferences (just don't overdo it).
Such a hardcore fantasia of smoked fish but also, such a beautiful room. I loved it. In the store I'd always wanted a place to linger but this I think is so much better.

I went to the cafe and the store front next to Katz Delicatessen. 
At the store front I got the Norwegian smoke salmon on an everything with plain cream cheese. Basic, but a classic and it was great! 
At the café I ordered the matza ball soup. Equally good and super comforting.

Came around 11am on a Sunday, and the wait for 2 was ~50 minutes (definitely try to come before noon, though, if you're visiting on a weekend. The wait had doubled by the time we were seated). They'll text you when your table's ready, so we just went elsewhere and grabbed coffee while we waited. Not bad at all! We sat at the bar and the bartenders were extremely friendly and very quick.

I'm not usually a fan of much more than boring cream cheese on bagels, but this place was so good I had to make an exception for the classic board. My friend and I split one board and just got 1 extra bagel, which ended up being pretty cost effective. I've seen several reviews complaining about the small amount of salmon that came with the board, so maybe it's just a crap shoot, but ours came with a TON--it was the perfect amount for splitting between 2 people. The latkes were also great, although nothing too special. I regret not getting the bloody mary or babka french toast, which people around me ordered and which looked amazing. I'll definitely be back!

Excellent choice. The food looks and tastes great. Highly recommend this restaurant. We also visited their market on Houston Street. I had fun, bought a few items. This was one of the highlight of my visit to New York.

Definitely come here on a weekday than a weekend, as the wait time for the weekend can be up to 2 hours.

Came here on a Wednesday afternoon with a friend and I thought there would be some wait time to get a table. Surprisingly, we were asked if we minded seating in the bar area and of course, we said no and were seated immediately. This was like a dream come true, since this never happens for brunch. But I suppose brunch is more of a weekend thing. 

The first thing you may notice is the people working there are wearing white lab coats. I wondered why they were wearing them, but I didn't ask (although, I wish I did). It seemed like a cool concept. Maybe we were all in a experiment that we were unaware about. Who knows. 

For drinks, I opted for a Cucumber Soda (Jasmine, Anise Seed, Dill Seed, Fennel Seed and Lime) since I have never heard of such concoction. My friend opted for the Cranberry Soda. They actually handcraft these drinks right in front of you. I actually saw the barista peeling some orange zest by hand for my friend's drink. Talk about dedication! The drinks were so GOOOD and refreshing! You have to try their sodas!! You have not lived if you have not tried it! I'm actually craving them as I am writing this review. That is how good they were! I definitely have to give props to the barista!

For entrees, I decided to get the Classic Board and my friend got the Lower Sunny Side. They both came at the same time! Although the portions may not seem that big, they fill you up (well, for us at least). The entrees were really good, but the sodas definitely were the stars. Definitely coming back for those!

Overall, solid place for brunch and you MUST get the sodas. It is not optional!

I cannot wait to come back here. My friend and I showed up around 10 am and for a party of two the wait was about ten minutes. Afterwards, more and more people started showing up so the earlier you get there the better for sure. 

We both ordered coffee (had to wake up super early and travel from the UWS to beat the crowd) and it had unlimited refills woooo!

The lower sunny side was amazing. The latkes made you think of your grandma's cooking. The eggs were perfect. And wow the salmon was to die for. It was cut thin and was delicious. You see the guy preparing and cutting all of the different smoked salmons which is cool. I saw people eating the platters which looked great for parties of 3 or 4! Definitely will be coming back again

Tremendous! The place for lox and bagels.  4 stars but they deserve 2 bc of service.  Food is amazing.  Service they can fix, so no sense trashing the restaurant. 

Here is the deal.  The wait is oppressive.  It is made worse because you are told a table will be ready in 90 min, so off you go to have a drink or two, see the neighborhood and return.  Only to find, noooooooo, it'll be another 20min.  For us that extra 20 was wishful thinking.  We waited 2.5 hrs.  Another couple, and i quote:  "you should be ashamed of yourselves."  Next twosome asked to see the mgr.  And so it went.  Not once.  Not twice, but every single party coming in had been told an incorrect wait time.  Suggestion:  either be honest or take brunch rezzies.  Would be better if you said 3hr wait.  Stupid way to wreck a restaurant rep when your food is so good. Hostesses admitted it was their fault and they are super nice and sweet.  Felt badly for them - but r&d you are mucking up people's schedules unnecessarily.  A 1000 other NYC restaurants figured this out ...

So proud of these guys.. We went to the cafe this weekend and it was amazing..  They are classic New York that some how is very current and very good..  The design is beautiful..It is very bright and clean with marble accents and these classic herringbone floors.  Waitstaff is dressed in white jackets and ties.  It's just beautiful.. 
 
The two of us arrived around 9:30 on a Saturday.. There was a slight wait but, we sat right away at their community table..We at a table with three other people.. They seemed nice.. I over heard the funniest conversation..  Old "New Yorky" father was talking about how you can't dance at some bars.. And he was retelling a story about how he was listening to a favorite song of his at the bar and was "moving to the music" when a bouncer asked him to stop dancing.. His wife added with her NPR voice "Wow, that is strange as you are such a beautiful and restrained dancer"   Now all I could picture was this old heavy dude dancing so beautifully and restrained.. But, anyway.. 
 
The menu is fun.. You can go in a few directions.. You can get eggs, you can get 80 dollar platters of fish for the table, you can get some sandwiches a few appetizers.. While, I must say, I was slightly offended by some of the names of the food.. Not the way people get fake offended and then shout it from the roof tops more like , "eh, I would have chosen better names"   The heebster didn't sit well with me.. I get it, it's self effacing or joking but, it's not my kind of joking.. Someone calls me a heeb, we aren't going to be splitting a sandwich anytime soon.  The Yom Kippured, eh, not that cute.. 
 
 
We decided on the Herring Plate.. It was Fan Freaking Tastic..  Like outrageous.. The best roll mops I have ever had.. They offered a trio of sauces.. There was a curry and some other bullshit.. We stayed with cream and get another one on the side..   The served with black bread but, we asked for matzah and I feel like it was a much better experience..   
 
The fish was so good though.. I reminded me of eating mackeral at the best sushi restaurant in NYC. 

 
We also had chopped liver. Flavor was super on point.   It's like Sammy's without the crispy onions.. pickled onions they serve along sidee are so freaking good too:
 
Our view from our seat was of this man just slicing fish all day.. He had such skill, the fish was so thin and windowpained, we had to try this salmon.. While the majority of their fish is from Acme, their gravlax is specifically not.. We went with this served with a bialy and cream cheese
 
This was the best cut piece of fish I have ever had.. It was so beautiful.. Just truly a beautiful thing
 
I loved my experience here and will be coming back regularly.. Hope to have dessert next time..

This was among the highlights of my recent NYC binge! I had the Lox platter and my first Egg Cream, and I highly recommend both. I'll definitely be back to try pretty much everything on the menu. The space is charming, and service was flawless.

My fiancé and I had heard good things about the Russ & Daughters shop, but opted to go to the Cafe for a more sit-down experience on our first morning in the Big Apple.  Everything was delicious, and I think it was a great introduction to some classic NYC cuisine!

We came on a Friday around 11:00 am, and were quoted a 30-45 minute wait.  They had a convenient text message notification system, so we left to grab a cup of coffee while we waited for our table.  We actually got called back about 20 minutes later, and were pleased to not have to dispose of our outside beverages when seated.  Maybe this is more of an annoying LA thing.

We were tempted by the crazy Soft Scrambled Eggs and Caviar, but ended up choosing some more conservative dishes.  I got the Lower Sunny Side: potato latkes, sunny side up eggs, and smoked salmon.  At first I was a little concerned about the single (albeit large) slice of smoked salmon, but it was definitely a big enough portion for me.  For some reason, the thinner slice of salmon seemed to make its flavor stand out more.  I also haven't had many latkes in my life, but I thought these were excellent -- super crunchy and flavorful with onions inside as well.  I loved the combination of textures!

My fiancé got the Yum Kippered, a board with a bagel, baked salmon, and the typical fixins.  Again, I was a little worried about the portion size for him, but we both left feeling stuffed and happy.  He also tried one of the specialty bloody marys -- the one with the smoked vodka.  He liked it, but it was too spicy for my taste.

I'm definitely keeping this place on my to-eat list for the next time I visit New York.  I really want to try some of the sweeter dishes, especially the Kugel.

My friend and I finally check this off our bucket list! This Russ & Daughters venue is fairly new, graphic and overall branding is terrific, as well as the general atmosphere of the place, with servers in white jackets, and products names on the bar/ceiling. 

Today is Sunday and the wait seemed too long. We arrived at 11:30 a.m. and the hostess told us 2 hrs.. We were like "no way, we resist 1 hour around and that's it." We got a coffee, came back after 45 minutes and two seats were available! 

We seated at the bar, and the two waiters was very helpful w/ suggestions and explanations.

I loved my potato latkes. Perfect rich latkes with creme fraiche and salmon roe. Delicious!!

Expecting a long wait!! Wait time usually from 45mins to 2hrs+. I came here for few times and the line was insane. Every time I was too hungry to wait then I end up going somewhere else. Finally one time my friends visiting from Asia wanted to go, we waited for 40mins. 
Must order anything with smoked salmon, it is what they well known for. I had The Classic Board, it came with bagel, cream cheese, onions, tomatoes and few slices of smoked salmon for $16. No doubt it's a tasty bagel, but the price is at the higher range. I can crossed out Russ & Daughter from my foodie list and not necessary to go back again.

Absolutely incredible. I had heard nothing but good things about Russ & Daughters (shop and cafe both) and the cafe not only met up to the hype, but exceeded it. I went alone, so I sat at the bar, and the service was attentive and friendly. I had no trouble ordering and my order came out in under 10 minutes, which was a pleasant surprise. The food - oh my God, the food. I had the classic board and it might have been my favorite meal I've ever had in NYC. The salmon melts in your mouth, the cream cheese has the perfect taste, the everything bagel is to die for, the garnishes are wonderful, and the wooden board it's served on is adorable. The coffee is also nice and complements the meal well in my opinion. I could go on for days about the Russ & Daughters cafe, and if I could give it 6, 10, or even 100 stars, I most certainly would!

It is so good that after going only last night for dinner, I already am plotting if/when I can go back again this weekend!

Definitely come hungry and try the "sampler" platters of everything. They say they feed 3-4 people, but I think an ambitious two could easily handle all of the food.

The fish is amazing. The bread is fresh and delicious. And the latkes are a must.

I cannot wait till I return again! PS, who doesn't like a good cocktail with smoked fish???

My mom and I had a great time here. We arrived for an early dinner on Saturday at around 5:30 and were seated immediately. 
She had whitefish soup with matzo and pickled herring that came with boiled potatoes, marinated onions and a shot of vodka (classic 5:30 in the afternoon snack). She was very happy with everything.
I got borscht that came with sour cream and pumpernickel bagel and the Classic board (nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, red onion, tomato, capers, and a choice of bagel or bread). The borscht was delicious and also vegetarian. The bagel that it came with was perfect. The board was spot on, the salmon is very rich and fresh. They slice it right there and then. 
Their bloody Marys are great too, I'd recommend the dill vodka that gets a bit of brine with it. 
Oh, and friendly service as well as very comfortable atmosphere!

I've first heard about this place via some article about great lox bagels in NYC so this place has been on my bookmarks for the longest! One morning I was around the area, my friend suggested that we should have brunch at Russ and Daughters. I associated this place with bagels but I wasn't in the mood for a bagel but I went with it anyways.  

We walked in and left our name and number, then we got quoted a 20 minute wait. The waiting time was on point because we got seated shortly after that.  I checked out their menu while waiting and still couldn't figure out what to order at the table. There was a nice variety of small plate starters, soups, caviar, sandwich boards, salads, fishes, eggs and sweet dishes. 

The bar had classic black & white signs with an old soda fountain bar. It gave me a nice old school delicatessen vibe. The staff wore white lab coats. They start you off with a carafe of complimentary still or sparking water. I wasn't sure which dishes were considered appetizers and which would be suitable for main entrees so I just had them all at once. 

FOOD: 

Fish Chowder: creamy, rich with a fair amount of fish chunks and matzo. It was really good but not amazing. 

Potato Latkes: three potato cakes with some salmon roe and sour cream. This was my first time having potato latkes but I wasn't impressed. It's over-hyped or it was just that day. There were too many onion in one latkes, the inside was too soft for my liking and the potatoes weren't starchy enough. I had one latkes and it was already very heavy. I only enjoyed the salmon roe part of this dish. 

Pastrami Russ: a good portion of pastrami salmon, cheese, sauerkraut, mustard, and pickles in a mini pretzel roll with a side of waffle-cut chips and a few pieces of pickles. I wasn't feeling bread that morning but the pastrami-cured salmon itself was really good though, with more of a pastrami taste than fish. 

Hot & Cold Smoke: A jar of kippered salmon mixed with a smoked salmon spread topped with chives with a side of waffle-cut chips. Must try! It was my favorite dish out of everything. It was fresh and perfectly seasoned. There's enough to place a generous amount on each chip. 

Babka French Toast: not your typical fluffy french toast, made with chocolate babka with a side of sour cream and topped with fresh strawberries and powdered sugar. This was also my favorite, I wanted to savor each bite of chocolate goodness! 

I thought about getting the matzo ball soup, "The Classic", some ossetra caviar  and Lower Sunny Side too but next time! 

At the end of the meal, they present the check with a piece of coffee candy which I am obsessed with! I asked them for extra before leaving. Can someone please tell me where to buy this amazing candy!?!?

The staff was friendly. Overall, a wonderful experience mainly because of my company and the food. I would definitely be back but not if it's more than a 30 minute wait.
Just like your bubbe used to make

I would eat here every day if I could, if you love lox this is a must! The drinks are delicious too, unfortunately my favorite person to eat with (my husband) can't stand salmon, I promise he makes up for it but again if you like loxs at all this is the spot!

My friend had been promising me for months that Russ & Daughters Cafe made a fantastic bloody mary, served outside of brunch hours. 

Cue a rainy Saturday night. That's when y'all think of drinking bloodys, right?

The place is terribly charming. I forgave the bartender's elaborate hipster mustache because he, too, was terribly charming. 

The bloody marys were great. I tried three of the four varieties available (the fenugreek one is closest to a traditional). While I'm always a proponent of a smoky bloody, I preferred the one with caraway and rye croutons skewered on top with cornichons. Each sip gives you a little tinge of delightful caraway, an underrated seed that we all should be looking for excuses to consume more of. 

The food is, obviously, fantastic. Russ & Daughters has been slinging lox on the LES for over a century. How could they be anything but the best? 

I'm not Jewish, but maybe as someone who grew up in NYC and sang the dreidel song during Hannukah as a kid, everything else rang as truly comforting, from the warm diner feel to the smoked fish and egg concoctions all over the menu. On a Lower East Side Saturday night, when Recent Grads from the rest of America attempt an early-twenties version of the Carrie Bradshaw life, Russ & Daughters was quiet and warmly lit. We sat at the bar, noshed on kippered salmon, and closed the place out.

Worth a hours-long wait at brunch? I'll leave that up to the aforementioned Recent Grads, brunch-frenzied as they are. But on a weekend evening (when the menu is exactly the same), this place was lovely. Worth returning to again and again.

Had a delightful late breakfast here one weekday, so didn't have to wait too long.  Expected to love my classic board, had high hopes for the latkes, was curious about the chocolate babka french toast and interested to try the house sodas.  Nothing disappointed.

Don't come here if you don't like smoked fish. Only one item doesn't have that I believe. I don't eat it personally but those with me were really into it. BEST CHOPPED CHICKEN LIVER I've ever had and I scope it out. Nothing bitter or weird tasting about it, and if you don't like that dish at other places that doesn't mean you won't love it here. To be honest it was better than most high end patê I've had. The pickles were not that impressive to me personally, but maybe I was expecting a sweeter taste and they were very salty and very bitter. 
Side note: very great coffee for no good reason. 
Our server was a good looking soho type guy, so with that was the jaded and slightly condescending too cool for school attitude. Everyone else was nice though, but he was odd enough for the whole table to notice. 

All in all a great place filling a great niche. I hope it doesn't become another hip bs place with rude waiters and bougie clientele because this place is on its way to being a NYC institution (much like the store).

Fantastic brunch. I put my name down at 11:45am on a Saturday while waiting for my friends to get into town. They told me the wait will be 2-2.5 hours. Got a text at 1:10pm, so just under 1.5 hours. Not too bad. I'm guessing a lot of people drop off.

The food was fantastic and the service was good. They don't rush you either. The booths are comfortable. Loved the smoked white fish dish the best. Chopped chicken liver pate is not bad either.

Had to get a smoked salmon bagel while I was in New York! Yelped and researched the best smoked salmon bagel store to go to and concluded to come here and it was a good selection! I yelped other Russ & Daughters locations and thought this would be a to-go type of deal but it was actually a sit-down restaurant.. an actual cafe. The other Russ and Daughters that I saw on Yelp was just a bagel store with a variety of bagels and different cream cheese behind a glass you could choose from. I was kind of expecting that but came here and realized it was a restaurant. The restaurant has its pros in which they have the platter which looks visually pleasing on a board and all the ingredients separated out. I would have imagined the non-restaurant version of Russ & Daughters to have more variety of bagels and different types of toppings and flavors of cream cheese. 

The smoked salmon itself was really yummy. It wasn't super salty and it was very soft and almost melted in your mouth. The cream cheese it comes with is just the normal regular cream cheese. Kind of wished there were more options of cream cheese to choose from but the regular cream cheese was sufficient!

Sturgeon is one of the most delicious things on the menu. Smoked salmon is like most smoked salmon, kind of blé even though the quality is higher than most smoked salmon. Bagel is just as delicious as their original shop and the price is high but you pay for the atmosphere that is very lovely.

Came across this little spot after a sweltering yoga class and was famished.  Decided to check it out and ordered the knishes and borscht...soooo good! I haven't had a knish since my college days, many moons ago and it was so much better than what I remember.  The borscht was the first time trying and it was just as delicious!  Also got to try their coffee soda, it was interesting to say the least yet i enjoyed it. 

Next time I'm going to try their mushroom barley soup and the potato latkes which seem to be popular as well by the patrons who were there that day.

FISHYyyyyy Love !!!

If you are in NYC and water to eat the best salmon with bagel and cream cheese do visit Russ & Daughters Cafe.
 Besides the salmon , what's really yummy is the Sturgeon eggs & onions.
The icing on the cake was their Jewish desert - Babka French Toast : chocolate Babka, is rolled into a French toast, topped with strawberry & sugar and served with sour cream on the side...Ul love every every bite :)

"First time for everything."

First positive review and first time being here. Very rarely do I eat at restaurants that make me close my eyes and roll them to the back of my head with a taste bud explosion of enjoyment (aka T.B.E.O.E). 
Russ and Daughters took me there. 

I ordered the classic board, classically. This is the best bagel and nova smoked salmon I have ever had. Even the bagel did not disappoint. It some how seemed to stay warm the entire meal. However the salmon is what I would go back for again and again. When I closed my eyes I would flashback to a memory I had of fishing with my grandma for salmon in the most remote parts of the Pacific Northwest when I was a kid. Portal food. 

The overall atmosphere was very nice, it was casual although I felt fancy. 

Only pet peeve I had was the waiter called me "bro." I'm not your bro, bro.

Enjoy all your favorites from the original Russ & Daughters, in a comfortable, sit down environment. The best smoked fish you're going to find in NYC, but you probably already know that. A New York institution just got better.

I was so happy when I learned Russ & Daughters had opened a sit-down full service restaurant. Since my first visit I've noticed changes to their menu but they're welcome additions. Anything that is primarily smoked fish is amazing. 

NOTE: YOUR ORDER MUST HAVE SMOKED FISH!

Old-fashioned diner setting and service was always attentive and pleasant. Walls are adorned with pictures of Russ and daughter and booths are comfortable. 

Desserts are interesting and very good!
Came here on Monday morning , it opened at 10am. Had the sunny side eggs - came with huge portion of salmon. Great coffee . Good service

Walked in and it brought me straight to Saturdays at grandma's house. The smells were equal to the authenticity of the flavors. High quality ingredients perfectly crafted in an environment that gently time warps. I will be back! The salmon spread was delectable. My fellow diner enjoyed her bagel.

I visited Russ & Daughters following a recommendation from a friend of mine who said they serve the best breakie in NYC. We arrived there a little before close and were promptly seated and provided with water. The menu offers an extensive array of cured fish and caviar and despite the fact I'm not a huge seafood fan, there were several appetizing offerings. 

Initially our group of 4 were each going to get the classic salmon bagel, however we were convinced by our waitress to split a platter instead. That recommendation turned out to be brilliant, as we were able to try 4 different types of salmon including the pastrami and gravalox varieties which were standouts. We matched the salmon with various breads and pickled vegetables which complemented the smokey fish beautifully. The food was extremely fresh and nicely presented - I can't emphasize enough how good this platter was!

I'd definitely recommend anyone who even slightly enjoys smoked fish to come by and check this place out. A great operation with fantastic staff who were polite and friendly!

I wanted to eat a good breakfast before my flight out of NYC, so I decided on a place close to my hotel, especially since it was raining.

Food:
I ordered the classic board, which came with smoked salmon, capers, cream cheese, onion, tomato, and a bagel.

You're given all the ingredients to build your own breakfast.

Very tasty!  Don't come super hungry because this meal won't fill you up.

Sides Notes

Ambiance:
There's lots of bar seating.

Service:
Waiter was friendly.

Overall:
If you're looking for a good breakfast that won't feel heavy, try this place!

Arrived at 10:25 on a Saturday morning, which was the wrong time since they only open at 10.  Had to wait until the first seating started to leave.  Fortunately two bar stools became open after about 30 minutes. 

Began with beet and cherry shrubs.  These were nice alternative drink options. The beet shrub was very tart, like a limeade.  The cherry could have been more tart; it was a little too sweet for me.  

Began with the herring platter, which consisted for four types of fish: 1. pickled herring, 2. "maki" herring; 3. schmaltz; and 4 one that tasted cinnamon-y.  The picked herring was very good.  The fish was firm and the pickling was perfect - not too sweet or tart.  The "maki" rolls were even better.  The fish was fantastic and the flavor just right.  The onions (which weren't pickled) went really well with these, adding interesting flavor depth.  The schmaltz is salty, however that makes it a good choice of eating with the three sauces - creme fraiche, curry and honey mustard.  We didn't care for the cinnamon one.  there were about 4 one inch pieces of each of the four types of fish. 

The other item was the Classic Board, of nova smoked salmon, an everything bagel, cream cheese, tomato, red onion and capers.  The bagel was outstanding - the best bagel I've ever had.  The cream cheese was smooth and not too tangy or thick and clumpy.  The salmon was good and had a nice smokiness. 

The service was friendly and fairly efficient.  Looking forward to coming back to try the latkes and knishes next time - they looked delicious.
Amazing place really old school look and really clean, great food really well executed and prices are ok for what your getting,

On a Sunday morning my friend & I headed there at around 11:30 only to find out the wait would be around 1.5 hours. We were pretty prepared for this news, and expected no less for a trendy, well-reviewed brunch place. Our wait-time went by pretty fast as we grabbed a cup of coffee from WhyNot (good study café with fun music and the surliest baristas) a few doors down. 
Although not the most adventurous order, we both ordered the classic board - which included lox, onion, tomato, capers, cream cheese, and your choice of bagel. (Not going to lie, after Sadelle's unlimited bagels I was kind of disappointed I had to limit my bagel choice to just one - but really I should be thanking them for letting me not eat more than one bagel in a single sitting). We also split the Potato Knishes to start.
Knishes: warm, doughy, and delicious. These were a great app. Accompanied with Dijon mustard to give the bite just enough kick.
Board: there's no doubt Russ & Daughters serves fantastic smoked salmon. In fact, it's likely that I haven't had better. But to be totally honest, the bagel & accompaniments were nothing special. Maybe it was the hour plus wait, or the fact that Jake Gyllenhal actually walked by the table when I had my head down, face devouring the lox, but my overall meal here kind of disappointed. The bagel was just okay - a little too tough, not warm enough. The cream cheese was fantastic, very tasty, but yet again was something I had tasted previously at home. All the accompaniments were things I could have easily whipped up at home. Funny thing was, after waiting over 1.5 hours to get a seat, we were done our whole experience in about 35 minutes! Russ & Daughters, you serve great lox. But your wait for sub-par bagels and tomatoes isn't enough to entice me to see you again...unless you can guarantee a Jake sighting (picture included).

After trying Russ and Daughter take out place on Houston street we decided to try to the sit down restaurant (called cafe) on Orchard. Similar to the first, the quality is excellent. I got the classic board with salmon, cream cheese, onion, caper, tomato, and bagel of my choice (the choice was not as large as at the take out). Loved it. The cream cheese is whipped and the salmon is buttery and no too salty. The wife tried matzo ball soup for the first time and loved it. Then she got the whitefish bagel toast which is smoked whitefish salad on a bagel that is shaped like toast. Also excellent. The service was professional and efficient. They have very tasty bagels and no one prepares fish better than Russ. This place is a winner!

I truly believe if you visit NYC and don't eat here, you'd be missing out on a unique dining experience. I've been here countless times since the cafe opened, and after each visit I want to update my review to help you get the most out of eating here--and maybe most importantly getting in to the place without a wait of one to two hours--if you expect to have lunch here. It's always crowded, especially on weekends when the visitors come to the Lower East Side seeking nostalgia. 
The reason they come here is because there's nothing else like Russ & Daughters Cafe in the city. About two years old, it feels like it has been an Orchard Street presence since the days the street epitomized the Jewish Lower East Side, with its shops and peddlers. This cafe is brilliantly conceptualized, using a decor that evokes an earlier time by borrowing details from the original and busier than ever retail store on Houston Street. The porcelain cabinets and trim, the graphics and even the signage look like they were installed in 1900. 
You come here for the smoked baked and pickled seafood. I recommend the herring and kippered salmon. There's also the whitefish. The beet borscht is the best I've ever had. It's not watery, but almost a purée. I've never had a better Bloody Mary. They have several variations, I recommend the one with caraway seeds. I haven't tried it, but my dining guests have raved about the chopped chicken liver. There was a time when every Jewish neighborhood had a restaurant that served what was called "appetizing" dishes. They were mainly dairy and fish places, no meat, because they were kosher. This cafe takes some dietary liberties, and the result is better than what you could get from the era it evokes. They also have a full bar. They also offer egg creams. 
A couple of practical points. Don't think you can stop in on a weekend for lunch. Unless you get there well before noon, expect a two hour wait to be seated. They don't take reservations for lunch, except (and I'm not sure about this) if you're a large group. I know we were able to make reservations for dinner. That's the time to come here. The food is the same, and the place is pretty empty after 6. Check their hours before you go, but they're open until 10 on weekends.
Service also gets five stars. It's efficient and they'll modify your orders if you request.

Had dinner here tonight. Enjoyed everything especially the potato latkes. 
Service and atmosphere were good too. Highly recommend.

No wait for 2 on a Tuesday morning, got to sit at the counter too!

Chopped liver is the right amount of creamy and spreadable enough to stick to matzah, rye bread, and bagel crisps. 

Brother enjoyed his "hot smoke/cold smoke" fish spread with bagel crisps. Also, liked whitefish soup. 

Kasha varnishkas had more kasha than bow tie pasta which I would've enjoyed more, good flavor though.

Chocolate egg cream needed more seltzer for fizz. Love that still and seltzer water is on tap. 

Would love to try bagels next time.

The classic is slightly better than your typical lox, cream cheese, and bagel with all the fixings, but twice as expensive. And we're not talking about slightly better than other New York ones. We're talking about all over. Not something to write home about.

I'd Gove the herring a try if you've never been to Amsterdam, but obviously it's not as good.

"Would you like your latkes or your blintzes to come out first?"- Is in the top ten questions I've ever been asked.  Russ & Daughters was outstanding.  After about a 45minute wait, we were seated and served immediately and everything perfect from that point on.  We started with egg creams, juices, coffee, and cream sodas along with the aforementioned latkes ands blintzes.  Then we each ordered one of the bagel boards, traditional lox for me, sable and goat cheese spread for my friend.  So bagels and smoked fish are forever ruined for this midwestern girl because of how freaking good this place is. This was too much food and drink for 2 people, but its also the only thing we ate until dinner that night, so live a little.

This place is the bee's knees. Everything is so beautiful - from the decor to the food. Definitely get a bagel board to try!!!!! It will be like discovering and falling in love with bagels all over again. Also tried the knishes (potatoey goodness) and halvah ice cream (AMAZING AND STILL THINKING ABOUT IT).

Everything we ordered was fresh and the smoked fish is amazing.  Portions are just perfect.  The potato latkes were tasty.  

The service was good and the recommendations were on point.

Ross & Daughers, wonderfully kitch and classic, produces fine Eastern European inspired noshes (small dishes, try the kinishes), platters, herrings and eggs. 

I started the journey with a dill infused Bloody Mary. Next, schmaltz herring with onion and a healthy shot of breakfast vodka.  Salty, smoked divinity.

My main was sunny side eggs with salmon and potato latkes.  I washed it down with an Egg Cream Soda - chocolate with Fox's U-bet chocolate syrup.

I had no room for dessert but ordered the sublime Babka Frech toast and Halvah ice cream with salted caramel anyway. 

I love my Eastern European inspired food and this NYC establishment certainly did impress

1 hour 30 minute wait time for Saturday brunch. I would suggest putting your name down and exploring cute coffee shops around the area. The waiting area was a bit crowded. We ordered potato latke (you can choose savory or sweet), eggs Benny, and lox, onions, and eggs. The food came out quickly and the salmon was really fresh. Be warned that the salmon that comes with potato latke has a really fishy taste. I like seafood but would not recommend to people who doesn't like that smell. Giving it 4 stars because of the price and the wait time.

It's Russ and Daughters. Five stars doesn't praise them enough. There's something about the way they do their salmon that I just can't begrudge them the long wait.
Even getting here when they open you'll encounter a wait but it's totally worth it. The Ida platter feeds more than 3-4 and that's including someone who shamelessly piles her salmon high. The platter comes with a bread basket, which has a sesame bagel, bialy, rye, pumpernickel, and challah. The Ida has: Scottish, Gaspe nova, pastrami, and Gravlax. A little fun fact: 
Lox is filleted salmon belly cured in a salt brine whereas gravlax is salt, sugar, & dill. Smoked salmon uses any part of the salmon, can be hot or cold smoked, and cured in a salt brine. All of the smoked salmon at Russ and Daughters is cold smoked, expect for their kippered salmon. 
I definitely recommend the hot smoke/cold smoke dip but be warned those everything bagel chips are too tiny for the dip. Instead, I spread some of the dip onto my bagel, added my salmon, then topped off my bagel with cream cheese. Maybe it's a bit much but who can resist smoked salmon?

I love me some nova. I ordered the classic with pumpernickel. Food was fresh, Bloody Mary was delicious. Nothing about this place is my idea of ground breaking, but the quality of the place makes it worth it. Will be back again, unless there's another hour wait!
Delicious smoked salmon varieties to choose from. Does take a while when it's busy but well worth it. Just make sure to grab a number on your way in.

Food gets five stars.  Smoked fish as good as it gets.  Although it's not on the menu, I love the whitefish board (not the whitefish salad, which is fine).  Nova is top-notch.  Service is friendly, albeit a little harried.  Loss of one star due to the extremely long wait.  It's still worth it.

Just because the service was surprisingly disappointing the last time. In brief, the plate I ordered contained much less salmon than usual and I kindly said it to the waitress and she replied that this isn't true because they weigh it first. I was still surprised that she wanted to tell me that they have this level of precision, when it was OBVIOUS that there was much less salmon in my plate. So, I asked what's the weight and she replied 2.9 ounces. Who of you are now laughing...because this is a ridiculously improbable and also low number for a salmon plate! She also offered to verify it and she took my plate. Then another waiter comes with my plate and says that it was correctly weighed, but they would complement me with some more to satisfy their client....and they bring a tiiiiiiny (really tiny!) piece of complementary plain salmon on another plate. Better not to bring it or bring a normal slice! It was clearly a joke. And I was surprised with the shameless greedy un-professionalism they've come to adopt, especially when I thought they were true professionals.

I won't return there any time soon. Thank you.

High quality smoked salmon, sturgeon, excellent pickles, all the good old Yiddish bubby food with great service in a retro fifties high end deli
A real gem
A bit pricey for breakfast but it's worth it. The salmon, bagels, and other breads they offer are amazing. The challah bread that they serve with the eggs Benny is amazing.

Possibly my favorite restaurant in the city. Perfect mix of a modern restaurant that still manages to fit in with the history of the neighborhood and their original counter location. 

Of course all the smoked fish is perfect and the bagels are surprisingly good. Also highly recommend their bloody Mary's. This place never gets old!
When my great grandparents traveled in steerage from Eastern Europe I'm sure that they always imagined their descents would be spending over $30 on herring and kugel.

It would be a 5 Star if the bagels were good.  

We got the lox platter with 4 different types of lox.  Everything was amazing.  I then went to the take out location on Houston and bought a ton of stuff to take with me home (on a plane).  Tell them you want it packaged for a plane and they'll hook it up.

This place is awesome, but extremely expensive (and worth it).

Best lox ever, hands down!

We went in on a Friday for brunch and we were told it would be a 40 minute wait. There's a Starbucks a couple stores down so the wait seemed short and the hostess was friendly and texted us when our table was ready. The cafe was pleasantly busy and the 1900s themed decor, music, and staff uniforms gave a cool and charming vibe. We ordered the Egg Benny and The Classic with everything bagel. The Egg Benny was delicious with delicate salmon, perfectly poached eggs, and soft bread. The Classic's cream cheese was on the lighter side and when everything on the board was combined it tasted great. Both dishes were under $20 each, asthetically simple and pretty, and came in reasonable proportions. I definitely recommend this place!

AMAZING!!!!! Homemade bagels. House cured lox and shmears. And you have about 6 different types or more of cuts of fish/curing method/seasoning and everything from caviar cream cheese to goat cream cheese. This place has ruined me forever. Amazing!!

I'm sure it's delicious but "good for groups"??  Can't even accommodate more than 4 people. How is that good for groups?  Have out of town guests with kids and now we are stranded on the sidewalk having to come up with plan b. Thanks...

Came for brunch at 11AM this morning, no wait at all, and waiters made sure to not keep as waiting whether it be for drinks or food. We started with an appetizer called Pastrami Russ which was FABULOUS. If you are a lover of salmon in a bagel, this will be the best appetizer you've had at brunch. If they made it a bigger version I would recommend this as an entree. For main dish I ordered an Eggs Benny since it's a go-to but it was such a unique eggs benny. The bread was so think and baked so well that if I just ate the bread alone I would compliment this place just the same. The smoked salmon was so nice and thick (even on the Pastrami Russ). My friend ordered Lower Sunny Side (scrambled) and it looked amazing as well. Would definitely come back in the next month or so! Sidenote: I like that there isn't normally a long wait time for brunch because there are so many two-person tables so it's quick.

It was really busy in here, and we only had to wait 5 minutes. The salmon here tasted so fresh and delicious. We had it on a bagel and also in an eggs Benedict style. Both were great and very well portioned! My girlfriend really enjoyed the candy that they give you when you get the check too.

Not worth the one hour wait.  So after waiting 1 hour (during which time my daughter got her eyebrows threaded) and getting a text message, we went back to the restaurant.  Only the counter seats were available.  Normally, I wouldn't mind the counter table, however it was so crowded that people waiting for tables were on top of me while I ate.  I found the matzo ball soup to be too salty.  The bagel with sable was not the best in the world.  The knishes were ok.  I did enjoy the pickled sour tomatoes, carrots and pickles.  Good pickles.  Just go to Russ and Daughters market to get the pickles next time.

I wish Russ would adopt me and maybe the name could be changed to Russ and Daughters and Son because let me tell you I would sacrifice a lot of things (kosher and not kosher if you know what I'm sayin) in order to have the bagel and lox every day. 

But seriously this is a Jewish deli established in the early 1900s and you can tell that they have perfected their art. I had the Daughters Delight -everything bagel with scallion cream cheese, gaspe nova lox, and salmon roe. Culinary bliss was happening in my mouth after every bite and not overly salty even though I read some reviews that noted that.
