They also have a dairy-free option for cream cheese which is a tofu cream cheese. In all honesty, it fooled me. Pretty gosh darn good. I would also recommend their pastrami lox. It gives you the spice flavor profile of pastrami with the lightness of the salmon.k

I had high expectations for this place and most of them were met. The old-fashioned soda fountain and waitstaff in white coats makes this place super cool aesthetically. You feel like you're grabbing midway lunch out of an episode of Mad Men. 

I got a good lunch starting with the latkes and noodle kugel (both really good). Latkes were huge and came with three & the kugel was perfectly-portioned for one and not too sweet. 

I also had the smoked salmon bagel platter but they accidentally brought me out pumpernickel instead of the everything bagel I ordered and I ended up liking that BETTER than the bagel. Only downside would be - the chocolate egg cream was flat :(

Russ,  can I be one of your daughters? I promise to do all the chores in the house.

The three of us came here around 8:30pm after happy hour and enjoyed our late dinner a little way too much. We ordered The Classic with an everything bagel, the pastrami russ appetizer, and an order of latkes.

The Classic - 5 stars. Came with a bagel, some cream cheese, and a few slices of smoked salmon, tomatoes, and onions. Put them all together and you've got yourself a delicious sandwich.

The pastrami russ - 4 stars. It's pastrami crusted smoked salmon and sauerkraut inbetween a mini plain bagel and served with a side salad. This was a little too salty for me with the smoked salmon AND salty sauerkraut. But still tasty nonetheless.

Latkes - 5 stars. So crispy and light! Who doesn't like fried potatoes? There are like flat round hashbrowns fried to crispy perfection. We chose to have these with sour cream and apple sauce since everything else was more on the salty side. We did not regret this decision and was the perfect end of the meal.

Our waiter showed great hospitality and helped us with any questions we had about the menu. Must visit whenever you're in NY!

Come here to try the superior and historic New York bagels. This recently opened cafe offers a great seating option while you enjoy your bagel and lox. 

We both ordered the classic bagel board. It came in a nice presentation of your choice of bagel, tomatoes, onions, cream cheese, capers, and slices of the famous smoked salmon itself. The salmon was perfectly smoked, thinly sliced, and not excessively salty. The everything bagel was full of garlicky goodness, but a bit too salty in some parts. You do have to build your own sandwich, and eating it can get a little messy. I do wish they had different cream cheese flavors. 

The decor of the restaurant combined old-fashioned styles with a modern flair. It feels as if you had stepped back in time, yet oddly still in the present. The waiters wear short white coats, like those of medical students. When you pay your bill, they give you a postcard as a nice touch. 

Great place for breakfast or light brunch. Don't expect to be full with just the bagel board if you want a full meal. We came on a weekday morning when wait was about 20-30 min. Highly recommended for anyone interested in trying bagels and lox. 4.5/5

I have a pickle to pick with this bagel joint disguising itself as a cute lunch spot. First off, we waited 2 hours to eat a bagel. A BAGEL. I'm from California and my mind is still blown to this day. 2 HOURS. 

I was starving by the time I got seated. They do give you complementary seltzer water, but that was the only redeeming quality of R&D.

I ordered a bagel to see what the hype was about. They barely gave me any fish the there was nothing special about it. They even charged my friend for extra cream cheese. We ended up paying 20 dollars for a bagel..I could have gone to Noah's bagel and been more satisfied.

This is a cafe version of russ and daughters that is very famous for its salmon lox.  At this cafe, they sell salmon lox that is sold on the store nearby, but also sell regular breakfast/lunch stuff.  One thing is that they are very popular, and you will have to wait for 1-2 hrs for brunch/lunch on the weekend.  

I have waited for one and a half hours before getting a table for three.  We ended up getting the platter which served 3 different kinds of lox w/ vegetable and bread.  Honestly speaking I didn't like it as much as lox bagel from the store, but was a still a good deal especially because you were able to taste different types of lox.  

If you really like to have dine in experience and are ok with waiting for a long time, try this place.  If you just want to have russ and daughters experience, I strongly recommend going to the store (2 blocks away) and grab a lox bagel.
The chopped salad was really tasty, and all the other dishes looked very appetizing too! Had a taste of my friend's latke and it was very good.

I lové this place, I often go there. The food is very high quality and i love it's history: 4th generation, father passing on his shop to his daughters after he started selling his fish on a cart in the LES. I like to go for dinner there s never a line whereas brunch is crazy

Excellent place. Bring your friends and visitors for a delicious Jewish food experience at Russ. Our shtetle sable plates where delicious and fresh. Tomatoes red onions and capers on the side. I coulda used a extra slice of sable. Ask for a table so you don't have to share the bench table with strangers. Only complaint was the price $50 for two bagel plates and two beverages.

No takeout at this location, and the solid much-IG'd babka ice cream sandwich isn't on the menu either. That said, solid cafe that was absolutely dead for weekday dinner (the 7/2014 NYT 2-star review long past), so we'll see if they collapse back to just the Houston St institution.

Does anyone know if any of Russ's daughters are single? Tell them that I'm a good Jewish boy and I'm dedicating my 100th review to them!

Two words: Pastrami Salmon. If that alone doesn't make your mouth water, don't come here. You know what else is incredible? The chopped liver served with matzo, as well as the matzo ball soup.  

Obviously the bagel and salmon platter are a must but in my opinion, the best item on the menu is the Halva ice cream... I can't describe to you how mind blowing it is. MUST TRY!

Thank you Russ, and your daughters. L'chaim!

Seating process is ridiculous.  They leave seats open for in excess of 15 minutes and then when folks don't show move down the list...sitting here watching no one seated at 3 places for the past 15 mins. No wonder they always quote an hour and half wait...

RUDE AND ARROGANT HOSTESSES. REALLY... I MEAN REALLY, I AM DISAPPOINTED. They don't respect or value customers and they do not accommodate for parties larger than four.  They have the "We are trendy and know we will get business attitude." If you calmly and kindly try to request that they split your party into two tables they will simply say "we don't do that." 

Do you know what I don't do? I don't spend my money where I am not welcome, and where I am basically thrown away as a prospective client. Talk about lame and unprofessional business practice. I am never going back there.

Oh, and we went to Katz delicatessen and had a blast. Thanks for indirectly sending us to a competitor of yours that is just around the block.

P.s- They have a six seated table and when I confronted the hostesses they rudely said "we are seating people there right now." I am not sure who you have to be to get a large table there but obviously my money and your money is not good enough for the snobs at Russ & Daughters. Go somewhere where you will be treated like a valued customer even if you go once.

My go to bagel joint when I'm in NY. This is definitely the one place I crave while on the west coast and it never fails to deliver the goods. The lox bagels are to die for but honestly the regular schmears are just as good.

Not gonna lie there have been moments where while visiting the east coast I've been tempted to drive into NY for these bagels. And as much as I love LA bagels, they don't come close to what this place offers.

It's a little pricey but lets be honest, you want good food you have to pay for it. And EVERYTHING in NY is super expensive. So if you're going to spend the money, why not spend it on something delicious. 

The lines can be long, finding seating can be tough but the taste is worth it.
We came on the weekend super early but the food took forever, and it just wasn't that great. Just a very normal breakfast place
Amazing!!! Such an iconic New York experience, we left so satisfied. The Matzo Ball soup and Classic Bagel Plate were so delicious. I can't wait to have it again. Service was lovely too.
Came for the famed bagel and lox and the place did not disappoint. Plates are a bit on the small and expensive side, but the atmosphere and service make up for it. Recommended!

Came for the babka ice cream sandwich, stayed for the herring sandwich. Gothamist got me with their tantalizing photos of the aforementioned ice cream treat so I assembled my squad (wife and brother) and phoned R & D original location to make sure they had enough in stock. Alas, they were almost out, so we headed to the cafe.

When we came in, between brunch and dinner time on a Sunday, it was very quiet here. They've got a throwback Jewish diner theme going with wait staff in labcoats that was a neat touch. Immediately my attention went to the rather steep prices, even by NYC LES standards, for nearly everything. But we were on a mission.

Before fulfilling our mission, I did order up a Dutch herring sandwich, served on a delicious brioche bun (the kind used in lobster rolls). My companion stared incredulously as I consumed an entire herring hero (all but the tail), then went to town on the ice cream sandwich: babka-flavored ice cream goodness between two babka buns. Awesome.

We are the third generation of Russ & Daughters customers. We have had happy memories involving their food over the years. This was my first visit to the cafe. The experience had a rocky start: we were 7 people and the largest table in the room seats six. We immediately offered to split into two smaller groups (three and four) and sit at separate tables. The hostess said that is against their policy because the two tables might be finished at different times. After a few minutes of waiting and negotiation, clearer heads prevailed and we were seated at two tables next to each other. Things improved greatly after we sat. We ordered a nova platter for the table of four. The wooden platter was a feast to view. Four types of nova, onions & tomatoes, olives, pickles, etc. with a bread/bagel basket. Everything was delicious (as you expect from Russ & Daughters). We talked and picked at the platter until all of the nova was finished. It was a great Manhattan lunch experience!

Repost of old review.

Picked by some food critics as one of the best new restaurants in NYC for 2016.
Easy to get a seat by the bar.
Enjoyed the lunch today:  Potato latkes with wild salmon roe & creme fraiche and Herring plate.
They also make unique sodas (tried the coffee soda and cranberry soda).

: 7 calendars

2pm on a Saturday and the insouciant hostess who was busy chewing and drinking herself informed us nonchalantly of the hour and fifteen minute wait.  Her attitude signaled that she could care less if we waited - note to owner - it won't always be peaches and cream with the adoring public willing to wait for a nosh that would have been a tenth of the price without the wait back in the day in the Bronx.  When told that we don't have text on our phone you would have thought that the hostess was experiencing an unpleasant bowel movement.  It seemed an insurmountable problem.  Well it was easily remedied as we went elsewhere.  Have eaten here once prior when first opened and a crowd was expected but now it's just not worth it.

The food is good but SO overpriced. Breakfast for 2 was $75 with tip! This was for two bagel and smoked fish "boards" + chopped liver + blintzes. Not a small amount but not $75. 

It's high quality, but we didn't order lobster and caviar.  We ordered Jewish deli food. 

And why are the bagels so small? 

Granted, if it was mind-blowing, it would have been maybe worth it. But this was standard, good food that's available in many spots in NYC. 

Service was also "just ok". Staff seems depressed. Not sure what the deal is. 

Place itself is cool inside. 

Would not return.

This place was so delicious, service was great and the owners (the 4th generation of the Russ and Daughters family!) perfectly combined the old and the new with the ambiance and menu selection. I had a meal from heaven- The "heebster"- a bagel-open faced sandwich- half with smoked salmon salad and half with white fish salad, adorned with cornichons,  the chopped liver with matzo and their home made ginger soda with lavender (!) which was a perfect compliment!
Hip, upscale and interesting Jewish cafe from the owners of the store by the same name. You don't have to be Jewish to love This place

The platters salmon options are pretty much what you would purchase at their deli on Houston. It.s phenomenal with all its accessories (capers, onions, cream cheese, tomatoes, bread options, pickles. It.s fantastic, good for 3-4 people. Chopped salad is great very filling. Chocolate egg cream is th best I.ve had anywhere. Bloody Maries are ok. Potato latkas are ok, I was hoping they were not hockey pucks but flatter and crispier. Nice renovation. SErvice is good. Food is nothing out of this world but it.s excellent.

The BEST lox bagel I've had (so far)! 

That is a pretty bold statement, but I just start to salivate when I think about this place!  The salmon just tastes so fresh and everything is balanced.  There is red onions, tomatoes, capers, cream cheese which is smooth and well creamy, garnished with fresh dill!  Must have it on the everything bagel too!  YUM!  I usually pair it with one (or two) of their House Bloody Marys, which are all delicious as well!  The dill one is very refreshing!

I also love the Potato Latkes with Salmon Roe (Ikura) and Creme Fraiche.  First of all the Latkes were great, not too oily, and good flavor.  Paired with the Roe and Creme...drool.  If you did order the lox then add some roe to it too!  

Their Eggs Benny was good too, but comes in third to the other two entrees. 

Staff is usually pretty attentive and nice.  I've never had to wait too long for a seat when I've gone on a weekday for lunch.  Weekends can be a different story.  

Overall, this place is a MUST for me in NYC!  NYC visit just doesn't seem complete without a bagel!

The rumors are true!

As a Seattleite, I'm not only really annoying about my coffee, I'm also really annoying about my salmon. And the lox here? Better than anything I've ever had before.

It was flavorful without overpowering the flavor of the fish. Served with a lightly toasted bagel, a good amount of capers, tomatoes and red onions (that have at least been soaked in water so they weren't overwhelmingly pungent), it was one hell of a lox bagel (albeit a steeply priced one at that).

Another highlight was the herring trio plate. I fell in love with herring a few years ago when I had it during an omakase meal. Last year, I had pickled herring from a cart in Amsterdam and decided that was even better than sushi. The pickled herring trio served on pumpernickel bread here is leaps and bounds better than my past experiences with herring. It showcased different pairings with the perfectly pickled herring. Again, delicately flavored without overwhelming the real taste of the fish.

Yes, the wait is ridiculous. Even on a Monday, there was a line before it opened. We were staying just across the street and ran over the moment it opened. We, along with everyone in line, were seated promptly. I would suggest putting your name down (and they will text you when your table is ready) for at least a couple of hours before you're starving if you decide to go on a weekend.

This is probably one of my favorite places for brunch in New York city, the menu is great and you feel like you want to order everything. The recipes are 102 years old and the taste is so great. I recommend to try the classic bagel with salmon nova lax and the blueberry and basil soda.

Ok there might be a lot of hype around this place but the food was legitimately amazing! Everything we ordered from the menu was fantastic. The matzoh ball soup, the latkes, the kasha varnishkas, the chopped liver. Everything! And the actual lox was the best I've ever had. As a New Yorker, I don't say this lightly. 

The only downside (and there's always a downside) is the wait. We came on a Monday for lunch and it was 45 minutes. From what I read there will always be a wait. I guess everyone else realized that this is the best lox in New York too.

We've been several more times since and unfortunately the food has been inconsistent. The brisket over mashed potatoes ($23) was heavenly and the cherry shrub ($6) wasn't bad, but the challah bread pudding ($9) was inedible last time: unevenly microwaved, with cold and hot spots throughout, and had an unpleasant mouthfeel. The soft scrambled eggs with paddlefish caviar ($50) was watery and too fishy, and the challah was dry and tasted old. The fishsticks ($11 for 3) were filled with ground-up overcooked fish rather than chunks or whole pieces of fish. And they burned our toasted bagel (and - as you probably already know - they don't even make their own bagels). On the bright side so far we have never experienced a wait, even for lunch on a weekday. It's back to H&H for this shiksa.

Russ & Daughters Cafe has easily become my favorite brunch spot in NYC. I am still thinking about that eggs benny because it was seriously that good. Besides the delicious food, the overall atmosphere and design of the cafe is top notch. Hiring designer Kelli Anderson was such a brilliant move because she did such an impressive job branding Russ & Daughters. Everything here, from menus to signage, is 100% Instagram-worthy. Maybe I'm being dramatic, but I genuinely felt like my entire brunch experience here was such a treat for not only my taste buds, but also all my other senses. 

The wait here is really not as awful as you may think. I'm convinced the staff intentionally overestimates the wait time. I was here at 11:30am on a Sunday (arguably prime brunch time). The waitress said my wait would be 1 hour and 40 minutes. I ended up getting seated within 40 minutes.
The chicken liver bought me back to my childhood.  Had the Classic Lox & bagel. Will definitely stop in again.
Food is great.  Get here early (before 9:30 AM  on weekends if you don't want to wait an hour to be seated).

This place is good and the service is good too. Seating on a Friday night for 2 was uncomplicated and we got seated promptly. We got the Hensch (sturgeon) and the herring plate. They were both delicious, except for one of the herring preparations. In retrospect, we should probably have ordered the classic, but regardless it was good.

In short:

Very,very long wait (100 minutes); as are all highly rated restaurants. No reservations. Perfect spot to take a date so you get to know each other really well, followed by a nice meal after your seat is finally available. 

The food is actually really good and almost justifies the wait. I'd give it 5 stars if we had went on a Weekday afternoon and only had a short wait, like the hostess advised. But the ambience and food plating was all 100% Instagram worthy and perfect to vibe with a date without being too casual or too classy. I loved it because the salmon bagel was light, yet relatively filling.

Last thing; do not get the coffee soda. I love coffee but this was simply a mistake.

Does Russ & Daughters need one more 5-star review?  The food options were fantastic, some expected, some unexpected delights.  Decor is unmatched.  Service terrific.  Waits are long -- go early for breakfast.  It felt like our group ordered almost everything on the menu between us -- so much fun.  The borscht was terrible though; I don't understand why they bother to make such a boring borscht.
Fantastic: lox, coffee, lox, service, bagels, everything, lox. There's a reason this place has a line every day. Absolutely worth the trip. Lives up to the hype. Go, go, go.

Absolutely worth the wait. I ordered: 

- The Classic Board
- Potato Latkes
- Bloody Mary with Fenugreek-infused vodka, celery.

Still thinking about it.

I had the smoked salmon on potato latkes that everyone was raving about. I was really disappointed as I'm a huge fan of smoked salmon and this was one of the more forgettable places I've been to. The saltiness of the salmon was so overwhelming it covered up any natural taste of the fish, and the salmon meat itself was mushy and had no texture. 

Overall I was prepared to love this place, instead I left disappointed. Extremely mediocre, overhyped food.
The bagel and smear are delish but their potato latkes. Oh my, are perrrrfect. Right crispness and oiliness. They serve with sour cream and applesauce. Order it, you won't regret.

So originally we walked into the deli on Houston street where people were ordering bagel sandwiches and to-go salads but I wanted to sit down so we walked around the corner to the cafe and it's completely different. I wanted to sit somewhere and have a freaking everything bagel sandwich with vegetable cream cheese, onions, nova salmon and tomatoes. The cafe only has scallion cream cheese and it's all served on a cutting board. We even got judged for both ordering the nova so we buckled under pressure and also got the gravlax, to be fair it was a good suggestion. So while I appreciated that you could build your own open faced sandwich situation, the bagel was really small and also like twice the cost of a sandwich somewhere else. I also rarely get to New York so I was bummed that I wasted my one bagel sandwich opportunity here. On the plus side there was no wait and the service was polite but curt. Next time I'll either just get my sandwich at the deli and make a mess walking around with it or go somewhere else.

We for a brunch Saturday. The hostess said there was an hour and 40 min wait--- she was dead on! One hundred minutes after adding my name to the list we we were seated. Since the weather was beautiful and the restaurant will text you to let you know the table was ready, the wait wasn't a big deal. We walked around got a cup of coffee and soaked up the fall sunshine. We were starving so once seated we ordered Bloody Mary's (YUM), pickled veggies (the tomatoes were fantastic) and a bread basket to start (pumpernickel and bialys!!!!) our mains did not disappoint! Latkes with salmon roe were also yummy as was the pastrami style lox and sunny side up eggs. Our waitress was also really sweet. If you're looking for quality food in an inviting setting this is the place for you. If your looking for a short wait then you should stay away.

I can't visit New York without at least one meal at Russ & Daughters. The decor is lovely, the staff are friendly & attentive, the food is delicious. They've accommodated a group of us for a birthday brunch, and also let me sit at the bar eating & drinking the hours away while I read a book. 

I always get some sort of fish platter. Ordering the knishes, latkes, sours/pickles, and/or breads are all great life choices. If you're eating with a group, don't forget the blintzes! 

Years ago R&D introduced me to shrubs and I'll never be the same. I hope everyone tries one!

I awoke every morning the following week thinking about the meal I ate at Russ & Daughters Cafe.  I spent 6 days in New York, (and not a novice trip) and this was absolutely one of the highlight meals.

SERVICE was on point for a Sunday afternoon.  I came with a group of 5 and we were magically seated immediately. It wasn't empty either. Menus were placed and a couple minutes later drink orders were taken and delivered.  Another server came by and asked how we were doing.  A friend had just peeped a pic on Yelp and asked if they could make it since he didn't see it on the menu - she said absolutely! So the matzo brie came out for him.  Delicious. Everyone's meal was great, lots of shared bites, and the perfect amounts of check-ins.


EAT
knishes with caramelized onions
latkes with salmon roe + creme fraiche
super heebster bagel toast: whitefish + salmon  salad with wasabi-infused roe on top and horseradish dill cream cheese
classic bagel + nova smoked salmon
kasha varnishkas  - buckwheat and bow tie pasta with caramelized onions + a poached egg
matzo ball soup
borscht
matzo brei (off menu)

DRINK
coffee soda - just, wow.
blueberry basil soda - blueberries basil, vanilla, elderberry, lemon
lower east side - tanqueray, lime, dill, and cucumber
schmoozer - rye, aquavit, bitters, absinthe rinse

Bring your appetite and be ready to enjoy. Trust me.

This review is solely based on their drinks. I had their Bloody Mary (they have 4 flavors and I had the Caraway-infused vodka, rye croutons with pickled vegetables) and it was absolutely DELICIOUS. My boyfriend had the Schmoozer and as a cocktail snob, he fell in love. We enjoyed the staff and the experience. We will definitely be back to try the food.

I was really looking forward to this Saturday morning adventure. The wait was a little over an hour when we got there around 10. I love the diner feel of this place. Good fish options for plates, boards and scrambles. I like that you can choose ANY of the smoked fish they offer on their large plates and have it on a board, etc. I would say that their portions of fish are not generous, but are not skimpy either. I got pastrami seasoned lox which was smooth and tasty. My husband got the sturgeon which also had great smoked flavor. He had the rye and I had the bialy. Rye was definitely the way to go! The pickled are a must have!!

Field notes: 

Pastrami Russ -- Who knew pastrami was a preparation applicable to even salmon? Crazy high quality, scrumptious, fresh. 

Potato Latkes -- fried potatoy goodness meets delicious and refreshing salmon row + creme fraiche. 

Daughters Caviar Flight -- (for the newbies like me) at a relatively affordable price, it's a great opportunity to enjoy a Russ curated trio of caviar, form an understanding, and probably an addiction. What did I learn? I would gladly shell out buckets of cash for American Transmontanus.

Yum yum yum! Group of three of us walked in on a Monday morning with no wait (SCORE!) and was promptly seated. Friendly staff and waiter. They have a really great selection of breakfast foods to choose from (small platters, to large, easy-to-share platters). I had the Eggs Benny ($18) which came with poached eggs, SMOKED SALMON (YUM), spinach, hollandaise sauce, and challah bread. Super simple and delicious dish. I really enjoyed the smoked salmon (not TOO salty) and the challah that everything sat on top of was the PERFECT bread -- it was soft which made it easy to cut through and take bites with, and it had a slight sweetness to it that balanced well with the other salty and savory flavors. 

Would highly suggest stopping into Russ & Daughters Cafe for breakfast! 

P.S. the bathrooms were really clean.

I was jet lagged and woke up at 6am on a Sunday morning so the first thing I thought of was to come early and eat at Russ & Daughters cafe since ever other time I tried for brunch was a big fail due to the crazy wait time. We got here around 9 and there was already a wait but a short one compared to the other visits. We ordered the potato latkes which was great, and it's a lot larger than I imagined. We also ordered the heebster and shared the Classic bagel with the BF. The heebster was a little too salty for me but the Classic was perfect and beautiful, just what I needed after 3 weeks in Asia.

The classic plate (bagel, lox, tomatoes, red onion and capers) was perfection. I love the atmosphere...it feels like you are back in time. We went in at 8:30 on a Saturday morning and were immediately seated at the bar. By the time we left, there was line out the door so get there early (unless I'm in town...then get there late ).

As anauthentic Jewish deli as you will ever experience - nothing has changed much since 1914! The bagels aren't made here but everything else is! Russ & Daughters uses its 100 plus years of caviar expertise to select and approve each tin of the freshest, highest grade, hand-packed caviar. Or the densest, moist and flavorful Babkas. The potato latkes! The bialys! 

Just go. It is an experience.
An amazing place for brunch. We over indulged with a little bit of everything and did not regret not one bite. The staff was friendly and attentive. Make sure to order some cocktails too!
The line is really long but the food is really good. It's worth it if the weather is nice because you  will probably eat in on the bench outside. You will not want to wait, really good food.

The hostess is terrible. She forgot about us or intentionally made us wait for an hour. Kept telling us we were next as others patrons walked in and were seated.  Finally asked for the manager, and manager eventually she sat us at a booth. She wasn't to swift either.  Thankfully we have this wonderful waitress we had before. Food is delicious. Unfortunately, hostess needs better communication skills and not give the customer a smirk so I know she did it intentionally.
Great for brunch but be warned for a long line during peak hours. Lower sunny side is great with some of the best smoked fish ever! Potato latkes are delicious as well. Friendly service.

4.5 stars for food
2 stars for service

I was here for the first time with a couple family members who were long time veterans. They wanted to show us an amazing breakfast, so we did the modest wait smashed into the small front waiting area and eventually got to our diner-style booth. All the waiter are dressed, interestingly, in med student short white coats.

The Food --
Eggs Benny: Delicious! The eggs were poached perfectly. The smoked salmon is the obvious MVP in this dish. This place is known for its quality and for a good reason. The surprise here was how amazing the toasted challah bread makes this dish skyrocket in terms of uniqueness and quality. One of the best eggs Benedict styles I've enjoyed.

Potato pancakes: I think this was my favorite thing here. I don't know how they could be so crispy on the outside and so soft and delicious on the inside. They weren't overly greasy and the flavor was perfect. Certainly impressive. I would come back just to get these.

The Service --
Probably one of the worse servers I've had. He was rarely around for most of our meal, which is fine because no one likes a helicopter server, but would have been nice to see him be more attentive. The real problem was what he said after our meal. After he brought us the checks and we signed them, some of continued to finish our coffee and were looking up how to get to our next destination (we're visiting and unfamiliar with NYC). Within 10 mins, he comes up and says that we should leave because "it's busy and other people are waiting". This is one of the rudest things I've ever heard a server say. Also there were 2 groups waiting when we left. We were all pretty stunned at this statement. I guess he didn't care because we already put down his tip and they took the signed copies.

Overall, solid food with SOME over hype (but not too much), with a rude server who soured the experience for some visitors and a couple frequent visitors. If I come here again, I'll just do takeout.

Disappointing experience today at R&D Cafe. Advised an hour to hour and fifteen minutes. Patiently waited TWO hours and was offered awful seats at the bar, right by the freezing cold entrance! Declined, as after waiting that long wanted to enjoy a proper table. Finally after two hours was offered another miserable table, a shared bench with three others in line with the freezing entrance. Hostess was not friendly or accommodating. Always willing to wait, but not when service is lacking so terribly.
Awesome! From the matzoh ball soup to the fish platter everything was great! Herring was the best I have ever had as well as the lox.  A must try however be prepared for a long wait for a table

Believe the hype. This has the best lox in the city. I could eat here everyday if I had the 45-90 minutes to spare waiting for a table. The wait is expected though so come here when you're not "hangry" or in a time-crunch. There's a few fun bars near by so you can grab a drink/catch a game while you wait. 
My go to is one of the boards (you can't go wrong with any of the 4) and preferably 2 bloody Marys (also of 4 different flavors).

I didn't expect to fall in love with this brunch spot, but I did. I went on a Thursday afternoon and they said that the wait would be 1.5 hours, however expect to only wait half an hour. It was surprisingly quick, so I would definitely say to walk around the neighborhood because there are some cute hidden boutiques. (There is a vintage candy store called Economy Candy around the corner and also a sex shop called Babeland that was quite interesting)  

This place is known for its remarkably fresh caviar, however I was not able to try it during my visit. I ordered The Classic Board ($16) and the Babka French Toast ($10) and I was amazed!!! I have never been to a Jewish Breakfast and Brunch before and I am thoroughly impressed. The Classic Board is essentially a deconstructed Lox Bagel (Onions, tomatoes, capers, cream cheese, and Lox). The lox was so thinly cut that the moment you take a bite of it, it melts in your mouth! The Babka French Toast had chocolate swirls and fresh strawberries on top. I would say it is a must try when you come here. I am lost for words by how good the food was and this is definitely going on my top 5 brunch spots. I also enjoyed their coffee ($3) which I thought was very fragrant. 

My overall thoughts for this establishment is that it is worth the hype! It had a modern yet 70s feel to it. All the waiters were wearing white coats that resembled doctors, which I thought was chic. I will definitely be bringing my friends here in the future. :D

Staggeringly disappointing. I don't run a restaurant, but...
... if half your guests are wearing puffy winter jackets inside, it's too cold.
... if you serve someone a $12 cocktail with a long hair in it, and the customer asks for another, don't leave the hairy cocktail on their table while you go tend to other customers.
... if your latkes taste like they were cooked in week old oil, your should probably change your oil.

Also, the bagels are pretty basic, not what you'd expect from a famed Jewish delicatessen.

Very New York experience.... nice atmosphere and delicious food - especially the latkes and of course the smoked salmon... so why not 5 stars you ask?? The portions were stingy!! I ordered the open faced/build your own bagel and they literally gave me 4 tiny little slices of smoked salmon- albeit delicious salmon but I felt seriously gypped ....

Russ & Daughters reminds me of a second date. 

The first time I went I wasn't "wowed" I just got the classical bagel board, and it was good but the bagel was tiny although lox was excellent...the second time, I got into the groove ordered more and was pleasantly surprised how good everything tasted. 

This Saturday at 10am we waited an hour and half for breakfast. In the meantime, we went to a coffee shop and they texted us 10minutes before our table was ready.

The four of us went a little overboard and got the following...

To start
- Knish (they are small, 2 to each order, so we got 2 orders) -$8 one order 
- Latkes (bigger size comes w/ 3 per order) - $9
- Hot Smoke/Cold Smoke - $13 highly recommend

The entrees...(one per person)
- The Classic Board (bagel, lox, capers, union & tomatoes) - $16 good but my least favorite in comparison to everything else 
- Eggs Benny -$18 we all enjoyed this, one of the better eggs Benedict I've tried  

For something sweet...
Blintzes - $8 (2 to an order, very very good)

It ended up being such a great experience. 
Glad I ventured out!

Awesome brunch! My ex girlfriend was a vegetarian and I was a meat eater but this place will satisfy anyone taste bud.

Love their poached eggs and potatoes are delicious. Highly recommend this place to anyone. 

I like visiting this place in the summer because they have tables outside and it makes for a great experience people watching 

Happy eating folks!.

There's a reason why this eatery has been around for over 100 years, the food is EXCELLENT. Don't be surprised if you have to wait over an hour, it's well worth it. Place your name and explore the Lower East Side and you'll receive text when your table is ready. Five of us dined yesterday. We shared 3 appettizers, had soup, and then 4 of us shared the Ida platter. The platter was more than enough for us 4 & it offered us the opportunity to try four different salmon cuts. Of course, a couple at the table must order a chocolate egg cream, prepared just like my grandpa made at his soda shop many years ago.

Unexpectedly fantastic (for dinner!) I was thinking it might be akin to Katz' deli. Was completely wrong. Incredibly thoughtful and inviting decor (including perfect lighting), lovely color scheme begin your experience. Next, head to an inventive drink list (including smallbut strong wine selection). And the menu is amazing. I had the Lower Sunny Side Up: eggs over easy, lox and latkes. Unbelievable. The eggs were perfectly cooked (and soooo pretty) and lox and latkes were delicious. Dessert - the babka French toast could not have been a more perfect ending. To top it, the service was exceptional. This is a must visit for New Yorkers!
The bagels were decent, but they weren't filling at all. However, the mimosa was good.

Love the vibe. The place feels just like the shop but a touch of classiness. However, service was a little lacklustre maybe because of where we sat. I was very very happy with my bagel but my friend was less impressed with the potato latkes. I rather much like the bagels for Absolut bagels but the salmon was the clincher.

Very unique menu. The food was great, as was the bloody mary. Lots of things like lox and capers and wasabi infused roe. The decor is pretty interesting as well. Kind of a science lab coat vibe, but it's working. More inviting than you may think. Great unique restaurant to go with friends for lunch/brunch if you don't mind the unconventional food offerings.

Excellent, but slightly overpriced Jewish deli food.  

My friends and I tried potato latkes, borscht, the herring platter with roe, and cucumber soda.  Overall, the sour and salty flavors were a bit intense (just the way I like it), but they were complemented well with the light soda and dark rye bread.  I thought the soda selection was authentic (old school diners with soda fountains come to mind), yet creative at the same time.  

I will come back again to try something different.

I am no lox connoisseur but this was pretty darn good.

WAIT: Came on MLK at 10:55am and it was pretty packed, they quoted 1 hour to 1 hour 15 min wait for the 2 of us and we said counter would be fine.  They text you and then text you again when your seat is ready so you can walk around the area.  We put our name down then waited at Starbucks.  We waited almost exactly an hour and got a nice little booth that could have easily sat 4 people, which was nice.

ATMOSPHERE: I'm assuming this is supposed to look like the original location with jars of items lining the walls labeled with old looking signs.  I wonder if the original place was also a pharmacy because all the waiters are dressed in white lab coats with pens in their pen pockets.  It's pretty cool.

The inside is fairly small and there is a counter so I could see why the wait gets to be so long.  Marble tables with paper menus with pretty fonts make it totally picture worthy.  Gotta get those tablescapes.

FOOD: We were going to split the classic board, latkes and matzo ball soup but since I'm trying to be gluten free I couldn't eat the Latkes or Matzo Ball soup.  They both have Matzo Meal, which has flour so not good for people with gluten or wheat free diets.

CLASSIC BOARD - probably the best option for someone who wants to try the classic lox bagel.  At $16 it does seem a little pricey but it actually fills you up.  There's no extra for a gluten free bagel but it's about half the size of a normal bagel.  If you want another they charge you $1.50 but it might be worth it since you usually end up with extra ingredients but not enough bagel. It comes with cream cheese, 3 slices of their smoked lox, tomatoes, onions and capers with some dill sprigs.  Put everything on top of your toasted bagel and munch away.  It was the perfect combination and very very good.  The lox had a soft silky texture with the right amount of salt and smoke flavor.  The onions also help add a nice kick.  The gluten free bagel was surprisingly very good.  It didn't have that disintegrating taste gluten free bread tends to have and it was very substantial.  My husband even said it was better than some regular bagels he's had.

LOWER SUNNY SIDE - also a good option for those that are sharing.  Comes with lox, 2 eggs and 2 latkes.  This way, you could have more lox and also get to try the latkes.  My husband said they were pretty good (essentially flat fried hash browns).

Overall, we enjoyed this place despite the long wait.  Sure prices are kind of high for portions that are JUST right and possibly leaves you wanting more, but worth trying and taking photos of!

This is a very nice place with great ambiance. It's upscale but casual, kind of feels like a French restaurant. We came here in the afternoon and it was pretty full but we were lucky enough to get the only empty booth. The maitre d and the waitress were very nice and attentive. Food came very quickly and our dessert arrived at the perfect time, I didn't even have to remind our waitress. Onto the food; I ordered sunny side up eggs w smoked salmon and potato latkes. I have only recently started to eat smoked salmon (I used to think it was pretty unappetizing), and the ones I've had so far were either too salty or too mushy. The salmon I had here was so delicious I couldn't get enough of it. These people know how to cure and fumee fish. The menu is filled with dishes that have fish and caviar. Lots and lots of caviar... There are also options without fish, like the goat cheese omelet, soups and salads. My friend had the mushroom barley soup. I absolutely hate mushrooms but oh my god this soup was so flavorful and delicious. It tasted like it was made that morning. As for dessert, we got the babka french toast. It was -surprise surprise- amazing. So soft and chocolatey.. Definitely try it. All in all a great place to grab a bite and enjoy some smoked fish, caviar (if you're a caviar person), and cocktails.

Even though the restaurant is only two years old, it feels like a restaurant from the1940, wth the same excellent quality as the 100-year-old store on Houston.  We arrived for a mid-morning breakfast at 10:30am.  The three of us shared the borscht soup, firm diced beets in a clean slightly tangy broth with sprigs of fresh dill and sour cream.  Superb!  My sister has the lox, scrambled eggs with onions which came with a beautiful small side salad.  Rob has the classic bagel board with Gaspe Nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, red onion, tomato and capers. The nova was smoky yet tender.  The best.  There are so many more items on the menu that tempted me: potato latkes, whitefish salmon salad, chopped chicken liver, Kasna Varnishikas, and more.  The white jacket waiter/waitress service was excellent.  And you get free seltzer with your meal.

Having had both brunch and dinner at Russ & Daughters' sit-down restaurant, I'm torn between 3 and 4 stars for a review. For either mealtime, most of the choices didn't appeal to me. But my food orders were well executed, given the self-imposed constraints of the niche menus. 

The potato latke pancakes with sour cream are a winner. The chocolate babka French toast is also good, though perhaps a bit bitter (that's dark chocolate). The best part of the brunch is the cherry sour, one of a series of distinctive fruit drinks.

For dinner, the knishes are some of the best you'll find. The moist and doughy savories come with a dipping bowl of hot (Chinese-style) mustard. The pastrami-fied salmon on a bagel is a creative stretch on a traditional Jewish dish. Spread a bit of that mustard on the sandwich, and it's even better. The meal goes great with the "Heads & Tails" margarita-ish cocktail.

Portions were definitely smaller than what you expect to pay. Decor was fun and clean. 

Service was good. We had several different people check up on us, but that might be because we were next to their station and kitchen entrance. 

The matz ball soup was ok. I'd say 3 stars. Taste like chicken broth, and a the matz ball like an extremely light meatball. Simple. 

The lower sunny side was good. The potato latkes is like others have mentions, a thick hash brown with more stuff in it like onions. Eggs are good, not overdone and the salmon was good too. Eating it together was great. But i ended up having more left over potato latkes and was wanting ketchup to eat with what was left. They didn't have ketchup bottles on the table and i didn't want to ask.

The shtetl was good. Kind of a small portion too. But i guess it is the price for the fish you're eating. A few of the fish filet were hard to pick up. But definitely eating it all together tasted really good! The capers give that burst of pickled flavor, the tomatoes made it light and fresh, the goat cheese gave it the creamy taste and helped kept everything attached to the bagel. I'd say this is rather fancy open fact 2 bagel sandwich.

Overall, i think it was a little too hyped. Food didn't leave a OMG i have to eat here again tomorrow feel. Would come visit if i have time next time I'm in town.

We had 3 dishes: 
the cinnamon babka with apple compote, creme freche, and roasted walnuts. 
The salmon, eggs, and potato pancakes. 
The classic board dish which is salmon, red onions, capers, cream cheese, and tomato. 
Everything was of high quality, generous (but not overwhelming), and put together perfectly. The classic board was the best lox style sandwich I've ever had! 
And I could've eaten the cinnamon Babka by myself.

Russ&Daughters deserves a spot amongst the best breakfast/brunch places in NYC, but one should not be in a hurry. With only limited reservations available by 5:30pm the previous day, walk-in waiting times can be very long. However, the wait is worth it, as the food is delicious. I tried the potato latkes with salmon roe and Creme fraiche, which are listed as small plate, but are in fact a huge portion with 3 latkes. Given the size of the portions, the prices are very reasonable and the service was very friendly and quick.

Great food but in my opinion, not worth the wait. 

Yo, I am really over this waiting for three hours for a meal trend that's always plagued nyc. Is anything really worth freezing for? Is anything really worth standing around in crowds and killing time nearby for hours?

I get there and the hostess doesn't even flinch as she tells me it's a 2.5 hour wait. Like damn. That does not even phase her. How did we get to this place??!! Sad sad.

Anyways, my party killed time by going to economy candy, bluestockings book store and a cafe. Finally, our table was ready! 

We got the latkes, classic platter, and the French toast. We also ordered the halvah ice cream. I would say the French toast might be my favorite even though I usually prefer salty plates. I liked the latkes a lot too, especially with the caviar. The bagel on the platter was nothing impressive which was shocking considering it's russ and daughters. I need me a NYC sized bagel! 

Don't feel the need to go back because I can find good bagels everywhere and if I keep eating that French toast bad things may happen to me...also I refuse to wait 2.5 hours for meals.

Walking in here is like taking a step back in time. Everything from the staff uniforms to the guest seating. I had Russ and Daughters booked marked for my trip to NYC and I was definitely satisfied. I knew I wanted to order a bagel, (DUH) so we took a seat at the bar and I ordered "The Classic - gaspe nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers".($16) Served with your choice of bagel, bialy, shissel rye or pumpernickel. This board is magic. The bagel was soft and chewy and the salmon was fresh. We also ordered the potato latkes because how can you pass that up in a Jewish deli?! They are huge and crispy and flavorful and I want them right now! There are 3 to an order and you have two options: 1. With applesauce and sour cream ($9) or 2. With wild salmon roe and creme fraiche ($14)Since we were sitting at the bar, we also got to witness the variety of craft cocktails they're whipping up. I suggest you make a reservation (like anywhere else in NYC for brunch), otherwise you'll be REALLY hangry. Definitely ordering more on my next visit!

Been here twice, been told we have to wait 45min -1hr, but actually there weren't that many of people waiting. And the cafe doesn't do reservation. Both times we took taxi here. Basically if you want to dine here, you have to get there before ten. Then its is not actually a true Sunday brunch. So disappointed
Came here for a third time, and now giving it a solid 3.5 stars.  I think I've had a lot of underwhelming bagels over the past year... so Russ & Daughters Cafe can move up a notch ;-)

I live right across Russ & Daughters Café and always see the gigantic lines to get in and feel super lucky that I can usually avoid those by coming in right when they open up to put my name down. I would advise folks to do the same. 

In terms of the food, it's pretty straight forward but all the best foods are. 

The ingredients are SUPER fresh. My girlfriend LOVED the liver here. I love a good LOX bagel so opted for that dish. It was presented nicely on a wooden board. It includes salmon, cream cheese, red onions, capers and tomato.  Best LOX style bagel I've had? Not sure. It was pretty gosh darn good but unless I had a mouthgasm...I wouldn't say that this was the BEST Lox Bagel in NYC. 

Iconic spot.
Delish food. 
Nice service. 

Overall, a good experience.

2 on a sunday, winter.

knishes
classic board
pastrami russ
beet shrub - delicious

The food is very good but it's just not worth the wait.  If dropping in casually for a short wait (under 30 min) sure, very nice.  What you do get is clean, classic flavors, delicious, and served in a pleasant atmosphere.  But it takes forever to get a seat.

Everything in the tableware and decor is well curated.  It's a very consistent visual throughout and it's very well composed.

The best thing I can say about them is that they are not moving to turn tables so you do feel welcome.
There is something very kind and hospitable about that.

We sort of stumbled upon this place when we were staying in the area. We didn't want a heavy breakfast so this was beyond perfect. There was a small wait but were seated close to the bar. 

We ordered:
The Classic - smoked salmon with a bagel ( VERY FRESH)
Lower Sunny Side - Eggs, salmon with potato latkes (SO GOOD)

Not much else to say besides the staff was great and the atmosphere was very classic feeling with the decor. I would definitely return.

This is one of those iconic eateries in NYC that I've bookmarked to try for a while now. Given that it's winter now, I'm really glad Russ & Daughters opened a cafe so we could enjoy our bagels indoors instead of having to takeaway from the original location! 

Visited on a Thursday morning and really wished that the cafe opened earlier on weekdays (opens at 10am on weekdays, 8am on weekends). We arrived right at opening and since it was a weekday, the cafe wasn't crowded (about 2/3 full). My boyfriend and I both went for the classic board - gaspe nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers and an everything bagel. Basically, a deconstructed bagel sandwich hah. Undoubtedly, every single item on the board was of high quality. The salmon was really good, the tomatoes were huge and really fresh, and they also did not skimp on the onion and capers. The bagel was ok - I prefer Ess-A-Bagel's. The portion was just right for me, so I did not leave feeling like I overate. However, for the price point ($16 for the board before tax and gratuity), other places gave more salmon and had bigger bagels... 

I saw that they do French toast using babka. What a treat! Perhaps I'll come back to try it.

This was my husband's equivalent to Jewish Heaven. We lived in the city for years and finally made it here on our last weekend in town. He would have ordered everything on the menu if I wasn't there. Not bad 45 minute wait for a Sunday brunch. We got Potato Latke with salmon roe and creme fraiche which was amazing. Creme Fraiche makes everything better, no? the Latkes are great without too. 

The classic board with all the fixings for your bagel (or toast in our case) and lox. Fresh salmon that tastes so smooth, we ate the whole thing, obviously!

Lower Sunny Side with more latkes, salmon and eggs..again, great taste, ate the whole thing!

For drinks we had the Chocolate Egg Cream soda which I had heard about but never had. It's basically Yoohoo with carbonation. It's worth it if you are on the fence about getting it. Also the cucumber soda has a nice little kick to it.

Challah Bread Pudding with apricots and carmel sauce for dessert is not a mistake. Share it if you think you're too full for dessert. The coffee is also smooth and fresh. We almost bought some beans to take home.

Underwhelming is the best word to describe my dining experience here.

I get it, it's one of those "you must go here!" places.  Upon arrival at 1pm on a Sunday (I know, prime time) we were told a 1.5 hour wait (no reservations accepted).  We assessed the situation and decided they were over-estimating, and decided to wait.  After 40 minute we were seated.  (Yay!)

Service was friendly throughout the whole experience, so I do give them a solid 4 stars for that.  The decor is also nice, so points there.

The bagel and lox was as standard as you can imagine.  It was fine.  It was not special.  Babka French Toast was fine, as well, but for the price I would have expected 2 pieces of bread, not ONE.  Matzo ball soup, again FINE.  Are you sensing a theme here.  Nothing was bad.  Nothing was great.

My friend got some eggs with latke.  The latke did not come with any sour cream or apple sauce, so she asked for a bit.  The waiter happily brought over apple sauce, which amounted to less than 2 tablespoons.  The amount was not an issue.  THe issue was that we were charged $1.50 for it.  Absurd.

Homemade sodas were the one exception to the everything being "fine" rule.  They were excellent.

Prices were comparable to others, but portions were small.  In other words, paying $15 a  plate is fine, but not for the amount of food provided.

Would not return, but glad to have checked it off of my "to do" list.

I've held off writing this review, trying to find the right words to express my love for this place. I hope by literally reviewing Russ & Daughters ON Valentine's Day, that'll convey my sentiment wholeheartedly. THAT should do the trick. It's like giving Russ & Daughters 5 stars and a heart. Which means it's the best. Perfection on a plate. Or platter. 

There'll be a wait no matter what time you show up (on a weekend). I've waited up to 2 hours for a table for 2 and would wait 7 hours if I had to. I think about this meal multiple times a week and my mouth waters every single time. This is not a new feeling... I've been to Russ & Daughters multiple times, but, you'll need to experience it yourself to understand. 

Here's what you want:

-Potato Latkes
-Classic platter w/ a scooped out everything bagel & scallion cream cheese
-Coffee
-Bloody Mary

If you're with a group of 3 or more, get The Ida platter and a couple of noshes to start.

*Disclaimer: when I give a 5 star review, it's serious business. Please see stars above.
Came here for brunch today and was very happy with service and food! I got the farm egg omelette with spinach and mushrooms and it was great! Would definitely come again.

This place is beautiful. I feel like if it wasn't a gorges atmosphere the food wouldn't be as good, if that makes sense. The food was very tasty and it was probably the first place we ordered more than one entree each. I had this on places to visit when I went to New York so I was going to go all out. Latkes were very tasty and and so was the bagel and lox. I ordered a lot of salmon roe and I didn't think it'd creep me out but it ended up weirding me out so I pushed that to my husband. I loooooved my fig shrub. While we waited I went to their website and read their history. Such a rich history story with so much family effort. If we ever go back to New York, I would return.

One word: YUM. Come to Russ & Daughters Cafe for food that would make your Jewish bubbe rest easy in her grave. My friend and I came around 10:30 on a Friday and were lucky enough to have no wait (we sat at the bar) but be warned - the last time I came was at prime brunch time (around 1:00pm on a Sunday) and the wait was two and a half hours, so we called it quits and went to Freemans instead. Russ & Daughters Cafe doesn't take reservations for brunch, so you have two options: either go at a weird time like my friend and I did, or just suck it up and shop around the LES for a couple hours while you wait. 

I ordered a bloody mary to start, which was excellent. They have four choices of bloodies: 
1) Caraway-infused vodka, rye croutons, pickled vegetables. 
2) Dill-infused vodka, fresh dill. 
3) Fenugreek-infused vodka, celery.
4) Smoked Pepper-infused vodka, smoked salt.
I had the first and thought it was exceptional - and trust me, I love bloodies so I know what I'm talking about :) They also have a bunch of fun sodas and egg creams on the menu, which I would love to try at some point. 

The menu is awesome, and I wanted to try everything but decided to stick with the Classic Board, which came with gaspe nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, and capers and I ordered on an everything bagel (if you choose to eat lox on anything but a bagel you're a fraud). My Gentile friend had the Pastrami Russ: pastrami-cured salmon, munster cheese, sauerkraut, mustard and pickle on a pretzel roll. Despite being stuffed after our meal, I still ordered the noodle kugel, which tasted like holidays with the Bernheimers and had me crying with joy. It took everything in my power not to get the latkes too, but at that point I don't think I could have fit anything else in my stomach. We ordered coffee to end our meal and they were GENEROUS with refills. 

The Cafe is absolutely adorable and I think that everything is priced appropriately - a bagel with lox at H&H will run you close to the same amount, and isn't as good. If Russ & Daughters had a weakness, it was the service - I did not find the bartenders to be particularly friendly, and when I ordered a bloody it was clear that she was skeptical of my ID (which is real). However, the food is just so damn good that I can overlook what was really not great service. 

Overall, Russ & Daughters is the real deal. Will absolutely return.
Love the food! It is really nice. First time tried and be surprised at the smoked seafood.

Nice brunch spot. Upscale diner decor.
Ordered the Classic lox with pumpernickel bagel.
Pretty small portion for the price.  Overall it tasted good but nothing to rave about. 
If I was craving lox and bagel I would still eat at my go to: Ess-a-bagel.

Tried Russ and Daughters on my recent trip to New York per recommendations from friends. Everything was great. I went for the pastrami smoked salmon and it was awesome. The pretzel bread bun was perfect too. The trout salad was a little heavy on the capers but delicious nonetheless. Latkes were very good. On the thicker side, but you really can't go wrong with them. Brunch was a 2 hour wait on a Sunday so I ended up coming later for dinner and it was super chill. The drinks sounded interesting but the ones I had weren't very memorable.
Loved the interior! Had the classic old school feel with a touch of modernity. The (brunch) food was surprisingly good, given how simple everything was. The staff was super nice.
Amazing smokefish platter and overall great experience! My only comment would be, I wish they had better bagels.

We were told it would be an hour and a half, but it was only an hour, and they texted us to tell us our table was ready so we were able to walk around the neighborhood! Loved the platter with the bagel and lox. The latkes were huge. The blintzes were delicious!!

Omg! One of the places I miss in NYC!  Be prepared to wait because this place gets busy! 
We tried different things this time, aside from the boards and bagel. 
Latkes are a must! Comes with 3 crispy fatty potato pancakes with salmon roe and creme fraiche. (They have applesauce and creme fraiche too for $9.)

Eggs benny were good but only comes with a super thin slice of smoked salmon.  Eggs were perfectly poached with the yolk running and soaking through the challah.  Each bite was loaded with spinach. 

Chocolate babka French toast was awesome.
Pickles were amazing too! $7 gets you carrots, cucumbers and tomato.  Yes pickled green tomato.. so good!! Firm and souuuuur!

Got the kippered lox bagel! The ingredients were fresh and the service was great! I was very excited to try out this place but my expectations were not met. The price tag for the bagel seemed steep for what you got! Also, I was not a big fan of the kippered style because it tasted a bit dry, I may have preferred the classic. My friend ordered the shtetl which came with goat cream cheese. The fish was good, but I was not a fan of the cream cheese!also the bagel itself was really dense and a bit dry! It was worth the experience, but I do not plan on returning!

Lives up to the hype. Matzo ball soup and kippered salmon salad. Best salmon I've ever had . Excellent soda - ginger lavender.
Loved it. Sooo cute vintage style. A mUST when in NYC!!!

4 stars for delicious food, fast and courteous service, cute decor and fun location. I got the sturgeon, eggs and onion and side of sours..YUM! Minus one star because there were bits of sturgeon bone in my eggs. At first I thought they were plastic and was quite upset. The staff explained and I was relieved but still a little annoyed that they were there in the first place. Overall though that's not going to prevent me from visiting again and trying more delicious food.

I never got to try this place. I am visiting from out of town. I called and asked if they were open during the snow storm and they said they are open. I said ok I'm on my way. I take an uber over and I get here and they tell me they close early. Shitty attitude and customer service. NOT RECOMMENDED! YOU COULD HAVE TOLD ME YOU'RE CLOSING EARLY WHEN I CALLED AND SAID I WAS COMING!

I brought a few out of town friends here, and it was very well received. We didn't make reservations and I'm actually not sure if they even take reservations, but the wait wasn't long. We were quoted 30 minutes, but seated in less than 5 minutes after we were given the quote.

I wasn't super hungry, so I ordered the kniches. I also tried some of my friend's french toast and some of the omelette. The kniches were a little dry, imo, and the size of the kniches were tiny for $8. I've definitely had better. However, I really appreciate their comprehensive breakfast/brunch menu as well as their drink menu - which consists of an array of interesting drinks such as house made sodas, malts, etc. Next time, I'm going to order a bagel and lox platter and get myself one of their specialty drinks!

I loved the ambiance of the cafe and the 60's New York diner setup. I will definitely be bringing visiting friends back here, and I'm sure my mom would love this place for a nice brunch venue!

I am so glad they opened a cafe. This is one of the best breakfast/brunch restaurants in the city. The boards are phenomenal and eggs bene wow the smoked salmon is so fresh melts in your mouth and eggs cooked to perfection. Have dined here many times since it opened and we return every time we are in NYC.

I was introduced to Russ & Daughters on my first trip and now whenever I'm in NY I make a trip here. I took a red eye flight from the west coast and got in around 7am. Dropped my bags off and headed straight here for my first meal! I mean, what better way to start a weekend off than with a good bagel with smoked salmon?

Their bagels have the perfect chew and I appreciate the options of toppings. Their consistency is on point and I've never had anything that wasn't delicious! A perfect way to start the day in my opinion.

We came here for brunch on a weekday. We waited about 10 minutes for a table. I ordered the Eggs Benny - Poached Eggs, Scottish Smoked Salmon, Sauteed Spinich, Hollandaise Challah. It was very nice! Would definitely try to return again before we leave NY.

big fight with the missus over this place you guys. she couldn't see past the nice decor and i couldn't forgive them that they put deli food on a plate and jacked up the prices. wearing a white coat cutting a bagel doesn't make you a chef right? you are still cutting a bagel.
coming for the kind of family that gobbles this type of food at home didn't make things easier. their latkes were hard, the cream cheese bland and my upcoming divorce it's on them.
One of my all-time favorite places to eat when on the Lower East Side. Can't go wrong with anything you order here. Love it.
The smoked salmon and the latkes were delicious! Unfortunately there was a long wait so that was the downside.

Always love this place.  Was engaged outside.  Nearly every dish on the breakfast menu will amaze.  Certainly pricey but awesome for a hearty breakfast or brunch.  Drinks are OK.  Sablefish is really exceptional / unique.

I think they try to classy it up by opening a cafe while using the brand of the old store, but the service is the worst I have had in NYC. The bagel and smoked salmon are good, but the waitress didn't even tell me there are options of cream cheese until I specifically asked. The old store is known for its varieties of fish and cream cheese, and the cafe people don't seem to care.

I had very high expectations for this restaurant as I have been going to the store for many years. So maybe when you have high expectations you are bound to be disappointed. The hostess was rude and the service was not great. Food was good but not yummy. I won't be back based on the service.

If you want fancyish bagels go here. 

I wanted to have a New York bagel. This is where you go for a fancy New York bagel. They have caviar on the menu. I didn't get that. 

I ordered the potato latkes. They were awful. I think the oil was old. You get three of these oil laden over fried potato globs. Skip the latkes. 

I also got the super heebster. Which was cold salmon salad on a bagel with wasabi roe on top. This would have been a disappointment if it didn't have the wasabi roe, gives it a nice kick. 

My friends got the bagel boards with smoked salmon and sable. They were tasty but kinda pricy. $18 bucks for smoked salmon and cream cheese on a bagel. 

I wouldn't visit again. It's too pricy for what you get.

3.5 star. And mostly on service not food. 

Hubby and I did Easter Sunday "Jewish" style by dining at Russ and Daughter's Cafe for brunch.  We were lucky, given the holiday weekend, the city was emptier than usual and we were able to quickly snag bar seating after only a few minutes wait. We were originally quoted 1-1.5 hour wait. It was pretty crowded, which large groups of people out back.  The hostess was very nice and attentive to me when I came in since there were numerous people coming in trying to cut ahead of me or just not realizing that we were there waiting to our names down. 

The waitstaff was something else, though. Very friendly, but a bit spacey and one of them had a bit of a stank attitude. Firstly, I ordered a cold coffee and the coffee was forgotten about until I reminded them and then I received a hot coffee. Lol. Fine whatever I didn't feel like correcting them. 

Our food took a really long time to come out- others got their food before us who sat after us, and the waitress with the stinky tude was like - it's coming, it takes time to cook. We are talking about two blintzes, it's a quick cook crepe with some farmers cheese, rolled and put on a skillet.... 

I think they messed up our order because another strange thing happened where they brought us the wrong classic board (with the wrong bread). And it went downhill from there. If you mess up, honestly that's ok, just acknowledge, it, apologize and move on. 

Everything did come out super fresh so maybe they just have a small kitchen. 

Anyway, moving onto the food. Menu has a wide variety of the tried and true ingredients found at their cafe - smoked fish, all kinds of spreads, caviar and all of the cooked jew food things you'd expect. 

We shared: 

- potato knish - nice dough, hot hot potato. Good house mustard 

- latkes - incredible. Maybe the best I had - fluffy, not too greasy, a combo of the shredded Potato and onion inside (don't like the mashed consistency inside) but had height and volume. Latkes came with good sour cream and apple sauce. Also a decent portion for $9 as they were three large ones. Well fried but not greasy 

- classic board - everything bagel was kind of eh but I guess it was a good vehicle for the board stuff- good lox, cream cheese (muted in flavor), capers, fleshy tomato. 

-blintz - delicious crepes rolled up and filled with farmers cheese. Came with sour cream and a very fresh fruit compote. 

Wish we had tried the house soda or egg
Cream but we missed on those.  Pretty sure they serve food on alcohol so you can get your cocktail if desired - and on this point, plenty of egg dishes too with lox or something inspired by their cafe. 

I enjoyed the bright, clean decor there. The restaurant has a cute brand. I'd come back but it would be immediate. Esp if there's a long wait.  But everything seems to be all about Russ & Daughters so I'm glad we came to check it off our list 

$60 for brunch for 2.

Are you guys low key racist ? My friend and I definitely felt racially profiled when we were dining at the café. We were one of the first people to get seated but for some reason the hostess decides to put us by the front near the bar. We were the only ones seated in the front and even the girls behind us got seated in the main dining area. As minutes wore on and more ppl got seated, the hostess kept seating the non Caucasians in the front of the restaurant and everyone that was Caucasian in the main dining room. 

Sure, your bagels and soup was pretty good but the vibe was definitely off.
The chocolate babka French toast  and of course the classic board. Im picky about salmon, and they definitely do it right. So good. Knishes were decent too.

Great traditionally cured and cold smoked salmon. Had the matzo ball soup, the smoked white fish chowder, the ida and the pastrami Russ. All great!! Our server, Mia, was thoughtful and considerate. She was happy to educate us as we had much to learn. Will be back!!

my friends and i wanted brunch, so we stumbled about this place. it was our first time having jewish brunch, so i wasn't sure what to expect. we came here on a monday around 10:30am and waited about 30-45 mins to be seated. the interior is very simple and old-fashion. our waitress provided us with self-serve tap water and sparkling water. we ordered a side of salmon, matzo ball, potato latkes, eggs benny, and the farm egg omelette. 

salmon - the salmon was indeed fresh and delicious tasting
matzo ball - i didn't really enjoy it very much
potato latkes - this was probably my favorite dish because i love crispy potatoes. definitely recommended!
eggs benny - small portion size for the price, but still delicious
farm egg omelette - i loved how smoothly the omelette looked and tasted

notes: the food was great, but a bit pricey. i can see why this place is so hyped up. the service was great too. our waitress was attentive and made sure that we were okay with our orders and substitutions. at the end of your bill, you get to keep a postcard of russ & daughters. i thought that was pretty awesome. we had a great brunch experience, though we didn't expect to wait so long on a weekday haha.

I have never given out a five star rating but this place is well deserving.  My brother, fiancé and I planned a trip for my parents' 50th birthdays.  They had never been to NYC and my fiancé put Russ and Daughters on our restaurant list.  I was hesitant at first because I felt it was too far out of my parents' comfort zone but everyone really enjoyed it.  The atmosphere is so retro and adorable.  I highly recommend getting an assortment of salmon, the chocolate babka French toast and an egg cream soda.  It was all so great and very, very tasty.  I will frequent Russ & Daughters each time I come to NYC.

Sadly, didn't meet expectations. Wish we'd just gone to the market instead of choosing to opt for sit down service at the cafe here. $51.17 for a bagel with lox and tomato, cream cheese and capers (build your own, so we split it), a side of sable ($11), and 3 latkes which came with sour cream and a tablespoon of roe. That latke app was the winner for our meal, by the way. 

The space is cool. We didn't have to wait since it's 2 pm on Tuesday. I wouldn't ever wait more than 5 minutes.

Snuck in for some late night nosh after hours of gallery openings. Portions are reasonable so you can get a few and share with your friends. The pickles were excellent, as were the latkes. There is sometimes live music, so if you want to talk, try to get a seat at the back of the restaurant.

I dropped by here the past weekend for a family Sunday brunch and I thoroughly enjoyed myself. Here is the breakdown of al relevant things:

Wait: When we arrived, there was a good line of people in front of us. Of course you can't really tell because their wait list is digital, so you can give them your information and they'l text you when your table is ready. I thought this was really convenient because it meant we didn't have to wait 1.5 hours (yup, that's right--1.5 hours!) out in the cold or cramped within the cafe. We were able to spend the time prepping ourselves for the meal...with ice cream.

Food: Like most other customers, we focused on the boards and the noshes. We ended up with two of "The Classic" (one with everything bagel, one with bialy), a "Shtetl" (with bialy) and a Potato Knish with Salmon Roe. We found that the fish were all incredibly fresh and you could tell based on the texture and flavor of it. Honestly, I've never been a fan of smoked salmon and this was my first time having a lox and cream cheese bagel but I'm so glad I lost my lox virginity here. I had The Classic and the quality of the ingredients really elevated my experience. I didn't have much of the potato knishes but was told it wasn't anything special--I guess it's hard to follow up after the boards. Only regret--if you're here with multiple people intending on getting the boards I highly recommend just getting a plate and sharing because I think it's a much better bang for your buck and you get to try more things.

Customer Service: Our waitress was incredibly friendly. I actually got the wrong dish, a Shtetl with bialy instead of The Classic, but she handled it gracefully and brought me the correct thing in probably less than a minute.

Atmosphere: I really enjoy the modern, bright and airy atmosphere of this cafe. I think it really speaks to the Sunday bagel brunch vibe. The waitresses all walk around in white aprons as well, which does give off a bit of a medical assistant vibe, but also a 90's diner vibe. I guess it's a pro and a con--maybe I just interpreted it weirdly. Overall, loving the bright atmosphere with the white walls and white booths.

tldr; everything was great, the food was yummy and I enjoyed my experience! Highly recommend you pop by.
chic environment. Their bagel with smoked fish is very delicious. I'm tired of oily dishes for brunch. So love this place. Plus their coffee seems is unlimited refilled.

My friend and I were dismayed by the service at this restaurant. I have never written a restaurant review, but this experience moved me to.  I had never heard of this place, but my friend really wanted to try the bagel and lox (to see if it lived up to the hype- she is a bit of a "foodie"). We happened to have been in the neighborhood after having eaten dinner. We were no longer particularly hungry. Upon entering, my friend asked if she could do "take out" and the manager said they they do not typically do that, but was not adamant about it.  We decided to sit at a table, have some coffee/tea, she would order the lox and attempt to eat some, then take the rest home. This seemed to be a reasonable, fairly inoffensive plan where everyone wins.  She ended up eating only a bit of the lox, as she really wasn't hungry. We asked the waitress if we could take the rest home (they definitely do allow that, as another table had their leftovers packed up). She looked uncomfortable and went to get her manager. The manager came over and scolded my poor friend.  She remarked that it looked like my friend had not eaten any of her meal and that she had told her that this restaurant does not do "take out". She was incredibly disagreeable (seemed like a somewhat unhappy person). She was unprofessional and condescending.  We are both physicians and meet a lot of people on a daily basis and rarely have I encountered someone this mean. She cited some sort of policy coming from whoever is above her.  We would have respected her more if she had been friendly about it and acknowledged that this was a somewhat strange policy, or perceived the notion that, technically, the food in my friend's plate was no longer "take out", but "leftovers". She then stated that she would take the unfinished meal away from her and throw it away. She took it away and it was, we assume, thrown away. What a waste of food- seemed particularly cruel. That probably pained me more than anything. She did take it off the bill, though! Will never go here again. It ruined our night, as we were treated quite badly. Our intention was not to trick her or do anything terribly conniving. All my friend wanted was some good lox.

Love the café for a slightly more upscale lower east side breakfast experience. Famous for smoked fish like lox and bagel boards.  Good table service but we love to sit a the counter for quick, good coffee refills and friendly service.

We were visiting friends from Miami where good Jewish delis can be counted on one hand. I knew the place was going to be great when we arrived and there was an hour and a half wait for brunch this past Sunday. It was perfect for us as it allowed us to walk around with friends to see the neighborhood and get coffee and tea nearby.
