We ordered a ton of appetizers to share from the latkes which were nice and crisp and not too oily. The pastrami russ is a must have; the delicious pastrami-cured salmon on a pretzel roll was phenomenal. My main was the lower sunny side - a healthy portion of eggs, nova and latkes.

The place was clean and service was good. It had an authentic feel to the ambiance and food that the other NYC staple delis lack due to institutional commercialism for decades without change.

This a superb place, having a perfect mix of old world charm with the sophistication of the new demographic of the lower East side. Both the food and the service were perfect, and I rarely say that. My only regret is that I didn't try any of their desserts. Loved the chopped liver appetizer, the sable board, and the chopped salad with generous chunks of smoked whitefish.

We came here with some local friends for brunch on a Sunday and as expected, we had an hour and a half wait. My feeling on the wait... we knew it would be bad so we really didn't mind. We had a little snack before we headed there so we were ready to go. We walked around the neighborhood and had some coffee to prep for the meal. 

The place is super adorable. Old school Jewish diner style but nicely updated. Many new Jewish delis totally fail at this so I was very taken with their decor. 

The menu was the placemat, which is great, but we ended up ordering so much. There was a study I once read that the longer you read the menu, the more you eat... proven by having this menu as the placemat. We ordered SO MUCH. We were 4 people and ate enough for 8.

The service was nice and the food was great. Worth the trip and the price. The nicest part was that even though we knew how long the waits were we weren't rushed at all at the end of our meal. We were able sit and chat for a little as we waited for the bill and embraced the food-coma.
Very good lox and bagels. Lox melts in your mouth. All and all one of the best lox boards ever

Warning: Bad food poisoning after ordering the fish sticks here. I noticed another review from just a couple of months ago reporting food poisoning from the trout salad. Bottom line--they seem to be using old fish in some of their dishes. This is an utterly unacceptable health code violation. I urge you not to go here if you value your health.
The bagels they have are very good, "The Classic" board was really good - unfortunately the staff was very arrogant.

Walked in in a lovely afternoon with friends. We waited for a couple minutes to be seated. We ordered a chopped liver, a classic board, and an egg Benny. The chopped liver was really good. I personally love pâtés, liver, foie gras, etc, and had tried many different kinds. But this chopped liver was impressively good. Would come back again soon.

We got the lox platter, eggs Benedict, potato latke with apple sauce and sour cream, and cinnamon walnut French toast. I did not like the eggs Benedict because there was a lot of spinach on it which made my challah bread more soggy with the poached eggs. I also did not feel the sauce was as good or flavorful. The lox bagel was okay but I did not like the texture of the bagel, it was more hard than chewy. The highlight of the meal was the potato latke and the cinnamon walnut French toast which was both very good.

Home Run ! 
Have been here now 6 or 7 times.  Never misses. Of course I'm a fan of the shop on Houston st.  If you understand what this is then you'll know it's about the best 

The babka desert is amazing. The mushroom soup perfect. The kasha just right. The fish well delicate fresh and served just perfectly

Pros: The latkes were otherworldly. The sunny side up eggs with smoked salmon were transcendent. The matzoh ball soup was the real deal. 
Cons: The coffee was a little weak for my tastes. The knish was meh. And the service had the hefty dose of snootiness so typical on the LES. I'm a hardened New Yorker, but waitstaff rudeness just isn't... kosher.

Deelish. The classic with Nova lox, bagel, and the fixings could not be better. The presentation was on a nice wooden slab. The Latke's could have used more onion and we're a little bland. Still good, bt not to my liking. Will come again though,...lots of other things to try.

I'm not a seafood person. My friends dragged me here telling me how great their food was. A bit skeptical and nervous but I gave it a try. We had the beet salad, salmon roe latkes, eggs benny and heebster. They were ALL GREAT but our fave was definitely the eggs benny and the latkes! Love Love Love! If you're a seafood person, this place a 5 star for sure :)

Came here for brunch a few weeks back with a friend. It being Russ and Daughters with notoriously long waits, we agreed to meet right when the Café opened at 9 am... Turns out, it opened at 8 am because when we got there, it was full but thankfully not too many people were in line before us! We sat around inside, looked at the menu, figured out what we wanted. We were actually seated not too long after getting to the restaurant because all the groups in front of us were 3+, so we were given a seat at the bar next to the door maybe 10 minutes in. We ordered immediately, getting a salted fish platter, him a lox bagel sandwich and myself a latkes-egg breakfast platter. I thought I knew salted fish, but definitely was not prepared for Russ and Daughters' versionI It was super salted - not my favorite, but I can understand why it's popular. He loved his lox bagel sandwich, and my latke egg breakfast platter had no surprises. The lady working behind the bar was very nice and answered our questions when we had them about the store, the food, the menu. Check came quickly. The type of food they offer is not quite my cup of tea, but I'm glad I tried it out!

Cinnamon Babka French Toast: the smell is divine. it might look underwhelming at first and have you wonder where the syrup is but it is just right. its a thick slice slathered with apples with candied walnuts. no syrup is required bc its super sweet (in my opinion) on its own - its just reflex to grab syrup when i see french toast. the creme fraiche is a perfect touch of creaminess. 

Potato Latkes: crispy hockey pucks of potato goodness. a bit salty for me but still delicious after eating the french toast. 

The Classic bagel board: looks clean and fresh and from what i was told yummy but not enough smoke flavor from the salmon

Cream Soda: not sickeningly sweet which is a nice change from the others ive had 

on a side note, i love the floor tile.

Russ and daughters 

Ordered:

Bissel of caviar
Lower sunny side 
Eggs benny 
Breakfast martini


First impression: the place has a classic retro feel but a bit modernized. Everything is very clean and although they specialize in caviar, smoked salmon, etc. there is no smell of "fish" whatsoever! 
Staff is very pleasant. Quick seating after waiting for about 30-45 minutes for a party of 2. 
Menu is great- a nice introduction to caviar and eating smoked salmon, sturgeon, etc. The price is decent although on the pricer side, especially the more items you get with caviar but that's not a surprise. 
Total cost of the meal for 2 (1 small plate as appetizer, 2 meals, coffee and a drink) totaled up to about $86.
Overall, a great place to try- especially if you wanted instaworthy pictures. Would probably come back once in a while if craving smoked salmon or caviar!

My exposure to Jewish food came in the 4th grade when a classmate brought potato latkes for international foods week. Though Jewish delis virtually had zero presence in the San Francisco of my childhood, we shared a similar "melting pot" culture as our east coast counterpart, & word of delicious latkes got to me just the same. 

The Lower East Side's Russ & Daughter's Cafe serves theirs three to an order with a couple topping options -- salmon roe & creme fraiche or sour cream & applesauce. Theirs are thick, rife with green onion, & have a golden fried exterior. I also ordered mushroom barley soup which had a rich beef broth & plenty of fork-tender carrots. My exact words after pilfering several spoonfuls of his soup -- "tastes like the best chicken noodle soup ever, but with matzo!" Safe to say that soups were a huge hit. 

My brunch companions indulged in what the menu calls "boards," a perfect serving for one person craving smoked fish with choice of carb (the bialy at the table looked absolutely mouthwatering.) We chatted up a regular outside who strongly recommended the sturgeon, to which my table gave decent reviews. 

In one of R&DC's comfy booths is a delightful place to take in your first meal.

After seeing the beautiful bagel boards on Instagram, I knew I needed to try it myself. 

We arrived around 1:30pm for a super late lunch, and we got a table right away. I loved the decor - very "fancy" New York vibes. 

I ordered the classic Board: Gaspe Nova Scotia smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, and capers.... with an everything bagel, of course! My fiancé got the eggs benny with smoked salmon and spinach. We also got two of their special sodas. 

The food was good, but honestly, I don't think it was that much better than the smoked salmon cream cheese bagel I had at a random deli. I understand that I'm paying for service, ambience, etc... all of which I didn't expect or need. To each his own, I guess.

Russ and daughters is one of my favorite places to get bagel. Now combine that with being able to sit down and enjoy brunch, I am in heaven. Their coffee was fresh, the bagels were just as good as the original location and the service was excellent. I highly recommend trying the cafe.

I love the ambience of the cafe. It's part old-timey diner, part chemistry lab, and I love it. It's like a 19th century apothecary, what with the oversized pickling jars and waiters in lab coats. There are a bunch of diner-style booth seats, and it's fairly spacious for a LES restaurant.

I got a pickled herring salad, and the pickled herring tasted exactly like what I had in Denmark. So, bonus points for that. The salad was also well-balanced with a citrusy dressing, red onions and capers. Since most of the food here is fish, things are going to be a little bit more expensive for the volume of food, but it's all high quality and it's worth checking out if you like cured fish like me.

Had to wait 45 minutes for a table at breakfast on a Friday morning! I had the cinnamon babka French toast. The slice was thick (it only came with 1 slice) but delicious. Had to try the honey cake with caramelized apple ice cream. Very small portion but fantastic! I figured I might as well try the challah bread pudding with apricots and caramel sauce. A bit larger than the honey cake and also very good. Overall good food, small portions and a little pricey

This is a classic NYC restaurant that you don't want to miss, if you are in the neighborhood. Perfect place to eat before your tour at the Tenement Museum. They also have a full bar and a breakfast martini!
terrif staff, excellent food. Sit at the counter, if you can for good people watching.
Amazing experience, staff was really patient with us and the food was everything we were expecting. Highly recommend their sweets!

Came on a weekday around 11 am and waited for around 10 minutes for a table for 2. They have the system where you can leave a phone number so if the wait is longer, you could leave the area and come back when they text you. 

The waiter said the most popular dish was the Classic board, which I ordered. I was at fault here because I didn't like that I had to put together the bagel myself, lol. But for those who like to customize, this would be a good choice. The ingredients were good, but nothing special. My friend ordered the Super Heebster, which she said was too salty. I liked that they offered sparkling water here. 

We really liked the candies that they gave us when our check came, and the waiter told us they are available for purchase at the Russ & Daughters store a few blocks away. 

Overall: not worth the extreme hype.
My first NYC Black and white cookie experience and it was amazing here. Will have to come back to have it again.

My wife and I used to live literally five minutes north of the original shop and, while we loved the food, the chaos and crowds made eating there/buying their smoked and other delicacies quite anxiety-inducing. 

For that reason we were thrilled that even though we had moved away, they had opened a sit down cafe with lots of the same fare as the original. We've been 5-6 times now and after trying lots of the menu, I think it's managed to surpass its much older namesake. 

The boards are all amazing (the mensch being my favorite), everything pickled is top notch, the chopped liver is amazing, the Super Heebster and Pastrami Russ are just as good as from the store, the Bloody Mary selection is great and the herring options are all world class. 

You will most likely have to wait unless you're there right when it opens (or at least before 11) and the service can be harried, but it's always worth it.

It was my first time to New York and of course I'm not going to miss out on the bagels and pizza. I was told that Russ & Daughters Cafe has a great selection of smoked fish, assorted bagels, and other breakfast items. I ordered their popular 'The Classic' board and their 'Sours' noshe which is a side of pickled vegetables. I was very happy with my choices. The smoked salmon was fresh and delicious and I've never had a better everything bagel. The pickled vegetables had a slight sweetness which I enjoyed. 

The only reason I gave four stars instead of five is because of the pricing. The board was $16 and the noshe was $7. It wasn't surprising since it is expensive to dine in New York.

Overall, I enjoyed the food, service, and atmosphere. I recommend stopping by get a quick bite to eat.

Fresh challah rolls, fresh, pickled and cream herring, lakes, salmon, sablefish, etc. Russ and Daughters does not disappoint. I had fresh herring in a challah roll with finely chopped white onions and corninchens. And halvah sesame ice cream with salted caramel sauce. Wow! Great egg dishes too. Lox. Caviar. Soups. Come here at least once while in NYC.

You come here thanks to the reputation but you stay because once you try the food you're hooked. 
Every item is distinct and delicious, authentic and other-worldly. 
The smoked sable and salmon are delivered on a cutting board, finely sliced and best eaten quickly without any fussiness. They  are smooth and tasty. 
Caviar- if you do it - comes nestled in a circle of tiny pancakes. It's tangy and exquisite.

We were anxious to visit this restaurant on our vacation.  Food was good but I found the staff very snooty, especially the hostess.  She made my family and I feel unwanted at the restaurant. When I raised my concern with the manager, she turned the table on me and made me feel like it was our fault.  I'm sure there are other restaurants in NYC that would make my family feel welcomed and appreciate our business.
The best. Service was great and the place really charming. The food was delicious. Don't miss the deserts!
The eggs benedict with salon were so yummy. We came on Sunday and it was a decent wait - only about half an hour. The service was quick and I will definitely be back some time.

Great place for seafood breakfast！Love the salmon, caviar and lox! 
Passed by for the first time and saw a long line waiting. Then came on the second day early without waiting. We go the best seat by the window and had a wonderful brunch.
Wasabi infused roe of super heebster on bagel toast was superb! 
Had too much but still had so much didn't get the chance to try... will definitely come another time!

Husband loves smoked salmon so of course we had to check this place out when we were visiting NYC. Sister lives in LIC and we've visited her several times but kept missing out on this well known spot. She needed a break from being a stay at home mom so we took her out for a day of eating and relaxing. This was our first stop and we're so glad we finally got to try their food. Salmon was delicious and one of the best we've ever had. Everything on the Classic Board was tasty and worked really well together. Such a simple meal with salmon, cream cheese, onions, capers, tomatoes and a bagel but there's something about it that's so comforting. We also ordered Potato Latkes which were delish but hands down we'd come back just for the salmon boards. Its no wonder this place is always so busy. Service was great and staff were friendly. Can't wait to come back.
So arrogant they don't do take out for bagels; it's really not good enough to justify this, so if you go here please expect this.

These five stars come with a caveat. I've wanted to go to Russ and Daughters for brunch for years but I never went because the wait is always so insane on weekends and I am not about waiting in line for food, especially first thing in the morning when I'm extremely hungry. However, I recently had a couple of weekdays off and decided to try my luck with some out of town guests and that is the way to go for sure! Cruised right in at 10 or 11 on a weekday and sat down immediately. 

As for the food, it's worth the hype (though maybe not an hour wait). I love getting the classic board with lox and a bialy. This is what people are talking about when they say no one compares to NY when it comes to bagels. The latkes are amazing as well and a very generous portion, with lots of sour cream and apple sauce. Those are the classics, of course, but I also really liked the pickled herring trio, which comes on little rye toast pieces. There's so much to choose from on the menu but it's hard to stray away from the classic favorites. Best to come with a group so you can try a bunch of things!

THE WAIT was LONG. But hey..I guess the wait is long at any trendy or hyped brunch place on the weekends. 

Absolutely loved the latkes which is why my review is where it is. Bagel is forgettable and tiny, boards aren't super impressive either. 

Definitely skip the line and head over the appetizer shop and eat it while walking through the LES/Soho.

Perfect smoked salmon, capers, red onion, tomato

For my gluten free friends....

Bonus is they have gluten free rye-bread and gluten free bagels

I finally had the chance to visit Russ & Daughter's after almost two years of wanting to go there -- I ventured to the cafe alone since the bf was at work (and it probably wouldn't have been worth it for him). I came in around 11:30 on a Wednesday in July, and it was pretty packed. Even though I was by myself, I had to wait around ~30 minutes to get seated at the counter. I did some research and decided on the cafe rather than the original store on Houston because I wanted to sit and enjoy my meal. The wait is longer at the cafe, though! 

The staff is super friendly, and I ordered the Classic Board, which comes with a toasted bagel (I got the everything bagel), cream cheese, smoked salmon, onions, tomatoes, and capers. For what you get, the price is a bit hefty ($16) but the meal was so delicious and I'd been wanting to come for so long that it was worth it. 

Since I was by myself, I wasn't able to try out any of their other dishes, but I definitely want to come back! Probably not great for people who are starving and looking for something super hefty and hearty, but perfect for me!

Came for brunch on a Monday and only waited 15 mins to be seated. Overall great experience!
Matzo ball soup- delicious!
Smoked white fish chowder- amazing!
Potato latkes with wild salmon roe and creme fraiche- really good!
Eggs Benny with smoked salmon- nothing special
Blintzes- just ok
Strong coffee

We had breakfast here. Had to wait in rain about 20 mins. Well worth it. Gaspe Nova was superb, best we have had. Sliced as thin as I've seen. Bagel and scallion cream cheese were super fresh. So good we ordered some online when we got home.

As a Russian Jew, I found this place felt like going home to me. Everything we had was so delicious--the borscht, the chopped liver, the lox and bagel, the pickles, the latkes. I would eat it all again. The cocktails were also really excellent. Authentic, delicious, wonderful. With a reservation for dinner it was no problem at all. I would gladly return (though I think my non-Jewish husband would probably take a pass).

A little pricey but all the food is delicious. We had the the bagel toast, the classic bagel and lox, the cinnamon babka toast, and the eggs benny. Be prepared to wait for a table, though, and make sure all your party is present or they won't seat you.

I went here on a recent trip back to New York and was pretty impressed. I think everyone always hears about the great jewish delis New York used to have and wants to try the food. But the original Russ & Daughters location can get cramped and there's nowhere nearby to really eat. Having this separate restaurant lets people sit down and enjoy the classics they've heard so much about. I went on a Tuesday morning for breakfast with a friend - so your mileage may vary on getting a table. I got the chopped chicken liver and a classic lox board. My friend ordered the bread basket (she's eccentric) which was actually quite a deal. All the breads were fresh and the bialy was really good. The chicken liver was really good - fatty and flavorful without being overpowering - however the dry matzo it came with should be substituted if possible. Smearing mine on my friends leftover challah and pumpernickel made it a lot better. The Classic Board was great too - everything you need for a proper bagel and lox. I also found the space really gorgeous and the staff was fairly attentive. Coffee refills kept coming and it was good. I'd recommend coming here for anyone visiting New York and wanting to try some of those classics they hear about - there aren't many places left that do them. I'm sure I'll be back on return visits. It would have been very easy for this place to just coast by on reputation alone - the fact that it's a solid restaurant that could stand on its own merits is the real treat.

Ambiance: A+. They really captured my Jewish grandfather's favorite diner in 1954-if my grandfather's diner had a gourmet chef at the helm and liked to experiment with caviar. This is the perfect place to bring out-of-town family trying to get a taste of Jewish New York. The "Sweet" portion of the menu was a favor journey down memory lane. I look forward to tackling the rest of the menu in future visits. Service was fast and prices were reasonable for the trendy, expensive area.

We decided to give this place a try because we love the original so much. It did not disappoint. The food selection was amazing, the bagels were top drawer, the borscht was vibrant, The matzo ball soup was divine, and the rest of our food was incredible. Even the cocktails were great. The atmosphere reminded me of an old style chophouse or fish house, which is perfect for what we wanted that day. The only complaint I have is about the service. Neither the bartender nor the server was very friendly, and the server was not very attentive. Fortunately, we had a good busser to help us out.

Loved the atmosphere and the cafe itself. The food was amazing, the staff is clean, well-dressed and the spot is very well-maintained. Great option when you're in the mood for a bagel but cannot make the hours of the original R&D. I had The Classic which was really delicious, wish they could be a little more generous with the salmon, tasted great!

My partner and I both got the egg and salmon locks with rye bread. I got an everything bagel on the side as well (definitely a must-try!!) since they're so well known for their bagels. Their coffee is superb, and the food was excellent (the dressing on the side salad is delicious). The inside of the restaurant is very inviting with high arched ceilings and a nifty bar at the entrance. Prices are pretty high, but perfect for a fancy brunch.

Came here for a late lunch on a Monday. It was quiet, which I appreciated. (This place is abuzz otherwise). Ordered some things to share: Knish, salad, salmon on a pretzel roll, and salmon and poached eggs. One of the orders came with a side of latkes. Everything is to die for. The knish was soft and pillowy, went very well with their homemade mustard. The latkes are huge, crisped on the outside. The salmon packs a lot of flavor --their pastrami salmon especially but honestly it's all very good. We also tried their homemade sodas, very refreshing flavors though a little on the sweet side (which I guess is to be expected with sodas).  The space itself is very lovely and the staff are  wonderful --Timely, accommodating, very nice and knowledgeable about the menu.

Everything about this place is great. Each dish is made with interesting, fresh ingredients and packed with SO MUCH FLAVOR! The staff very nice. The decor fresh&clean. The sparkling water free!! ;D 

Tip: go Sunday evening to avoid the line. #bagel #salmon #lox #datenight #sunnysideup #egg #breakfast for #dinner #dinnerdate #fish #soup #wasabi #tobikko #nyc #les #brunch
Best breakfast I've ever had. I don't like bloody Mary's, but my spouse got the caraway infused vodka one and I couldn't stop drinking it. Caviar was incredible and the herring was off the hook.

I wanted to be adventurous so I got the Super Heebster plus an order of three latkes with apple sauce and creme fraiche. The regular Heebster is $10 and it is the size of an english muffin (there is the large sandwich version also). Sadly, it tasted average and salty, much like tuna on toast, which isn't bad, but tuna on toast is as plain as it gets. The latkes were quite nice--crunchy and chewy. 

If I come back, I'd go for a classic bagel with salmon so I know what I'm getting in to. My favorite thing here is the Break-Fast Margarita. It smells like black licorice, which is gross, but contains absinthe, it tastes like lemonade, and it will hit you before you know it :)

Every time we've gone in to eat, The hostess has made me want to leave. She's rude and should just quit her existence cuz she's just trash at what she does and with her personality. It's been twice that I've been stuck with her depressed face and it's cuz of those two times we've left.

Had fish sticks, pickled herring, mushroom barley and whitefish chowder for meal, noodle kugel and chocolate babka toast for dessert.
The whitefish chowder was my favorite among the food. 
It's good to mention that the noodle kugel is extremely mild for American standards of sweets. I recommend eating it right after the salty, before any other sweets.

the ambience is very cool but the food is MEH. Everything I ordered - including the knishes and latkes - needed an extra dose of flavour. They should consider adding sauteed onions or seasoning or something to the knishes and latkes. I love simple comfort food but this was plain and lacked thoughtfulness.

I love having brunch at this place!  The food and atmosphere is great! The only downside could be the wait but you can always avoid that by going earlier.  

I've tried the classic board and the potatoes latkes with wild salmon roe and creme fraiche.  The classic board is a deconstructed nova lox that you put together yourself.  The salmon is fresh and it went perfect with the everything bagel I chose.  I also really liked the potatoes latkes from the appetizer selection.  It is crispy on the outside, but soft on the inside.  The salmon roe gave it great flavor as well because the salmon roe gives a bit of saltiness.  

I would definitely recommend this place when you want a classy brunch.

Russ & Daughters cafe is where breakfast/brunch/lunch dreams go to die. The wait times are frequently an hour+, and they are very ill equipped to handle the crowds. There's not really a seating area for those waiting (with the exception of two window bench seats that can hold five people each at most), resulting in terrible congestion at the front of the restaurant and a terrible dining experience for those eating up front near the crowds. They do have a good system for texting people so you can walk around the neighborhood, but it only works as long as the weather isn't miserable outside. 

The food itself is pretty good, but ultimately not really worth a lot of the hassle. Parts of the menu also seem deliberately and almost hilariously unattainable: anything with caviar starts at $50+. Service is spotty, if down right awful at times. Waiters will forget orders or disappear for the entirety of the meal, only to present you with a check at the very last moment. 

Overall: I'd be more willing to recommend this place if we were only judging by the food and the interior decor. And at the end of the day, it still makes for one pretty good Instagram photo.

Finally made it here after all the times I wanted to try it and there were two hour waits on weekends. Lucky for us, we got to come here on a Tuesday for lunch. There was a five minute wait but we got seated pretty quickly. Service is pretty prompt and friendly. We were served complimentary sparkling water. They took our order and the food came pretty quick. We ordered the classic and the herring plate. The classic came with a toasted Bagel (or bialy). Tomatoes, onions and capers along with some smoked salmon. Fresh and good. We prob could have used a few extra slices of the salmon though for the price they were charging ($16). The herring was good. I think I actually like the herring better. It was cured with salt and the other was cured with sugar. And there were two herrings that were rolled up in onion and vinegar. Served with pumpernickel toast and three different dips. Tasty. Would I come back? Perhaps if I was being lazy and wanted to pay $16 for a Bagel with a few slices of salmon. Annnnd...ONLY if there was NO WAIT.

Delicious!!! Must go! We went there late weekday morning, and were seated right away, by the time we left around lunch time it was packed. It's a good place for a brunch but go early. We ordered on of their boards with 4 different types of salmon. It came with pickled veggies, two different types of cream cheese, butter, a basket full of bread (plenty for 4 plp), lettuce, tomato, onions, capers. Everything was fresh and delicious. The ambiance is nice, cute lil place. Service is good. Loved it and will definitely go back. Stopped by their shop down the street, their original place and it was very cool too, lots to buy to go.

I've probably been giving too many 4-5 stars for places I went in new york, but they're all so good! This place definitely is worth it. I had 0 wait, and even though I was a solo diner they didn't treat me weird or anything. I had the classic lox, a herring, and some chicken liver. It was all beautiful and delicious. We don't have jewish deli food as good as this in California. I wish I could eat more!
PS I would highly suggest to the owners that they have a fish platter, where you can just pay x and get a bunch of different type of fish. That shit was so good. I will definitely come back here  if I'm in New York, and you should too!

It's a time machine, eye candy, and the tastes and smells I love.  Everything is so appealing it's hard to make a decisions but I did:  borscht that was puréed with lots of beet flavor but no tang--it need more sour cream/yogurt, a little pepper or salt and a squeeze of lemon, and the sturgeon board.  I asked the attentive waiter what the. difference was between sturgeon and sable.  He said sturgeon has a more earthy flavor so I tried it.  I might have been able to really taste it if there had been more than four small, sheer slices.  For $22, it just wasn't worth it.  My husband's lox and eggs were divine.  The wait was worth it and the staff was very solicitous.  It would help if the accessible door had been open; as it was, we knocked and a customer opened it.  We'll be back but no sturgeon and if the portion is too tiny, I'll speak up.

Came here for the classic lox bagel. It was amazing. It's a pretty hefty bagel considering how much salmon and cream cheese they give you but it is pricey at $16. Well worth the money though. It is the best smoked salmon I have ever had, there was zero fishiness to it, just a light smokiness and the butteriness of the fish itself. The cream cheese was whipped and pretty good, there were also some tomato slices, raw onion slices, and capers. Amazing! 

We also got the knishes which weren't that good. It was basically just boiled mashed potatoes with some good mustard on the side. $8, not worth in my opinion. 

Food came out really fast, service was a little slow.

Finally got to check this place off my bucket list! If you love smoked/cured fish and Jewish noshes you have to check it out!

There was an hour wait, as we expected since they don't take reservations, so we went elsewhere for a drink first and were texted when our table was ready. 

We came with a group of 5, which I definitely recommend doing so you can split a platter($90 divided between a group isn't that bad).  We had the Anne Platter, which came with Nova salmon, sturgeon, sable, trout, and salmon roe.  Also included were pickles, cream cheeses, tomato/onion/caper/etc., and a bread basket (challah, sliced breads, bagels).  We also got the "hot smoke / cold smoke" salmon spread with everything bagel chips, and an order of latkes.  For 5 people this was a feast...more than enough food for everyone.

INCREDIBLE. We ordered the chocolate babka French toast and the dish with latkes, eggs and salmon (can't recall the name) and it was all DELICIOUS! The french toast was honestly the best I've ever had. 
Do be warned, the wait is very long. Luckily for us, they told us our wait would be 1.5 - 1.75 hours, but our table was ready in less than 45 minutes!
If the wait is too long, check out the Russ and Daughters appetizers store on Houston, because you can get so much of the same food there for cheaper and without the wait. However, overall I loved the experience at the cafe and it is a MUST if you want some classic New York fare.

Great eastern European Jewish food. Latke is to die for. Loved it. Smoled salmon is also great. Staff is very friendly and attentive. There is usually 10 to 30 minutes wait. Nice clean modern yet classy touch to this place.
This review is solely based on their smoked salmon platter - it's as good as it gets. One of the original places to get smoked fish in NYC, this cafe doesn't not disappoint. The staff is lovely too.

We ate here after already trying their food at the location in the Jewish Museum which was amazing. The service there was great too, despite it being close to closing time. If this had been our first experience, we wouldn't have bothered to go to another.  Maybe it was the fact that the service was so lame that the food seemed less impressive. If this is the only location you can get to, then by all means, try it out. If you find yourself up near the museums (Met, Guggenheim, Cooer Hewitt) I'd recommend you go there (plus you can get baked goods there, unlike at the cafe.

I had ordered take out from Russ & Daughters before, but this was our first time at the Cafe.  Ordered the Classic with nova salmon.  DELICIOUS!!!  The wait is long, but if you know this and go prepared-not a problem.  They will call you when your table is ready so you can take a walk or just make new friends waiting.

Had to try R & D after reading the great reviews and had been itching for good lox while visiting NYC.  The good.  Great service, food came quickly and was very good tasting.  Had the Lox Board and an order of Potato Latkes.  Excellent and enough for two people.  The bad, and I hope the management reads this.  The seating host, a tall gentlemen with glasses has no business being in that job, and if he's not happy, your customers pay the price by making the experience less than 5 stars.  Your small waiting area is packed, tables popping  open as well as counter and he's just making people wait.  At first I thought maybe they were reserved, but after a few minutes, this guy just didn't care.  All of the others waiting like us, we were just looking at each other dumbfounded. People are pouring in and he's just saying "25-30 minutes" and not seating people.  I guarantee that this restaurant is losing a complete turnover of customer seating.  You need to send a mystery diner in there to see what's happening.  Other than this, everything was great.

The latkas were amazing and it was my first time eating them with salmon eggs. You really can't ruin lox and bagels. Their drinks were pretty tasty here. I got the breakfast martini and I have to say it had me feeling really good for this meal and afterwards. The bialy was nice and soft...something my late grandmother would have loved. The nova salmon was prepared well and melted in my mouth. Come here for some breakfast or lunch...it makes for a perfect start for the day

This is one of my favorite brunch spots in the city! Their throwback 50's diner vibe meets your Jewish grandmother's cooking is amazing!

Do yourself a favor and order the classic board. The gaspa nova is the best lox I've ever had! Pair it with the cream cheese, tomatoes, onions, and capers and I'm in heaven. The bialy was the only part that could use improvement.

The latkes were also amazing! They are very thick. So they were able to achieve a crispy crust without a greasy taste.

The only downside is the length of the wait. They don't accept reservations and my wait was 90 minutes last time.

This place gets all the stars. We've been two days in a row on our trip. The first day was a 20 minute wait on a Thursday mid morning, the second day was an hour at lunch time on a Friday. Still worth it both times. The hostess is really sweet even when she's being hounded by impatient and hungry customers. They have a good system where you leave your name and number and they text you when your table is getting ready. The service is fast and friendly. The Interior is so well done, clean lines and white tile throughout. The food is ...... amazing. I had the Yum Kippered board with kippered salmon a bagel and all the fixings, a bowl of matzo ball soup and their seasonal blueberry soda. Holy cow. So delicious. So satisfying. So worth the wait. The second day we got potato latkes and two more bagel boards.  If I lived in NYC, I'd be here a lot. Love this place.

I came to Russ & Daughters Cafe for one thing and one thing only: the lox. As you can tell by the 5-star rating, it did not disappoint. Listen, I was expecting the lox here to be amazing, but that heavenly piece of smoked salmon shattered my expectations. Even though I did enjoy pairing the lox with the bagel and cream cheese, I could honestly just munch on the lox itself. It's the star of the show and you'd be a fool to come to Russ & Daughters without trying it.

Talk about old school authentic!  Matzo Ball soup, amazing. The classic board ; smoked salman, cream cheese tomato and capers, potato latke... wow!!!.  A must do in the big Apple. And of course the service was great, friendly and helpful...

Well this wasn't the Russ & Daughters I wanted to eat at, but amidst the confusion we sat to enjoy breakfast on our last morning in NYC.  My sister loved her dish, salmon was super fresh and she said best hands down.  I am not a seafood fan, which is what the majority of their dishes are here.  Did find a veggie omelet that was very good with some goat cheese and got my bagel I really wanted.  The space is small but we didn't feel cramped at our table for sure.  Service was pretty good as well.

I came in for dessert but wow next time I'd definitely come back for brunch. The lady next me was having the beautiful lox and bagel plate and looked really good. 

I had a babka French toast and halva ice cream. Appropriate portion for desert. And my decaf coffee was never empty because the server paid attention to me so well. I was satisfied with their service. 

Can't wait to come back for fish! Lox! And those beautiful cocktails!

Let me preface this review by stating that I'll eat/try anything. Let me also state that I don't love salmon. Or even like it, really. I remember going to a restaurant once, maybe...14-15 years ago?...and the chef sent over a smoked salmon amuse bouche. Awful. I hated the front/during/after taste. As the next 14-15 years went on, I tried it every now and again (never ordering it on my own, but sampling someone else's preparation of it). Nope, still don't like it.

That brings us to July of 2017. Up to this point, I had heard so much about Russ & Daughters (all good things!) and was itching to try it. July 2017, I'm in New York. My friend and I wait 45 minutes to get a table. We order a few things to split, one of them being the salmon platter. I figured that she would eat my half of the salmon portion if I ended up not liking it.

Let me tell you, my friends. No salmon-sharing happened. I. Ate. My. Own. ALL OF IT.

It was amazingly delicious. Everything bagel, cream cheese, tomato, capers, red onion, salmon...AH! Just listing all of that out makes me want to eat it again at this very second. It was ridiculously good, and more ridiculous than that is the fact that I WAS EATING AND LIKING SALMON. 

Other honorable mentions:

The cold borscht was very tasty, though as a product of Eastern European lineage, I find that I typically prefer my borscht hot. Still, super yummy.

The latkes -- YUM! So hearty, crispy, and tasty. Well done, R&D. 

The service was warm and welcoming, and the decor was quaint and charming. 

I'm already dreaming of the day I go back to eat a salmon platter of my very own. HSH (hey, salmon, heeeeeeey)!

A bit pricey, but lovely.  An old-school diner feel, serving classic Lower East Side Jewish fare (which overlaps sizably with classic diner fare, and with classic brunch fare) plus some interesting standouts.

The classics include smoked fish boards -- salmon or sturgeon or sable, tomatoes and onions and capers, cream cheese or butter, some sorta tasty bread.  If you like this sort of thing, you can't go wrong here.  They have individual boards (less than $20) or large platters meant for three to four people that go for $80-90 and come with an eye-catching assortment of all of the above, and then some.  (The platters are named after the eponymous Daughters--Hattie, Ida, and Anne--aka The Sturgeon Queens.)

Some interesting standouts:

* Halva ice cream.  If you like halva, this is a must-have.  If you don't know what halva is, this is as fine an introduction as any.  If you don't like halva... I don't know, man.

* House-made sodas.  These are just syrup with seltzer, but each has a teeny twist of sophistication.  For example, the lemon-line soda layers in flavors of anise, dill, and cardamon. That seems like it should be off or too much, but was refreshing, and I don't even like anise.

(One heart-crushing thing to be aware of: the famed babka ice cream sandwich is "a summer thing", according to our waitress.  I don't understand this menu madness, but it is what it is.)

We came here after fasting for Yom Kippur.  The Cafe opened off-schedule for the holiday, at 5pm, and a small line had formed outside the door by 4:45pm.  Russ & Daughters brought out smoked salmon canapés for the folks in line--a lovely way to break a fast.  Service was solid to great throughout.  

Thumbs up.
Great matzo ball soup. Lox was outstanding. Could only have been better if the bagels had been fresh and if they had not charged 1.50 for an extra tablespoon of applesauce!

Came by on a Wednesday at noon to no wait for counter seating. Here's the assessment. Is this spot a NYC staple? Yes. Is the food off the chain? Hell yes. Should that give them the right to charge 20 bucks (with tax and tips) for 3 pieces of lox, a bialy, cream cheese, and some vegs? Uhh questionable. I meannn, I get it. Your foods good. But $20 for a lox cream cheese bialy?! That's excessive. 

But let's talk about the restaurant itself. Super cute. Modern diner feel. Was planning to go to the deli, but good thing I didn't. It was nuts in there (up a few blocks frm the cafe). I had a much better lunch experience at the cafe. The deli is a grab and go. This is a sit down. 

I went to a few other bagel and bialy spots during my visit, and they're just as good IMO, and don't charge nearly as much as Russ and Daughters does. Sooo there's that. Am I glad I tried this spot though? Yes. Should you come by and try it as well? Yes. Will I come back again? Maybe to try something else. 4 stars.

Full disclosure: I am Jewish. I LOVE Jewish food and it reminds me of home. 

I finally had the chance to try out this institution with a friend who loves herring as much as I do.
There was an about 20-30 minutes wait, the hostess took my phone number and said I can go and they will text me when they are ready to have us, and we will have 10 minutes to come back. WOW! so brilliant, easy, shows a ton of respect towards the costumers. I wish all restaurants would have done so. We spent our 20-something minutes buying candy at Economy Candy on Rivington st, then when we got the text we headed back and were sited immediately. The waitress who took care of us was the nicest!

We ordered a three mains to split - the herring platter, the smoked salmon bagel and the Sturgeon and what can I say that hasn't been said before? Everything was delicious and fresh, you can't ask for a better quality. We also ordered one Matzo-ball soup for the two of us just to get a taste of it, and the waitress split it to two little bowls without even asking us, so we didn't have to eat it together awkwardly. 

The house coffee is good and free refill! yay!

I love this place because it is so unpretentious. They manage to keep the vibe relaxing and pleasant even though the lines are long and they could have easily gone blind by how popular the place is. Yet, they have not. The food is fresh, the prices are reasonable and the crew is welcoming. I felt very valuable as a costumer there. 

Can't wait to go back again & again & again and sample the all manu!

This lox lover could not have been happier to dine at Russ & Daughters! Was my eggs and bacon fiancee just as happy? Maybe not, but he left satisfied in the end.

It was a Friday morning and even at 11:00 am, the wait was almost an hour long. Thankfully, they take your phone number and text when your table is ready, so you're free to pop into a bar or coffeeshop nearby while you wait. We eventually landed a seat at the bar and were ravenous. 

We started with the latkes which were among the best I've had. They were thick and piping hot. Great when paired with the sour cream and apple sauce. From there, I got the classic board which came with lox, a bagel (everything, please!), tomato, onions, capers, and cream cheese. There's a reason why people call these the best lox they've had. They simply are! My fiancee got the cinnamon babka French toast which he devoured. 

The bartenders were our servers and they certainly had a lot on their plates so I didn't feel super taken care of, and our order got a little wrong but they were quick to correct. 

I'm happy I had the experience. I probably wouldn't rush back and opt for their grab-and-go spot instead; however, it was worth the wait this once for fish lovers like me!

This restaurant interior is so quaint. They really did a good job decorating. 

This is the kind of place I would bring a small group of friends too if everyone likes fish. 

That being said, the menu is dense, but all contain fish. I wish there was a little bit more selection. 

On this occasion, I sat at the bar. I ordered the eggs Benedict, and it was delicious. 
(But also priced high)
Random note to the restaurant: your barstool second from the end is very uncomfortable and is inconveniently placed too close to the farthest stool. 

I was happy with my food and with the service.

Came to NY for business and decided to stay to watch the game and venture a bit. Found this place on the way from Katz Deli and decided to try it. This is probably the best bagel I've ever had in MY EXISTENCE. The smoked Irish salmon had a delicious light smoke flavor and melts like butter. Just amazing....they filmed an episode of Louie here and always wanted to try it but couldn't remember the name. A definite must try if you're venturing in NYC!

The boyfriend and I came here on a Tuesday for lunch and it was packed!. We were told it was roughly a 20-30 minute wait. I gave the hostess my number and we took a walk around the neighborhood. Within 15 minutes we received a text and made out way back. We were seated at the counter, served our water and looked over the menu. I order the shtetl platter with a everything bagel and latkes and he orders the herring trio. Everything came to us at once and looked amazing. The sable was buttery, latkes crisp and herring was right amount of salty and sweet. I wasn't a big fan of the bagel and the latke needed some salt. But I will be back to try the rest of the menu.

This is what NYC is to me. Amazing Lox and Bagels in a low key, trendy clean environment with an unfortunate 2 hour wait time for brunch. 

So try to skip the two hour wait and came on an off-time for some much needed light nosh and Matzo Ball Soup to get over my jet-lag/funk. This soup is sooo amazing. 

Things to Note:
1) This place is always busy anytime of the day but weekend brunch is insane.
2) Potato Latkes with Wild Salmon Roe and creme fresh. SOO GOOD.
3) Lots of different boards to try and share. 
4) Shahakshouka is probably my favorite Israel breakfast type dish with Northern African Spices - but it's made with lamb here vs. vegetarian.
5) Very nice people and I'm just generally surprise when I have service like this in a cafe style environment. 

This is honestly where you take your out of town friends for that little bit of the NY institution lifestyle. Or let's keep this a secret from all the damn tourist.

Visited for brunch, hostess told us it would be a 30 minute wait, in fact we only waited 15 minutes. The breakfast was delicious. We had Knishes to share, my wife had the Classic board(smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers, bagel) and I had the Eggs Benny(salmon, spinach, eggs, hollandaise on challah). Everything was very fresh, the portions were ample and everything tasted great. The service was attentive and the atmosphere was outstanding. This place has a great style and great food. A unique experience and a must try.

Hands down the best breakfast in the City. I make it a point to visit for breakfast each time I'm in town - the lox and bialys are the best I've ever had. Cocktails are tasty, service is friendly and prompt. Good always arrives super fast. Definitely worth the stop in.
One of the best Lox and Bagels & motza Ball soups I've had. Definitely recommend if you like Lox!!

Wonderful Jewish Deli in a cafe setting. From the smoked salmon to the herrings, potato latkes with sour cream & applesauce, pickles, bagels, matzo ball soup and delicious desserts, we were in heaven! The service was excellent, especially our hostesses, Jill & Bianca who couldn't have been more kind & professional. Be prepared for a long wait for a table and at the counter  but the wait is so worth it!

WOW! Just.....wow. Every good adjective comes to mind when thinking about the food here. Scrumptious. Delicious, Spectacular. Mouthwatering. I would wait endless hours for their food. I went here for lunch the other day and got the latkes with creme fraiche and salmon roe with a side of lox. The latkes were perfectly crisp on the outside, yet bursting with flavor and softness on the inside. Combined with the creme and the roe, it was absolutely spectacular. This is what Jewish food is. I also had a Bloody Mary, and I usually am very judgmental about my Bloody Mary's,  but this one was amazing! A perfect combination of vodka and spices/tomato juice. If I didn't have class later that day, I would have had more than one! Will absolutely be making Russ and Daughter's a staple of my dining choices!

We visited here for brunch. Got the pickled herring trio, white fish chowder soup, and the classic. I've got to say the classic was a hit, that smoked salmon, the flavor was on point- just delicious ...personally i didn't prefer the pickled herring. Soup was alright..

I enjoyed the overall atmosphere.
I'm not even going to go into details but this place rocks as long as you're into your smoked fish and Jewish comfort food.  The space is well designed and service is perfectly executed.
Service was good. Bagel was mediocre to bad, which is unacceptable especially considering there are many great bagels to choose from in NYC.

Great place if you like fish! Came here for dinner with a friend and the wait was about 5 minutes. I had the Cobb salad and my friend had the eggs benny. The Cobb salad had fish in it and I found some bones and fish scales while eating my salad (minus one star). Overall, the atmosphere was good and the waitress was very friendly. I would come back again to try something else!

The best bagels and lox I've ever had! Originally I was looking for the original Russ and Daughters, however by chance I ended up at the cafe. Such a charming cafe with wonderful staff and excellent food.

Delicious lunch worth the slightly insane wait 
The staff were super nice and the food was unreal. 
Eating at this cafe is like sitting in the 1920's and the menu is incredible. The herring is a MUST.

While expensive and with a queue that can extend up to 3 hours, this historic café definitely delivered in quality food. I've heard to never order an eggs benedict at a restaurant but would happily order it here. The eggs were poached to perfection and the hollandaise sauce was delicious. The real star of the show was the Halvah Ice cream. Not too sweet and with just the right amount of texture, the Halvah ice cream served as our appetizer and an excellent start to the meal. Come here for hype and delicious food. Don't come here if you want to get seated immediately.

After visiting the original location to take out some of the famous lox bagel, I felt obligated to try the dine-in location as well.
This place has more of the real Jewish dishes that you heard about, but never dared to try.

From Latke to Motze all the way up to caviar. All the goodness of smoked fish and heavy Jewish cuisine can be found here. 
A lot of the time you will not be lucky to get in as there's a wait, even for bar seating.

I had the luck to get in rather quickly at 1 pm for a lunch but if you really commit to try, walk in between 4 and 6.

The smoked fish is just as good as the original location. I have tried some of the other dishes but it just wasn't to my taste.

I would prefer going to the original one if you are okay with eating outside or staying close by so you can enjoy this amazing culture well.

Amazing breakfast joint.  Best breakfast place for nova lox and latkes.  Kids can get French Toast and it isnt soaked in cheap maple flavored syrup.  Throw back Jewish deli breakfast menu.  Great alternative to the line at their storefront  if you have time for a leisurely breakfast.  Ambiance is awesome as well.  50s era diner vibe.

Went today with a guest from Australia for breakfast. After 30 min into the meal , the waitress started to
Bother us to take off the dishes while we were eating. My guest ordered another dish and after an hour and twenty min, the hostess came to our table saying that she wants to bring the bill and they are used to people eating fast and leaving... We said , an hour and twenty min is normal to have breakfast with few dishes and she said we are not used to this. We payed our bill and left but told many others to avoid this Touristic trap , with high prices and they treat you like an ATM !!!

Russ and Daughters' store was very crowded when we walked in, so we figured for the wait, we might as well get a sit-down meal at the Cafe a few blocks away. That was my first choice anyway, but sadly, the cafe was disappointing. While the atmosphere was super cute and retro feeling, the food was no better than any other Jewish deli (hi, Wise Sons Delicatessen in SF or Saul's in Berkeley, CA!). In fact, I'd say it was one of the less delicious of the lox plates I've had of late. My fiance and I both had the lox plate - one with a bialy and one with a bagel. Both bread components were bone dry, and the salmon and accoutrements were nothing to write home about. They have cute homemade sodas but it was not worth the long wait to get in (they can text you when your table is ready but you have about 10 minutes to get back to the restaurant before they give your table away).

We were here a few weeks ago for brunch with our 2 month old.  The service was good.  The food was great.  Huge bonus points for the large family bathroom with great changing table!  Space is obviously at a premium in the city and it was so nice to be able to change the baby comfortably!  Matzoh ball soup was nice. And eggs benny were cooked perfectly!

3.5 stars
The wait is insane, we were quoted an hour and 45 minute wait, though to be fair it was prime brunch time on a Saturday. 

After we finally got in, we orders the hot smoke cold smoke appetizer, and I ordered the lower sunny side for my entree, which came with eggs sunny side up, latkes, and smoked salmon. The hot smoke cold smoke was good, and went especially well with  the bagel chips.

The lower sunny side was solid comfort food, though the latkes were enormous and rather thick while the outside was a little bit too hard for my liking. Smoked salmon was good, but there were only a few slivers of it on my plate. I also tried some matzo ball soup (for the first time) which I was fan of for sure and tasted just like a warming bowl of chicken noodle soup. 

For dessert we were seduced by the honey cake, which in reality, was a glorified spiced muffin. Quite small as well for the price. All in all, not a bad experience, and would come back if the wait wasn't so ridiculously long.

With the exception of the hostess rushing a very obviously pregnant woman out of the restaurant who was simply waiting for someone in her party to get out of the bathroom, I would say I had a good experience.  

Dear restaurant manager: the date of this occurrence was 11/24/17 at Approximately 2:30 pm.
Cozy, classic interior with friendly yet attentive service. Delicious, nourishing comfort food.
Great food! Good for all times of the day. Staff is really nice. Cozy atmosphere. Sometimes there's some waiting but it worths it :)

I do very much appreciate some smoked fish on bagels. It's always been a morning staple of mine. The potato latkes was impressive. Not super oily with just the right amount of crunch. Cocktails were endearing. Usually I would have done coffee but I felt to try a cocktail and went with their martini. We got the platter as there were 4 of us and I do recommend if you are with a group. I mean, why not? Perfect time to sample everything. Service was a little spotty but overall experience was nice.

Personally the food, nor the service, were worth the 45-minute wait for ONE SEAT AT THE COUNTER. Having visited the LES many times, the constant lineup at both the Russ & Daughters cafe and the store piqued my curiosity. So, on a Tuesday, just before noon I figured I wouldn't have too long to wait - and boy was I wrong. I was honestly hoping for just a bagel and lox, though the cafe doesn't have that option. So instead, I got the dish with the latkes, the lox and 2 eggs. Admittedly, the latkes were AMAZING and the lox was pretty great, but worth the wait? Hardly. Worth a try if you don't have too long to wait. Otherwise, there are so many other amazing places in the LES, and NYC in general to waste time in line here.

Food was great, but the wait was shocking. Granted, we did happen to go on a Saturday during the height of brunch time, but still, an hour and 45 minute wait is outrageous.

We started off with the hot smoke and cold smoke dip, which was amazing. I could not get enough of it, and I thought the portion size was surprisingly good as well. I also ordered the eggs benny. Eggs Benedict is usually pretty indulgent, but the smoked salmon and challah on the Russ & Daughters eggs benny was even more indulgent than usual. 

At the end of our meal, we were also enticed by the honey cake, which was actually pretty disappointing because it was more of a muffin topped with ice cream.

Ultimately, a great place and I would definitely return -- hopefully at a time when the wait isn't so insane.

Exceptionally rude staff and outrageous policies. After waiting 2 hours for a table (ps: I'm 8 months pregnant), they tried to kick me and my party out of the restaurant mid-meal because they found out I had a fish allergy. There were plenty of non-fish options on the menu for me to choose from so I didn't have an issue finding something to eat. When I asked them to show me language on the website or a sign in the restaurant that indicates they don't serve people with food allergies, they couldn't provide me with one and kept insisting they wouldn't serve us. After we refused to leave, the manager sniped "if you get sick, just know its on you" and walked off. 

Most restaurants bend over backwards to accommodate those diners with food allergies. I've never been told to leave a restaurant mid-meal. Will not come back nor recommend this restaurant to any of my friends - many of whom have food allergies! 

Date of occurrence 11/24/17 @ 2:00.

Pricey but delicious.  Nice, helpful staff.  Had one of the assorted smoked salmon platters (said to serve 2-3) but shared it among 5 of us along with latkes and some other delicious thing that I can't remember right now.   We went for a late lunch (2-ish) on a Tuesday - no wait.

First stop of my long overdue visit to NYC. Was this worth it? I'd say sure, must try at least once. Good food, nice 1920s interior, interesting wall decor which is also found in the washrooms and NO insane wait as I have been told it gets crazy!

My friends and I made a visit on a weekday afternoon just probably after the afternoon rush. We were seated approximately after a 5 minute wait and there were also empty booths that had just left. We were served water quickly, which was great and our server took our orders shortly after. We were hungry after a long flight delay and we were glad to be seated and served quickly. No complaints with the service!

Our orders: 
2 classic boards (Smoked salmon, Cream Cheese, Bagel/Bialy)
Eggs Benny (Poached eggs, smoked salmon, spinach, hollandaise sauce)
Lower sunny side (Smokes salmon, sunny side eggs, potato latkes)

I have to say the presentation of all 3 dishes were nice and clean and picture worthy. The one dish which I thought was more of value and quality was the eggs benny...It just looked yummy and satisfying.
The other dishes looked good but pretty much what you would expect on a wooden board or plate. 
Our meals generally tasted great, maybe also because we were deprived of food...Was the lox and bagel worth $17...Mmm not sure about that...

I would definitely give it a try if you are in NYC (especially with all the hype) but for next time I will just get the lox bagel at the cafe as I am told it is more of a grab'n'go kind of thing.

P.s I really like the "number ticket" wall paper in one of the washrooms...Unique idea!

I came here with a party of 4 on a Saturday morning at 9:30am and the wait was 45min- 1 hour... I was actually surprised since 9:30am is considered early for a New Yorker. To pass the time, we waited at a coffee shop across the street. By the time we came back around 10:30, the wait for other parties was 1.5 hours.

When we were finally seated, we ordered the Ida platter that serves 3-4 people. It had 4 different types of salmon for us to try alongside with toppings and bagels/bread. I would definitely recommend this option for those who want to try a bit of everything! The slices were extremely fresh and rich. 

I would recommend this place for sure, but I probably won't be back anytime soon as the wait for this place is so long and there are other delicious places around the area.

Every time I'm in NYC I make sure to grab breakfast at Russ & Daughters Cafe. I enjoy the service, the atmosphere, and I really love a delicious bagel with pastrami salmon.

As others have mentioned there can be a wait, especially on the weekend. I typically go around 10am during the week and have never waited longer than 15 minutes. 

I always get the bagel board that comes with whipped goat cheese and swap in pastrami salmon, so yummy. My husband and I will usually also share an order or the latkes. The latkes are thicker than most people expect but they're seasoned well and cooked to perfection - I recommend the sour cream and apple sauce combo.

I'm not a huge fan of their coffee, but their sodas are super delish.

Is this place pricy, yes. Is the service great and the decor on point, yes. I love this place and don't mind dropping the extra cash for greatness.
I really like the whitefish chowder and latkas, this place is great. Really like the atmosphere and connecting with some good Jewish food! Thanks!

Had to show my boo the food of my peoples so came here during our trip to NY. He loved it! The whitefish on a bagel with wasabi caviar and wasabi creme fraiche is legit! Got a shrub soda (can't remember which one) and enjoyed it thoroughly. Only thing we didn't rant and rave about, surprisingly, was the lox plate. It's beautiful for instagram but we both agreed the lox had very little flavor. Maybe we ordered the wrong kind, but the flavor was way too subtle for our liking. Would be willing to try again though since they had numerous varieties and I'm sure we'd find something we'd like better.

A sit-down offering of the famed counter location serving Jewish cured fish specialties. Probably not the cheapest out there but the quality and reputation is partly what you're paying for. If you're ordering latkes, go for the salmon roe and creme fraiche.

Russ & Daughters is definitely worth the wait! I went at 12:30 on a Thursday and we had an hour long wait, which was a bit absurd, but well worth it. We ordered a matzah ball soup, chopped liver, the classic plate, and latkes. The matzah ball soup was delicious!! Compared to Kat's down the road this one is much better considering there are chicken and veggies in the broth. My boyfriend devoured the chopped liver and said it was some of the best he's ever had!! The latkes were not bad, I think they were a tad bit overcooked, but not terrible. 
My only issue with the meal was the $17 bagel with lox. Granted the lox were the best tasting lox I've ever had, we were only given 2 thin pieces, all on a mediocre bagel. If the bagel were better I'd say $27 was worth it, but it was just a pretty okay bagel with really excellent toppings.

We drove to New York for a "food trip" on a Saturday morning. I should have gotten us a reservation because the wait time was ridiculous. We had to wait an hour to get seated so call in advance and get reservations because this pace gets busy. 

My girlfriend and I shared the classic bagel which is basically smoked salmon and we picked scallion cream cheese and everything bagel. We shared a bagel because we were going to another place for lunch right after but if you are coming here for brunch then I say get one for yourself. 

I was first hesitant/shocked that a bagel would cost $17 but it was worth it. The bagel had the perfect texture and the salmon was so good. I loved the scallion cream cheese and it also came with onions, tomatoes and capers. They have a variety of cream cheese including plain, goat cheese, tofu cream cheese and few more that I can't remember. I enjoyed every bit of it.

Th service was great. Everybody was super friendly and nice. They do not rush their guests which is a good thing but can become problematic when the line is so long  and the interior gets crowded. The place is also neat.

Was it worth the hype? Yes but will I come back? Probably not because its expensive just for a bagel and the wait is way too long. However it's a one time must try place.

I'm not sure if it was just that day but the bathroom smelled bad/was dirty  like I couldn't use the restroom because the smell made me nauseous. I

2 hour wait for average food. Bought luxury caviar from Russ and Daughters store and did not Le me eat it in the restaurant. 
Bagel and lox was decent
Goat cream cheese not as good as normal cream cheese
Sturgeon fish was nothing special
Kugel was good
Halvah ice cream was good

Overall not worth the wait, overpriced, and catty staff

Spiritual. Fulfilling. Adventurous. Bold. Daring. I can use as many words as I need to in order to distract myself from analyzing the amount of food I eat at Russ and daughters. The wait is almost always an hour - today is was 90 min - but we have a good time walking around the neighborhood. It's the best meal in the world and the best place to have it which makes it arguably the best restaurant in the world.

Food was not good and service was worse than the food.   We waited for about 15 minutes to even get water.  The lox were ok the bagels had no flavor.  We ate at Katz deli and it was actually worth the hype.  Along with the board, we had a knish, the barley and mushroom soup, a blintz, and a latke.  The only thing we liked pretty well was the barley and mushroom soup and the latke was ok.  Totally underwhelming for a huge price tag.

4 stars for the matzo ball soup. This is a very cute and photogenic place. Wait was a big long for New Year's Day. Didn't expect it to be packed but everything was fresh. I especially loved the matzo ball soup. I also got the classic platter (lox, cream cheese, onions, tomatoes, capers and choice of bread. I got the everything bagel). Nothing really blew my mind or stood out from the platter. I think next time I'll try a fish spread. But for sure coming back for the matzo ball soup. Highly recommend.

Great cafe.  Really enjoyed our breakfast/brunch last weekend.  It's a really busy place so get your name on the list and expect a wait unless you get there early.  The atmosphere is nice and the food is excellent.  The staff was attentive and nice.  Even though it was busy we didn't feel rushed.  The latkes were excellent, the gaspe nova salmon was great, and the eggs and omelettes were prepared well.  All in all this is a great place!

Wow! What a meal! Had to wait about 40 mins on a Saturday afternoon and it was worth every minute. I'm in love with this cafe, we ordered the chopped liver, borscht, matzo ball soup, salmon plate, and the lox, eggs, & onion dish. Everything was AMAZING!!! You will not regret coming here, it's on the pricier side, but worth the splurge.

We came here at like noon over the holidays (maybe the 28th?) on a random Thursday and the expected wait was 2 and a half hours. We ended up waiting about 1.5 hours which is apparently not the norm during the week but is during the weekend. 

Between three people we split an omelette with gaspe nova, the gaspe nova sandwich over rye, and a chocolate french toast. 

First off, the salmon is fucking fantastic, top tier, 5/5 would recommend to everyone. You have to try it. The capers, onions, and tomatoes come together and just blow your mind. 

The bagels are not that great. They're like... fine? but there are definitely better bagels in a 2 block radius imo. Clearly someone else likes the bagels and they're intentionally made that way, but I recommend getting the sandwich on something else. 

Omelette was pretty good, nothing mindblowing. Person with us said that the slightly warmer salmon on the omelette tasted richer but I didn't taste a difference.

Chocolate french toast was just alright, which is disappointing considering how good the salmon was. Fruit was a little sour and out of season, toast was a little dry. Wouldn't recommend. 

4/5, get the salmon and salmon related products.
Fantastic lox and a stunning place to enjoy it in. If you're heading there for brunch arrive ten mins before opening or you'll be waiting a while. Presentation is impeccable.

The food is great. I had the classic board and the bagel is so on point, chewy and fragrant. so good. Though this place was packed when we ordered but we didn't wait long for our food despite the crowd which is good.

Stopped here over the Holidays on a frigid morning with a party of 6, and luckily didn't have a long wait. My wife insisted on wanting a lox bagel, and this place seemed to be the winner (and was).

The food was delicious, and I'm not a huge cured fish kind of guy but thoroughly enjoyed my meal and the coffee. I wish I had a bigger appetite as everyone raved about their latkes and french toast.

The original NYC's Russ & Daughters Appetizing Store has been serving the best smoked fish in the US for more than 100 years.  It's a true must visit.  Located nearly next door to Katz's Deli creates the epicenter of New York's Jewish food culture and an unforgettable back to back noshing experience.  Russ & Daughters Cafe is what happens when the next generation takes over and merges the old with the new.  In this case it's the 4th generation of the Russ family finally giving their customers "a place to sit down".

The Cafe keeps all the flavors, charm, and heritage from the original R&D and apply it to a new expanded menu.  The smoked fish remains the star but it is part of an inventive dishes like whitefish chowder or pastrami cured salmon.  For the classic experience you can order the smoked fish platters which come with a bread choice and all the expected accompaniments.  If you are local it's a perfect meal.  If you don't get to visit often and you want to try multiple dishes you can order the not on the menu fish only boards to get the same flavors at half the size and price.  Their menu even expands past fish to include perfect potato pancakes and amazing chocolate babka french toast.  

Once you sit down this place lives up to the hype but unfortunately they don't take reservations.  Expect to wait even at odd times and like most places in NYC there is very little space to wait.   You are better off walking around this historic neighborhood while you wait which will make your eventual meal feel even more authentic.

If you haven't gone- GO! Best bagel and lox experience in the city. They don't take reservations, it's first come first serve so there is always a wait and it is worth it. I went this morning right when it opened and every seat was filled in about 15 minutes. This place has become a weekly Sunday staple for myself and friends and we're always satisfied with the standard board. The ambiance has a very authentic Jewish deli feel. Not to mention Russ and daughters is one of the oldest bagel and lox establishments in the city. If you want to venture and try more on the menu the latkes are amazing as well as the Babka French toast.

We were told our wait was 1 hr 20 min so we stopped by Supermoon nearby. We got a text saying our table was ready in about an hour so we were pleasantly surprised to be seated earlier than expected. My bf got the classic board (everything bagel, smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onions, capers) which he thoroughly enjoyed. I got the eggs benny which was served with sauteed spinach and challah french toast which was perfect! The salmon was flavorful and the challah added a really nice sweetness to the dish. We were in and out of there in under 40 minutes so their turnover rate is really quick (understandable for such a busy brunch spot). Good spot to try out if you've never been but not sure if I'd come back again for brunch (was just a little too busy for me).

Let me first start off by saying, I'm a big Jew, and not just in the high holiday sense. I grew up in a house full of Yiddish speakers, practice regularly and my identity is strongly linked to the heritage and flavors of the home. My great grandfather owned a clothing factory in the Village and used to get his fish from the main store back in the early 20th century. Quite some history to this place. The decor inside Russ & Daughters was nostalgic; photos of the original owners etc. Maybe  a little cliche with the manischevitz matzah boxes but I loved it. I've been here half a dozen times and although I eat a lot of these types of things regularly, they put their own spin. The latkes are thick and not too oily for all those concerned with health. I highly recommend the super heebster bagel, the classic board with the lox, onions and capers etc. Make sure to ask if they have the pickled herring, which is actually the whole fish and not the fillets. Finish it all off with an egg cream and you've got the perfect brunch. I cannot comment on the eggs, soups or deserts but I'm sure they're phenomenal. Looking forward to my next visit to this gem.

Yummmm! This classic comfortable cafe is a great place for brunch. Greeted warmly by the hostess- thanks for charging my phone!

Sat up at the counter/bar and shared a smoked salmon benny with kale and perfectly poached eggs on challah- sooooo good! Also had the blitzes with a blueberry compote and sour cream.

I can see why this is a local regular spot- I'd be mine too if I lived here!
Greatness all around. So glad we checked this out while back in NYC. Great food, great service, great atmosphere. Can't wait to come back!

This is my first time and probably would be my last. 
I only gave it two star cause the food wasn't bad. But the service was so bad, the staff was rude. The only nice people that work there are the cleaning guys and maybe the cooks ( maybe because they're behind the counter ). 
This is New York and it's 2018. Is it the first time your staff has seen an interracial couple ? It was too obvious what they're doing right in front of us as we eat our food. Maybe change the name to Russ & Bitches. 
So disappointed in it.

Amazing!!!! Worth the 40 min wait for the most incredible smoked salmon I've ever had and fish salad. No joke-we dream about this still. If there is one time to be super patient, it's here-worth it!!!

Great place for a Jewish feast if you have an hour or two to wait for a table. Very cute and old school scene inside with a long countertop seating area and white paper menus. I got the Lower Sunny Side, which came with some lox and latkes, and a side of knishes. The food was delicious, but can definitely be found at other places in NYC without the wait and at lower prices. I would definitely return if someone else wanted to go, but would probably not seek out another visit myself. Worth a try though!
Wow! So excited to come here. The food and service are amazing. It was so close to our hotel, we had to check it out. Get the potato latkes! You won't be disappointed.

We really enjoyed this place .
Looks like an old fashion pharmacy fountain .
Staff so sweet and deliver attentive service .
Food is all so good .
We were lucky to leave our name and took a 30 min walk & heard them call us upon our return .
Made it more enjoyable .
Really want to return , sometimes we see some R & D sandwiches , at the Plaza , in the market place downstairs , my friends grabs them delightfully .
Check it out , unique and a classic Jewish cafe .

We waited about a half hour for a table on a Friday afternoon and heard the hostess express that the wait is usually two hours. I must say, it was well worth the wait and one of the most pleasant dining experiences I had during my trip to NYC.
