We had knishes, pickles, the salmon pastrami, and the pickled herring. The first dish came out and it was delicious. Each time I didn't think it could get better, and it did. 

For something sweet, we ended with the chocolate babka French toast - which was incredible. I would like to end every meal with that treat.

While in town, I had to try an authentic deli.. Russ & Daughters came up several times when asking around. Friendly staff and great atmosphere. I ordered the "Classic" which included smoked salmon, capers, red onion, tomato, and choice of bread (I got the everything bagel). I was really impressed by the freshness and quality of the smoked salmon. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic lux.

Had The Classic with a bialy instead of a bagel - along with thinly sliced smoked salmon, cream cheese, capers, onions and dill.  The food was fresh, delicious, and just the right amount.  The service was excellent.  Loved the background music from the 50's and the overall ambience. I'd say this is a New York experience not to be missed.

Great atmosphere and food. We got there around 11 am on a Monday. It was crowded but the kind host was able to seat our two top quickly near the front. Loved the decor and menus, although there was a cold gust of wind every time the door opened, which was often. 
The service wasn't great, our server wasn't very friendly and seemed hurried, although it was moderately busy and he probably had a lot going on. The food was great. I got the classic with pumpernickel bread, and it was soooo good. Fresh tomato and plenty of onion. The presentation was beautiful and the smoked salmon light and delicious. The coffee was good and they immediately offer regular or sparkling water, which I appreciate. The water service is nice too. 
I would definitely recommend this place and I can't wait to go back next time I'm in town. I would love to go later in the day and try some of their cocktails.

Great atmosphere and friendly, attentive staff. We shared the lox platter with an everything bagel (toasted). It was the perfect portion and the salmon had a beautiful mild smoky flavor. Everything was sensational. One of the best breakfasts I've had. This is an effortlessly relaxed, no fuss type of place. Highly recommend and will return when back in NY.

I really wanted to like this place. Unfortunately we found the food just OK and the wait to get a table too long. Service is uneven (we were not offered a choice of sparkling or still water until we asked for more water, we were not offered a choice of bagel with our lox plate by our waitress even though we realized later there were different ones to pick).

Would have been a five but the service was the worst ever.  The white fish salad was fresh, tasty and filling. I did not need the side pumpernickel bagel but it was yummy.  My husband ordered the lox, eggs & onions. He said eggs were very good. It came with/a salad, which was not mentioned on the menu. The so called toasted bread was barely warm. A great place for tourists.
It's like the theme park is better than the movie.  Don't miss out on the cocktails or the borscht.  Very curious about the large format platters.

this place has been on my NY-Deli list for some time and I was happy to finally try it and its amazing lox.  The menu was a little different and "trendy" for my husband's liking but we were still excited for the meal.  We came on a late Monday morning and the wait was still over 30 minutes. Once we finally sat down, we were "greeted" by our waiter Ben, who I felt was a little distracted.  We ordered a variety of things to try - matzo ball soup, borscht, knishes, lox, bagels and eggs. I thought some things were super yummy, and some were just average, so based on this, I would come back.  However, the service was very poor.  I had to keep asking for coffee refills and every time we'd ask for something, Ben was so nonchalant about it, it felt like he really couldn't care less.  At one point, he was carrying on a conversation with a fellow staffer, and dropped a few f-bombs...right by our table.  I've served my time in the service industry, and I get it - but we are in a very small, tight space and as a patron, I don't want to hear it.  Overall, yes, I am a fan and would be back.
Magical. My favorite  breakfast/lunch spot in LES. Old school diner feel. The lox is fab of course. Don't miss the Shrubs. Very friendly service. Not to miss!

It's been almost a year since I've lived in LES and have yet to venture to this staple. A few friends (6 total) decided to meet for an 8am brunch at a nearby favorite but of course, it was a ridiculous time to meet. Since that was closed, we ventured over to Russ&Daughters right before it got super crowded.

We all ordered boards with the exception of one who got a sweet toast. I got the classic board as I wanted to try something simple. 

First, aesthetic af. I will say, it was much messier than I anticipated building my own bagel. I'm actually a really lazy eater so having to build and eat was a bit of a ‍ for me but at least it all tasted great. 

Other favorite? The sodas are pretty darn good and worthwhile to try if you're happy to splurge ($5 for a soda is like wow why tbh). But if you're only here once (in a while), why not?

Anyways, definitely worth the stop for a LES staple and you're super into the type of food Russ&Daughters has to offer!

If you're looking for the best bagel experience in NY, go to Russ & Daughters.  Now it's important to note: there's the original (which is a deli-counter / take-out place), then there's this cafe, which is a sit-down.  Both are walking distance from each other.

Which one to choose really depends what you want.  In my opinion, the deli one is way better for bagels because there's far more customization, and cheaper too.

For the cafe, expect to pay more, but you get comfortable seating and other menu items that aren't available at the original.  If I go back, these are among the things I would try: latke, french toast, blintzes, eggs.  But not the bagel, unless it goes down a few bucks in price.

Went there for brunch. No Reservations but the wait wasn't as long as they told us it would be, we gave them my number and they texted us when the table was ready. The food was good, the potato latkes were just divine, but I had the eggs benny, and the eggs were slightly overdone, with a skimpy amount of salmon. The challah bread beneath it was delicious, but I was underwhelmed. In general everything was a bit perfunctory, and the wait staff seemed as disinterested as their lab coats suggest in being functional but not overly attentive.

NO LINE AT 4PM ON A SATURDAY! Had the pickled herring trio which was perfection. My dining partner had the cinnamon babka French toast which came with a light and delicious creme fraiche. Would order the creme fraiche on its own if I could.

Wow this place was packed. An hour and a half wait (it turned out to just be an hour) at this Lower East side Jewish diner.  We went for a short walk and took in the introduction movie at the Tenement Museum (which is a short walk away).  Is the wait worth it: absolutely!

Russ and Daughters rocks the diner vibe. Booths and Jewish memorabilia abound.  It has a bar that serves egg creams and sodas. There is comfortable seating in booths and the din was never enough to overpower the conversation. 

Oy vey is the menu to die for - latkes, knishes, chopped liver, lox, caviar, oh my!  Matzoh ball soup (a bit thin and salty but with big fluffy yummy matzoh balls) was great on this cold morning. 

We ordered the Ida platter which serves 3 (very comfortably) or 4 depending on how hungry you are. It came with four types of lox - gravlox, pastrami, Scotland, Nova Scotia - with insanely tasty classic Jewish breads - challah, bagels, pumpernickel and rye - alongside tomatoes, onions and tart sides - pickled green tomatoes (omg good!), capers, garlic dill pickles, house cured olives, and pickles carrots - and spreads galore - cream cheese, cream cheese with chives and butter. Its a platter to lie down next to.

Russ & Daughters Cafe..What can one say? Plenty and it is all good. I wish my father was alive...He would be in the kitchen cooking along side  the cook staff..

I have been here several times, Afternoon, yesterday..I have been going through the menu. Fluffy matzoh ball soup, The kasha, omelette (My childhood Sundays) with nova..Got there at 3 and the place cleared out by 4.. We had the cafe to ourselves. We just chatted about life for the next hour or so.

Portions cater to my 'genetic food insecurity' LOL

Can't believe it was my first time visiting Russ & Daughters. The wait is usually a few hours long, but I decided to go yesterday around 3 PM and there wasn't a wait for two. Inside the restaurant looks like an old-school diner, has a great ambiance with beautiful decor. 

The menu was overwhelming with many options we wanted to try. My mom and I decided to share the mushroom barley soup, which they nicely split into two separate bowls. It was delicious! Then I had the potato latkes with apple sauce & sour cream, one of the best I've had. My mom had the baked salmon board and thought it was excellent! 

Overall we had a great experience and wish we had come sooner. The prices are actually pretty reasonable too! Russ & Daughters is a must try and worth the wait.

Came by myself for a late Friday lunch around 1:30PM and was told that it would be about a 20 minutes. Long waits are not uncommon here, which is why I never went before. I actually waited only about 10 minutes before being seated at the bar. I ordered a Lower Sunny Side, which came out fairly quickly as the dish required little cooking. The potato latkes were seasoned well and had a very crunchy exterior, sunny side eggs were left unseasoned which was nice because the salmon lox is already salty. Lox tasted as fresh and good as expected. I opted out of getting the Classic Platter as I was told their bagels are not that great, but may try it next time with a different carb. Definitely want to come back to try the other menu items and their egg cream. Best time to go would be after open and maybe mid afternoon.

This is my favorite place for lox and great Jewish food in the city. The lox are just perfect every time and my favorite thing on the menu is the Eggs Benny. The best part of this place to me is that they have gluten free bagels and rye bread options for people like me with allergies! I've also had their lox, eggs, and onions plate which is fantastic. The Hot smoke/Cold smoke is also absolutely divine. My friend got this on our last trip and it was so good I just ate it right out off the plate without needing to ask for gluten free bread or bagels (it comes with bagel chips). 
The only thing I do not particularly enjoy here is the smoked martini but that's not their fault. I try to make it a point to go here at least once every time I am in the city. Note for new visitors that there are TWO locations. One is the regular storefront and this is the cafe where you can sit down and enjoy a meal. Everything they serve here is available for purchase at the store. Sometimes we get lucky and can just walk in and get a table and other times we still have to wait even if we have already made a reservation. Always worth it though, but just be aware and make a reservation in advance to be safe.

A  neighborhood classic that I hadn't visited in a few years as I moved a few blocks away and revisited this weekend with a friend visiting from Italy. Everything we had was amazing, well priced and packaged. There's a large selection of foods and extras for sure, but their expert staff is kind, helpful and patient and are quick to help all the way. My friend was impressed and I bought this jar of tuna in olive oil that has been excellent with simple pasta, and so cheap.

1. We love the Russ & Daughters deli so were excited to try the cafe. It's has that old school lunch counter/soda fountain kinda vibe. But as if you stepped back in time when it was brand new. 

2. The food and service were excellent. We got both the smoked sturgeon and the smoked sable sandwich boards. Both were amazing. I also got their made in house coffee soda. They make their own coffee syrup and it was tasty as heck.

3. This is a great place to get lunch after visiting the nearby Tenement Museum. It is on the pricey side, so at least for us it's a place to go for a special meal.

Lucky to have it in my neighborhood an A+ visit every time I've never waited for a seat at the bar .the fish sticks are Perfectly crunchy the egg dishes are always spot on ..I just wish they were open earlier so that could come for breakfast before work every day ....

Delicious. I had the chocolate French toast and it was amazing!!! We also shared the latkes with the salmon ... Amazing! They brought out the wrong order of French toast at first (apple instead of chocolate) and happily and very quickly replaced it. I loved the whole setting and experience. Get there early! There was a line out of the door by the time we finished!

This is my favorite place to eat! I LOVE the eggs Benedict and chocolate babka French toast. I still dream about it because it's THAT good. It's a really cute and cozy cafe and was seated pretty quickly. It's also not far from the original Russ & Daughters bagel shop.

Highly recommend this place. Service and food were both stellar. Sparkling water when seated was great. My daughter loved the Babka bread French toast. The eggs benny were perfect and my wife's omelet was made to perfection. The coffee was also constantly flowing.

Nice place to go if you like salmon or herring:) They have pretty good fish plates. I liked my Eggs Benedict as well. Atmosphere and service was pretty good. The price might surprise you tho, it's a little high for this kind of place. Overall it was a nice experience

Ugh, I do not have enough words in my vocabulary to express how amazing this restaurant is. Came here on Easter Sunday, and of course, it was packed, BUT the 30 minute wait was totally worth it. THE SALMON LOX BAGEL BOARD was literally the best thing I've ever had for brunch in my life. That, and the pickled herring flight. Literally one of the best things in life. I wish I lived in New York so I can have this brunch every week. I really do.

I came here on a rainy Monday morning expecting the longest wait of my life. Instead, I got a table immediately. It took me longer to stick my wet umbrella in the bucket than it was to get a table. I was shook. 

Anyway, here's what I liked:
-The staff was nice and super chill overall.
-The cafe is a welcoming space with good-lookin branding.
-The Latkas were SOOOO crispy.

Some improvements:
-Bigger coffee mugs? I had to get multiple refills. Not very practical for me or the staff.

I visited Russ & Daughters Cafe today after stopping by the Russ & Daughters shop yesterday and the cafe delivers food just as good as the shop. The cafe opens at 9:30 a.m. and when we arrived at 9:20 a.m., there was already a few people waiting in line. Definitely a popular spot so if you don't want to wait, come when the place opens.

I ordered the cinnamon french toast with apple compote (applesauce basically) and it was exactly how I like my french toast - fluffy not dense, not too sweet, and light. There was a little container of creme fraiche as well if you're a fan of that. Overall, I'd definitely recommend the dish if you're on the fence about it.

Food aside, the branding at Russ & Daughters Cafe is so good! Even if you don't have a designer eye - I don't, you can definitely appreciate how everything comes together. Everything from the mugs to the menu placemats to the decor, things feel very well thought out, much like a diner you'd find at Disneyland. 

If you're in a rush, I'd advise you to stop by the deli instead of this location but if you have the time, treat yourself to some great food and atmosphere at the R&D Cafe.

My first time in new York and we went to Russ and daughters. The nova Lox was fantastic and we tried a little bit of everything else too. Latkes, blintzes, egg cream, etc. the wait staff was helpful and it wasn't terribly crowded, but it had just opened. I recommend a visit.

I officially like smoked salmon! I didnt like it before my visit and was hesitant to try the bagel with smoked salmon. I had tried it somewhere else before and was convinced that it just wasn't my thing. But... Russ & daughters changed that. The flavors were great and portions were on point. We also shared the chocolate babka french toast (highly recommend). 

Although we had to wait an hour to get seated, the location is perfect for wandering around. We walked to a coffee shop (Irving Farm) and got a cup of coffee and relaxed. Then we walked around the area and walked into random little shops and art galleries. Overall, we did not mind the wait.

This place is so good.  Had been going to the deli for years but first time going to the cafe.

1. Matzo ball soup - tasty, very homemade feel
2. Chopped liver- amazing - my favorite item and also my favorite chopped liver anywhere.  Perfect with the pickled onions and the incredible matzo.
3. Smoked salmon board - just like I remember it.  The salmon is lightly smoked then hand sliced to paper thin sheets. 
4. Sours- the perfect accompaniment to the meal.  A variety of pickles - carrots, cucumbers, green tomatoes - and these are done the right way - thrown in a huge barrel and slowly fermented.
5. Malt egg cream - classic

Atmosphere: bustling + modern

Service: attentive + informative

Food: expensive + delicious

I didn't know what to expect when I first walked in. I saw the place on Yelp but thought it was totally different than the Eastern European fusion I observed. Luckily, I love me some Georgian and Ukrainian dishes and this place had a good variety. My friends were impressed with the assortment of fish and the aesthetics of the boards, but we settled for some eggs Benedict and my flakey potato thing (the name escapes me). 

Overall it was worth the price and was a great last brunch for my trip back to New York.

I am really torn between 3 and 4 stars... I think every place has things they do well and things that are more on the average side, and sadly all the things that are important to me felt very average here. First of all, we came on a Monday late morning and even then there was a small wait! I cant imagine what the café would be like on a weekend... I don't think their food is worth more than 30 min tops... I was told that their lox is the best in the city and since I don't eat lox its hard for me to say one way or the other. The bagels were sub par, the omelet I got was super flat in flavor, and the knish appetizer was ok... the potato inside was a bit dry and the dough was far from the best I have ever had. Overall I just was glad that we didn't wait for that long.... I was told their bagel spread with cream cheese, lox, etc, was really good, so for me its just not the right place to go, but overall it just seems from what I know about them, they grew so fast and it can be hard to keep up with quality when you are working so hard on the quantity. I did appreciate the great customer service and things came out very quickly!

Russ & Daughters is absolutely a must-try. The smoked salmon (lox) bagels are amazing. I ordered the classic board with scallion cream cheese and an everything bagel. The bagel and the scallion cream cheese were delicious, but the salmon really stole the spotlight. The board came with three slices of salmon which was more than enough for my bagel. The salmon was so fresh, with just a slight smoky taste. The only difference between the cafe and the deli is the bagel comes deconstructed on a board in the cafe. The board was beautifully plated, and I enjoyed being able to assemble my own bagel.

I came here with a friend on Friday around noon. We were told that the wait would be an hour and a half, so we walked over to the Russ & Daughters deli. 20 minutes later, we were told that our table was ready, so we rushed back. Not sure if this is a common thing, but the wait is absolutely worth it. I wish Russ & Daughters would open a location on the West Coast, but until then, I'll have to wait until my next New York trip to come back.

Glad I was not disappointed by Russ & Daughters. After a year and a half of...I want to go there...finally did!

My friend and I shared a classic board with a pumpernickel bagel and a apple cinnamon babka french toast. The salmon on the classic board (and even the tomato!) tasted very fresh. It was light and well with together. The French toast was very soft, on Challah I guessed, and it was light and not too sweet.

We showed up around 9:30 and waited about 15 minutes for two.

Definitely would recommend!

I can't wait to get back to this place. It will be a staple whenever I travel to NYC, which is seldom, granted, but great things are worth waiting for..."3,000 years of beautiful tradition from Moses to Sandy Koufax, you're d$&@ right I'm living in the past!"

Their spot is so stylish and neat, lots of marble and glass and wood, attention to detail for sure. Megan was our server. There's a tasty selection of beers on tap, and the food is so deliciously prepared; cured and pickled and baked and so forth. I just loved it. I had a pickled herring appetizer on bread cubes, and a bagel with lox. I had a coffee and a pilsner as well. I left feeling great. I one hundred percent recommend this place.

I haven't been told the next table gonna be 1.5 hour wait ..but I got their message in about an hour!
It looks like an old pharmacy inside, event the staff were wearing the white robe,pretty cool!
I got the whitefish chowder and it's awfully sweet.. had to put lots of salt in it! The classic board is so good you can't beat it! That's why it's called classic!
The French toast was great too but the taste is very light...can be sweeter and use wipe cream instead of sour cream would be greater!

The wait is forever but that doesn't justify not giving this place five stars.  The lox on the bagel board is divine.  The blintzes, the sable, the soup.  Just throw a dart and order food you'll be fine.  Order the heebster as an appetizer especially if you like a little kick the wasabi fish roe is nuts.  Can't wait to try dinner and for that they take reservations.  A must stop on the LES!

Doesn't disappoint. Not really their fault but 4 Stars because it's impossible to get in.  If you don't want to wait, you can walk up to their take-out store. If you do wait, you will be treated to a menu with delicious options and very attentive service.  There are definitely other options in the city but you cannot deny that they are one of the best for Jewish cuisine.

Great breakfast, brunch or snack spot. Prefer the cafe location, historic decor is wonderful to explore. One of the highlights of the neighborhood for natives and visitors for sure. Very friendly and accommodating staff are a pleasure to find here. Good menu selections, something to satisfy everyone. Basic bagel and eggs are awesome in addition to lox, salmon, & caviar selections. Might be a wait on the weekends.

The wait list for the breakfast was 1 hour. 
 The liver paste wasn't my favorite but in general the food is nice.
For me a huge disappointment is no cappuccino. Only regular coffee.

I love Russ & Daughters! Always a must-stop whenever I'm visiting the Lower East Side when I'm craving a snack before dinner (although you could eat a full meal here). I've had the Classics board along with the Sours appetizer. You get to pick your choice of bagel - I always go with sesame or poppyseed. They also have rye bread as an option. There's just something about the right bite of cream cheese spread on a bagel with smoked salmon and a few capers on top. Scrumptious! 

I never would've thought their Bloody Mary's could be so good, but trust me, you HAVE to try them even if you're not a fan. I think you could be convinced. And if you already are, well, your tastebuds will thank you. I've had the caraway-infused one, dill-infused, and fenugreek. All of them are amazing but my favorite is definitely the fenugreek. Just the right amount of flavor and spices to make a perfect concoction. It's hard to get just one. 
The only thing about Russ and Daughters is that unless you're going on a weekday or right when they're open, there is most always going to be a wait and usually about 30 minutes to 1 hr. But what can you expect! It's super famous and well worth it in my opinion. Just go at an off-time like during the afternoon on a weekday or if you don't mind waiting, they'll text you when seating is open and you can walk around in the meantime. Just go, you won't regret it!

A food blog I read recently posted a list of the best French toast in NY and the offerings at Russ & Daughters Cafe came in first. Being a French toast fiend, naturally had to come see what the fuss was about. I ordered both the Chocolate Babka and Cinnamon varieties. Both came with delicious toppings. However, both seemed dry. I will also echo other reviewers in thinking that maple syrup is NECESSARY, the sour cream/creme fraiche just didn't help balance out the dryness of the babkas. I'm glad I sampled these unusual French roasts, but they are not the best in the city. I still enjoyed them and would come here again.

Had the smoked salmon sandwich on a sesame bagel with chive cream cheese which was simply delicious! It was a bit disorienting coming in as a first timer because there was a huge crowd and I wasn't sure if there was a line I had to follow but it was later clear that a ticket system was in place thanks to the signs they put around. The shop itself is very cute, lots of Decorations and food options. It got a bit crowded but as long as you're not claustrophobic and love bagels you should stop by!

Best smoked fish in New York City. Make sure you try the Blintzes with farmers cheese and blueberry compote and potato latkes! Another must try is the "Classic" salmon board. If you prefer a smokier salmon ask to substitute for Scottish smoked salmon at no additional charge. Everything on the menu is a winner. A New York gastronomic mainstay.

Great service. I felt very comfortable here with large spacious booth seating and the old school feel. Had the latkes with crime fraiche and salmon roe. Was terrific. Latkes Gentry crisped on the edges and the creme and Roe played nicely together. Had the classic bagel and lox with capers. Bagel wasn't huge but was a good size. Lox was thinly sliced and so were onions dill and capers gave it a nice kick. For dessert we had the halvah ice cream and it was great!  It has caramel and sesame seeds on the top.

Russ and Daughters definitely will fill any cravings you may have for old school Jewish food. Think bagels, smoked salmon, white fish and Matzo ball soup.  The "nosh" sandwich made with pastrami smoked salmon, sour kraut, Muenster cheese on a pretzel bagel was amazing, simply one of the best sandwiches I've ever eaten.  My problem with it was that it was "nosh" size and I wanted more.  This is definitely a great place for brunch, lunch or a lighter dinner.

Absolutely a 5-Star place for Jewish comfort food!!  Matzoh ball soup, bagels and lox, best kasha ever, blintz's, latkes. . . . At good prices!  Wish we lived here -- would be a regular (and probably then weigh 500 pounds)!  DELISH!!
Simply amazing!  Breakfast for dinner is never not an option. Great service, tasty food, and awesome atmosphere.

The food was excellent and so is the customer service. I had seen place in several youtube blogs and it was on my lists of places to visit while in NYC. My husband and I got a board and shared it and I miss it already! Can we get one in LA?! Pretty please with a cherry on top!

So we had to wait 45 mins-1 hour to get seated at this place. While the food is good, it is not as good as the deli. I personally think the cafe is overpriced and not worth it compared to the deli. I guess if I was comparing this place solely on food, I would give it 4.5 stars. But 1/2 star deducted b/c the deli is better, and another star deducted b/c the wait wasn't worth it.
This place hit the spot. We were unsure what to expect but we were pleasantly surprised by the quality of food and service. Go Navy, Beat Army!

Quintessential Jewish Delicatessen. This place is my favorite stop in the city. The hot smoke/cold smoke, with everything bagel chips is delicious. If ordering a board or a platter, don't forget to get the bialy (like a bagel but, oh so much better).

Good bagels and a lot of hype.  No amount of branding makes a bagel worth $18.  I've had plenty of authentic New York bagels that were just as good, if not better, for $5.  My friend and I both ordered the classic bagel board and a cocktail.  The cocktails were quite small for the price and the bagels didn't stand out as something I would return again and again for or really recommend to friends.  Overall a fine experience but not one that stood out in my mind as exceptional.

Best smoked salmon I've ever had. I ordered the Classic Board with poppyseed bagel. A definite must-try if you're in the area. 

For dessert I had the chocolate French toast, which was lighter than I expected and fluffy. My other friends raved about the bread pudding. 

The atmosphere itself is clean and aesthetically pleasing. Staff are very friendly and timely.
outstanding! this place brings seafood deli to another level....like top! We have been there now twice in one week....run dont walk...

A friend and I sat at the counter and received perfect service. I ordered the Mensch board with a bialy. The bialy was perfectly baked and the white fish was fresh and tasty. There was also a perfect amount of the goat cream cheese to accompany the bialy, capers, tomatoes and onions.
Also does anyone ever talk about how great the coffee is here? I think of myself of quite the coffee snob too- we are talking blue bottle, lucid standard NEVER Starbucks. And I was pleasantly surprised at the nutty, well brewed cup of coffee I received. Also my waitress kept topping it off at no charge!

Plain bagel was ok, don't like the hard outside. The vegetable cream cheese was good, they are not shy about loading it on. The heebster bagel was delicious and pricey. Definitely recommend trying any of the bagels with fish in it if for the price.

Yes, yes & yes. My new found love for Jewish cuisine is all thanks to Russ & Daughters. After trying countless amounts of Jewish Delis through out New York, I thought hope was lost. Fortunately, after hearing RAVING reviews, I decided to give it another try. & thank god I did! 

Decided to come on a Sunday morning for brunch (not the smartest decision considering everyone else had the same idea) - the wait was about 2 hours. The hostess was incredibly nice and accommodating. I even witnessed a few patrons get very angry due to the wait time, she kept her cool, props! 

After the wait, we finally got a nice little booth. The inside is very nice, and authentic. Even though it was crowded, it had a nice cozy feel about it.

Our servers were incredibly friendly, they helped us pick the best choices off the menu - & they were certainly right! We ordered the potato Latkes w| salmon. DELICIOUS, highly recommend!! For my entree I got the classic board which was delicious. 

This is a great place to bring friends from out of town for a true New York experience! I will deff be back.

Honestly, this place is overrated. But I'm not going to be a negative nancy here. I've been wanting to come here for a while and I had a friend choose this place who was visiting from out of town. 
-Decor: super clean and retro chic. I like the waiters' outfits with the white coats. Cheesy--but you feel you're in a movie.
-Food: It's high quality cuts and you can tell by the way the food is prepared and presented is. Potato latkes were tasty and not greasy at all. Loved the board layout with the satchel, goat cheese pairing. The beet salad was fresh but it could have had more potential. My friend ordered a ginger lavender drink (non-alcoholic) and it was really flavorful.

Overall, I think you're paying mostly for the ambiance and setting which is fine. But I've gone to better delis in the city and less pricey. However, I would try this place if you haven't been before: it's a New York classic.

Wow the smoked white fish chowder is so delicious!!
Their bialys are obviously top notch. I would recommend this place for breakfast or brunch.

Been here dozens of times.  NY native / LA resident. Come back every time I am in NY. 
Pros: Lox is delicious, perfect, like butter.  Great seats at the counter. 
Cons: Katie, the hostess enjoys seating "friends of the family" first, before other customers who have been waiting for half hour +.  
Hey, Russ and Daughter's Family- at least let your hostesses know that they should be a bit more coy about their transactions.
The Super Heebster is one of the most delicious noshes in NYC, and the Smoked Whitefish Chowder has an unexpected zing from the crushed red peppers.

My quest to find the perfect blintz has landed me in some of my new favorite places in new York. Not only are the blintzes near perfect here, but it's such a cool modern version of an old school Jewish deli / lunch counter. The woman behind the counter was super nice, and I just felt totally at peace there. I will be back for sure.

I had to try because this was apparently a go to place for the lox sandwich, which I enjoyed but it was... salty. A little pricey for what it was worth I think. My sister really enjoyed it so I think I'll return when I go to nyc again but there was actually a place in Brooklyn which had really good pricing AND one of the best herrings I've ever had. I'm going to search for that one so browse through my reviews!

The most yummy latke I have had in years!!!!  Other than maybe my grandmothers. The egg creams were so delicious and the service lovely.  It's a small place so if you have to wait know it is worth it.

Incredibly disappointed in this NYC institution. Russ & Daughters came highly recommended by NYC locals. If possible I would give it a 5 for the Coffee Soda and a 1 for food. My friend had the Salmon Ruben. She thought it was good, but not Ruben-ish. I ordered the Spinich, goat cheese omelette. YUCK! The eggs were rubbery and tasteless. They reminded me of the old "egg product" that fast food restaurants used to use.
Came in with a friend to grab some grub-- The food was great. Our server was rude and had a bit of an attitude, but we'd still come back since the food was great.

We got the salmon variety fish platter for a family and it was enormous and did not disappoint. It was basically lox five different ways. I recommend. The ONLY reason I took back a star was that (1) the hostess appeared to seat some new arrivals before us like she was taking care of friends and order didn't matter and we wound up waiting an hour to be seated; and (2) their specialty drinks were horrible and they should get rid of that part of the menu and pretend they never knew about it.
Great quality smoked fishes.  The service is more than fantastic.  We wish we could get table easier so we can go there all the time.  The price reflects the quality of the food.  A great experience!

We had the "The Classic" and it was delish! I also tried the Matzo ball soup and it was good too! Staffs are friendly and a little wait to be seated. Definitely will
come back again!

This was our first time here, in our recent vacation to Norwegian county my daughter try for the first time Lox salmon and she loves it. This is one of the very few places in the city where you can find the best Lox guarantee it was absolutely delicious.. definitely recommend this place to everyone who visiting the city.

I was looking for a great Jewish deli type place throughout my trip and I think this spot filled that void. 

Atmosphere: cute old time style soda shop feel. Relaxing environment, they even have newspapers available if you want to read while you eat and drink your coffee. 

Staff: very attentive. I used my coffee cup never being empty as a measure of their attentiveness.

The latkes: nice and crispy, not greasy. The apple sauce was great. We went the fancier version with the fish eggs and creme, which was also very nice and yummy (when in Rome, treat yo self)

The classic: the salmon was the star. Nice and smooth, melts in your mouth.

The shtetl: the fish was very fresh. The goat cream cheese was kind of bitter/tangy? Which was interesting (I would've preferred regular cream cheese but I'm sure someone would enjoy this. But overall good.

If you're going to do a board, I would choose the pumpernickel or rye bread over a bagel. I've just had better bagels (I tried the everything bagel and the rye bread). 

Check it out. Great place.

Oh how I loved the beet soup! I absolutely would have licked the bowl clean if I was not in public. I have been here a couple of times for brunch and I loved it! The food is always spot on. Portions are not huge so sometimes I was craving something else after, but the food was always delish. I love the platters with the smoked fish and the bagels. Service is quick and friendly. Coffee and seltzer just keeps coming. Such a good brunch spot!

More like 3.5 stars..
Pretty busy even for a weekday early lunch. 
Ordered the classic board and it was A+, the salmon was perfectly smoked and just right amount of saltiness, the fluffy cream cheese and my bialy perfectly toasted. The potato latkes were nicely fried but felt like something was missing (maybe not enough salt?!) but good nonetheless. The coffee was tasty. 
Now the cons: the hostess(es) were not very welcoming, not friendly, they didn't even walk me and my party to the seat and just pointed it out to us. I've read reviews they pick and choose who to be "friendly" to and I saw that. The service was a bit slow, waited over 10 min just for coffee and water refill.
Ps hostesses- at least look at the patrons when they are leaving if you're saying good bye. Just common courtesy IMO.

Bottom line: go for the food not the hospitality

Grabbed the Classic Smoked Salmon board here and it absolutely hit the spot -- comes with your choice of a bagel (I chose everything, toasted), tomato, onion, capers, and cream cheese.  All the pieces you need.  The inside of the cafe has a nice upscale diner feel and is in a great location.. def recommend the board!

Here is the 3-1-1: 

Food: With the reputation of great deli's in NYC, Russ & Daughters is one of the historical establishments that is known for their cured fish and fresh baked breads. For starters the Matzo Ball soup was a great wake up a call after a red-eye flight as the warm chicken broth filled with carrots, celery and pulled chicken pieces surrounded the tennis sized fork tender Matzo ball. Next on the list were the Knishes which I had high expectations, as never eaten it before I wanted a flavor punch but it was tasted a little bland. For the main course the board of tender cure salmon (skin on) served with a very light cream cheese with slices of beef steak tomatoes, red onions and capers accompanied 2 slices of toasted Bialys was amazing; and since the salmon portion was generous, we had to order a bowl of bagel chips to makes sure we devour every last bite.

Service: Super friendly and efficient staff that were helpful to explain the menu options.

Ambiance: Classic diner feel with historical pictures covering the walls and vintage signage throughout.

There are a lot of great bagel places in NYC, but few make eating bagel with lox such an artisanal fair. Just look at how everything is plated so beautifully on the board, visually appetizing already, taste and texture are first tier as well.

Wow what an amazing bagel!!!! I came here with 2 others ro try the infamous bagels and we were not dissappointed!! There were so many different types of cream cheese, bagels, types of lox, and toppings! I ended up getting the onion bagel with the horseradish cream cheese and Norwegian lox. WOW was it the best bagel I've ever had!! My brothers got the pastrami lox and the scallion cream cheese....WOW again! They are also very efficient, at least 4 of their staff asked us if we had been helped already. They also answered any questions we had about the different types of lox, which was super helpful! Originally I wanted to try the belly lox but one of the staff told me that was the saltiest one they had, which I really appreciated because I don't like super salty stuff. All in all great experience, great bagels, happy tummies!
One of the historical food place in NY, classic and amazing! Bagel good as always. I really enjoy the simple combo of the smoked salmon cream cheese tomato onion with bagel, so classy so good!

Awesome food. I went here twice whilst in New York City. Both times I had the bagel with smoked salmon. It was quite delicious. Beautiful the way they present it too. Also had the Lower East Side which was very good on a hot day.

One of my favorite recent dining experience. The service is old school yet modern enough to be kind and very professional. The food is absolutely amazing. Herring with a think piece of bread, melt in your mouth lox and by far and away the best chocolate babka desert i have ever had  and blitzes. Latkes had this great flavor and terrific onions in them. The drinks were good but the prices were equivalent to very fancy restaurants and I thought that was a bit disappointing.
A must for anyone wanting to explore a taste of New York!  Expect a wait but it is well worth it.

I love Russ & Daughters Cafe for their succulent salmon and incredible bagels. I often order a classic board with an everything bagel. Add some latkes if you're extra hungry. Friendly staff, a cozy retro diner feel and incredible Jewish comfort food make Russ & Daughters a must-visit in the East Village.

The wait is long, but the food is worth it! And when you get in you don't feel rushed at all. The Eggs benny was absolutely delicious, and the chocolate babka French toast was out of this world! Also the Ginger soda with lime and lavender was amazing. So much flavor and so refreshing. Wonderful experience and delicious food!
I have no words to describe how delicious the food is. Plus they have a great cocktail menu. Best Jewish food in the city. Awesome service.

I've been going to the original Russ & Daughters for 20 years. Might be my favorite place in the city. I love it so much I feel like I'm betraying a friend by admitting how disappointed I was in my visit to the café. But the slabs of kippered salmon on my Yum Kippered platter were bone dry (and I'm a kippered salmon vet so I know it can be fatty and delicious); my toasted bagel arrived ice cold; the cream cheese was meager and pasty; and the cutesy wooden board the spread showed up on was awkwardly small for its contents, so once I'd dressed my bagel halves I had to just lay one of them on my placemat. A clear style-over-substance situation, doubly underwhelming at $17.00. A bagel platter from Russ & Daughters should be - are you kidding me? - the best in the city. This looked cute, tasted meh, and left me wishing I'd gone to the original spot and ordered a sandwich at the counter. All in all, a sad lunch date in a lifelong relationship.

Came here for an early lunch on Tuesday.   Right away got seated to the bar and then ordered a classic board and one potato latke.   Wow, loved the classic board with an everything bagel and the potato latke was the best potato pancake I've had.   Perfect blend of onions and potato.    Nice setup and a lot of different options for lunch and breakfast.   Highly recommend if you want to sit and eat.  Hidden in a smaller street.

Finally made it to Russ & Daughters Cafe. This modern Jewish deli is the real deal! I went with a friend and we enjoyed the Classic Board with whitefish, Latkes, Eggs Benny and of course Bloody Mary's. The atmosphere was adorable and the food was great. Will definitely be coming back here soon.
Legendary provider of Jewish noshes with emphasis on excellent fresh and preserved fish.

Russ & Daughters is the most perfect New York City breakfast spot. 
I've only ever gone for breakfast or brunch or desert. 
Bagels are amazing. Coffee is great. The aesthetic of the restaurant reminds of a Jacques Tati film. I love it so much. 
These are my favorite potato latkes. 
This location is just a few minutes from the M train or right off the Williamsburg bridge if you decide to walk or bike from Brooklyn. 
They only allow takeout with their cold food. 
They accept credit cards. 
They have a full bar and their cocktails are delightful. 
You need your whole party to be there before you can be seated. We arrived at 9am on a Thursday and there was no line or wait. The place was packed by the time we left at 10:30am. 
The food was so good that I didn't want to stop eating it even though I was completely full!
The wait staff was quick, knowledgeable and friendly but they were kind of aggressive about getting our dirty/used plates etc our of the way while we were still working on things. I think because it gets so crowded, they definitely don't want you to linger which I understand. Unfortunately I had just ordered a cold brew and we were still picking on our appetizer. 
The fish is A+ here. I can't say anything good that hasn't already been said. 
The vibe is modern is a 60s way. 
Someone else called this place "adorable" and it's really true--that's what this place is. I love Russ & Daughters.
We shared the platter with 4 different kinds of cured/smoked salmon.  So good! The rye and pumpernickel bread was great too

Yes, it *is* everything you imagined.

We came here at around 10:15am on a holiday Monday, and the wait was about 30 minutes - perfect amount of time to wander over to Little Italy and back.

The ambiance was super cute - the bar doubled as an old-fashioned soda fountain, and it had the feel of the deli I would go to with my grandparents when I was a kid.

I had the homemade cream soda which was for sure the best homemade soda I've ever had. You could even see the specks of real vanilla, and it had a beautiful citrus backtone.

My partner and I always split everything; to start, we had a sandwich with pastrami-cured salmon, muenster, sauerkraut, and a pickle on a pretzel bun. As expected, the pickle was perfect, and the kraut was pungent af.

Then we got the classic board - you know, nova, cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers on a bialy. There are other interesting boards and in cases like this I usually get something less traditional, but I am so glad I went OG.

This was my grandmother and grandfather's favorite meal. I felt like they were there with me again. Nothing was too salty, and there were the right portions of everything. 

We ended with the blintzes.. I was expecting cherry compote, but it came out with the most spectacularly purple homemade blueberry compote ans tangy sour cream. It was absolutely delicious. A perfect, not-too-sweet ending to a perfect meal.

It took everything in me to not get some rugelach to go.

If you grew up in a Jewish or Eastern European household like me, this place will make you remember all the greatest parts of your childhood and family.

I loved Russ & Daughters. The Smoked Scottish Salmon with a Bialy we had here was outstanding!! Just delicious. The bialy was perfectly toasted, the salmon melts in your mouth, the cream cheese was devine, the tomatoes actually had flavor and tasted like tomatoes should taste, everything was just fantastic. Service was excellent too as was the atmosphere. This was an easy 5 stars and somewhere I'll definitely be returning to on future NYC trips.

Food amazing and breakfast cocktail a great way to start the weekend.

I love the Kinishes and homely food. Great vibe

Service average.

There were so many things on the menu I wanted to try, but knew if this was my one chance to come (I'm from out of town) I had to get the classic plate. It didn't disappoint! Everything about it was flavorful. The capers were super salty, the bialy was expertly toasted, the tomatoes were fresh, and the salmon was absolutely perfect! Will definitely be back in my next trip.

I usually love this place and the food is always exceptional, but the service was awful to the point that I don't know if I'll be going back. Our bartender was extremely rude not just to us but all of the guests sitting around us at the bar. It got to the point where we were looking around at each other being like "is she being serious right now?" 

On top of that she did not get my drink order correct and got defensive when I asked for correction so it got to the point where it wasn't worth it to stay there and deal with her negative vibes.

I understand if you are having a bad day, but this is the service industry and people don't go there to be treated like a piece of trash.

While we were visiting NYC last week, we spent a day exploring the Lower East Side, and I knew we had to try Russ & Daughters Cafe. It was a Friday around lunchtime, and they had an 80-minute wait. But they take your phone number and text you when your table is ready. We got a quick snack and walked around for an hour and were hungry for Russ & Daughters by the time we got a table!

The inside of the cafe is classic deli. And beautiful. And the service was great. I got the Yum Kippered board (kippered - baked - salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, and capers). All boards come with your choice of bagel, bialy, shissel rye, or pumpernickel. I went with shissel rye and it was great. 

My husband got the eggs benedict which he enjoyed. We also shared a side order of kasha varnishkes, which I love but my husband had never tried before. R&D's kasha varnishkes is definitely heavier on the kasha and lighter on the pasta than other versions of this dish I've had, but it was very tasty (my husband isn't sure about it, but I really liked it). 

It's definitely on the pricier side for a deli, but the food lives up to the price. That kippered salmon was maybe the best I've ever had. Great meal. Would definitely go back. It's a good place to take people who aren't familiar with deli (especially as it's not Kosher, so they have everything in one place) and are maybe trying it for the first time!

When I was watching Phil Rosenthal's NYC episode of his Netflix series, I noticed he and Tracy Morgan were in a booth at Russ & Daughters. Hmmm, I didn't recall any place where you could sit in n the classic deli on East Houston (review), but then I finally discovered the fourth-generation owners actually opened this cafe on Orchard over four years ago. Who knew? I sure didn't, and when I saw what Phil was having, I thought it would be a good place for Jamie W. and I to meet up with Carlos for breakfast on our last day in NYC. 

He couldn't meet us until 10AM (...not a morning person), and I thought, "Oy! We'll wait forever for a table. Interior should live so long." Little did I expect how organized the hostess would be in giving us an accurate 45-minute estimate for a table. Jamie and I arrived a half-hour early, so it turned out to be almost perfect timing when Carlos got there a few minutes late. We got seated in the thick of the action smack dab in front of the counter where the salmon and whitefish gets sliced to put on their housemade bagels (photo).

The menu was full of expected pleasures like noshes, boards, and herring, but also eggs, something sweet of course, and salads. Salads? Who put those shiksa dishes in there? Anyway, Carlos decided on the $12 Chocolate Babka French Toast with sour cream and strawberries (photo: http://bit.ly/2AlGF5F). Mmmm, good. Jamie ordered the more savory $18 Eggs Benny, a plate of poached eggs, smoked salmon, and sautéed spinach sitting on freshly baked challah and absolutely coated with hollandaise sauce (photo: http://bit.ly/2AmydmL). Oy, that was good, too.

Me? I'm glad you asked. I had the $18 Lower Sunny Side, a full breakfast of sunny side up eggs, smoked salmon, and crispy potato latkes (photo: http://bit.ly/2CyMu1l). Mmmm, good. Since I was here, I figured I should have the $5 Chocolate Egg Cream 'cause who's to know (photo: http://bit.ly/2POhdv4). It was surprisingly not as satisfying as I hoped it would be. As if our respective tuchuses didn't have enough, we also shared an $8 pair of Knishes which were compact, flavorful, and potatoey, especially with the stone ground mustard on the side (photo: http://bit.ly/2EG5kpT) - though they were about to be overshadowed by Yonah Schimmel's shortly (review: http://bit.ly/2CZrgLa). It was geshmak enough you should pardon my Yiddish.

FOOD - 4 stars...mmm, good
AMBIANCE - 4 stars...clean, white and bright
SERVICE - 4.5 stars...really attentive crew here
TOTAL - 4 stars...Joel Russ and his three girls would be pleased, I'm sure

RELATED - Looking for other dining options in New York? Here's a collection of places I've tried and reviewed: bit.ly/2C7MvsK

I couldn't leave New York without getting a bagel! I saw some pretty good reviews about this place so I decided to head out here on my last day in the big city. 

They have a system where you have to grab a number right when you come in and wait for your number to get called. The place is very small and everyone was packed shoulder by shoulder. I waited about 40 minutes for my number to get called that morning (10AM). 

My boyfriend and I shared the Daughter's Delight ($18) - The combination of the roe and nova cream cheese was too salty for us. I wouldn't recommend getting this!  

They had a large selection of cream cheese, caviar, fish, and etc. I would say, just buy some jars of cream cheese and salmon separately to make the bagel yourself.

Loved this place - Great lox and bagels at a historic NYC institution! Tried the "The Classic" board with an everything bagel: Gapse Nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion and capers. Fantastic service, delicious food and great memories - I want to come back to try the bialy, matzo ball soup, chocolate babka and other Jewish deli delights. Yum!

My partner is allergic to shellfish and I am a clam chowder addict. We were both thrilled to try the delicious smoked white fish chowder. Must get that recipe - or get to New York more often than once a year. Their chopped liver was excellent as well. Service was attentive and professional. Portions were a bit diminutive, not something my adopted Bubbe would approve of and the only reason I guiltily took away one star.

Been dying to make my way to this place for the longest time! I decided to come here on my lonesome because I figured I could get seated right away and boy was I right! I recommend this if this is something you'd consider because I was sat right away to my surprise.

The staff here is very attentive and courteous. I knew what I wanted right away. I ordered the Lower Sunny Side which has sunny side eggs, smoked salmon, and potato latkes. The presentation was on point and I couldn't wait to dig in. The food came quite quickly. They refilled my water. Couldn't be happier!
We came here around 8am,so we didn't have to wait for a long line. We got the salmon bagel. The bagel was so so good, i can't get wrong with that. Highly recommend.
What a spot!! A must to hit up while in NY if your looking for the real deal, 105 years old...

Coming from Toronto and LA where I would say we have some very good appetizing/ deli food I was curious to try the Jewish establishment that all my friends were raving about. We traveled to the one in the Jewish museum on the upper east side which only required about a 10 minute wait. I will say that I was a little bit shocked by the prices that were posted for each dish, but I will get to that later. We sat down and I decided to go for the hot smoked salmon that was being offered because that has always been my favorite item in any deli. It came accompanied by cream cheese, a poppy seed bagel, tomatoes, onions and capers. The portion was not huge, but it was filling regardless. The cream cheese was extremely well whipped, the bagel perfectly yeasty and the fish was fall apart tender. The salmon was a little moister than I had anticipated it to be which did not necessarily hinder my experience but also did not make it any better. I would say that the best part of my meal was actually the bagel and the cream cheese. The bagels were clearly made in house, being mildly salty and perfectly crispy. The cream cheese almost replicated the whip cream, being extremely silky and smooth. At the end of the meal I realized that the tip was included by pricing up each item on the menu. I am not sure how I feel about that but in any case the food was splendid. If I returned to New York I am not sure I would return due to the fact that I don't know if I have the money.

Horrible customer service.  The owner and the people there have no idea how to treat people.  Disgusting.  Josh is the owner. Arrogant. The manager Arthur is just as bad.  The bad service stems from the owners and managers.  I feel sorry for anyone who goes there.

Dull and indifferent service, beginning with the hostess. Tired cocktails sitting in the glass without ice or  garnishment -- the cream soda has more pizzazz. Mostly unexceptional renditions of the usual fare. The potato latkes with creme fraiche and salmon roe are pleasing, but can be had elsewhere. All in all, an inspired concept, but an uninspiring experience that needs no repetition.

This was a disappointing experience... Not only was it expensive, but the dishes were small and the flavors are just.... Disappointing!!!!

I expected the food to taste good and come in a modest amount but no. I ordered a egss Benny and lower sunny side up and the flavors were just not there. The spinach in the eggs benny was a bit of a turn down. It would've been nicer if it was on the side because not everyone likes spinach and the taste of the spinach soaked into the bread. Even the hollandaise sauce was just disappointing it didn't really taste like much. As for the lower sunny side up, there were hash browns, a big THIN piece of salmon, and two sunny side up eggs. The hash browns was also a turn down because it was just so burnt, I was getting sick. The salmon was alright, not as good as other places I've had it at, and the eggs just tasted like eggs. Honestly a disappointment. I also ordered an orange juice and they gave me so little for a high price, it was probably worth about the same as if you were to buy it somewhere in rockefeller area but more expensive!! The only good thing was their customer service and smoked whitefish chowder, but I don't think it can make up for my disappointment.

No wait for bar seating on a Thursday morning at 9!!! 

We ordered The Classic board with bialy and an eggs benedict. Both were delicious! Bialy was perfectly toasted and tasty, and it was served with more than enough lox. 

Bar service was quick and friendly. I think we were in and out in 30ish minutes. Hoping to come back again soon. They have so much more to try!

I'm seriously so happy Russ & Daughters opened a cafe, it's probably the best thing to happen since I've been back to NY. Please do yourself a favor and eat here. The food quality is unmatched, service is wonderful, and the cafe has the quintessential diner feel. Comfort food at it's best!

The food was mixed. The latkas were amazing. The matjes herring too. And the halva ice cream. All fantastic. But one of the herring trio was grossly oversalted, the pumpernickel bread was dry n stale, the bagels not much better. 

The service was mixed. The woman serving us was great, friendly, helpful, quick. On arrival they told us we could have the table till 6:30 - there were several empty tables at 5:00pm when we arrived. Which is fine, but it is not fine to spend 15 mins telling us our table is nearly ready in a far from full restaurant. Either be fast and efficient or be relaxed about time, but don't rush us if you can't rush yourselves. And they messed up the way they allocated the bill between credit cards. 

So, mixed....

We had to wait a while to get in, but we got in sooner than we expected. Everyone was so nice, and the food here was absolutely delicious. Every time we come to NYC we had wanted to get food from the Houston Street location but never had the opportunity, and was delighted to hear about the sit down cafe. Will definitely come here again.

Absolutely the best place for bagels & perfect place for dining !!!! Every time I come to NYC, I bring an extra 22" carry-on suitcase just for bringing home 6 dz bagels ! Yep, 6dz .. great for freezing & will keep me from withdrawals until my next trip up NYC . I have tried various bagel places in NYC (Manhattan & Brooklyn). In my opinion, Russ & daughters is the Best ! Bagel is the perfect size (I found that Big at some other places does not mean better). Also the perfect chew & perfect exterior 'crust' ! I eat it plain, sometimes lightly toasted with a bit of butter or evoo or smoked salmon. Love all the different 'flavors' or should I say variety !

Nostalgic, comfortable, and worth the wait. Made my mother proud with this home-style cooking. Large portions coupled with quality preparation makes this a standout brunch worthy of high recommendation. Definitely recommend taking some rugelach home with you.
WOW. 10/10 best cream cheese I've ever eaten. Everyone at my table was beyond satisfied with their meal. Will DEFINITELY be returning.

I am not the first one to be saying it but this is one of the amazing cafe/diner I have ever been. They are unique and wonderful. 
I would suggest anyone to take a reservation before getting there they typically have 40min-2hour wait time depending on day of the week. 
We got a spot near the bar they have great bloody Mary's and mimosas. 
They have a wide range of salmon and caviars. I could see many people eating traditional smoked salmon with capers, onions,tomatoes,cream cheese on a bagel. Well paying 10-12$ for that is worth it. 
I tried a dish with buckwheat with a poached egg it was quite a wholesome meal. 
We tried the bread pudding it was 10/10.
Overall this is not overrated place this is a great place to be and definitely for people who want to try different caviars.

This was on my must visit list when I heard that Russ & Daughter's is responsible for introducing the first smoked salmon bagel. I ordered the classic with bialy and added a matzo ball soup. I enjoyed the soup! Savory and not too salty. 

I wouldn't say this was the best smoked salmon sandwich I've had, but I can certainly appreciate the quality and understand why it became a popular brunch option. 

I was not planning to have an expensive meal that morning, but hopefully I'll return one day to try their herring and caviar.

The Russ & Daughters Cafe is worth the wait. This is my second time eating there and the food was just as good as the reviews and the memory of my first meal. 

When they take your name and number down for the wait list, their automated system will text you an estimated wait time that is accurate to within 5 minutes (computers!). There are only 2 small ledges by the windows on which to perch yourself, so I recommend planning your brunch/lunch to include a coffee at the Starbucks around the corner if you are going on a weekend. 

For this particular meal, we started off with the pickled herring trio which is served in the style of canapés. The flavors of our trio were comprised of dill (the simplicity of which allowed the herring to shine), green apples with a mustard sauce (the sweetness of which balanced out nicely with the tartness of the herring), and pickled onions with sour cream (stellar flavor combination). 

Our second shared dish was the potato latkes which we had served with salmon roe and crème fraîche. This is the only way to go, unless you order a side of one of their fish options (I highly recommend the Gaspe Nova smoked salmon to go with the latkes). Ordering a "side" means that they will bring out several slices of whatever fish you ordered on a wood plank. There is an option is to have the latkes served with apple sauce and sour cream. Why? I don't know...

Our mains were a Classic (bagel with Gaspe Nova smoked salmon) and a Shtetl (bagel with smoked sable and goat cream cheese). For our previous meal we had a Mensch (sturgeon) with a side of lox. We liked the sturgeon better than the sable (personal preference), but beware the lox as it is extremely salty (perhaps we got an end-cut, but I had to really work to eat through the salinity).

We didn't have dessert this time as we had planned to swing by Katz's (which is also around the corner), but a sudden rainstorm curtailed our plans as we walked out the door. Don't make this mistake, the desserts here are good, particularly the halvah ice cream which we had during our previous meal. They have managed to transform halvah into ice cream, complete with all of its flavors, which are complemented by a salted caramel sauce and toasted sesame seeds.

You also get Hopjes with the check. If you don't know what Hopjes are, 1) you are missing out, and 2) a meal at the Russ & Daughters Cafe is a great way to find out.

Or read my photo caption.

Either way, enjoy!

I told my sister in law, Sunday I'm getting to your house 9:30am sharp!  We zoomed into NYC, there was no traffic? We find a free spot to park on the street and step to the hostess stand. 90 minute wait sir, we'll text you when your table is ready. A lot of hustling on my part and the restaurant was packed out!

Pssst, We're from New York. We can wait because the anticipation of what's coming. And trust me, it was soooo worth the wait. 

I'm going to start with my favorite items and work down:

Halava Ice Cream
What type of mash up is this?? My favorite childhood candy in the form of ice cream? Topped with caramel sauce, this dessert is not to be missed. The Halava flavor as well as the big chunks throughout is worth the wait alone.

Smoked Whitefish Chowder
Picture ordering a New England Clam Chowder. There are celery bits, potatoes, carrots and creamy goodness not with clams but big hunks of the famous Russ & Daughters smoked fish. Mmmm.. This bowl of soup was so decadent, it was just heavenly.

Potato Pancakes with smoked Roe and Creme Fraiche
These fried potato pancakes are simply amazing. A little dab of creme fraiche, a dab of the roe, that first bite was angelic. 

Hot Smoke / Cold Smoke
Big chucks of Baked Salmon mixed with Scottish Salmon, makes this dish insane. It was so good! The bagel chips out of the bag is kinda throwing me. Still, I couldn't put it down. I was double dipping the chip, I didn't care!

The Classic Board
Gaspe Nova, toasted bagel, onion, tomato, cream cheese and capers, Oh my! I like my nova a little more saltier, this was the quintessential New York breakfast.

Bissel of Caviar
I like my caviar with Champagne and toast points. The mini Blini and creme fraiche combo worked. The caviar was mild but still packed a decadent punch. 

Cinnamon Babka French Toast
Does this French Toast dish come with anything? The candied walnuts and apple compote was nice, I wanted some syrup, something to kick it up a notch. 

The Kinishes and Noodle Kugel were just ok. It was too much food and if we didn't order these items I would be ok.

Here's the reason why there is a long wait. The four of us are eating, tasting, talking and laughing. Russ & Daughters cafe is a place where you can kick back, eat and enjoy yourself. The waitstaff was eager to please as we kept on ordering and sampling.

I highly recommend Russ and Daughters Cafe. Did I say  quintessential New York breakfast spot?
Yep

I have dreams of this place.... can't wait to be back in the big Apple so I can swing by this place again. The salmon is just so delicious. U can't go wrong with that bagel platter, but I've tried a few things and I loved it all. Must try
Whoops. We stopped by here not realizing it was a dining experience. Head on down a block or two over for their quick grab and go.

So excited to visit NYC and this is our first stop. So many things to choose from but since there were three of us we tried a little bit over everything. Got an eggs Benny, Shtetl, and Pastrami Russ. To good times with good friends!

Go to the original deli instead if you have the time/a small group.

We walked right past it and stopped in for a few minutes, before realizing how long it would actually be to stand in line. But the atmosphere there is really lively and endearing, and the cafe is a bit of a tourist trap. Maybe the deli is a tourist trap now too, but it certainly feels like it's preserving the neighborhoodly deli experience.

The one advantage here is that you can put your name in for their super long wait (45min-1hr at 9:30am weekday lol) and walk around and visit other things to wait for a text. We got to try some coffee and walk around the city for our last morning. Plus, it's a little bigger and you get to sit down, esp nice if you have luggage. But where's the fun in that!

The food itself here I found to be overpriced and unmemorable. $20+ for 4 transparent razor thin slices of fish, a dried out bagel, and waaaaaay too much toppings for the portion of fish. Matzo ball soup was okay. Service was like... people sick of tourists and just want you to leave, but I guess people say that's just new york.

Overpriced, tourist trap.

I had eggs benny and smoked martini. They were superb. The ambient and the vibe were amazing! I am visiting nyc just for a few days, but i ll definitely come back here in the future as I ll have a chance

Without a doubt the most incredible bagel with lox spread I have ever eaten. While waiting in line, delivery after delivery kept coming in of the fresh, smoked fish. In addition, the cream cheese spreads were FANTASTIC. Go for the best NY bagel experience.

Been here 3 times.
Brunch time is really really busy with 1h to even 2h wait. The good thing is that they text.
The last time went at night around 8 amd
We were seated right away.
All kinds of smoked fish are delicious and it comes with the peefect veggies and cream to pair it.
The atmosphere is like an old diner and seating is pretty spacious.
Food is really really good!
Will come back again and again

Y'all are crazy if you don't think this place has some of the best bagels and lox on the planet. They been doing it forever and the cafe is such a great addition to their little lox empire. Sure, the wait times can be ridiculous but, it's worth it people!

I normally get "the classic" board which is all the standard fix-ins for a lox sandwich and it never disappoints. On top of my wonderfully standard order, I got the matzo ball soup and the latkes because I was still in the window of Hanukah. They were super tasty and I'd definitely get the soup again...souper comforting, get it ;)

Thank you for existing Russ & daughters. You bring a tear to my eye every time :)

My boyfriend and I were pretty disappointed by Russ & Daughters. We're huge fans of lox & cream cheese bagels and heard that they were incredible here. We've tried better in NYC and in Toronto. 

The platter was super-expensive and not worth it. I mean, it was good. Just good. The ambiance was decent and the mimosa was yummy, but the service was very average and so was the food. 

Wouldn't recommend waiting 30 mins-2 hours to be seated, but if you're looking for a quick, satisfying meal, I'd suggest giving it a try. Maybe the other items on the menu are better.

I came here as a party of 2 on a Monday for lunch! The line was insanely long - the wait was about an hour. So we put our names down and walked over to the nearby starbucks to grab coffee and walked around the indoor market nearby.

The interior of Russ & Daughters is fashioned like a diner! I love the vibes you get from that - we sat at the counter. The waitress was super helpful in helping us digest the menu and figure out what to order. 

We got the...
-LOWER SUNNY SIDE: which is potato latkes and sunny side up eggs with smoked salmon. Eggs were done perfectly and the latkes (my favorite part of this dish) were crispy on the outside and delicious with the egg. The salmon was also on point - this was such a good combo and I would highly recommend getting this! 
-CINNAMON BABKA FRENCH TOAST: this comes with an apple compote on top as well as creme fraiche. The combination of flavors (sweetness from the french toast, and then the tartness from the compote) was amazingly delicious. This only comes as one thick slice of french toast which was slightly disappointing given the price you pay for this and how delicious it was! I wish the portion was bigger for this! 

My only thing was that the portions came to be smaller than I expected, especially for the price you pay for it. But I'm not from NY so I probably don't know what to expect haha. Delicious place with good vibes and friendly staff - great experience for sure :)

Great spot that my wife and I absolutely loved. 

Cafe is cozy. It's designed like it's from a time long ago. You may not have been alive when that aesthetic was in style, but it just makes you feel good. It's timeless. 

Food was delicious. I ordered the Russ Pastrami. It was amazing. The waiter said it's pretty small so I should get something else to go with it. I got the matzo ball soup. I was able to eat some of it and it was delicious. My wife stole the rest from me and wouldn't give it back because she loved it so much. 

There was one weird thing I noticed. The hostess kept telling everyone who checked in that they would have to wait forty minutes. I asked someone next to us how long they had to wait. They said the hostess told them forty minutes, too. But they only waited five minutes. The same thing happened to us. And, even when it got slow after we were there for awhile, they kept telling people the same thing but seated them shortly after.

What a delight. We sat at the counter and the wait staff was attentive and pleasant.  I had the Bagel, lox, capers and tomatoes.  Also got the sour pickles and green tomatoes. There were both half and full Sour Spears that were perfect.

Fresh brewed coffee was hot and flavorful on a cold day. 

Can't wait to come back on my next trip to NYC.

Off the chain good! Fresh, fun, clean and amazing!!! We shared the IDA between 4 of us! It was so good!!!! I love it!!! We also indulged and had a blintz! The perfect  true Jewish restaurant! The Service was  impeccable! The ambiance is perfect for the theme. We sat in a booth which was very spacious. I highly recommend this restaurant for a true Jewish experience. But, expect to wait s but. We waited 30 minutes which gave us enough tine to have a quick cup of coffee a block away.

Went here for my birthday on sunday. Wait was an hour 20, which i figured was about average considering how popular the place is. We had kugel, kasha varnishkas, latkes, matzah ball soup, halvah ice cream, a few cocktails and shrubs, and the platter with the sturgeon and sable. Everything was spectacular. The smoked fishes especially were a cut above anything ive ever had before. None were oily or greasy or too salty. The sable just melted and the trout and sturgeon also incredible. Got the halvah icecream for dessert. This is definitely our new special occasion restaurant, cant believe ive lived in ny this long without going here.

Yup this is the place - you want bagels, nova, cream cheese, latkes, CHOCOLATE BABKA (BEST IN NYC), matzoh ball soup?????????? Russ and daughters has it and has it delicious!!!!!!! It's worth the wait for the soft yummy bagels, creamy cream cheese and perfectly fresh fish. I'm not lying when I say my bf and I buy a loaf of babka, and eat it on the bench outside. Straight loafin. Ppl watch and are like word. Bc they know the babka is straight fire and they understand. Bring the rest of that loaf home and warm it up with some butter- instant nut.
Unique with so many choices. The latkes and borscht are great. Pastrami Russ make s nice snacking sandwich. Boards of smoked salmon and caviar round out the menu. Very nice little place.

With the amount of hype surrounding Russ & Daughters, I definitely had my expectations really high (given I am an all important Yelp reviewer :P). I got there about 5 - 10 minutes before open which turned out to be an excellent decision. The place quickly filled up and was packed within 30 minutes!

I ordered "The Classic" dish which essentially allowed me to make my own lox bagel. Was definitely a cool experience to do it yourself and to determine how much of each ingredient you want. The salmon was really really good, and you could taste the difference between here and some of the other famous delis in New York. You could taste the richness of the fish without it feeling too fatty. 

On the negative side, I feel that the bagel was underwhelming. While not bad in any way, it certainly didn't live up to the high quality set by the salmon.

Overall, while a cool experience, I think I might settle for the other location in the future, mainly just given the price differential.

I took my parents here last week and we enjoyed our meal a great deal.  The lox is some of the best you can find anwhere in the entire NYC, or New Jersey area.  The service was OK and the prices are a bit steep, but I would come back here for a special occasion.

Okay, this place was like having a food orgasm. 

My friend and I walked in on Christmas Day at about noon. They told us there was a two hour wait, which was no problem since it's an interesting neighborhood to walk around in anyways. I can imagine why it was so popular on Christmas since it's one of the few places open and we weren't in the mood for Chinese food. 

About an hour and a half into our wait we decided to walk in and ask if they were ready and sure enough they were. I don't know the name of the woman bartender but she whipped up two cocktails for us while whipping up drinks for other customers too and chit chatting with five people all at once...it's like she had ten hands or something, she was clearly very good at her job and getting stuff done, working in an extremely busy kitchen.

The food was to die for. My friend convinced me to get the whitefish chowder, which normally wouldn't have been my thing, but the fish was so fresh it almost tasted sweet. It had a mixture of vegetables inside it too and the broth was the icing on the cake. It was honestly the best food I have ever had in my life.

After the cocktails came the salmon with cream cheese, lox, and capers but by then I was just totally stuffed. The bill was about $100 for 2 people which isn't bad for a Christmas meal. It was incredible food, kind of packed but why wouldn't it be over Christmas?

When a restaurant has a retro theme, you expect the service to be "old world" friendly too.  With the waiter we had - not so.   [the other waiter seemed much nicer].  Applicable descriptives: "snarky," "disinterested,"  "impatient" and zero enthusiasm for the food.   For instance, the herring platter came with 3 sauces not readily identifiable -  but no descriptive explanation was given and if we had asked, I'm sure we would've been given an annoyed, terse answer. Such a shame because I was expecting a special experience here.   Also - the restaurant is well designed with a museum like feel....but the booths seem to be retro too -  back when Americans were smaller.
