Very little leg room and I would think a challenge for anyone with a large waist.  I suppose this is why the snarky service was the deal breaker.  When you're crammed into a booth,  a friendly, enthusiastic waiter can make all the difference.  Ya know?
The food, overall, I'd give 4 stars.  Terrific herring and salmon, of course. The rye bread was a bit dry and stale...and the mushroom barley soup too watery.  Dressing on the beat salad could use more pizzazz.

Although the wait is ridiculously long, the food makes for it. The elegant yet simple plates are just enough, and leave you more than satisfied. I recommend the bagel and lox, the egg creams, and the latkes.

Late lunch while on vacation after visiting the 9/11 memorial.  We walked in and were asked if we wanted a table it was only a 10 minute wait or we could sit at the bar.  We sat at the bar and service was super attentive.  My wife and I shared a Matzo ball soup.  Then we ordered the bread basket (comes with 2 bagels, 2 pumpernickel bread, 2 Rye, slice of hallah and bialy) comes with butter and cream cheese.  Also, purchased an order of potato latke with the applesauce and sour cream.   The potato latke of which were 3, very big and absolutely awesome, the sour cream was super think and delicious as well.  We did not finish all the bread and took the rest home.  Will be back as this was only my first visit.
Great place , authentic New York . Gives the real flavor of a new york hot spot . Raglauch lox bagels . All the best nyc has to offer

This is my go-to for brunch. The wait is painful, but they will text you when your table is ready. My friends and I usually walk down the block to start cocktails, then return when our table is ready. The boards are great, the soups are great, the caviar is awesome - you won't be disappointed. Everything is on point except the greeters/hosts, they're rude. The board is definitely great if you have a group of four or more.

We came in on a Thursday and there was no wait for lunch. As lox fanatics, we had to try the the classic board, choosing to go with an everything bagel. It was probably the best lox bagel I've ever had. The bagel was soft and had a chewy texture. The amount of lox was perfect. And it was fun to construct everything yourself. 

The potato latkes were great as well. They were a little dry on their own but smearing it with the applesauce and sour cream drastically improved them.

Overall: 4.5/5 Food: 4.5/5; Atmosphere: 4.5/5; Service: 4/5
Good for: Brunch, dates, causal
Bad? Long waits

Food: 4/5
*** = would eat again
- ***The Classic (board): A spread of lox, creamed cheese and vegetables to make your own bagel. Yum yum. Lox so fresh!

- ***Eggs benny: Delicious!! Eggs perfectly cooked. Hollandaise so good. 

- Chocolate babka french toast: I love babka and french toast. The babka wasn't as decadent as the one at Breads, but with the sour cream and the berries, it was super unique. While I liked it, I'd probably try something different next time.

- ***Cream soda: I'd never had a cream soda, but I'd recommend. It's like a fizzy, milky drink.

Atmosphere: 4.5/5
So cute. It's like an old school diner, but a little sterile, which made it seem even more retro and a little futurist. The decor was heavily white influenced, and the waiters were wearing white coats and white aprons. I was surprised because I thought it would be more old school and refreshed when it wasn't.

Service: 4/5
Really friendly! Only issue here is the super long wait. If you want to eat there probably have to hop into another cafe to have a coffee or drink while you wait it out.

On my last morning in New York (a Friday) I decided to take the subway from my hotel in Greenwich Village to the Lower East Side and eat breakfast at the Russ & Daughters Café. It's a spinoff of their appetizing counter that has been on the LES since 1914. It's on Orchard Street which is really cute. I walked in at 9:05 and got a table immediately. I decided on a hot tea and the Potato Latkes with wild salmon roe and crème fraiche. The latkes were hot and crispy, the roe was fresh and salty, and was perfect with the crème fraiche. Best breakfast I've had since my last trip to New York. I don't feel bad about doing something really touristy because I would never get to eat a meal like this in the Midwest where I live. It's simply not available and I absolutely love this food. It's in my DNA. I can't think of anywhere better to eat smoked fish...
*I walked all the way back to Greenwich Village after to walk off my breakfast!

Come early to avoid the wait, or go to the original location for take out. The food was delicious and I wouldn't mind eating here every day. The staff was kind and even offered us samples of the different smoked fish. The smoked fish went well with the fresh new york style bagel and the latkes with ikura were a definite winner.

I've been to the bagel shop (for lack of better terms) of Russ and Daughters one too many times. How can you not get the classic lox bagel for breakfast when you're in the area? Anyways, Russ and Daughters Cafe is a cozy place a couple blocks away that has a seating area while the "deli" does not. They also have a much more expansive menu, but me being me, I stuck with the bagel and lox and shared a platter of potato latkes with a friend. Luckily there is a more than adequate amount of everything, especially that delicious melt in your mouth lox- it's literally amazing. 

I'm not sure if it's from ACME or somewhere else but you got to try it if you like smoked fish. Since there's a lot going on, definitely eat each half of the bagel individually or else it'll spill out (as a witness of my friend's bagel lol). In regards to the potato latkes, they were definitely filling and super crispy as well. I'm not a fan of applesauce but that's why there's sour cream. I can definitely see myself coming back and will hopefully try the babka french toast as well.
I hesitate to gush but the secret is out. If you like cured fish and picketed anything, this is the jam.

Bring your own cream cheese. I went with my wife and kids for brunch on Sunday. We waited almost 2 hours for a table. We ordered the classic board (bagel / lox), the eggs Benedict, and matzah ball soup. The eggs were fine, the soup was not .  I think the biggest disappointment was the bagel and lox, something I expected to be the best I had ever had. While the lox was very good, the bagel was only marginally better than the frozen food section of a supermarket and definitely not as good as my local bagel store in NJ. The prices are astronomical, which was expected and fine but the biggest disappointment was that they give you only enough cream cheese for a 1/2 a bagel. When I asked for more, it came quickly. When paying the check I noticed they charged me another $1.50 for another thimble full. I called over the manager (Emily) and let her know we had a nice experience and enjoyed the restaurant but suggested that the waitress either inform customers about the charge, put a small note on the menu or simply give people enough. Her response was to inform me that if I didn't like it I should never come back. That was a good suggestion. I'll find some other overpriced tourist trap to eat brunch in the future.
Wonderful lunch with a fun and attentive staff. I am so glad to have found this gem! They specialize in fish and chopped liver, not deli meats.

Yum, Fantastic service and delicious Bagel,Lox platter,Latkes and blintzes. Super small plan to wait a while for a table. Put your name in and they will text you when your table is ready. The staff is very helpful and friendly.

Russ & Daughters is, of course, a New York institution so I was super excited to finally get to try their legendary smoked fish. And upon first bite it was apparent why they have the reputation that they do. 

My husband and I went on a Friday afternoon and not surprising there was a wait. I think we waited about 30-40 minutes so not horrible. We got a booth towards the back and settled in. The atmosphere is perfect - an old diner feel without being overdone or cheesy. Just classy, clean and cool.  

We started with drinks. I got a chocolate egg cream and he got a soda. Served with a metal straw, the drinks were a great way to start off the meal. Felt very "soda fountain."

Next came out the latkes and matzo ball soup. The latkes were simply amazing. I could have eaten a dozen of them. They come three to an order so I savored every bite of my share. The soup was good but not great. A little bland, actually.

Then came out the salmon! I got the classic - salmon, bagel, cream cheese, onion, tomato, capers. There was a generous portion of the salmon so I grabbed the bagel, slathered on the cream cheese, piled on the tomatoes, salmon and capers and went to town. Each bite was as good as the last. Probably the best smoked salmon I've ever had. 

From the atmosphere to the food to the service we loved every bit of Russ & Daughters. A highlight of our NY trip for sure.

If my friends were here, we would definitely come here! So freaking good!!  We saw Andew Zimmerman here, we left him alone cause we didnt bother him.. Thank you Anthony Bourdain for the recommendation!!

Finally tried this restaurant. First the wait is insanely ridiculous. An hour and 45 minutes is a waste of time if you came specifically for this restaurant. First, to avoid the wait time, come down here and check in to know how long is the wait, you'll get a text when it's your turn for a table. While waiting you can go to a nearby coffee shop or other places around this area to kill time. Otherwise it's not a good use of your time to wait. Im glad I finally tried this place, I am not sure I will go back again to wait that long. No doubt the food is delicious. They have all kinds of salmon.... nova, lox, smoked etc and it's delicious. The chopped salad is quite different but also tasty. I loved the matzoh ball soup. It's a good experience and overall I enjoyed the food except the wait.

My mom and I came here on a Saturday at noon and was told the wait would be 2 hours; we put our name down and started walking around the neighborhood! 2 hours later, we were told it would be another hour. We patiently waited around the area and got coffee nearby, and finally got seated at 3pm. Thankfully, the wait was worth it because the latkes and smoked salmon spread were so good. While the food is definitely delicious, the wait is ridiculous and be aware that you will not be seated for a while. Next time I will be going to the store front on Houston instead of sitting down!

I tried a bagel with smoked salmon in it. The smoked salmon pieces were really good. I usually don't eat cream cheese but it went well with the salmon. Unfortunately I'm just not a bagel person as bagels are too dense and hard for my taste.

It's quite pricey here, I spent a good $18 for my bagel.

We also tried the black and white cookie and that was really good! It was lemon-y and the chocolate was flavorful. The cookie was pricey too. $4 for one cookie!!!! It was like the size of my palm.

This place served a lot of different sweets as well and they all looked good. They serve by the pound.

You can also purchase their cream cheese and their smoked salmons by the pound as well

This bagel and lox obsessed girl was so excited for the meal at Russ and daughters. 
I got the classic (of course), nova, cream cheese, tomato, red onions, and capers with a bagel or bialy (of course, I got an everything bagel). Delicious, although I would have hoped for more nova and more cream cheese.
My friend got the eggs benny, a thick slice of challah bread with spinach, nova, poached eggs, and hollandaise. This was also an incredible take on an eggs Benedict.
My boyfriend, who is not the biggest fan of smoked salmon, ordered the goat cheese and spinach omelet (which usually comes with mushrooms, but he got it without). This came with a side salad and rye bread and butter. The omelet was pretty small but was good. 
The nova was mild and cut thinly, its claim to fame and the cream cheese was perfectly whipped. 
I recommend it for nova-related items, but maybe not as much those who are not as big of fans of smoked salmon. 
Will definitely return, hopefully to try the latkes and matzo ball soup.

Our wait time was about 40 minutes and it was well worth it. The decor is super cool and the food is great. My eggs benny were perfect, with the tastiest lox. My bf got the goat cheese and sable board. I took a bit of this bagel and let me tell you, it was everything you can ask for in your morning bagel.

Smoked sable with side of toasted rye was attractively presented, but a bit thin on the fish compared to salmon board. Honey cake arrived warm, causing steam to arise as spoon dipped through caramel apple ice cream. Black tea paired well with both. Smoked whitefish soup had crisp chunks of carrot and potato. Halvah ice cream was topped with sesame seeds. Beautiful interior design.

Russ & Daughters Café was very underwhelming at best, and poor at worst.  Mostly snobby staff who think they're a gift to the world just because of Russ and Daughters' reputation.  I came alone, dressed well, and was treated like a dog, denied a table although several were available (it was mid-morning on a non-holiday Monday) and forced to sit at the bar.  The bar has a wall in front of your legs, and it was worse than sitting on an American Airlines international flight (those of you who have had that wonderful experience will know what I mean; those who haven't can infer).  I am giving this place two stars instead of one because the food was decent (had a smoked salmon and egg with toast), but it was nevertheless overpriced.  The supposedly legendary Matzo Ball Soup was fairly good for NYC standards, but I can make a much better bowl without much effort, and at $9 a pop, Russ should be able to bestow all his daughters with Gucci bags on your dime.

Their lox platter is classic....the Yum Kippered platter is my favorite....the latkes are perfect....and there might not be a more satisfying lunch in all of New York or the world. The wait on a weekend is 2 hours, but their texting system is excellent so put your name down, got get a coffee, and be ready to feast.

I took myself on a me-date last weekend and wanted to eat here. SO SO SO GOOD. I had the lox and cream cheese bagel spread. Very clean, fresh and everyone was so attentive. I had to wait a few minutes and they texted me when a spot was open. It was so fast!

This is definitely a place to go to in NY for lox.

I had the lox bagel plate, the borscht and matzo ball soup, the kippered salmon salad and the knisch.

I really enjoyed it!! The salmons, both the kippered and the lox, were the best part of the meal, so make sure to load up on salmon and other fishes when you come here.
The lox was glistening, it was so fresh and the flavor was so delicious. The kippered salmon was perfectly baked and had a very nice slightly pickled taste. I really enjoyed the dill and capers that were very present in the salad...very fresh!

The ambiance is very nice too. Dimly lit at dinner time and not too crowded because who goes for bagel and lox for dinner??
Too bad we don't have the eggs benny, classic board, chocolate egg cream and cream soda in Brazil.

2nd favorite thing I ate in NY was the Classic Board. (Most fave was the cookie at Levain!) 

But had to come here twice in one trip bc it was that good!! This place felt really homey, comfortable and familiar to me (although it was my first time in NY). 

Prompt, kind service and good eats. Couldn't ask for much more.

Russ & Daughters gets all the hype in the world, and I don't see as how it's merited. The fish is good, and my portion of kippered salmon was very generous.  But good lox isn't hard to find in New York.  The borscht is watery and weak, pink consommé with a some beets floating around and not much flavor.  I make much better borscht myself, and I'm no chef.  The bialy wasn't particularly exciting.  The cream cheese was whipped - seriously, ladies?  And clearly they don't know about the NY schmear, because the portion was downright skimpy.  The coffee would have been average for a diner.  Having spent $35 on this meal, I'd say don't waste your money.

OY! Russ & Daughters Cafe is where every Jew wants to go to heaven. Wrap us up in lox and bury us with the bagels. This place is as good as it gets.

We've been to the regular Russ & Daughters many times over the years, and our post-wedding brunch was even partially catered by them. We'd tried going to the cafe a couple times before, but the wait was so long that we always gave up. Since yesterday was our five year anniversary, and our daughter was blissfully sleeping in her stroller, we decided to stick out the wait, and we're so glad that we did.

We ordered a lot of food, starting with the pastrami russ, which is a great small bagel bite of smoked deliciousness. SO GOOD. The matzo ball soup was also fantastic, but the whitefish croquettes stole the show. Whoever thought to turn whitefish into croquettes is a GENIUS (thank you, madam/sir). Our only lackluster dish was the chopped salad, which tasted fresh but didn't really come together all that well. The shtetl board was wonderful, and to finish the meal on a sweet note, we got the halvah ice cream. It was BEYOND: creamy, sweet, slightly salty, perfect frozenness level....take us baaaaaack....!

Other than the chopped salad, we only have one minor gripe with this place, and that's with our specific server, who seemed to be excelling at amateur hour. The hostesses, runners, and all the other servers who helped us were great. 

Russ & Daughters really is next level, and we're so happy that we finally tried it. We don't dole out five stars very often, but these are very well-deserved.
Excellent bagels. Some of my favourite. Very unique and a lovely atmosphere. Try some of the signature bagels.
Food was very good, we got the chocolate french toast, Lox bagels and omelet. Would recommend for the food. Although the hostess was RUDE and on her phone the whole time.

The potato latkes were so GOOD. I'm a vegetarian and they had a couple of options such as the potato latkes with applesauce and sour cream $12, the Classic and instead of getting it with the smoked salmon you can substitute it for cucumber or avocado $18 and borscht soup $10 just to name a few

This is one of my favorite breakfast places in the city. First off, it's incredibly charming and sleek, almost transporting you back in time with the light box decor, and retro countertops. The food was humble and delicious. I ordered the chocolate babka French toast (LOVE), a lox platter, and potato latkes with apple sauce. It does get quite busy on the weekends so I recommend getting there early as there are no reservations for breakfast. I can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

We popped in while walking around the neighborhood without realizing what a treat we were in for. We got the latkes, knishes, original combo (bagel, cream cheese, salmon, onion, capers, tomato), kugel, and babka french toast (cinnamon) and a couple of beers and a ginger soda. Can I please have it all again immediately, right now? (I have figured out how, by the way, as apparently several of these items can be shipped).

I think it is sad I can only give you 5 stars!!!
I live in South Carolina and it has Been a long time since I had the perfect deli breakfast . Thank you, Russ and Daughters '

Russ & Daughters Cafe is legendary for a reason. Despite the high price points, the service, atmosphere, and incredible quality of the food are really worth it. I got the Lower Sunny Side, which is smoked salmon with potato latkes and sunny side up eggs. It was perfect and exactly what I was craving. My friend got the matzo ball soup and said it was divine. To round out the meal, we shared the halvah ice cream, which altered my perception of what ice cream can (and should) be.
If time and money were no object, I would eat here every day. Alas, I'll have to eagerly wait for the next special occasion to visit.

Russ & Daughters serves one of the best lox bagels I've ever had! I ordered the classic board which contains smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onions, and capers. There was a generous amount of salmon so the salmon to bagel ratio was superb. Russ & Daughters lox is leagues above any other lox I have ever tasted! Not only was the smoked salmon super flavorful but the bagel tasted great as well.

Smoked herring wasn't too salty, matzo ball soup was clean and yummy, latkes were well portioned. Everything was delicious but nothing particularly memorable.

Came here on a rainy day and didnt have to wait at all. Service wasnt the best, but food came out quickly and it was easy to flag down a server for whatever we needed.

Very good for brunch with friends. They do not take reservations so expect a wait on Sundays. We were a group of 8 and waited about an hour, which I thought was pretty fast. Service was good and restaurant is very Instagram friendly. While very good, I was disappointed by the prices and portions. The French toast was $14 for a single slice of bread and three mini potato latkes for $12 :/ definitely left hungry. Would probably not go back to the cafe, but may try the Shop.

Food was so good. I didn't know what to choose first. I wouldn't normally wait this long for a restaurant but roaming the neighborhood and getting a drink at another place while I waited was all just fine.

I was planning my trip to New York and was all over Insider looking for the best places to eat and this restaurant popped up as the best smoked salmon bagel in NYC, so I knew this place had to be on my itinerary. 

I'm not from New York but I think this place is located in the Lower East Side. I had a bunch of stuff planned throughout the day, so this ended up being a dinner "take-out" type of deal, but it was still worth it. Upon walking in, I realized that this place is an actual restaurant and not your regular bagel shop. I had no idea that they also sold a bunch of other stuff, in my mind I thought it was strictly bagels. I asked the host what she recommends, and she automatically said "The Classic". It's basically a whatever type bagel you want, with smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion and capers. I had it with the everything bagel but had to have it to go, so I couldn't really sit down and I can't really review the service other than the hostess was super professional and helpful. 

When I got back and settled down, I finally got to try it and I was blown away by how good this tastes! It's absolutely delicious. The salmon was so fresh, the cream cheese was the perfect compliment and the capers gave it a perfect crunch! This is definitely a must try, even if it's an 18$ bagel.

Excellent setting and ambiance. The food was delicious. I really liked the matzo ball soup. Yum. Cocktails were also quite tasty. 
We were on the early side so for seated fast. We chose the counter. They even have live music some nights. 
Service was courteous and prompt. I shall be back.

Russ and Daughters is nothing short of exceptional. We were visiting from San Francisco and I would definitely recommend visiting this establishment.

Due to the popularity of this place, expect to wait at least an hour to be seated. They have an system that sends a text and calls you when your seats are ready. 

We ordered The Classic, the Knishes, the Smoked Whitefish Chowder, the Pickled Herring Trio, and the Blintzes.

Everything was outstanding, both the food and the service. Don't except large American portions when eating here, but we didn't mind, because we wanted to try a bunch of different dishes from the menu. 

The Salmon used for the classic wasn't overly smoked or overly fishy, it was prepared perfectly. 
Also, the Pickled Herring Trio was my favorite. The three preparations for the Herring bites highlighted their pickling skills, for both the fish and the pickles they used.

I know this will continue to be a New York staple and I can't wait to come back!

Super Cute Café.
Love all the menu choices.

Hot Smoke/Cold Smoke.
Potato Latkes.
Smoked Whitefish Chowder.
The Classic Board.

Deeeelicious!

Egg Benny was really good. All the notes work well together. It does have only one texture, soft. But the egg was cooked perfectly and it's a lot for one person. I can barely finish mine.

The classic board was great, good portion and the bagel was crunchy. The perfect size bagel with fix-ins.

They have a drink menu which is creative and their uniform is quite cute.

I came around 11:38am and waited 50 mins. They do text you so you can roam around. At first it was 75min wait but we didn't have to wait that long.

I love this place. There's a little piece of me that feels completely at home here. Buyer beware, this review is 1000% colored with a deep nostalgia for my grandparents. That said, the food and service is spot on. 

Tonight we had a lower east side and an old fashioned to drink. Both were absolutely delicious- clean boozy and everything you want in a cocktail. We had the chopped liver which is almost identical to the stuff my grandfather used to serve except he would do a little parsley and grate or chop some boiled egg on top. That stuff brings me RIGHT back to my childhood. So now that I've completely regressed, they serve up the smoked sable and goat cheese bialy (the "Shtetl") and it too is amazing. So amazing that my husband- now drunk from his second old fashioned-orders a second. Finish up with a chocolate babka and we both stumble to our Uber to frankly take a nap. 

Cheap? Nope. Delicious? Yup. Old school? Absofuckinlutely.

The wait even on a weekday is over an hour so arrive early to put your name down on the list and walk over to Houston to their deli to pick up some bagels to go because there is also a shorter wait there (note: grab a number as soon as you enter, if you're only buying baked goods there is no wait on the opposite counter). Once seated in their cafe, you will notice the menu which is on their placemat. The open board sandwich was beautifully presented. Omlette was very fluffy with an abundance of lox. Even tried their dessert recommended by our server. Fresh fruit juice and refillable house coffee.

I went back and forth about coming here for Sunday breakfast, and I am SO happy we did. We arrived a few minutes before opening, and were seated in a booth right away. We ordered coffee, borscht, smoked fish chowder, knishes, and the smoked fish under noshes. Everything was excellent! Both soups were seasoned perfectly-- so flavorful. And the pumpernickel rye bread that came with the borscht tasted freshly baked. Service was great, decor is interesting. This place serves classic Jewish food-- expensive, but worth it. Yum!

The fact that I've yet to review Russ & Daughters Cafe is appalling. Shame on me!

Simply put, though this annex doesn't have the history of the small Houston outpost, it was a legend the moment they broke ground. The grocer comes to life in the form of a full-fledged restaurant that's as important to the fiber of Lower East Side as any cultural powerhouse that's made the neighborhood famous throughout the world. Whether it's breakfast, lunch, or an early dinner--this IS New York.

I find myself there mid-morning most often, and you're going to have to wait if you time your visit even slightly incorrectly. Once you're there, grab a board with any number of different seafood items, and don't sleep on the breads. The bagels get the most love, but the pumpernickel is a standout as well.  Also, the whitefish chowder is the perfect accompaniment for cold days in the city.

Tourist from L.A.  Came based on recommendation from NYC native friend- was told it was best bagels in NYC.  Was expecting a zoo-like overpriced atmosphere like Katz's deli, but was pleasantly surprised.  The ambiance at this cafe is very nice and modern.  We had the lox and bagel boards and a third member of our party had the mushroom, spinach, goat cheese omelet.  Everything was amazing, quality was superior, service was great, seating was like at any normal restaurant (we had 20 min wait for table for 3 on a Tuesday at 10am).  The total cost for 3 was $50, which is amazing for the quality of food and fact that we were able to get breakfast in a peaceful, ambient restaurant in NYC.  Would come back again- adding this place to my list of NYC faves.

Loveeeeeeeeee!! The wait is ridiculous but I recommend you put down your name, walk the streets of East Village until you get that text that your table is ready -- Trust me, it's worth the wait. It's super packed but the food is delicious.

What to order? Cream soda to drink. Salmon platter with an everything bagel.

The salmon was perfection. The decor was so retro vintage, I loved it. The service was great, the staff was friendly. I can't wait to go back to NYC to visit them again.

Came here on my first morning in NYC after I hit up a workout at Barry's (I had to for what I was about to eat). Ordered the Nova on a sesame bagel with the scallion cream cheese, fully loaded and a Nova on everything with plain cream cheese, fully loaded. Good thing I worked out before this and it was worth every minute and drop of sweat. You walk in and take a number and it's an old fashioned kosher style deli/shop. I would stand in line for an hour just to experience the people and atmosphere--and of course a bagel.

Superb quality fish:  Lox and sable boards with bagel. Drinks great too:  Bloody Mary and something called a Smoked Martini, with Lillet, Gin and St Germaine.  All great!  Popular place though, plan on a wait. One block from the Tenement Museum.

As a recant NYC transplant and a long time fan of FRIENDS (my favorite sitcom), I had to visit Ross and Daughters. With every bite of the bagel I could imagine David Schwimmer building his character to new heights. A must visit for fans of FRIENDS and the big Apple alike. I waited about 2 hours for a table, but the art gallery across the street had open WiFi, so I killed the time watching YouTube compilation videos of Ross's best moments on FRIENDS.

EXCELLENT service. We were told this was the place to go and boy was it worth the 105 minute wait. They text your phone though so you can walk around and enjoy the area while you wait for your table.
The lox was fresh and delicate, the schmear was so yummy, and the drinks were both aesthetically pleasing and strong. Best matzo ball soup I've ever had.

I can't believe that it has taken me so long to review this place! This place is a treat in all ways. They opened this place around the corner from their shop which has been around forever! I have always gotten the bagel from there religiously and they are very good! I tried the knish which was very good along with the chocolate babka French toast. They were excellent! My friend got the classic board which is a must try if you are visiting this place for the first time. It is not very easy to get a reservation or table as we had to wait a while to get ours! It was well worth the wait!

Had been here before about 4 years and was anticipating the return visit. However the discourteous and disinterested hostesses at the entrance made us turn around and leave. Once we were finally acknowledged, we were told that there would be a 30" wait. Didn't seem plausible considering that the restaurant had many empty tables at 10:30 on a Wednesday morning.

I can't stop thinking about the amazing meal I had at Russ and Daughters. I came with 3 other friends and we split the Ida platter. It was worth every penny. The platter comes with free refills of everything except the fish, which was good because we ended up needing refills on everything because it was all so tasty. We each ate easily 2-3 bagels. The bagels were perfectly toasted and chewy in the center, yet surprisingly light. The cream cheese was flavorful and light. Their dill pickles were crispy. The fish was all amazing, with my favorite being the pastrami cured salmon.

We arrived around 10AM on a Friday, and ended up waiting approximately 45 minutes. Every minute was well worth it.

Food can't be beat! Best smoked salmon, herring, latkes, kugel in the city. Our waitress was very friendly and didn't rush us. 
The layout of the cafe is a bit odd and the wait is ridiculous. They had several empty seats the entire time we waited. They know it is an extremely popular place so not sure why they don't either keep it fully staffed or have the waitlist better organized. Seems sloppy and unprofessional. 
I recommend getting take-out from the Russ & Daughter store instead

Overall, the experience didn't live up to the hype. Yes, the food was great, but the service was far from it (I'll specifically mention the hostess here because she seemed like she wanted to be anywhere but here on Monday morning and it showed). There are plenty of places across New York that offer both great food and service but if you're in the area and there isn't a huge wait then why not?

Good food, but not at all worth the wait.  They have alot of hype and a one hour wait is considered lucky.  Two hours is more usual.

At the prices they charge, the salmon is a very good deal.  The beer selection is weak ad the cocktails are stupidly expensive.  Bafflingly, the bagels are well below average.  I do like the set up, it's a pleasing atmosphere for my tastes.  All the staff was pleasant.  We sat in the booth by the cook station.  The cooks aren't exactly careful about how teir hands touch non-hygenic things and then the food.

Would I go back?  Hard to say.  Its a four star place that loses one because of the wait times.  It's just not worth the wait overall.

Be prepared to wait, and then be glad you did!

It really doesn't get better than this.  From the nova to the bagels to the chopped liver, everything is amazing. Whether you're a local or a visotr, this should be on everyone's list.

Five stars. Looking forward to our next visit!

Came in, signed up for a table, was told it would be an hour wait and that I should've received a confirmation text. I come back 15 minutes later and tell the host & hostess that I didn't receive a text, so they send one after I brought it to their attention and confirm my telephone number. After and hour and a half of waiting in the area with no update, I figured I would never be contacted about the table and I had wandered too far out to go back to the locale and ask what happened. I was never contacted by Russ & Daughters about when my table was ready, not even by the next day, and therefore never was seated. The host & hostess are clearly incompetent if they can't even get the waiting list right. Would not recommend.

I waited two hours with my boyfriend to eat at Russ and daughters, and it was worth it! We put our name on the list and explored the neighborhood, checked out a dope coffee shop, and even popped over to Soho for some shopping before we made it to our lunch time. The lox
board is soooo incredibly delicious and totally satisfying. Bloody Mary is crack on as well! Highly recommend a soda if you have the appetite for it to. Well done, Russ and daughters, well done. The cafe is also adorable (HUGELY instagrammable) and the waitstaff is very kind! Wonderful service and wonderful meal!

Tried the everything bagel with cream cheese, Scottish lox, capers and tomato. The lox and bagel were very good. The lox was flavorful, fatty and a little salty (as seafood usually can be). I have not tried lox and bagel this good in my life before. That is not to say that there doesn't exist a place where lox and bagel are tastier.  

$$: a little overpriced, but I imagine that the lox is smoked in house and cream cheese is also made in house so you are paying for quality and that I can understand. 

Service: some of the helpers are nicer than others. The first time I came a male who was middle age, light complexion and thin helped us out. He was not as friendly as the gentleman who helped us out the second time. He was also a middle age male, clean shaven, with a bigger built. 

I would definitely recommend this to anyone who would like to try authentic lox and bagel. A couple of blocks away from this location is a sit down Russ and Daughters. I prefer to come to this one as I like the ambiance, how the salmon is cut in front of you. Also lox and bagel is more of a to-go and enjoy in the park sort of food.

Nice spread with perfect combo and plenty of ingredients, was a tad too salty for my taste and the bagels themselves are nothing special. Toaster wasn't working either, but overall the combo of the ingredients is to me what makes the visit worth it

Great food for Saturday morning refreshing. I like the soup best but the smoked salmon is a little salty. Bagel is heated and crispy, better than the bagel I tried before. You need to expect waiting for 20min if you come later than 9:00am on Sat. morning.

So good.  I've never had a bad meal here.  My only regret is that I can't eat here more often (okay, generally that I can't make it to NYC more often!).  

It does get very crowded, and the wait is getting longer, even if you come early in the day.  Maybe time for another cafe....?

The chocolate french toast was amazing and the scrambled eggs were okay after adding salt, pepper and hot sauce. The service was great and the only downside was the $4 grapefruit juice in a tiny glass.

yesterday, i went in after seeing an art exhibit across the street. i wanted to order a meal and take out my order.
cafe employee: "you can't take out here."
me: "why not?"
cafe employee: "we don't have a take-out menu."
me: "my stomach won't know the difference."
cafe employee: "no, you have to go to our E. Houston St. location."
i left, but later i realized that i neglected to ask: "if i stay to eat, but can't finish all my food, do you have doggie bags? or are doggie bags considered 'take-out' and not allowed?"

Love this place! Nestled in the heart of LES, you can find all your favorite Jewish food that bubbie used to make. The novas are so fresh and flavorful and bagels are just the right texture. The blintzes were my favorite!

This place was awesome! We had 3 people on our party and we decided to go with one of the platters. It's a great way to try the different smoked fish varieties. This was also my first time trying sable and sturgeon and I have to say it won't be my last. The board is great way to set this dish up since it allows you to portion everything how you would like. I find that lox bagels all too often are always to eat and sometimes very dry or nice versa. The additional pickled veggies and bread were also delicious and interesting. 
I paired the meal with a glass of champagne and it was light and refreshing for an early afternoon brunch. Will definitely make this a stop on any future trip to New York.
I can not seem to come to New York and not head here for a bagel and lox board.  True taste of New York.

Easily one of my FAVORITE places in NYC. We arrived at 2pm on Saturday and the wait was an hour for 2 people. The waiter was informative and polite. The interior was very cute. 

- Smoked whitefish chowder soup: They were able to split it into two bowls for sharing which is appreciated. The soup had the most perfect creamy consistency. It was slightly sweet which went well with the salty smoked whitefish. There were plenty of bite sized vegetables. I do wish they offered more fish.

- Shtetl (smoked sable) platter: This was life changing! Do yourself a favor and try it instead of getting the usual lox. The sable was SO delicious and buttery. Paired with goat cream cheese, tomato, onion and capers on top of toasted sesame bagel....it's one of the best things I've had not kidding.

I CANNOT WAIT TO COME BACK AND TRY THE REST OF THE MENU!!!

Best breakfast hands down. 

Ordered the cold smoke, the classic board, pickled herring trio, and the whitefish croquets. All were perfect. I can't find the words to describe how amazing these dishes are. You just have to go an taste it.

I had the best potato pancakes I've ever had here. (Latkes) But I've heard so much is great here, that people wait for a long time. I guess that's the only drawback - the wait. But it's an interesting neighborhood and you can go to galleries while you wait and they will text you when your table is ready. Good system!

Obligatory NYC stop! But also one of the most delicious! Boyfriend ordered the matzo ball soup and then we shared the smoked sable open faced bagel! So much yum on one platter! Definitely would recommend to anyone visiting NYC, wanting to sit down instead of waiting in line at the original Russ and Daughters!

This is my happy place! Nothing beats the Classic board at Russ & Daughters. Hands down the best bagel and lox in the city. This is my second visit here and it did not disappoint. Salmon is super fresh and the bagels are delicious. The atmosphere of this place is great; reminds me of an old school upscale diner. Good service, great food, and free refills on coffee. My favorite place in the city to get breakfast. Make sure to get here early to avoid a long wait.

Food: 4/5
Stopped by for dinner with a friend. We ordered the chopped salad, the mixed green salad with salmon and a side of smoked salmon. The mixed green salad came with a house vinaigrette and it was delicious! It had a very generous portion of salmon and capers! My friend enjoyed the chopped salad as well. The side of smoked salmon was very savory and not too salty. Four slices for $11. 

Service: 5/5
Our waitress was a delight. She recommended my salad and I was very satisfied. She was courteous, sweet and accommodating. 

Ambiance: 4/5
Very cute and charming little place in the lower east side. There's a bar in the front and seating throughout the back. Had a charming bistro/cafe feel. Seemed like a great place for brunch. 

Overall: 4/5
Great place to grab a bite. If you're craving lox or caviar, this place is the place to go!

There's a reason we had to jump into a 2 hour waiting line to get a table here on a Sunday afternoon! The food was fantastic. As a southerner, i'm not extremely well versed in Jewish or more specifically Eastern European cuisine, but the soup, pudding, french toast and eggs benny from this place took me down a unique road of flavors! Must try when in nyc!

One star is for the service not the food. 

We went in at around 5pm on a Sunday with 4 adults, a kid and a toddler. Was seated by the rude hostess within 10 minutes. First I thought it's NYC and I totally get why service industry people are cold as being on your feet for your full shift with streams of people coming in is not easy. Russ and Daughters is somewhat of a NYC landmark and obviously tourists are here all the time with regulars. However, when I saw her pour her smile onto the next few customers coming in, I realized that she just didn't like the face of us and was just plain right rude. The 10 minutes we were there, my husband had the dare to ask her for a glass of water for our toddler and was told " you can ask the  bartender yourself" in one of the most rudest tone I have ever heard. 

The first server who took our order seemed to be under the notion he was doing us a huge favour. And  forgot 2 of our items with this same attitude. Thankfully things looked up when someone else took our table and we were served like a pro. 

We enjoyed the food. Yes it is expensive - we were paid almost 200 for 4 plates of fish and bagel, 2 soups, 2 starters and a few drinks. I like their menu and would obviously like to come and eat here next time I visit NYC but if you are from the west coast and are Canadian get ready to get one of the most rude services ever. In here it's ok to be selective and be nice to friends in front of people who you have been rude to a few minutes ago.

This place is just as good as their deli. The food is incredible and the service was excellent. Ordered the classic, the yum kippered, the barreled vegetables, the potato knishes and the bread pudding. Everything tasted good and the cocktails we got were also very nice. I'll come back here in a heart beat the next time I visit NYC.

It's a classic New York Jewish experience you've gotta try, but if you don't eat meat or fish you will likely be disappointed here. The bagels are poor, confusing being in NYC. I got the mushroom, spinach, and goat cheese omelette which was fine. I wouldn't come back here as a vegetarian, but who knows maybe their lox is great!

Yummy!!!  It's never enough food, though. I don't know if it's my appetite or their portions (prob a little of both), but I always order more after my initial order. The smoked sable is my favorite. followed by the smoked salmon, and my daughter and I usually end up getting something sweet - the kugel is ok but the babka french toast is stupid good. Just can't get it every time!

Great decor and design, not too retro or trying to be too hip. Great fish and delights. Love the egg creams. Cocktails are classic and not too sugary. A little expensive for a bagel. Dining area is way too hot though, someone turn up the ac!

The omelette was cooked just right. No brown spots on it just as it's supposed to be. Perfectly cooked. The mushroom goat cheese inside was delicious. And the shissel rye was delicious. More flavor than rye I have had ever. A must visit place especially if you like traditional Jewish food.

Had an overall excellent experience here for brunch. The interior is bright and clean, and the booths are especially nice to have a good catch-up with friends and family. Anything involving lox or smoked fish here is (of course) amazing, but an additional highlight was the blintzes, which were the best I've had in the city. The filling was not overly sweet and the crepe was perfectly prepared. With NYC prices these days, the cost of the meal also felt reasonable. Would definitely return and recommend.

I'd give this a 5 if it were easier to get a table and really have a long brunch but that's the only reason to deduct a point.

Yes, this place is touristy to an extent. And yes it is an instagrammers wet dream. Most importantly yes this is an institution.

The food is fresh and quick. The produce is of the highest quality and the waiters are delightful and knowledgable.

We have definitely had our fair share of lox, smoked salmon and gravlax and this has made the list.

Tips: book in advance, don't plan the lazy brunch here. The staff are attentive and respectful but the line out the door will have you moving on before yo?3 finished catching up with the friend you haven't seen for 5 years.

Incomprehensibly good, and since it's a popular brunch spot is seldom busy for dinner.  Love all the fish; the whole herring in particular was transcendent.  Service is knowledgeable and extremely friendly.  The goat cream cheese is also a marvel.

Russ & Daughters Cafe is one of my favorite spots in New York. I just love the atmosphere and the staff. Had a great time and can't wait to come back to try more things on their menu.

What to order - Definitely try the Classic - Gaspe nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers and served with a bagel, bialy, shissel rye or pumpernickel. I love salmon so if you do too, you'll have no regrets ordering this one. It is a bit pricey but it's NYC so I already expected to pay that much for a bagel with salmon. I will tell you guys that the smoked salmon was the best smoked salmon I've ever had.

I come here for breakfast each time I'm in town and get the Eggs Benny which is out-of-this-world delicious. It and the place never disappoint. If you go on a weekend, it gets very busy around ten o'clock. But the wait is well worth it.

My husband and I had an early dinner here after tour at the Tenement Museum. 
The food: the white fish croquettes - AMAZING! As are the non-alcoholic sodas. The ginger and lavender was especially refreshing! The beet salad was good! Also, the scrambled eggs with salmon and onions was tasty but a bit runny and, sadly, the everything bagel was far from having all of the seasonings. 
The service: gets 2 stars! Our server disappeared and only returned when we asked another server for our check (she never checked in with us). 
I would love to check out another location.

I love their bagels and different types of smoked fish. Truly a New York classic. The ambiance is pretty nice but can feel cold and sterile which isn't the best dining atmosphere. A bit on the expensive side too.

My Jewish friend took me to this place and I loved it. The deviled eggs had fresh caviar on it and it was delicious. I got the lox with eggs and latkes and although it is more of a brunch dish, it still tasted yummy for dinner. They have a lot of fresh seafood on their menu, so I would like to come back and try some of their other stuff. Their apricot bread pudding was so soft and the apricot added a nice sweetness to it. I would definitely recommend coming here since you can probably only get this in NYC.

The food is fine. But that's not enough. The staff is inflexible and imposing. There are other fine places to eat deli food in the neighborhood. Go to Katz's, for instance. 
This morning, I wanted to join my wife and two friends who were already seated at a table that would have comfortably allowed me to join them. Minutes later, a presumptive manager appears and tells us there is no room at a table at which I was already comfortably seated. He then proceeded to scold all of us that he wouldn't have seated the three of them if he knew I was coming (an hour) later. 
To hell with Russ and Daughter cafe.

This is an outstanding breakfast spot, but always super busy on the weekends. The wasabi roe is amazing, and a great accent to lox, among other things. The cocktails are also very well made by the mixologist. Staff is all on-point and friendly always.
Excellent food. Went father's day and had a long wait. That was the negative. But it was worth it!
Loved the ambiance, the bagel was absolutely delicious however it was 19.00 for one bagel!!! I would go back however it wouldn't be often due to the price. If your visiting I would recommend going.

I've visited the Russ & daughters cafe at the Jewish museum, and the original spot on Houston - out of the three of them, this cafe is probably my favorite. I tried the potato latkes (which they don't have on the menu uptown) and classic board. Everything was delicious, and the service was great. I also recommend the babka French toast.

Was looking for a great place to meet friends for a Sunday breakfast and found a Winner!   Even though we had to wait an hour to get in it was worth the wait.   Started with a smoked pepper Bloody Mary.  Spicy but delicious.   Went with the combo platter that included two perfect sunny side up eggs, smoked salmon and 2 great potato pancakes.   Also had the noodle kugel that had an ample supply of raisins which I loved.    Everyone loved their meal and the service was great also.    If u don't mind waiting add this to your list of must tries while in NY.

Wow! This place is totally worth the hype!!!

I got the classic board which comes with cream cheese, lox, tomato, capers, red onions, and your choice of bread, bagel, or bialy. I had a pumpernickel bagel, because I can never turn down a pumpernickel bagel. The salmon literally melts in your mouth. If you are a fan of lox, this is definitely one of the best!

There are two Russ and Daughter's within blocks of each other. Make sure to come to the cafe if you're looking to dine in. The other location is just a deli with no seating inside. 

If you are visiting New York, this is a must!

I hate to wait for food. The host told us 20 minutes and she was exactly right. The food was worth the wait. This place had the most amazing smoked salmon bagel sandwich. Don't bother looking at the rest of the menu.

Really top notch quality fish. Everything is fresh & scrumptious. You really can tell they've been doing this for a long time & perfected the process. My only gripe is with the check in process, the wait is long & a bit disorganized.

Very cute diner/cafe. It's a nice sit down experience compared to the deli on Houston. It's really high quality product and great service. The wait is insane though so recommend eating before / putting your name down and then going somewhere else for a drink in the meantime.

Always a classic. Great food and service. My only gripe is that it is a bit expensive for the amount of food. An extra slice of fish would be better. All the food was great however. Fish is smoked to perfection and latke's fresh and hot. Also, you can't go wrong with the matzo ball soup. Come and leave happy.

I have been to the Russ & Daughters store where you order to take food out, but I had never had the time to wait to get into the Russ & Daughters cafe...until this past weekend!

If you are going to visit Russ & Daughters Cafe on a weekend, be prepared for a wait.  My girlfriend and I arrived around 11am on a Saturday and were told we would have a one hour wait.  We left our number and were put onto a list to receive a text once our table was ready.  Fortunately, if you're into walking around the city, especially a historical district, then killing that hour will not be a big deal.  A quick walk around, a visit to Economy Candy and then a quick run through Essex Market and an hour had already passed!

As if there were an alarm set at the restaurant, exactly an hour after I had put my name down I received a text saying they were ready for us.  Once you receive the text, you need to respond with a confirmation and your table is held for 10 minutes (so don't stray too far away). 

We wound up sitting at the bar, and I have no problem with that.  The bar seating was comfortable and there is something wonderfully old fashioned about sitting at a bar in a classic New York City styled eatery.  While Russ & Daughters Cafe is not the original location, it could certainly pass for it.  The lighting, shelves and signage are all modeled after the original store.  Mostly made up of white, black and silver colors (with some greys tossed in), you definitely get the feel of an establishment that was opened decades ago and then recently renovated.

Since we sat at the counter/bar, the bartender had to double as our waiter and she did a fantastic job.  She was very open to questions about the menu and she whipped up the drinks we ordered super quick.  Here's a rundown of what we had:

COFFEE SODA
Made from the soda machine at the bar, this drink uses a syrup made from Russ & Daughters' own roast.  This drink was absolutely delicious.  If you are a coffee fan, I would totally recommend it.

FERSHNIKIT EGG CREAM
Made from a combination of Kings County Distillery Chocolate Whiskey, Fox's U-Bet Chocolate Syrup, Milk and Seltzer, this drink was absolutely delicious and had just the right balance between sweetness and a hint of Whiskey flavor.

SOFT SCRAMBLED EGGS (W/PADDLEFISH CAVIAR)
This dish was a very decadent, which is exactly why we ordered it!  Go big or go home, right?  The eggs in this dish are scrambled, but instead of your typical chunks of egg, this was a custard-like dish of eggs with a line of caviar lined on top.  You would think this amount of caviar would not be enough, but in fact it was plenty!  The caviar's flavor was potent enough that there was enough to have the caviar flavor permeate very bite.  

The caviar was served with toasted challah bread.  I wound up spreading the eggs and caviar on slices of bread like it was some insanely expensive butter and it was fantastic.  Every bite was delicious with some crunch and chewiness all at the same time.  This is a very pricey dish ($75 when I ordered it) but it was worth trying at least once.

SHTETL
This dish comes with smoked sable, goat cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers and a bagel.  The sable was delicious.  Smooth, creamy and the smoked flavor was not overwhelming.  I really do recommend combining all the ingredients on the board for the most flavorful and satisfying bite.

CHOPPED LIVER
This is more of an appetizer than a main dish, but they do not skimp on the amount of chopped liver.  Several Matzo crackers are included along with pickled red onion.  Trust me when I say you want to combine all the ingredients into one bite for maximum satisfaction!  I was impressed by how the liver was not too heavy or gamey.  It also spread on the crackers perfectly without breaking them into bits.

I absolutely loved my first experience and Russ & Daughters cafe and I really look forward to another trip to try more deliciousness soon!
Amazing.  Cannot wait to come back good.  Bring a friend and get a platter. I don't think I can say enough about this place.
If you like bagels, even just a little bit, you must check out Russ & Daughters. Either location is a must go for breakfast if you're in New York.

In a city with as many food options as NYC has, there aren't many restaurants I'd go back to when there are so many new ones to try. Russ and Daughters definitely qualifies as one of those restaurants however. Their salmon is spectacular, of course- the classic board is perhaps the best smoked salmon sandwich I've ever had. But it isn't just their salmon that makes his one of my favorite brunch spots; their potato latkes are perfectly crispy and very flavorful (I got them with the creme fraiche and salmon roe, which makes for a pretty good combination of flavors). I also really like their whitefish chowder, which has beautifully large pieces of fish in it. It can get busy so if you're going in a large group, I'd recommend getting there before 10. If you're going by yourself, it's usually not too difficult to get a spot at the bar.

Easily the best experience I have ever had at any restaurant. Hands down. They give you a pitcher of water AND seltzer (at no extra charge) right when you are seated. The cafe itself is lovely and nostalgic. The service was wonderful. The food, delicious. Everything about my bagel and lox plate down the the capers was delicious. The lox you get here cannot be compared to anything you would get at the grocery store. Wafer thin and delicate flavor. The matzo ball soup tasted like my mom's. Even the beet juice, something I wouldn't normally try, was fantastic. I love this place. I can't wait to go back!
Smoked salmon from heaven.  Yes there is a god, i'm going to going to church, i don't care which one.  Go here, and that other LES establishment a few blocks north, but this one first.

The people are rude and unwelcoming. In particular, the bar staff. The interactions were cold - as if we were being punished for coming to eat there. I don't care how good and restaurant's food is, good customer service is critical. And these guys get a big fail in that department.

The very best herring - all four kinds - I have had! My wife's babka french toast was incredible. The cherry shrub was one of the most interesting beverages I've tried. The staff was exceptional. Will return the next time we're in NYC!!

Sooooo good. I ordered the Eggs Benny and loved every bite of it. Portions are pretty big and I ended up not finishing the entire thing. But I did contemplate trying to finish my food even if it meant me passing out into a food coma for the next 5 hours. But then thought against it. Which I now regret.

Space is super cute and workers are friendly, patient and answer all your questions about the menu in full detail. I absolutely loved my first experience and Russ & Daughters and am looking forward to going back!

Looks like a classic diner when you walk in - counter seats and booth seats. I love that their windows allow so much natural light in. I also love the little doodles they have around the bathrooms. Servers here are super kind and were willing to answer all the questions I had, especially when I was half brain-dead and was having trouble formulating my questions in the easiest way to understand. 

You can't go wrong with the classic! I like that it's deconstructed so you can decide how much of each ingredient you want to put on your bagel. The bagel was toasted just right, where it was crunchy on the edges, but not too much in the middle. Cream cheese was nice and fluffy, tomatoes were fresh, and salmon was also very fresh. There was definitely a handful of other items on the menu that I would have loved to try. Hoping to come back soon to taste them!

After my bagel fail the previous day at the original Russ & Daughters, I had to redeem myself. I could have went back there, but I also kinda didn't trust myself either LOL. Anyways, the Cafe existed, so I figured I would try this instead because I knew they would make things way easier for my noob self.

Kept it simple, ordered The Classic...this time with a proper everything bagel! I guess the right kinda bagel really does make a massive difference. Aside from that, the overall package was phenomenal. Bagel was the right amount of toast, salmon was flavorful, cream cheese was on point, and onions were fresh. I like how all the items were separated out, so I had the choice of how much I wanted to put on there. Of course, I stuffed the whole thing...was more of a burger than a bagel at that point. 

Service here is fantastic. Everyone is super welcoming and very helpful. Which is obviously helps when dealing with my noob self.

I guess I also got lucky on the wait, because there was none at all at 5 pm on a Saturday. Apparently, that is not the case most of the time.

A note on the interior. It's a throwback diner, so you feel like you're in the 1950s. I don't care that much for that kinda thing, but others do.

In any case, I felt like I got my redemption on bagels, which is all I wanted. Happy to come back here, they sure know how to make a proper bagel!

Our Sunday morning was ruined by the rudeness of the restaurant greeter Pao and bartender who for no reason gave us tons of attitude when we were asking for a seat. Our friends were arriving 10 min late and we asked if we could sit at the bar, which was empty at the time, to order a drink to wait
Before they seated us. The bar was was completely empty except for one customer, but after we were seated at the bar, we were told we could only stand against the wall with our drinks to wait and can not sit at the bar..... I'm not sure if this is because we are people of color, but the rude attitude and treatment was uncalled for, and unacceptable for a restaurant that works in providing service for others.

I guess now they have a sit down restaurant not too far from their original location. You won't get all the selection you get at their original location, but they offer what matters (the salmon lox, duh) along with other brunch fare. The potato cakes were so good especially with a side of caviar and crepe fraiche.

This place always seemed like a destination restaurant. Having grown up in Brooklyn I was used to having what was called appetizing in my youth. 

We figured we'd try Russ and Daughters and reconnect with my family's roots at the Tenement Museum across the street. 

I had sturgeon on a buttered toasted bialy. Just like the old days. Only it wasn't. The sturgeon was dry and instead of the onions baked into the bialy they were what appeared to be sautéed, not browned, and lying on the bialy. 

It would've been nice to write a review about how Russ and Daughters reminded me of my youth in Brooklyn. Instead it reminded me how much better the appetizing was then. 

Sigh.

Now I wanna try out their other location at Russ & daughters... this place is bomb!!!!

Interior--located in Little Italy (or super close to it), this place got the right vibe: laid back, classic diner, with subtle quiet music in the background. The interior is very modern, and they for a bar and bunch of booths. 

Service--excellent!! My friend arrived late and they let me wait at the bar and provided great services during my wait. When we were having a hard time deciding since my friend didn't want fish, the server offered great helps on suggestions :)

Food--dang, my first savory bagel experience and this place did the magic. The bagel was toasted just right, the cream cheese tasted so light yet flavorful, and the smoke salmon was freshhhhh. 

No wonder this place is always on travelers' "NYC bucket list"!! I can't wait to be back!!!!

Exactly what I was hoping for. The sable was melt in your mouth tender. I had the shtetl board and the potato knish. I can't complain, also I got to explain the Yiddish on the menu to the Belgian couple sitting next to me at the counter- so there's that.

Food was awesome (husband had the classic, I had the eggs benny). Service was alright. 

Expect a wait (we came at 1pm on a Monday and waited 40 mins)... but the food justified the wait.

I've been a frequent visitor for Russ & Daughters for 3 years and never been to this cafe. It's really popular!!

Came here on Tuesday around 11am, the wait for 2 was about 15-25 min, which was not too bad for us. We ordered eggs benny, chopped liver & lower sunny side. 

The chopped liver was fresh, and the amount was pretty good in terms of the price. (We didn't finish the liver with all the crackers) highly recommended if you are fan for this.

The eggs benny & lower sunny side are classics for brunch, the eggs were cooked just the way we like, and the lox were so fresh.

Poor service, my server to kick my bag under the table and then spilt my juice as it was put down. If that was a 'fine' establishment a new one should have swiftly followed with cleaning of the spill. Neither happened. Food was ok, but I was so put off by the antics of the server that the meal was ruined from that point for me.

On a recent Friday lunch we met Nikki, one of the owners.  She was genuinely interested in hearing about our many visits to the cafe, it's no accident that this establishment is thriving. Attention to every detail, the best food, exciting new takes on traditional food.  A true NY treasure.well worth the wait

This was a must when I was planning my trip to NYC. I love bagels and smoked salmon so I had to stop by this place. There was no wait when my friend and I arrived and got seated right away. It didn't take long for us to decide what to order. 

Food:
-Classic board (Gaspe Smoked Nova Salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion and capers). The smoked salmon was so yummy!! I love how they put the ingredients on the board and we got to assemble our own bagel. Such a fun experience!

-Whitefish Croquettes (smoked whitefish, potato w/ tartar sauce). Everyone needs to try these because they are amazing! They're crispy on the outside and soft in the inside. The tartar sauce gave a nice balance and added the perfect touch to this dish!

I wish they had this back in CA, craving for this as I type.
Expensive but you know that coming in. Flawless execution of fan favorite dishes is what you're coming for and that's what they give you. Caviar course is great.
Portions are smaller than they should be -- couldn't fill out a bagel properly with how much smoked fish they provided -- but they do a nice job otherwise elevating this genre of comfort food.

I am a longtime lox junkie.  I've eaten it at many places.  But none as great as the Ida's Board at Russ and Daughters Cafe.  There were four types of lox included on a beautiful board with two types of cream cheese, sliced tomatoes, sliced red onions, capers and pickled vegetables, in addition to a bread basket of bagels and other breads -- the best presentation I've ever seen.  By far.  The gravalox literally melted in my mouth.  My wife liked the pastrami-cured the best.  As good as it gets.
Excellent place for all the time. Personally really like fishes especially salmon so this place is great for me. "The Classic" is one the the best meals in this restaurant. Well balanced and tasty.

Wow. I have never waited for 2 hours to eat a bagel until I came to Russ and Daughters. The bagel was delicious. But was it worth the wait? I think not. Their Babka French toast was delish! And so was their Latkes. The interior is also gorgeous~ overall its a solid place. If the wait is like an hour, I would go for it but if not, it's a hard pass.

Food: 5/5   Price: 3/5  Service 3.5/5 Ambiance: 5/5  Bang for your buck: 3/5 

Recommendations: If you want to splurge, you have to get the latkas. 

Would I come back?: Yes! 

Tips: Get there early to get a table or put your name down. On a first date? Get a seat at the bar to sit next to your date and have a more intimate talk. 

Review: Russ & Daughters is probably one of my favorite bagel shops, so I was very excited to get a chance to go to the cafe finally. We made a mistake on going on Memorial Day, which made the cafe packed and chaotic. Since it was closing at 3 (make sure to check for holiday times), there was a waitlist and wait for an hour for two people. They continued to take names and phone numbers until 2, where they would rudely turn people away. 

Once we were alerted for our table, it was another 15-minute wait until we were finally seated. However, once we were sitting, it was a fantastic experience. The cafe has a modern diner feel, with waiters wearing stylish white coats. The menu had a range of items to enjoy from challah toast to eggs benedict. However, the classic is a build your lox plate with your choice of bagel. FYI, your menu also serves as a food mat, which makes it all the better. The bagel was amazing as a Russ & Daughter's bagel should be and the option to make your lox bagel the way you want it was delicious.
This is definitely one of my favorite spots in NY. I always leave with a smile. Best bagels in town.

A very solid choice in a sea of great options. We had one of their boards it easily feeds 4 people. The matzo soup was delicious . 

One very surprising thing was a great spritzer. Not what I expected at a deli/restaurant

Went for an early dinner with a group of 5, including a 1 y/o baby.  Severs were very accommodating and helpful, setting up a high chair and bringing us challah for the baby.  We ordered drinks (egg cream, lower east side), matzo ball soup, knishes, and the Ida platter.  Highly recommend, especially the pastrami-cured salmon.  Can't wait to go back!

Limited menu, eggs were cooked terribly. The coffee wasn't good or refilled and at $3 a cup they're just ripping people off. The cream cheese was crumbly, feel apart, and condensation at the bottom of the cup. The bagel tasted like it was from Thomas bros found at a local grocery store.

Amazing breakfast but I've only been once because the line is insane. Worth the wait once in a while for the warmth of Jewish cooking including smoked salmon, trout, matzah ball soup, and so much more. Wish they had more locations!!!

I was looking forward to trying this supposed NYC staple and was sad to find that it didn't live up to the hype. The wait was an hour and 45 minutes, during which the hostesses were annoyed with the crowd and in grouchy moods. Bad attitudes in customer service are such a mood killer. The bagels and lox at $18 weren't any better than your local deli at half the price. But the most astounding part of our experience was when the GM, Emily, came to our table while we were finishing up and told us we needed to leave "now," since other people were waiting. This was embarrassing and rude. The couple next to us was seated before us and was not asked to move or leave. She told us we could finish our drinks standing up. I've never experienced such inconsideration. Russ & Daughter's staff doesn't value their customers and finds them to be inconvenient. I recommend that you go someplace else where the food is at least better.

Food was good but the wait was not. I didn't mind the 10-15 minute estimated wait. I didn't mind the actual 25 minute wait until we got buzzed. I did, however, mind the additional 30+ minute wait after we got buzzed. 10 minutes into the second wait we were told they were cleaning our table. 10 minutes after that we were told they customers are paying and they will clean the table. They seemed to just give us standard lines regardless of the reality.

Best smoked salmon ever!!  We got the platter, salad, and soup. Then we went to the shop to get more to take home. Be prepared to wait though... today we waited 2+ hrs. Lucky Jacks next door is a great place to spend the wait.

Decided to check this place out based on the rave reviews on Yelp. I have to be honest I was disappointed with the place. There was a two hour wait for lunch. Place had a text messaging service set up so at least we didn't have to stay on premise and could wonder around the neighborhood. That was a plus. Once we were notified our table was ready it was just a short 5 min before we were seated. So far so good. We ordered the Classic Board with the beagle with smoke salmon and the Herring plate.  While smoke salmon and bagel were decent they were not any better or unique compared to the other bagel and smoke salmon I had at beagle shops in west coast (Ie Noah's bagel in east coast would be as good if. It better in both accounts ). The quality certainly would not justified a 2 hour wait. 

The herring plate was good but really nothing that stood out to me. 

Personally for me I do not think it is worth the wait time for table to dine at this place. If there were no wait I would consider revisit. But if there is a wait longer than 10min then my advise would be to go else where.

I came here for a leisurely lunch after a friend recommended it to me. Since I was by myself I easily got a spot on the counter but there was quite a bit of wait for parties of two and more so be prepared for that if you come. I ordered latkes and pastrami smoked salmon and tried the breakfast martini. Everything was pure indulgence! It was a fantastic solo lunch and I must come back! That said, I wish it were less expensive! With the menu prices I'm more inclined to purchase the goods at their store and have the meal at home. But it's certainly a great spot for a special brunch or lunch with good company.

Too many rules about seating. We had a third joining us and were willing to order for that person but still would still not allow it. At this time still waiting. Not even sure I can enjoy my meal because I am so annoyed right now.
Ridiculously expensive for lox and bagel, but at least try once! I have never spent $18 for a bagel with lox, but it was delicious and service was great!

We were not expecting a 45 minute wait on a Thursday afternoon, but we signed in and waited. It was only about 25 minutes.  I had the Classic Board and my wife had Matzo Ball soup and Potato Latkes.  We both enjoyed our meals very much and I would have everything else as a second course...but that would not be prudent.

Wait staff was not very friendly but the food was tremendous.

Although I did not go to the original location (because I wanted to sit down and enjoy my meal; the original location is a "grab-n-go"), we went to this location instead. 

Arrived just after 10:30am and although packed, the wait time was about 10 minutes so a plus that I didn't have to wait too long!

I am a huge fan of lox in general so I immediately went with the build your own lox and Everything bagel board. It is such a simple dish but worth every bite. The lox were fresh; the capers, tomato and cream cheese added good flavor. Only thing I wish I could have asked for was whether I could order a different type of cream cheese and not have the original, but either way, super delicious!

Whether or not there is a wait, if you're in the area, check it out. This is a known place and there's a reason for that.

This place has limited seating and make sure you are there at opening time. I was there at 8 so I was seated immediately. Within 20 min the place was fu and had a waiting time of 20-30 minutes. So make sure you come early if you want to be seated immediately. 

IMPORTANT: Google navigated me to the back of the building (Allen Street), but the place is on 127 Orchid Street. Just be careful. 

Coming to the food, I was intrigued by the name and history of it so went and tried. It was good food but kind of pricy. I had the classic with smoked salmon. I had to put the cream cheese and assemble it by myself which was difficult as I didn't know how to put them together and have a good bite without making a mess. May be worth trying once. The waitress was polite and attentive. I was seated at the bar though. 

They do not do takeout orders here. If you want to take something there is another location couple of blocks from this place. You should go there.

Did I just walk into the 1940's? Wow is this place heavenly. I mean true, well made Jewish soul food. They take some license with the menu but even that is an amazing excursion from the ordinary.

Everything is crazy good. The cafe is wonderful and the staff efficient and helpful. The coffee Is brilliant. I would eat here every day if I could.

Bottom line: if you are visiting California or Alaska or Australia, take a side trip to NYC to go here.....it's that good

I came around 12:30 pm on a Friday and waited about 15 minutes. They take your phone number and text you when your table is ready. I'm not sure how this works with international visitors.

The hostess who was working that day was very calm and helpful even though it was busy. 

I was dining solo so they sat me at the counter. The bartender was very attentive to everyone sitting at the counter.

My Classic Board with a Bialy was great. I never had a bialy before and I'm glad I did. I thought it was perfect for eating my smoked salmon with since it was thinner than a bagel. The smoked salmon was also sliced thin, which is how I like it. The tomato was even good and I don't like tomatoes that much!

Yummy! Love their pastrami lox! The service was good. The wait time was a bit long but well worth the hype . Definitely make a reservation ahead . Ordered the drinks . Bloody Mary was ok . I've had better.

Rude service and over priced meals. Could not wait to be done with my food and leave. It felt like the staff was doing us a favour by serving us food.

Food was okay, nothing spectacular.

First time at the cafe and I gotta say... I felt like I have been missing out BIG TIME. 

I have been eating from the grab and go for a while now. But the cafe? The cafe is delightful! 

Today I had the smoked whitefish chowder and shared the croquettes and potato latkes with the wild salmon roe and creme fraiche. I found the croquettes to be a bit pricey since there were only 3 bites. But honestly? Didn't care, the quality of the fish, really is that good! 

That was my evening today. Soon, I will be coming back for brunch. And even though I already know we will have to be up early, I'm certain it will be worth the effort.

This place is amazing! Breakfast here is now a must whenever I'm in NYC. Get there when it opens, it quickly gets busy. Do yourself a favor and order the following: latkes with caviar and creme fresh, matzo ball soup (they can split one order into two bowls to share for the perfect serving amount) and any of the boards - I really enjoyed the classic with an everything bagel. All the drinks are also delicious. Try the egg cream, if you've never had one. It's hard to find a better breakfast/brunch in my opinion. The staff are also fantastic and the food came out quickly, but timed properly.

This is a hella late review but it was for my boyfriend and I's experience over the summer. The first visit was sooo good. I got the lox board and it was probably the best lox I've had.
