We had to come back and we did on our last day in the city! UNFORTUNATELY that was a mistake on our part :( we came for breakfast and both ordered the lox and latkes, and I wasn't feeling well right after so we went home to rest. An hour past and oh boy... we both got food poisoning and suffered the whole afternoon till our flight. Idk what happened? My boyfriend said he did notice the tomato tasted like the board? Maybe the boards weren't cleansed enough.. but sigh what a waste!

I've been wanting to try Russ & Daughter's for a while but never really wanted to come all the way out to the LES and wait for a bagel. This location is a sit-down cafe (I didn't even know there was a second location!) I finally got the chance to try it when we came here for a team lunch. They don't accept reservations and we were a large group (9). Luckily, we were seated pretty quickly when we came in at around 12:45 on a Tuesday. They don't have a table that large so we were split up into two tables.

I never had an egg cream before. I found out about it when watching Phil Rosenthal's show on Netflix, so I figured - what better time to try it? I asked the waiter which was their most popular one and he said it was the chocolate. It wasn't bad - it basically tasted like chocolate milk with seltzer (there is no egg or cream in it). For food, our table shared the Potato Latkes (with applesauce and sour cream). These were nice and crispy. Just make sure you eat them while they're hot. I preferred it with the sour cream as opposed to the applesauce. For my main, I went with the Classic (gaspe nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, capers). I figured I should start there, since I've never dined here before. I had an everything bagel, which could have been a bit more toasted but it was a pretty solid bagel overall. They use whipped cream cheese, which I like. The salmon was great as well.

I've heard great things about the pastrami-cured salmon (and I love the Trader Joe's version of it), so I think I'll try that next time!
For people who enjoy long waits and being treated like sh*t. Hostess was a b****! What else do u need to know?  Went next door to Good Thanks. Great experience.

First time at Russ & Daughters and I will definitely be back! We ordered "The Ida" platter between four of us and it was exactly the right amount of food. We loved being able to try different types of salmon. The pickled vegetables were also delicious! Great service and coffee, and very unique decor. My father was especially wowed by the experience, having remarked after our meal that he never imagined such a restaurant existed.

I had wanted to go to Russ & Daughters for a while now, but the wait is usually so long and I didn't have time to wait. I finally had a day where I was able to wait out their expected 2 hour wait time.

We ordered the Pastrami Russ because of all the hype I've heard over the pastrami-cured salmon, but this was a bit underwhelming. Additionally, the dense pretzel roll may have detracted from the taste of the pastrami salmon.

On to the platter we got to share. There are three options, all of which sounded good, but we went for The Anne for what sounded like the most variety. The platters all come with cream cheese, red onion, tomato, capers, pickled veggies, and a bread/bagel basket. Not a fan of most of the pickled veggies or capers in general and the bread basket could have done with more bagels, but I'm happy with the cream cheese, red onion, and tomato accompaniments. On to the fish offerings - absolutely loved their private stock sturgeon (favorite from the board), always love sable, the New Zealand king smoked salmon is a classic staple, and the wild salmon Alaskan roe added bursts of salty flavor that paired well with others, but the smoked brook trout wasn't as big of a hit.

Now that I have specific items I know I love and specific items I'd rather steer clear of, I think the better option would be to visit their storefront down the block. The sit down is much less customizable, but a good way to be able to sit around and share a platter with others.

Really love this place as it's a neighborhood spot. Food is great, vibe is relaxing and the staff is normally super nice. Unfortunately, we just tried to have dinner tonight here at 9:51PM (on a Friday) after spending a few hours at the hospital. We rushed to get here. We asked for a table of 2. The hostess said we close at 9:55PM. We said we just came from hospital which was met w a blank stare. Silence. We had to leave. Russ & D closes at 10pm, not 9:55PM. We were very annoyed by this. Pls change Yelp to close earlier or stop serving people food

Finally made it here! Woke up early on a Saturday and made it right before it opened at 8am (in the past I have left when told to wait 2 hours, which is the norm for walk ins during regular brunch hours). My boyfriend and I ordered 

+ eggs benny (thought this had a bit too much spinach, which made it soggy. Would have liked less spinach, more salmon)

+ potato latkes with creme fraiche and fish roe (really enjoyed this! Latkes are crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and the creme fraiche balances out the saltiness of the roe well)

We really enjoyed the coffee brew -- they also have free refills. I'd be interested in trying their bagels and desserts next time around.
I found this restaurant by chance. The food was excellent as well as the service. Very unique place.
Had the Pasrami Russ and the knishes on the side. Quick friendly service. Food was fast and fresh. This is a great lunch time treat.

First time here after hearing the SHOCK from fellow foodies that I'd not been.

Friday midday arrival - was a 75 minute wait. Unable to reserve upfront for 2, so that was a little bit of a bummer since it took 45 minutes in traffic to arrive. 

Friendly staff. Relatively fast service. Inviting environment.

Latkes were crisp, hot, delicious & addictive.

Traditional lox-bagel-cream cheese was good. For me the poppyseed bagel was good but didn't blow me away. The lox however was DELICIOUS. Coffee was good.

Husband tried the pretzel bagel with the pastrami lox & liked it, but found the portion a little smaller & he would try something different next time.

I'd definitely go back & try the salmon whitefish salad next!

True Jewish soul food! I can't believe living in NY all my life, as a MOTT (member of the tribe) I never heard of R & Ds. Having seen a piece on CBS Sunday Morning, we ventured here for a Hanukkah breakfast. Delish.

Once you get by the wait for a table,(OyVey! the wait) you get to enjoy some of the best of potato latkes, smoked salmon and herring in cream sauce. The latkes warm and crunchy offset with either sour cream or natural applesauce, a must. The smoked salmon on a plain bagel with cream cheese. I'll give it a 'Good, not great' and the herring in cream sauce, I'll do it again. But for the next visit, which there will be, we will be making other selections so as to try what look like other delicious items.

The service was great with no complaints. Our waiter was accommodating and attentive. 

Lastly, the atmosphere. Sitting amongst what seemed to be a step back in time, the 1940's or 50's (Before my time.) Kinda looked like it was setup to film a "The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel" scene.

Will definitely be returning but at an off peak time.

Food is average - very overrated. The hostess staff was aggressively rude. They were also ignoring customers and bragging to each other that they make celebrities wait longer than necessary. Bad vibes, bad food.

This place had a very neat and enjoyable vibe. I loved the plating for the bagels and would love to come back here for another brunch. The waiters were very nice and we had a great meal here. Overall, this place was very much satisfying.

I've always seen Russ & Daughters floating around my Yelp feed but never really took the time to check it out and see what it was all about. Then, sometime last year my brother was telling me how great it was after visiting their original location. This intrigued me - and since my brothers and I had to go to the East Village to pick up some goods for Christmas Eve, we thought it would be a good idea to grab breakfast here at the cafe. 

The original R&D has been open for over 100 years, and is mostly a takeout spot serving a variety of Jewish cuisine. The Cafe opened in 2014 which serves the same fare but also provides table service. We arrived on Christmas Eve around 9am and were lucky enough to not wait more than 2 or so minutes for a table. The decor was perfect - it had a diner aesthetic with a mostly grey color scheme. Along the walls were banners with the names of different Jewish food along with jarred versions of them. 

The menu has a great selection of Jewish foods - apps, soups, salads, and more with emphasis on fish and other staples. Even though I'm not Jewish, my grandmother loved the food so I grew up eating matzo and blintzes - I was immediately brought back to my grandmother when looking over the menu. Anyway, we decided to order some potato latke, cheese blintzes, and three boards (one for each of us). The latke were great - they had a nice thickness to them and were served with salmon roe and creme fraiche which really complemented the latke. The blintzes were also great - the cheese had a nice flavor and again were complemented by fruit compote and sour cream. 

I decided to get the classic board - this contained smoked salmon, onion, tomato, capers, cream cheese to spread, and my choice of carb (I went with a pumpernickel bagel). While I'm not the biggest smoked salmon fan, I wanted the full R&D experience so I dove in. I had no regrets because the board was delicious - the salmon was tender, the bagel was soft and chewy, and the accents really made it a perfect meal - I was super impressed.

Service was great -all the food was served in a timely manner and all of the staff were very friendly. Overall, I had an awesome experience at R&D Cafe - they really are a premier spot for Jewish cuisine in Manhattan and I will definitely return for more of their offerings.

The Classic with bagel was good. The omelette was the worst ever, worldwide. 

The receptionist was so rude to sit people after us first, even after she was told we are the first in line. The waiters are super nice in comparison.

That makes food 2.5/5.0 and service 2.5/5.0.

The longstanding deli on East Houston is amazing so a restaurant is exactly what was needed. 

The menu prices fluctuate anywhere between an inexpensive matzah ball soup to the delicacies of caviar by the ounce. Traditional jewish cuisine and quality fresh fish such as herring and lox. Not much one can say poorly about R&D. The food and menu is straight forward. 

The only small concern was when the kitchen kept over-toasting the bagel. Sent it back once and it still came back slightly burnt, so we didn't bother sending it back again. The burnt outer rim was just peeled off. Not the worst thing. Would still recommend coming here.

Not much to say about the service. I am indifferent about it. It was not poor, but there isn't much to remember about the wait staff either.

Be prepared for a wait especially on the weekends.

This place has been on the NYC bucket list for a long time... The Hattie Platter, Pickled Herring Trio, Bissel of Caviar, Chopped Liver, Whitefish croquettes, Latkes and the Challah Bread Pudding. Everything was a highlight!

Happy Hanukkah, and to all a good food coma!

Absolutely amazing meal. Had the bagel and lox which were super delicious - best I've ever had and nothing yet has come close. If you're in the area you should definitely stop in (the wait can be long but it's worth it).

Will you be waiting a long time for a bagel? Yes. Will you be paying a lot for a bagel? Yes. But is it worth it to try one of NYC icons? Absolutely!

First time here, so went with the classic board. It's a little DIY board with plenty of nova lox, tomatoes, onions, capers and cream cheese! I chose a bialy and my friend got an everything bagel. Everything was just amazing quality!!! It's not an every day bagel spot, but definitely come in at least once!

My husband and I went here for breakfast. He had the classic board, and I had the omelet with a bagel. We both said that the bagels were probably the best bagels that we have ever had. 

The atmosphere was great, too. Didn't feel too tight like a lot of restaurants in the city.

I came here for brunch on Saturday at 10:10 and waited 20 minutes, which is not bad at all!
After I got seated, I ordered the pastrami Russ, which was very good. The smoke salmon was fresh. The pretzel bagel was warm and chewy. The pickle complemented the smoked salmon quite well. 
I also shared a honey cake. The cake was warm, moist and not too sweet. You can taste the Apple pieces I'm the Apple ice cream, which went really well with the cake. 

In terms of service, the server was slightly disrespectful when I tried to order pastrami Russ. She kept telling me it would be too small and asked me 3-4 times if I was sure.

WOW literally the best bagels I've ever tried!! I got the caviar cream cheese that has scallions inside with capers, tomatoes, onions, and the Norwegian salmon. When you enter the restaurant it looks more like a deli and you have to grab a number first. Then they call your number and take your order! The guy that helped me was super friendly and he also let me sample some cream cheese. You can also sample different salmon but I already knew which one I wanted. There's also tea and coffee you can grab as well. Definitely recommend!!

Food is very good and unique, atmosphere is nice and service is friendly. 

I'm taking off a star because portions are small. You might need to order several dishes for a hearty meal.
absolutely worth the long lines if you're looking for a sit down meal. Highly recommend the sharing platter so you can sample the most options and the bloody mary packs a punch!

Russ & Daughters did not disappoint!!  There was a bit of a wait but totally worth it. I had a little bit of everything. The NY egg cream is a must have along with the potato pancakes! If you're looking for some good Jewish cuisine this is the place to  go!
Phenomenal. Can go shopping around in Soho while you wait. Insane food. Gotta get the caviar and smoke sturgeon.

Stopped by this place after watching a Mark Wiens food vlog, and I knew it would be good. I ordered the smoked salmon on an everything bagel with scallion cream cheese.

They make it right in front  of you, and you wait in line by grabbing a ticket. It got there at around 10am and waited about 20 mins for my turn. The place was pretty packed. 

Overall the best bagel I've ever had in my life. The salmon melted in my mouth and had a buttery texture with the fresh taste of smoked salmon. The cream cheese was a great addition, and paired nicely with the salmon. The bagel was toasted perfectly and tasted fresh and had great texture. 

Solid 5 stars here and will be returning!

After waiting for 1 hr (as predicted by our host), Guy and I received a text that our table for 2 was ready and that we needed to claim it within 10 minutes of the text. We first ordered vanilla-chocolate egg cream, which basically tasted like a root beer float but without the creaminess of vanilla ice cream. I wasn't too much of a fan for the egg cream because it didn't go well with the classic salmon bagel that I ordered. Guy however really enjoyed the drink. The classic bagel and laktes were good just like how everyone raves they are. I recommend others come try it at least once during their visit to NY, however, I personally won't be returning for a while because the inconvenience of waiting so long and the cost of this meal.

Everything we ordered was amazing. My friend had been looking forward to coming here forever and we were thoroughly satisfied and impressed. Thank you for taking such good care of us and having such amazing food.

Their big spreads of fish, breads and fixings have become a go-to treat for family get-togethers.  The first time we visited, they won our heart when the waitress overheard my wife reminiscing over the pickled green tomatoes and spontaneously brought a couple in a little box to go.

Omg I love everything salmon related and everything was SO good here! There was definitely a wait when we first arrived (and we didn't make a reservation) but it was definitely worth the 30 min wait! The menu form sweet things, to platters, to small dishes - we got the hot smoke/cold smoke small dish, the classic lox board with an everything bagel, and some latkes! The small dish was basically a smoked salmon dip that you ate with everything bagel chips and it was surprisingly SO good - the dip was amazing and everything bagel chips is definitely a must! The board is a classic and comes with some onions, tomatoes, capers, creamcheese, and like 4 slices of salmon! I wish it came with more salmon but overall, the quality was so good! I loved the latkes as well and the applesauce paired SO well with it! It's definitely pricey but I think it's worth trying!

Five stars food, one star service. I've been here a few times and have found the food consistently excellent and the service and ambiance consistently bad. The wait for a table on any given morning is long, which attests to the restaurant's popularity. But I'm not sure it's worth the wait. I have yet to be seated in the back room which seems to more spacious and tranquil. The front room is very crowded and noisy with waitstaff rushing by in the narrow aisles and waiting customers hovering restlessly nearby. On a cold winter's morning that front room is especially uncomfortable as there is little protection from the constant stream of customers coming and going. I'll give Russ and Daughters one more try with a goal of snagging a seat in the back room to see if that enhances my experience.

Went for dinner which turned out to be a win since there was no line and there is no bad time for a bialy with lox. My partner got an everything bagel and the sable which was good, but I thought the lox was better. The spread (something like fish hot and cold?) was the best part. Black and white cookie was the perfect ending, albeit a little silly to pay $9 for two cookies. This is a beautiful and special place.

Stopped by Russ & Daughters on a Sunday morning during my recent trip to New York. My friend and I got there at 11 am and was told there was an hour and twenty minute wait. There's a small waiting area inside for about 8 people to sit and wait but other than that most people were waiting outside. About 50 minutes later we were offered counter seats. 

Both my friend and I ordered the Classic Board which comes with a toasted bagel of your choice, smoked salmon, tomatoes, red onions, capers and cream cheese. I had never had a New York bagel before and the lox bagel here was delicious! We also ordered a bowl of the Matzo Ball Soup which they kindly offered to split for us. I didn't think the soup was that special so would skip it next time and try something else. 

Overall glad I tried Russ & Daughters but don't know if I'll be back for another $18 bagel with an hour wait anytime soon. Good to try though at least once!

Every time I go to New York I have plans to try a new place for brunch but somehow always end up at Russ & Daughters. I just can't quit you. I think we got there on Sunday at 9:30 but still had to wait 15 minutes for 2 people. And it was Superbowl  Sunday. I always get the Classic Board, and will switch between an everything bagel or the bialy. They don't have my favorite bagel but I love their Nova smoked salmon. It's sliced perfectly thin and is not overly salty. It's DELICIOUS. Definitely a New York staple.

Best smoked salmon I have ever had and better than most service. We got the eggs benny and salmon/bagel board. Highly recommend both. We also split matzo ball soup which was great for a rainy day. Phenomenal New York bagel and lox

This place has charm, BUT, our white fish salad had a very long hair in it, the rugelach was hard and stale, the bagel -meh. The hostess had no charm at all. I couldn't believe people were waiting an hour and a half for that. So many better places in NYC for bagel and a schmear. Barney Greengrass, it ain't

I can't recommend this cafe.  It serves as more of a tourist spot and a relic of the famous brand than a place to eat regularly.  Before my meal, I had assumed that locals eat at Russ & Daughters all the time.

Some redeeming qualities were the charm of being served in a notable establishment, with the decor and history of being at Russ & Daughters.  If you are in to that sort of dining, you'll have that here.

The food portions are fairly small when you consider the $20 price tags on each selection.  This would be fine if the food was a step above competitors that serve bagels and salmon at $10.  But it's not.  At most the quality is equal.  At worst, you're getting half the quality for double the price.  If you normally get 4 slices of salmon elsewhere for one serving, you can expect to get only 2 here.

We ordered two selections from the menu.  The first was called the Shtetl, smoked sable w/ a bagel and cream cheese.  The second was the Lower Sunny Side, a breakfast plate of two latkes (hashbrowns), two overeasy eggs, and lox.  Our drinks were served in dirty glasses with debris floating on the surface.  It seems like this restaurant does not store their glasses overnight, and leaves them face up to collect dust and dirt before first use.

The less than friendly hostess didn't say much or offer any sort of greeting.  Our primary server was devoid of expression and seemed to want to be elsewhere.  The two other servers who stopped by to check on us were friendly.  We only saw our primary server when we placed our order, and to collect the check.

The best bagels are from small delis and hole in the wall places around New York.  But if you find yourself still wanting to try Russ & Daughters, the takeout deli on the main street comes out ahead of the cafe in terms of service and quality.

In my opinion, this is the best breakfast place I have gone to for a bagel and lox. It is a little chaotic and you have to be ready to know what you order, but you feel like you're in somewhere very historic and there's a lot to look at on the walls! The portions are also so huge

I've been to the deli before but last night was my first visit to the cafe.  Though Yelp indicates no reservations, I noticed on Google a link to Resy so I booked a table for 4.  We came by for the Potato Latkes, which did not disappoint.  The stand-alone order gives you 3.  I ended up with the Lower Sunny Side which was 2 sunnyside eggs, 2 potato latkes and some smoked salmon.  The eggs were eggs but both the latkes and smoked salmon were excellent.  I didn't try any beverages but they had a number of options including homemade sodas, egg creams (including one with whiskey), beers and wines.  The only item I don't like here are the bagels - I had one a while ago and it was small, not at all fluffy and lacked any of the great bagel flavor I expect in a New York bagel.  However, if potato latkes or smoked salmon you seek, then Russ and Daughters Cafe will not disappoint.

Wow... in a city full of amazing places this place is unlike any other restaurant! A must order! Babka french toast everything was amazing. Just don't tell anyone else. I don't want to wait in longer lines. Coffee is also very good

I've heard phenomenal things about this place, especially the smoked salmon, so I of course had to come and try it. Knew that their lines can get very long, so we decided to come early. We got there at 9 am on a Saturday, and the restaurant was already full. The wait wasn't too bad, though: only half an hour. We were able to hang out at a nearby Starbuck's while we waited for our text. 

Once in, we were seated at the bar. We ordered the classic board, which came with gaspe nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onion, and capers; as well as the potato latkes with apple sauce and sour cream, both to share. I was so excited to try the smoked salmon, and honestly, it didn't disappoint. The salmon was so wispy, with the perfect taste and texture. Wish there was more of it. I can see why they're famous for it! The cream cheese was light and airy. Normally I feel like cream cheese is too heavy, but I felt like I was eating a cloud. The platter comes with a choice of bagel, bialy, shissel rye, or pumpernickel, and we had ours with a bialy, which I tried for the first time. It was essentially a thinner, less dense bagel.

The latkes weren't a let down, either; complemented by the apple sauce and sour cream, they felt like a perfect combination. They had the right amount of crunch and texture. Perhaps my only complaint is that they erred on the heavier side, though that's to be expected of something fried.

I love the design of their menu, from the color scheme to the font choice. It's a cute Jewish diner and definitely worth the visit, though I'd come early to avoid the crowds.

If you want the best bagel with lox, you found it. This is absolute BEST bagel place I've ever been to and could eat this everyday forever.. they have a huge variety of bagels and fish options and tons of different cream cheese flavors. The long wait it definitely worth it, just make sure you grab a number inside! Do yourself a favor and go here for breakfast!

I ordered the classic board, was a good bagel with salmon and cream cheese. I got a nice spot on the bar and the bartender was a friendly guy. I was not in the mood for alcohol beverages but the cocktail list looked great.

I honestly don't get what people like about this restaurant. It's so overhyped and when I see 5 star reviews, I'm like ...what are these people on? I think it has to come down to it's history and the atmosphere is what people like. I went with my boyfriends family and so, I got to try a little bit of everything. I usually don't bring money up, but the prices do not reflect the quality or value of this place. Portions are skimpy. And once I bit into my stale bagel, it was all over for me...

Place for tourist
Very expensive and doesn't worst the hype
18$ for 3 very tiny piece of lox, a bagel, and cream cheese...come one it's ridiculous.
Service is good
Place is clean but they try to much to play the old fashioned establishment...

Always love bagel.
classic board- bagel, smoke salmon, cream cheese, onion, tomato, and capers.
You can make your own bagel!
Their smoke salmon is not too salty, so you taste of more salmon flavor more than salt. 
Everything balance so well together! 

I came here on weekday lunch so no wait needed. I heard  weekend is aLways packed.

Come hungry, but not too hungry because you'll have to wait over an hour to get seated! 

The presentation is the nicest part of this meal. The lox gets served on top of a small wooden board with the ingredients on top. 

You'll have to put the ingredients on a bagel, of course, which adds to the experience of the this place. 

-1 because we felt like one of the bussers had a major attitude. Seriously makes me feel no need to return for some time.

This place is off the hook. Very unique...... especially if you reside in Charlotte NC (even though we travel the country often). The Bloody Mary was excellent, only mistake I made is I should have ordered one while I waited my hour for our seats. Hot smoke cold smoke platter was simple but so damn good. The potato latkes with the salmon roe is worth the trip all by themselves. The roe is a must with the latkes. Don't skip them. We also had the Matzo ball soup. This is just Jewish chicken noodle soup but my Wife loves chicken noodle soup. So this was her pick and it was perfect. The matzo was light but yet didn't fall apart on you till you went in with your spoon. My wife and I make usually 1 trip a year to NYC so we try not to just keep repeating the same places but it's hard not to go here every time. It's definitely one of the top 5 or 10 places I recommend to friends who have never been to NYC as a must stop.
Excellent food and service, well worth the wait. We had eggs benny, latkes, Classic with salmon and whitefish.

Thursday morning brunch at Russ & Daughter's was fabulous.   We were seated immediately in a corner booth in the back.  We ordered the smoke salmon platter and bread basket to share.   

Food was good.   Nothing mind blowing.

My first R+D experience was at the deli back in 2016 and I absolutely loved it. I had no idea they had a cafe, so when my friends and I made our way to the city, I knew this had to be on the menu. 

I got the classic, which is basically a deconstructed bagel sandwich with Lox cream cheese tomato and capers. I also got a mushroom soup and shared some latkes with the table. 

Personally I like the deli better as the bagel comes already made. I found that while the presentation makes for a good picture, the taste is just better when it's already made for you. The mushroom barley soup was good, but nothing special. I will say the latkes here were really freaking good, and each order comes with more than enough for sharing. 

I think the price point is steep for this bagel, but am unsure what the deli costs are nowadays.

I still do prefer this over ess-a-bagel though (though many of my friends disagree)

LOVE!!! I love bagels but have a hard time finding something good because I don't eat dairy, but Russ & Daughters had a great dairy-free tofu cream cheese option. I got an everything bagel with tofu cream cheese, lox, and capers. It was EXCELLENT! The bagel was very fresh - soft and chewy at the same time and very light. The smoked salmon was also amazing - potentially the best smoked salmon I have ever had. Not too salty, very thin, and melts in your mouth. Perfect taste and texture. 

Everyone else loved their food as well. Price was a bit steep, but for the quality well worth it. I'm looking forward to trying the bagel shop - instead of being deconstructed, the bagels are already made. The prices are a bit lower there too.

It was packed on weekday lunch, which is understandable seeing as it was delicious. Thank you for a great meal!!

The wait was SUPER LONG!! We were able to go around and explore the area before our table was ready. I really love the idea how all the ingredients come in a board and you build the bagel the way you like it! I think the experience and the food was amazing!! Though the price was more than if you went to a local cafe for a tasty bagel. 

The bagel was soo delicious! It was a fun experience building the bagel as you wish! 

I would definitely recommend for the experience and the taste! It is worth the wait!

As a jew I take my bagels very seriously and Russ & Daughter delivers!!!!!!! Would recommend the classic on a toasted everything bagel and a chocolate egg creme. I make a point to go there at lease once or twice a month because you cannot escape the call of the food that brings you back. The atmosphere and service are also amazing and the waiters are the nicest in the biz! I cannot stress enough pay Russ and Daughters a visit you wont regret it!

Amazing breakfast. Never really a big fan of lox but never had it here before.  It was incredible.  I miss it already. Babka French toast also out of this world. If you don't eat breakfast/brunch here you are missing out.

Russ and Daughters is my favorite place in NYC for lox and bagels. They have a few locations where they sell their bagel sandwiches, but I like the Russ and Daughters Cafe on Orchard because it's a sit down place where you can just take your time and relax with a cup of coffee or a drink. 

They have an extensive menu, but I always order the lox and bagels and nothing else. I don't even have to look at the menu because this is where I get my lox and bagel fix in the city. I also like the DIY style of their lox and bagel because you can pick and choose what you want to put on it and how much cream cheese you want to add. 

If you have some time to sit down and enjoy breakfast one morning, head over to Russ and Daughters Cafe for their lox and bagel!
Excellence is mastery of the basics, and that's what you'll get here - fresh, filling, well thought through.
Incrediby overpriced and over salted. There's literally better places around the corner. Probably worst coffee in town. Wouldn't recommend it to anyone.

First time trying Russ and Daughters. I decided to come to this location to start my day, because they offered outdoor seating. The seating is first come, first served. I haven't had a lox in years. And based on reviews I was headed in the right direction.

Service was good. I was able to go inside and place my order. They do have sanitizer on the counter and the employees wore masks and practiced social distancing. 

The lox was good but felt there wasn't enough salmon on my sandwich. See picture for reference. That is why I gave it a 4 or of 5 star. Would I come back? Yes,  to try other options on the menu. Again, lox was good but not enough salmon.

Ordered the classic (gaspe nova lox on everything bagel with scallion cream cheese and tomato) for pick up around 11am. Pick up itself was smooth. 

The bagel itself was kind of hard, which was disappointing (expected something softer and chewier). Good amount of salmon, but overall the sandwich was pretty salty, but not sure if it was the bagel or the salmon that was too salty.

Picked up a little late (around 20 minutes), but don't think that would've affected the bagel texture much, so maybe got a bad batch. Consistency is part of quality though, and for $15 I expected more. :(

Stopping here for a quick Jewish Brunch was a nice way to round out our morning after dropping off our daughter at JFK. Plus we caught up with an errand in the area. Located on Orchard St- between Delancey and Rivington, Russ & Daughters Café takes no reservations, you order in person at the door, then grab a table outside. 

Even with the chilly Saturday weather, sitting outside was legit especially with their tables being spaced accordingly. Mimosas were a nice hit. So were our toasted chewy bagels that were lightly stuffed with Scottish Smoked Salmon, a super-thin schmear of cream cheese (for me) and the usual sliced onions and tomatoes. And that my friend- was music. But my moist and buttery Chocolate Babka....was a symphony.

If you aren't lucky with an outside table or have hangups sitting outdoors, take your meal to go and have your own picnic or pop the trunk and enjoy your nosh.

It took me 29 years of life in NYC to try Russ & Daughters, but I eventually made it and that's what really counts. This is the go-to spot for lox and bagels, especially if you are looking for the sit-down experience (the other location is strictly takeout). The old-school design is a testament to the century-old establishment's legacy.

While they don't take reservations, we didn't seem to need one when our group arrived on a weekday. We ordered the Potato Latkes w/ Applesauce and Sour Cream for the table ($12) which were very good. These are best eaten immediately or else they will get soggy. I also had the Classic Bagel and Lox ($14) which comes with your choice of bagel AND the option to switch out the regular cream cheese for tofu/vegan cream cheese. I decided to try the tofu cream cheese which was just as good as any classic cream cheese I have had in the past. They also provided a really solid amount of salmon for the price, and the quality was top-notch. Presentation was 5-star.

The service was okay. Left a bit to be desired. But overall, had a good experience here.
I was visiting my friend in New York who took me to this spot.  I'm usually not a fan of bagels but this is the spot for lox and bagels. It was really good and fresh. Definitely will go again.

You feel like you're stepping back in time, yet the cafe feels completely up to date.  The cafe opened in 2014, on the 100th anniversary of their take away counter location on Houston. A special treat for anyone who likes smoked fish and other delicious Jewish comfort food. Whitefish, lox, baked salmon, whitefish/salmon combo salad, latkes, bagels, bialys, pickles ... whitefish is especially delish!

Pre-covid weekend wait times would easily take 45-120 minutes, put your name down on the list and go walk around the neighborhood, it's worth the wait. Not sure if wait times are the same during the pandemic but I wouldn't be surprised if they were.

Just ordered the Chanukah Essentials to my son and they delivered it right away.  Excellent customer service on the phone.  Easy to order online.  It was snowing in Manhattan but they delivered it before the expected delivery time.  I'm very happy about it and just a great way to order food.  Delivery by DoorDash.  Of course we love the quality as well.

Went here last weekend. Takeaway online was 70min, so we went in stores to order and got it within 5min (so pro-tip if you want your order fast, go in in person!)!! 

We got...

- daughter's delight ($20). this bagel was filled with gaspe nova smoked salmon, wild alaskan salmon roe, and cream cheese.  we went with the host's recommendation for bagel and cream cheese type, and added onions + capers, but it turned out to be really hard to eat! the salmon roe kept falling out, so it was as if we didn't really get much in our bagel, and on the whole, it was WAY too salty... the bagel itself was a bit chewy/rubbery, making it hard to bite the sandwich without all the fillings spilling out. definitely did not feel worth the money and we couldn't finish this because of the saltiness.

- classic bagel & lox ($14). this bagel had pretty much the same story as the previous one, except none of the hassle / cost of the salmon roe  I'd honestly recommend this one over the daughter's delight, because it's the same bagel minus the $6 for salmon egg which just fall out anyways, so they really taste quite similar... however I'd just not recommend this place as a whole because the bagels are subpar and way too salty!

i heard so many good things about this place, but i was kind of disappointed with my experience.
-they're available for delivery on doordash and caviar. i placed a pickup order through doordash.
-they accept card, but i'm unsure about cash.
-they had a small outdoor dining set up outside on the street at the time. i'm unsure if they've changed anything about it for the wintertime right now.
-the workers were friendly when i went to go pick up my order. other than that, i didn't really have an interaction with them. 

8/1/20
-chocolate babka french toast: i love babka and french toast, so this sounded amazing to me. unfortunately, it just wasn't what i was hoping for. while the chocolate flavor was very rich, the texture of the toast wasn't the best. it was slightly mushy on the inside, and the outside could've been crispier. i'm unsure if my order was made too early or sat for too long in its container, but it just didn't taste freshly made. it was lacking sweetness, and the portion was so small. it was just one thick piece of french toast with strawberries on top and sour cream on the side. the cost of this was over $14 with tax, which was too overpriced and not worth it. (3/5)
-classic bagel and lox: i had high hopes for this, and i was pleasantly surprised. i opted for the everything bagel with scallion cream cheese. this specific sandwich came with gaspe nova lox, and it tasted so fresh and delicious. the bagel itself could've been toasted more. but, i really enjoyed its dense, chewy, and doughy texture, along with the crispy exterior. the total of this bagel came out to be pricey and around $15.50. it would've been $1.50 cheaper if i hadn't asked for tomato, capers, and red onions; yet, i don't think that this would've tasted as good without them. the portion of lox was pretty fair, so i don't have any huge regrets. (4/5)
-potato latkes: an order of these comes with 3 latkes and a side of sour cream and applesauce. while i liked how crispy and delicious the latkes were, they were just too oily for my liking. they went well with the sour cream and apple sauce, but wouldn't have tasted as good alone. the latkes were pretty decently sized, and i would've given them a 4/5 if they weren't over $12. (3.5/5)

overall, i would give this place 3.5 stars if i could. although i don't have a big problem with the food itself, i just think that the prices are way too expensive. i really wanted to love this place, so i might give them a second chance in the future. i think takeout just doesn't do their food justice, and i hope to have an in person dining experience sometime. 
my favorites that i would recommend you must try would be the potato latkes and classic bagel with lox.

We ordered for pickup from the café on Valentine's Day morning. We figured the level of detail would be the same at the store, but we were wrong. 

The bagels were stale which ruined the entire lox and bagel experience. I ordered an onion bialy, but wound up with a plain bagel. I would have been okay with this if not for the fact the bagel was stale, as were the other two bagels in my order. 

Combined with the borderline inch thick slices of red onion, this was a really poor experience.

Please put in a little more effort when you're selling a $16 bagel.

Food: Daughter's Delight - everything bagel with plain cream cheese, Scottish smoked salmon, capers and salmon roe

Pretty damn solid for being not toasted, cold and eaten while walking in gloomy rain.

Lox to bagel ratio was okay but flavor was savory and satisfying. Slightly chewy bagel with a crisp exterior.

Came here for the first time last week and excited to try it. I was disappointed though. Ordered the classic bagel and lox. The salmon was fresh and good but didn't like that the bagel was not toasted. Even if it wasn't toasted, it was stale like it was days old and very difficult to chew. Apparently, they don't toast the lox bagels so you have to tell them when you order, but there's no way to select toast on the app which is the only way you can order.. doesn't make sense to me?
Ordered chocolate babka French toast from here. It was very delicious! Super thick but very pricey for the amount of food you get

Wow, I had no idea that a bagel with cream cheese could taste this good! I reside in California and I must say that we do not take our bagels as seriously as we should and can learn from the east coast. I had the everything bagel with the scallion cream cheese and it lived up to its name because it was everything to me! The smooth onion flavor and creamy goodness on a savory toasted bagel was a great morning starter. I unfortunately have a fish intolerance so I could not attest to their smoked salmon, but they had all different kinds and was definitely the hot commodity over here.

came here during covid. 

i moved to the bay area, so i always always eat bagels when i go back home. 

they had outdoor seating so that was a plus. i actually came here super early, so no waiting. 

this time, i got a gaspe nova smoked salmon with horseradish dill schmear, wasabi fish roe, onions, tomatoes on a everything bagel. it was so good!  gotta have my side of mimosa of course :)

All the baked goods ordered for delivery from this place were stale; black and white cookie hard as a rock, hamantaschen (mini versions with no choice of flavors) dry, coffee cake was dry, rye bread was crumbling apart and didn't taste like rye bread, bagels were underwhelming, rugelach were dry and overcooked. The only redeeming thing in the other was the matzoh ball soup. That was not bad. 

Lesson, DO NOT order any baked goods from here.

I love Russ n daughters but today was a bit disappointing. I spent $17. N I'm still hungry. The onion Bagel was hard n not soft; stale like. This was an instant disappointment.  It definitely did not taste fresh at all. There was literally 2 capers on only 1/2 of bagel, a super light smear of horseradish cream cheese which I think was actually plain cream cheese. Both sides of bread skimpy, cc.  2 pieces of nova but lots of red onion n 2 tomato's. Not worth it. Bummed out. I was looking forward to eating  a hearty sandwich, with all those great flavors fusing together. I love your establishment and highly recommend but Sorry Russ n Daughters...today, not worth $17.

I stop by Russ and daughters every time I'm in NYC. I love their bagels and smoked fish. Didn't want to wait in line this time and saw I could order online, but only for the cafe so here we are.

This was the worst experience I've ever had at R&D, and would not recommend the cafe in the least. The bagels were stale and hard. I had them remake my nova bagel which was inedible and it still came out bad. Not a fan of the whitefish sando either - the wasabi roe completely takes over the entire sandwich, and when your bagel is hard as a rock all of the whitefish just falls out of the sides. We ended up throwing away the sandwiches which is crazy considering I'm a founding member of the clean plate club. 

Also ordered rugelach - the raspberry one was good, chocolate was hard.
Simply the best jewish smoked fish delicatessen in NYC. My regular order is a super heebster, a fresh squeezed oj and a quart of matzo ball soup to go. Enjoy!

Ordered this place for takeout because the lines are always so long. If you don't mind sitting outside in the park and eating ordering ahead for pickup can save you an hour of time!

Got a couple of things to try out from the menu. Or the knishes, came in 2 and had really good mustard that came with- very soft and densely mashed potatoes on the inside.

I really liked the potato latkes- it came with sour cream and apple sauce. Both dips were great and fried potatoes that were perfectly crispy on the outside but soft on the inside were the best complement to the soft and flavorful sauces.

We also got the lox bagel which came with a generous serving of cream cheese and salmon- opted for an everything bagel.

Solid bagel spot and hearty food, iconic for nyc so worth a visit.
Went for the famous smoked salmon bagel. The salmon was a thin layer, not enough against the girth of the bagel, and overall unimpressive.  I'd rather go to a bagel shop for lox sandwich.

We ordered online and came to this location to for pickup on a weekday, our order was finished pretty quickly which was nice. Overall the bagels and lox were okay, but there wasn't that much salmon in my sandwich for the steep price. The bagel was decent but nothing really special, it was a bit too chewy for my taste and didn't really taste fresh. The taste of the salmon was pretty good at least. Maybe I would have had a better experience at one of the other locations but I don't think I would order the bagel and lox here again.

I have been wanting to try Russ and Daughters for the longest time and when I finally found the time to  make it to NYC I had to put it on the list.

Unfortunately, I hate to say, but it was a huge let down. $16.50 for a small bagel, negligible amount of salmon, some cream cheese, and an extra dollar for capers and onion. 

It's a good bagel and the fish is good, but it is not worth 16/17 dollars in any universe. Wish there was a way to try the other types of smoked salmon, like a flight or something. Don't have the coin to buy the half pound of each. 

I'm not from NYC, but I have to imagine there's many places in the city who do the same or better for half the cost. 

I would not come back.

Excellent experience this morning. I ordered one bagel with my selected toppings as a pickup order, walked over and got the bag with my name on it on time, and headed back to my unit. 10 minutes in I got a call that they had given me the wrong order- for someone else with my name. I went back to exchange the bags for my correct order, and not only did they let me keep the incorrect order, but they voided the charge for my original order. Everyone I spoke to was so apologetic over something that was clearly an honest mistake, and I ended up with 4 free bagel sandwiches to start my day. Top notch customer service

The first Bagel shop we visited for our first time in NYC. I've always heard Bagels hit different in New York, so I was excited to try Russ & Daughters. I'm a big fan of popular places that offer online ordering so that you can plan your trip there and not have to wait too long.

Classic Bagel & Lox ($14.00): We got the Everything Bagel and Scallion Cream Cheese. I thought it was cool how they had a variety of Bagels to choose from but also Cream Cheeses! Maybe this is common in NY, but any other Bagel spot I've been to, they only have 2-3 Bagel choices and the single Plain Cream Cheese. HOWEVER, the variety of choices did not make up for how stale, dry, and hard the Bagel was! I was so shocked biting into it - it was legitimately so difficult to chew because of how stale it was. Maybe we got unlucky with our batch, but this was definitely not the Bagel experience I thought I'd have.

I'm willing to give Russ & Daughters a try again the next time I'm in NY; the Cream Cheese and Salmon were delicious, so I'm thinking we just got unlucky with the Bagels themselves.

Smoked salmon is pretty ubiquitous to bagel shops but I haven't seen one that served roe with their salmon bagel. There's no way I was passing up on this during my visit to New York. 

The Daughter's Delight comes cut in half and honestly, it's enough food for two people. There was no way I could eat both pieces in one sitting. You can opt out of onions, tomatoes and capers but get all of them for the full experience! It's really oily though so grab extra napkins.

We were staying a couple of blocks away and decided to order to go. Ordering online, we had a pick up time for an hour later, so plan accordingly!

Logistically pathetic. 

This morning I wanted to buy three black and white cookies from this place for my work. Woke up early today .. raced through all the BK to Manhattan trains. I call ahead to see if they have them .. and was met with a auto response. 

All orders are to be made online still.. so I quickly try to place an order online fresh off a train standing on prince street. 

But was met with a ordering system that needed a price requirement to even be delivered. From Orchard street to West Broadway .. I was stunned 

Does this place even want customers to their cafe? Is it a full on pet project while they do catering. 

Heard great things about their cookies but it really shouldn't be this hard to purchase 3 cookies from a cafe. 

This is long division math basically.

I've lived in New York for a few years now, and finally decided I had to try to famous Russ and Daughter's lox bagel. We decided to order online as the line outside the store was pretty long, and if you order online you need to pick up at the cafe instead of the original location. 

The lox was delicious - not too oily, not too salty, with a delicious smoky flavor. If you get add-ons like tomatoes and onions, they're 50 cents each. The only reason I gave this place 4 stars instead of 5 is because I wasn't the biggest fan of the bagel. It was really dense and small, and I bet some people prefer that but it wasn't really my cup of tea. Everything else was great, if a little bit expensive.

Heard the lines were long, so I decided to order for pick up instead. Needed to order around 30 minutes in advance, but they give you a very specific time to pick up your order, so that was convenient. 

Got the everything bagel with salmon - it was pretty good, but honestly very very expensive for the amount of salmon it had. The bagel was too hard for my taste - honestly not the best bagel at all, so that was disappointing. 

I'm sure you can get a better and cheaper bagel with salmon elsewhere. Not recommended.

I wish I would've read the previous reviews a little more. Like other people are saying good variety but the bagel is very tough to chew and pretty small for a bagel, and it honestly feels like a chewing endurance event trying to eat one.  I don't know if that's the style or not, but it's not for me, especially when it comes with a hefty 15$ per lox bagel price tag, I want to fully enjoy the meal and not feel like I'm working to get thru it.

Found this place on DoorDash as wasn't in the mood to go there in pouring down rain without an umbrella. :-)

Ordered the chilled Borscht soup, white fish & baked salmon salad. Classic lox & super heesbster which was whitefish & baked salmon salad with horseradish dill cream cheese and wasabi flying fish foe on a bagel.

They used thick kraft/butcher's paper to wrap the bagels. Everything was delectable and impressive. Next time I will go in person and see it in person.

The classic lox and bagel was exceptional. Perfectly toasted everything bagel, cream cheese, red onion, with capers. Reasonably priced considering top quality. Recommend the iced coffee, too.  We were in town for the 4th of July, and were seated at a table within 10 minutes. Looking forward to our next visit. With Covid protocol, you order, and they bring each item nicely wrapped in a bag to your table. We appreciated the cleanliness and attention to detail.

I ordered as takeout and the delivery experience was superb. Everything was packaged perfectly and in a way that would keep the food contained in transit. Food arrived in a timely manner so I wasn't worried about anything having been sitting in the heat for too long. I was extremely impressed. 

Now onto the food. I was a huge fan of the raspberry rugelach the jam was really delicious. It had some chunks in it which I liked. It was not too sweet while the pastry was crisp. Very addictive to eat, I was only suppose to eat one but I devoured all four.

The pop and saltiness of the salmon roe on the Daughters' delight sandwich was a very unique experience. For me, that paired with the scallion cream cheese made the sandwich. I wasn't as impressed with the salmon itself. It was good but didn't significantly stand out and there wasn't much of it. I'd order a sandwich with just the salmon roe on it. The scallion cream cheese was also very very tasty. Some of the best I've had hands down. The everything bagel felt a little tough for me on this sandwich but the bialy was much easier to eat. In future orders I think I would get it on a bialy. 

The super heebster was tasty as well. The wasabi roe smells like wasabi but I wasn't getting strong notes of that flavor so it isn't as intimidating as it sounds! Same with the horseradish cream cheese in the sandwich, it is not overwhelming in flavor against the taste of the fish as the taste of the fish is very strong. Texture-wise it's reminiscent of a tuna sandwich but salty and smoky in flavor more like herring. I was glad I tried it.

Overall the food was good but for the price the only things I'd go out of my way for is the rugelach.
Best lox selection I've seen for a bagel spot! The line is worth the wait, very good bagels! I waited about 40 min in line, but so yummy.

We went for breakfast and sat outside. It's nice that there are tables outside so we could still eat there. We ordered on our phone and it came out really quickly. The potato latkes were delicious. My boyfriend really enjoyed his bagel with cream cheese, salmon and capers. I got the assortment of the chocolate and raspberry cookies and they were very good. We also got a chocolate babka to bring home. I'd never had chocolate babka before. I loved it. It's definitely best the same day if you're just eating it plain. I'd definitely recommend stopping by Russ & Daughters if you're in the neighborhood.
Pastrami cured salmon is incredible. Bagels are perfectly chewy & delicious. Whitefish croquettes were also very good. 1st time going, we'll be back next time we're in NYC.

This place is incredible. My friend and I went for Sunday brunch after a late night out and this lox bagel with some latkes was exactly what we needed. The latkes were nice and crispy with the right shredded potato consistency and the bagel was super fresh with a good combo of flavors. Coming back the next time I'm in NYC.

In the city for a few days and wanted to check out really good breakfast options. Russ & Daughters lived up to recommendation I had been given. We ordered bagels with lox. The bagels were fresh and the salmon was outstanding!

VERY RUDE AND DISRESPECTFUL HOST! 
We were suggested to go to another place if we want something "cheap and trashy" and that "this place is for adult," which makes the environment very unwelcoming even if we wanted to dine here.

Stopped by Russ & Daughters for a quick bagel breakfast and was not disappointed. There was a bit of a wait as they were only seating outside, but tables were first come, first serve. We ordered a classic lox on an everything bagel with chive cream cheese, and an onion bagel with tomato chive cream cheese as well. 

The bagels were not quite as soft as I would like, but were tasty overall. The lox was amazing and they give you a good amount of it. We also ordered potato latkes which came with apple sauce and sour cream. Highly recommend!
Hands down worst bagel I've had. Very disappointed. The bagel wasn't toasted & hard, it had way too much onion, and like no schemer. The picture says it all.

Pathetic customer service. Asked to add flying fish roe , which they have in-house, to a classic bagel and lox. That was too overwhelming for the kitchen. If that overwhelms your kitchen, get a new kitchen staff. Or learn to run the one you have.

Finally tried Russ and Daughters after numerous trips to NY, admittedly always a bit turned off by the price. Their lox/smoked salmon is definitely the best I've had, it even feels sashimi quality, and the smoked flavors are just perfect without it being overly salty. That being said, their bagels were nothing amazing in this city with the best bagels in the country. My ideal situation is to pick up smoked Salmon from here and all my other ingredients from another beloved bagel shop to avoid paying $$$ for 2 lox bagels, but of course I understand this is not ideal for efficiency :)

I was walking out of Katz's a couple weeks ago after the big storm and went by a place with a line out the door-- R&D's main store.  All I had to do was walk a few more blocks to their cafe and presto-- they were uncrowded.  I had placed a takeout order for babka and lox (no, not to eat both in the same bite) and, although quite expensive, I will tell you this: They filled my order even though I was 30min early, and the slice on the lox was just stellar.  You could read a newspaper through it and it suited my personal taste-- that is to say, not too smoky.  When I got back to Idaho with my precious payload of Jewish carbs, my wife decried the babka as too bready.  I can understand this criticism but insist that the  moistness of the babka was winsome.  Toasting produced a pleasant golden brown crunchy exterior but it was still great and chocolaty.  The price is what would keep me from making R&D anything but a special occasion, though.

I thought this place would be soo good based on the reviews over it and the pictures but the bagel was so cold, hard and very very small.

There was a lot of smoked salmon which was nice but it wasn't very flavorful. The pictures are pretty but the taste really wasn't worth the price in my opinion. Maybe its because it was take out so it wasn't as good because it tasted like they used old bagels or prepared them a day ahead and left it in the fridge.

This place had friendly staff, and employed a great system for diners in the age of COVID. It's first come, first served, but the staff helps keep the line moving and fair. (In other words, they look out for people already in line, discouraging line-cutters and confusion.) A friendly employee greeted us the moment we slowed down in front of their door. Excellent! Welcoming!

I ate the classic lox bagel. It was great! The tomato on it was quite good, flavorful. (I note that because sometimes an otherwise good lox bagel sandwich is marred by a disappointing tomato.)

The food was delivered to our table without delay.

I also add a note for hot tea drinkers here. It's hard to get a decent cup of British-style tea anywhere in this country, I've found. Russ & Daughters made me a fine cuppa, though! It was served already prepared with milk and sugar, but they did it right. I was happy. A good cup of tea is a huge comfort.

Wanted to pick up some bagels to go and I am so glad I picked Russ & Daughters! Since I already had something to eat prior I wasn't hungry for any food but when I brought the bagels back home to toast up, it was solid. You know you've purchased a great bagel if the reheat value is there. There's something special about NY bagels and this place is definitely a place worth checking out. 

Make sure to place an online order in advance if you're picking up to go. I placed an order in the morning to pick up after lunch and when I went to pick up my order, I decided to order more and they were already sold out of some of the bagel flavors! I will definitely be back to check out the food.

Way overpriced for the quality of food. I am willing to pay good money for good food. This place is not it. Latkes was burnt outside and bitter. Coffee tasted like it had been sitting there for a while. Their bagel with salmon seems to be popular but without salmon, it was like something you would get at a supermarket. I had been here before, was not satisfied. Wanted to give it another chance,  now the verdict has been made. Will not come back. Will stick with Barney Greengrass, which never disappoints.

The pro tip here is to order ahead. The second pro tip here is to specify to have it toasted, which I forgot, and ending up with a cold lox bagel.
It was yummy nonetheless. And for that $15 price tag, you just gotta convince yourself NYC bagels are worth that much.

Of the "top 5" bagel spots in NYC, this one is a huge downer and falls at the bottom. Z

The cream cheese and lox was the most expensive out of all 5 joints running you close to $20! The bread itself was chewy, I believe my bagel has been at least a day old. The salmon on the other hand was very fresh. 

Outdoor seating and fast service. 

Price per portion, visit the other 4 resturaunts - this one isn't it.

Had a great breakfast of a bialy, some pickled onions and a bagel with lox. The bialy was light and fluffy with some really decent caramelized onions. I topped it with the pickled onions that were some of the best I've ever had. We were just eating them straight for a little bit after that. Topped it with some bagel and lox, which was the best I've ever had. I don't know what they did to smoke that salmon that way but they should keep doing that. 5 outta 5 would recommend to a friend.

I will say I had pretty high expectations for this place at the price point of $15-20 per bagel and the hype surrounding this spot but I was so disappointed! And sad! :(

Paid about $56 got 3 pretty small bagels. Pre-ordered to skip the line, got the Daughter's Delight ($20.50, VERY fishy so don't order if you don't like roe!!) and the Classic on Rye with Capers ($16). You can pick your type of spread and bagel. The bagels were kind of stale/hard. The lox was good and fresh and the spread was nice and creamy though.

Love this place! The horseradish cream cheese is so good and so it the matzo ball soup. My friend had the bagel with lox and loved it. Only taking off a star because my bagel was burnt and the workers were kind of rude

So sorry to be writing this cause my experience earlier this year was completely different and I was soooo looking forward to hitting up Russ & Daughters. Might have even been longer ago as I was able to go inside last time. This time, the everything bagel was not just too salty but very chewy. Last time I went they packed the bagel FAT with salmon. This time, after paying extra for the good stuff, there was a very lean layer of salmon.  I mean LEAN, like a if i pissed someone off lean. This, after an hour wait and it's NOT cheap. I don't mind paying for quality. I would've been more satisfied with bagels and lox from Costco...

The wait on a Friday was almost 1.5 hours long, I believe you can pre order and get it at the cafe. Loved the current protocols during Covid, allowing maybe 3 groups max inside at a time (5 people). The interior was very cute and vintage looking. They had tons of different kinds of fish to choose from. 

We got the classic and the daughters delight. Both was delicious. Smoked salmon melts in your mouth! The bagel was on the harder side probably cause we toasted and left it alone for around 15 mins. 

Highly recommend if you love smoked fish paired with a bagel.

The delivery service used by Russ and Daughters, Door Dash, failed to deliver an order I made on line. When I called Russ and Daughters, their customer representative kept interrupting me as I tried to explain the problem, insisting that I hadn't provided complete delivery instructions. She kept insisting that I hadn't explained that the Door Dash Delivery person had to first obtain entry to my building via the doorman, then take the elevator to my apartment and ring the door bell. She kept cutting me off, repeating that I hadn't provided correct delivery instructions. I still haven't received my order. If Amazon provided delivery like like Russ and Daughters, they'd soon be out of business!

Hands down best lox bagel I've had in my life. 

I am saddened by the idea that I've only tried this for the first time today. Wish I a time machine to gain 8 years of this bagel experience.

Had everything bagel, lox, scallion cream cheese, red onion, tomato, and capers. Was delicious even through delivery. 

Will be ordering every Saturday morning moving forward.

One hour and a half wait for a table seems excessive until you get in and the delightful fishy aroma hits you. Russ & Daughters is a true smorgasbord of New York Jewish thoroughfare and offers everything from lox to borscht to chocolate babka.

We came for a double date and ordered the Ida platter (4 kinds of lox, assortment of bagels and bialys, pickled veggies, tomato, onion, and capers) and the pickled herring with vodka. The buzz from the vodka shot set the mood for the rest of the meal and we finished everything. Food's a little pricy so Will be coming back for special occasions.

A really really good bagel place! We ordered online and just had to pick it up, but even so, it took a while for our order to come out. 

I don't think it's worth a crazy long wait, but it's a darn good bagel.

This place is amazing. The best bagels I've ever had. Before I went here, I really did not think that bagels would be a worthwhile stop. But, I am so glad that I went. I understood. 
The lox with the salmon with the red onions is sooooo good.
Try this place once. 
But, it's pretty expensive. So try it and then try to find another place that's a better value for the money. But try a real NY bagel here. Do it.
Long lines, and overpriced fare, but as delicious as any cafe in the area and worth it if you don't mind the above

I'M DISABLED
love this place. It's a landmark. They don't need my review, but I just wanted to suggest outdoor seating for people waiting to pick up their orders. It was not a disability friendly process. 

As of February 24, 2022 there is no dine in and no outdoor seating. Take out only. 

We saw some folks inside waiting for their order, I let them know my partner and I were disabled, no seats were provided, and we were not invited to come in. Even with proof of vaccination.

Russ and Daughters was not very friendly and although their website says a seated cafe, they were not accommodating. They made us order online from a QR code outside and it was cold and rainy.  I personally heard the owner say that it was much easier to do take out that they were going to ride that wave as long as they could. I was disappointed in the customer service as I had traveled a long way to visit the establishment.  They need to update their website to "online orders only". The owner was snarky and unfriendly as well.  I don't think it's going anywhere but maybe they will cheer up a little and be nice sometime soon.

Our order:
- everything bagel, pastrami lox, scallion cream cheese, tom, onion, capers
- pumpernickel bagel, pastrami lox, horseradish dill cream cheese, onion, capers

Review -- if half stars were available it'd be 3.5 --
Ordering online and picking the order up outside the shop was convenient and safe. The order wait time for pickup at 11:30am on a Saturday was an hour.

The food was definitely good, however we weren't impressed with the bagels. We've had better at random bodegas and elsewhere. I intentionally ordered a pumpernickel bagel because I was expecting a strong flavor, but it was super subtle if anything at all. The pastrami lox was definitely delicious and good quality. But overall a $43 meal of just two bagelsl sandwiches and an hour wait -- my opinion is save your money and time and go somewhere else that is decent.

Poppy seed bagel and scallion cream cheese. Best bagel I've had. I ordered online for pickup and you actually have to get it at their other location around the building. Very nice service and they have an extra bagel :)

A bit pricey but the lox is one of the best I've had so far! You can tell it's fresh and pairs so well with an everything bagel. Also their mushroom soup is very yummy and hearty for a cold day! 

Also, you have to order on their website. There's no more indoor seating anymore so my fiancé and I brought it to the Starbucks around the corner to eat inside (and also ordered Sbux drinks too haha).

Dear restaurant, thank you so much for introducing me to a variation in my morning bagel routine. I'm excited to say I've added tomatoes to my salmon bagel and I love love love it. It was very nice visiting your location. Love from Virginia!

Really good lox but their bagel is lacking. There are better bagel places but Russ and daughters has the best lox I've tried so far. This location is takeout only so you have to order online and then pick it up. Pretty fast to get our bagels. Definitely checkout for their fish!
Extremely hard bagel. Very little cream cheese. Wouldn't visit again. Ordered from doordash for pickup and it was ready in under 5 minutes.

COVID had ruined everything!  It was pouring rain and we couldn't eat inside so we stood under an awning to eat our bagels.  The bagels were cold (despite us waiting under said awning for the bagels to be ready) and mine was definitely NOT toasted well -- just a smidge at the edges to let me know they DID know they were supposed to toast it but chose not to do it well.

If you're going to charge the money and put your name on the order, you better deliver!

Picked up the saddest bagel and lox sandwich here, EVER. I know there is the Deli around the corner, but this one actually lets you order ahead online minus 90% of the attitude and frustration, so we took the bait.

The bagels:
- tiny and stale. Must have been made a week ago. 
- about HALF the size of Essa

The lox:
- the smallest amount I've ever seen
- not enough flavor, just salty

The price:
- how much are you charging for this sad little sandwich? 

Public Service Announcement:
DO NOT GET THE BAGEL AND LOX HERE, EVEN THO IT'S ON THE MENU!

So, go to their Deli around the corner for the frustration and time sink and it'll cost you a lot, but it's a better sandwich.

Better alternative? Go to Best Bagels or Brooklyn Bagel, it's fast, they have online ordering, and it's 87% as good. Or go to Essa Bagel, but you'll have to commit more time.
Got a pretzel bagel with scallion CC and lox. So good!!  Costs about $15 which seems about normal for NY but can feel pricey.

Russ & Daughters Cafe is currently take out only. You can order online and skip the lines of the main location. I ordered the classic lox bagel with onions and tomatoes, which costs an additional $0.50 each and half a pound of the nova smoked salmon. I was a bit disappointed by the bagel. It was small and the nova was a bit too salty. It wasn't as satisfying as I had hoped. I had better.

This is an unpopular opinion seeing as how Russ & Daughters is beloved in New York, and I'm hoping I went on an off day. It was winter and cold and the cafe was still closed due to the pandemic so we ate outside where they had set up some tables and chair. 

I thought the bagel itself was hard and chewy, and the salmon was really salty. I did, however, take home a loaf of chocolate babka and that was really good! It wasn't too sweet. I sliced it thick to toast with some butter and also used it to make french toast. Both methods were delicious!

I woke up today and decided I was craving some Salmon Lox. I did not even wash my face. I walked straight here as I quickly ordered my bagel online on Toasttab half awake. No regrets. This was an amazing Sunday breakfast treat.

Ordered online because I was afraid there was going to be a line at the other location. Anyway, I've been trying a bunch of different of bagels in the city and after trying two other places (Best and Ess-a-bagel), Russ and Daughter's had the smallest and hardest bagels. I do think their smoked salmon is the best though.

Information in this restaurant is not updated on the  Yelp portal. 

It was quiet a disappointment to have arrived at the cafe after 45 minutes walk to  find out that they have not established full service, for now is only take our orders.

Russ and Daughters is THE BEST. For the first time we ordered delivery instead of going to the restaurant. It was entirely easy to do that and the food arrived very promptly. Smoked Sable is the best thing we've ever tasted. As always the lox / smoked salmon was amazing. Lovely bagels! Babka to die for! This is it one of our must-stop-there eateries in New York!
Amazing!!!! I love that it's old school! Must go and get the classic bagel! Great service too!

We had the pastrami-cured salmon on an everything bagel. The salmon was divine - tender, luscious, smoky - truly exceptional, unparalleled with any other cured salmon that I've ever had. The bagel was average - didn't taste particularly fresh. Relatively expensive for a bagel sandwich - nearly $20 - worth trying for the salmon but not the bagel.

It was the most amazing experience we could have hoped for. Great service, great food, beautiful story of the family business and it's displayed on the restaurant walls with original founders welcoming you in their place of sanctuary from over 100 years ago.

Highly recommend as one of the must visit food staples in NYC!!!

Really, really wanted to check out Russ & Daughters food (bagels, lox, cream cheese) during our recent trip to NYC, but also sit down and take our time. The answer? Russ & Daughters Cafe.

We arrived one weekday morning last week -- maybe 10:30 or 11:00. No wait for a table -- were shown to one in the back right away. Ordered seltzer water all 'round, plus the bagel/lox platters and a side order of latkes and an extra onion bialy. 

The food and service were both GREAT. The best smoked salmon I've ever had (and I've had LOTS) and the bagel was no slouch either. The latkes were excellent -- freshly made -- and the bialy was super.

We had to pay our bill quickly after we finished eating because a big thunderstorm was brewing outside. We made it back to our hotel down the street (Sixty LES) just as a downpour started.

We'll be back!

This might be one of the best breakfasts we've had... ever... the latkes are amazing and so thick. Delicious. I was worried that The Super heebster might be too spicy but the fish and the wasabi infused roe was perfect. The pickled herring trio was my personal favorite. The flavors were insane. The stetle was good but probably the least favorite of the bunch, we would probably get the classic lox next time. The challah French toast was custard and delicious. We had the Bloody Mary with caraway infused vodka, breakfast martini, and smoked martini which were all great. Our waiter was so friendly, all the staff were great. The atmosphere is awesome. I highly recommend this place to anyone wanting a delicious fish forward breakfast with incredible cocktails.

So, off the bat, the food & service is good.  My only gripe, and it's a big one for me, is that they skimp on the smoked fish (Sable in my case) when ordering a platter (basically smoked fish, bagel, tomatoes,  onion). In my opinion if I put the above combination together I should be able to see the fish...  and for $28 especially.   They should at least either cut the fish thicker or give you double the amount that is given.   4 razor thin pieces of Sable for $28 doesn't cut it imo.  I would go back and I guess pay Xtra for a double portion.  The latkes and eggs scramble with sturgeon was good.  Anyway, that's my take

Being an upper East side guy, a retail purchase of an item on the lower east side gave me an opportunity to try a NY staple of smoked fish; the new Russ and Daughter's Cafe. First off, I was impressed with the old time layout, cleanliness, and staff. The menu was replete with all that a deli maven could want on 
the dairy and fish side as well as old  favorites like an egg cream. It also had a nod to the drinking clientele and happy hour crowd with a very fun separate drink menu. The prices are on the higher side for a lower east side cafe but times have changed on old Orchard and Delancey streets; millennials have arrived in droves. I ordered a mainstay of the name; their nova platter with a $22
price tag. The nova was very fresh, individually sliced thin and tasty with a delicious whipped cream cheese on the side. It was served on a cute wood board to add some nice presentation. I had the fish with a poppy seed bagel. My wife, not being
overly hungry, had a bowl of matzah ball soup. 
As for the lox, it was very good; was it the best I ever
had; not really,  but very good. The portion could have been a  bit larger for the money but it was adequate. I have had better tasting and larger bagels but it was decent. For $12, the matzah ball soup was of modest  size; good but not outstanding, and served with, well nothing. I would return when in the area and recommend it to others.

My first visit to Russ and Daughters! The inside perfectly fuses retro and modern chic design, I love it! My friends and I put our name in around 12:15 on a super hot Saturday and were quoted a 45 minute wait. When we got the confirmation text, it said 35 minutes. It was enough time to go grab an iced coffee nearby. We came back on time with our party dropped down to 2 and were seated right away at the end of the bar. I loved the bar! Super cute, great bar stools and friendly and attentive bartenders. Be sure to specify tap water when you're asked if that's what you want! We started with a round of bloody Mary's - my friend ordered the dill infused and I ordered the pepper; however, the bartender said the variety with the vegetables is most popular. I'm unsure if we were actually both given the dill cocktail but who cares because it was fantastic and quite the large pour - makes up for the $18 price tag. We split a matzah ball soup and without asking, the staff split it to two bowls for us - one ball each. The matzah balls were the best I've ever had! The chicken left something to be desired - this would have been perfect with just the matzah and vegetables, but protein does the body good!
