After debating over the breakfast board, we both opted for the Lower Sunny Side - 2 eggs, latkes and smoked salmon. As to be expected the salmon was exceptional! I wish I had asked if I could have different styled eggs, but the sunny side up were fine, just not my favorite. The latkes were also super yummy but a bit too much food for me, as they were quite thick. This was a bit pricey for breakfast at $22 for the entree - I guess we're paying for the salmon. Worth it! I'd love to get some to take home but the line at the salmon shop is regularly lengthy. Huge fan of the coffee candy that comes with the bill! A nice surprise after a savory meal.

horribly, horribly overpriced for what you get. mostly tourists who go to the cafe. don't waste your money on this overpriced tourist trap. Go tor Katz's deli around the corner for a better meal at a lower price.

I would recommend to sit at the counter and ask for a plate of herring.
It's a good place to go too after or before a visit at the Tenement Museum as it's only a block away
Walked right in on a Saturday @ 9 am. Plenty of seating and served right away. Had the classic board. Seriously the best nova I've ever had. I'll be thinking about that for a while.

Hear ye, hear ye! I have finally made it to Russ & Daughter's Cafe! Only took four  years of me living in NYC and constantly saying that we should reeeeally check it out SOON! But you know how it goes in this city - so many restaurants and only so little time and stomach space to go around.

I showed up during brunch hours on a Saturday to find a bunch of people lined up outside as expected, put down my name and number, frolicked around exploring the neighborhood, and got a text saying my table was ready about 30 mins later rather than the original ETA I was given of 45 mins. Not too shabby.

I honestly enjoyed all the food and my cold brew, and our server dressed up in the signature white lab coats could not have been friendlier. The matzo ball soup was great and a must order, in my opinion - full of flavor and nice big chunks of chicken and veggies and quite a sizable portion as well. The bagel and lox board was satisfying, but about what you would expect, nothing out of the norm. The item I probably could have done without simply because I didn't find them to be anything special was the white fish croquettes, but I did enjoy the creamy dill sauce these came with.

This was a big check mark on my never ending NYC establishments. Expensive, crowded, but tasty and a must nevertheless. Dare I say I feel accomplished? I dare! This would be a fun spot to show off to out of town friends and family.

We've wanted to come here for some time, and since we did last week, we can't wait to return.

Caution: waits can be very long, so go early - it's not the place to go on a last minute whim - you have to plan ahead, or go early, as reservations are not accepted.

The food - we had the nova and the sturgeon plates - both were outstanding - "like butter" as my mother used to say.  The latkes were ok, a little too thick for my taste, but still good.

The service - again, terrific - special props to the front desk - they have to deal with a lot of disappointed folks who are not able to partake, and to add to that, as of this writing they are only open until 2:30PM - hopefully that closing time will soon change.

Highly recommended, and don't worry, if you can't get it into the cafe, the original R&D shop is a few blocks away for those who's hankering can't wait.
Best french toast ever!!! I ordered the cinnamon and apple. I'll never eat french toast anywhere else again

Loved this for brunch! The cafe was so cute and the staff were so helpful and friendly. The fish was delicious! The bagel and latkes yummy. Fully recommend! We did stop by the storefront first but decided we wanted to eat in person, so we came to the cafe.

We tried to get 2 bagels at the original Russ & Daughter's appetizing store on Houston Street but we were at least a hundred spots behind in the ticketing system and the line did not seem to be moving very fast at all... everyone ahead was putting in big orders of at least a dozen bagels or more because I guess they were locals and wanted to get breakfast for the entire week for their families? 

Anyways, we were called for the cafe after spending about 40 minutes on the waitlist. This was on a Sunday afternoon in the midst of Labor Day weekend so we were expecting this. 

I wanted to come here specifically to check out their smoke salmon (one of my favorite foods) so that's what I ordered. It was absolutely amazing paired with their everything bagel and their house made cream cheese. I just wish they gave more than 3 slices so I could smash down some salmon by itself. 

What really surprised me was their Matzo ball soup. It had really deep flavor and was the perfect antidote to a nasty hangover brewing from yestereve. Their house made sodas are also awesome and highly recommended from me. They pair really interesting botanicals and flavors with fruity syrups.

I can't imagine a New York City without a stop at Russ & Daughters, the original location. And the somewhat new cafe (OK, three years...) didn't miss a beat and follows up on the excellence of the original location. I had smoked sablefish with goat cream cheese on an everything bagel with tomato, capers, red onion and a bit of dill. Sublime. And the coffee here is far above average and beats some of the so called coffee spots that dot the neighborhood.

Service was polite, impeccable, friendly, simply spot on.

For those that complain about pricing, well, yes, it is on the high side. But everything in this city is. Staying in an affordable illegal (I suspect) airbnb so I can forgo the $600-$800/night and up postage stamp of a hotel room with amenities such as sirens going by every 30 minutes. Try buying a 600 square foot flat here. You'll be out a very, very health 6 figures. I digress. Everyone should know this. If you want cheap, plenty of those places, too, but not with this kind of quality.

Can't wait to return to try it again. R&D is like a piece of history, a must experience in the city in my humble opinion.

It doesn't get better than this. Everything is insanely good, but try the matzo ball soup and a custom soda in addition to the fish board. Obviously can't go wrong with lox but the sable is another great choice. Also love the modern/retro ambiance.
Best bagels around. If you're in town, this is a must added stop. Authentic NY bagels and Kosher. Can't be beat

10/10. This is a MUST on your NY itinerary. I was a solo traveler & stopped in for brunch on a weekend with no reservation. I was initially told the wait was 45 minutes but the hostess was kind enough to tell me to wait as she suspected seats at the bar were opening up. She was right. Not even 5 minutes later, there were 3 seats available!

The hot coffee was delicious. I ordered the eggs Benny on challah toast. And it was just MM MM GOOD! Chef's kiss! 

The service was fast & easy. I had zero issues ordering & the entire staff was friendly & accommodating. I had a bagel to go from their other location, but I am so so glad I popped in for a full service meal!

So so sooo good! Wait was about 30 minutes on Friday but ended up being less which was great. Definitely order the latkes and get an ice coffee. Some of the best I've ever had!
Our waiter (who was amazing) convinced us to get the whitefish salad, and so glad we listened to him. 10/10

We have been wanting to try the cafe since they opened and finally got the chance. No one does smoked fish better. My wife had the scrambled eggs, Nova and latkes; I had the board of Nova, bagel and cream cheese with tomato, onion and capers. Both excellent. A special thank you for the great service. My mistake, I miss-ordered my egg cream, and our server replaced it at no charge! Gotta have the chocolate. I had no idea that there were other kinds. Thank you!!!

Came here for breakfast. I like the atmosphere here, it's relaxed and staff are very helpful. Wait time for table for two was appropriate. It's a clean place with very nice food presentation. The taste is subjective but in my experience, I wish it was more unique.
this place is iconic. really lived up to hype. the lox is not to be missed and it's good any form you get it in!! the latkes were also incredible.

This was my first time here and I loved it! The atmosphere inside the restaurant was very soothing and relaxing. The food is fresh and the service was excellent.  It was a very nice experience. I loved it so much that when we left the restaurant we went straight to their shop located two blocks away (Houston St). Note: They close for dinner and they don't accept reservations. I do recommend this restaurant and I can't wait to come back.

A must stop when in NYC. I always get there just when the open and grab a seat at the counter. Their chopped liver is the best in the city. I usually get the mensch board (smoked sturgeon) since sturgeon is harder to find back home compared to lox. This time I tried the lox, onions, scrambled eggs with a side of latkes with salmon roe. Pure heaven. Super service from the attentive staff. I wish I could have stashed a pound of chopped liver in my carry on! Looking forward to my next visit.

The original Russ & Daughters has been around for over 100 years and never disappoints. Get in, get your number, get the goods, and go. Expect a line. But this new sit-down location is fantastic. Had the bagel board but looking forward to going back for more.

We were in town, and like everyone else, we wanted to go to the bagel place, which was rated high on yelp.  Luckily it was very close to where we were staying, we got there on Friday morning around 8:30 am and got seated right away at the bar.   I didn't realize the original one is also near, but it's not a sit-down cafe.  We are glad we came to the cafe to experience the whole thing. The place had a clean, white, simple look, like a typical Israeli restaurant/deli. I ended up ordering bialys instead of a bagel with smoked salmon.   It was the most expensive "bagle lox " I ever had at $22, but it was delicious, and we enjoyed the experience.  I actually liked bialys more than bagle and now I will have to look for that in SD.  The customer service was great and I would love to come back to try different things on the menu when I am in town next time.

The cafe is a full-service version of the famed shop a few blocks away. The first time I visited, it was during  a pandemic flare and they were doing takeout. I ordered as-is bagels and fish to go, along with a toasted pumpernickel bagel with butter and lox and pumpernickel bread. It was easy to order online and pickup. And everything was delicious.

I went back a year later for a sit down breakfast. A short line formed before opening and the cafe filled quickly. It's got an old-school diner feel. I ordered the bagel board with a pumpernickel bagel (shocking). It was great. The staff is super friendly and I look forward to returning.

Stylish, great service, and delicious food makes this a solid brunch spot - just be sure you're willing to wait for a table.

They make everything from scratch.  The bagels are delicious and the lox is perfect.  The other smoked fishes also look amazing - I definitely want to come back here and share a platter with the table. And the latkas are a perfect appetizer - crunchy on the outside and soft gooey potato inside.  So good!

Just be ready to wait for a table.  Our group of three got there at 9:15 on a Saturday and it was a thirty minute wait.  Ten minutes later, people arriving in a three person group had to wait fifty minutes.  I recommend not getting here past 9:30 unless you're okay with waiting an hour or more!

The perfect NY deli for smoked salmon.

Absolutely beautiful cafe with delicious and fresh smoked salmon bagels. We got the classic everything bagel with smoked salmon, eggs Benedict and French toast. 

Let's start with the everything bagel with smoked salmon. Did it live up to its name? I honestly think it did. The salmon was super high quality, the tomatoes were fresh, the red onion and capers were good and the white cream cheese spread east like butter. Mmmm super yum! The eggs Benedict had spinach in it, but the spinach was cooked perfectly - not too rough or wilted. The French toast was sweet but not TOO SWEET. You know that's the best compliment an Asian person can give about sweet things. 

Got here around 11 a.m. on a weekend and we were seated around 12:00 p.m. which I guess wasn't terrible. You go in and give them your name and number and they'll text you when they have your table ready. There's also just Russ & Daughters which is a to-go kind of spot and we tried to go there too but it was an even longer wait than here which was surprising. I guess New Yorkers are really passionate about their bagels ‍ but I can't blame them, I'm one of those people too!
The (everything) bagel was good! Only took a point off cause I was not a huge fan of the cream cheese. Definitely order ahead to avoid lines.

Discovered a new love to lox bagels here, which I'll miss dearly one I'm gone from NYC! I love how no-frills and straightforward this place is - take a ticket, wait to be called up, and watch as they slice the lox and other fish/meats right in front of you. Classic, tried and true, and for good reason! Only taking a start off because it can get crowded and you might be waiting for your number for a while, so I don't advise this place if you're in a rush.

Life is great when the plan you had before does not work out, but when Plan B works out better than you ever imagined, better than the original plan you had.

This is what happened, and I guess it would be appropriate to say it is a Chanukah miracle. My original plan for lunch today was to go to Katz's Deli for lunch. When I saw the line outside was basically wrapping around the block, I abandoned my plan and decided to go to Russ & Daughters Cafe instead. I have been to the flagship store and know the food is good, but had never been to the cafe for lunch, as I never had the opportunity, and thinking it would just be alright. 

It is more than alright, it is a treat. A beautiful experience transposed onto a bowl, a board, and a plate. Just be willing to pay up because this will not be cheap. For me at least, since I decided to ante up and go for several things.

For starters, the hostess sat me at the counter. No loss. It was a 45 minute wait for the seat as it gets fairly busy for lunch. I can certainly do that. 

As for the food... yeah buckle up buddy boy. 

Matzo ball soup: A hearty blend of one golf-sized matzo ball, chicken, some carrots, and a bit of celery. It works beautifully. The presentation is a bit poor because the broth overflow onto the plate it is served with below, but the matzo ball is tasty. This one does it right. However, give me noodles with it and you have a five star appetizer. Score: 4/5 stars

Cream Soda: Starts out strong, but quickly fizzles out. Save your money, unless you like quick and easy drinks. Score: 3.5/5 stars

Potato latkes: Jewish potato pancakes cooked to maximum effort. Three solid sized bad boys served with your choice of either applesauce and sour cream or cream cheese and caviar. I opted for the former and it was delicious. My Jewish origins were speaking to me as I was eating this, but only in a whisper. Unfortunately I could not eat the last one because it is a dense treat. That being said, I highly recommend these. Score: 4.5/5 stars 

Shtetl: I was torn between the Classic and this, so I asked my server at the bar. Since I told her I had tried their lox and knew it was good, she directed me to the Shtetl: It is excellent. The goat cream cheese marries well with the sablefish, which almost tastes like whitefish without the mashy mix. The everything bagel is perfectly toasted and perfectly coated with garlic, poppyseeds, and sesame seeds. Even the goat cream cheese is terrific. I could have eaten this alone just out of the ramekin, but restrained myself from doing so. It is also served with tomatoes, onions, and capers, but I am simple. No need for these! Reminder my Jewish origins whispering to me? They were speaking pretty loudly after this one. Score: 5/5 stars 

Now, for the topper...

Egg cream: This is as New York as it gets. However, I learned too quickly that you have to drink this fast as the frothy top disappears, and then you are left with a borderline nasty mixture of milk, seltzer, and chocolate syrup. Still solid way to end any meal, but drink up! Score: 4/5 stars

***Bonus***

During Chanukah, Russ and Daughters sells a limited time offer of three jelly donuts that they make, as jelly donuts are an iconic food during Chanukah. One that is of the black and white cookie style, one that is an original jelly donut with strawberry jam, and one that looks and tastes like a strawberry rugelach that also has strawberry jam. All three are fabulous and you will wish they served these year round. The fact the servers everywhere were hyping this up is telling you to get this either as you walk out the door, or as a sweet treat to wrap up a flawless lunch. Score: 5/5 stars

---- 

A Lower East Side without Russ & Daughter's and Katz's is unfathomable. It still transplants you to a time when these establishments dominated Delancey St and W Houston St. Thankfully, if all continues to go well, they will continue to be here, and continue to remind customers, now and in the future, what made this area so special and unique at the turn of the century.

Life is a funny thing, is it not?
I love Jewish soul food, so this was my kind of heaven. I wish they'd let us call ahead for the line- we waited an hour. But I'll go back every time I'm in the Lower East Side.

Absolutely the best bagels i ve ever tried. Shtetl is to die for! We have also tried matzo ball soup, latke, and the babka french toast; I think among those babka french toast was a killer, highly recommend.

Got seated super fast in the late morning. The service was lovely and there was sense of community at the bar seating area. The food was great and this is a very good alternative if you want the famous bagels but don't want to wait in line or also want to sit down and relax. Tucked on the corner just a couple blocks from the original.

We just finished visiting a Jewish deli exhibition and thought it would be prefect to top it up with a lunch at a famous Jewish deli ! The iconic Russ and daughters deli was the selected location . 
It's a more upscale establishment compared to Katz , and the prices are a bit higher , but we had a great experience overall 
We came in at 12:30 and had to wait for only 5 mins before getting seated. Not too bad.we were a party of 3 and here's what we ordered :
1) chopped liver - excellent . Wife just loved it . Good portion , very tasty and goes. Curly w the accompanying Matza crackers . 5/5
2) herring trio - the waiter warned us it's small but 16$ for six bite size herring bites ? The fish was excellent - fresh and tasty, salty exactly at the right amount , but the procenn the price is too high 3/5
3) pastrami- like salmon bagel - very good bagel (a mini one ) the salmon was super fresh and we loved the pastrami - like flavors  ( the restaurant does not serve meet btw) 5/5
4) salmon bagel plate - the salmon was again, just excellent and in good portion. The bagel was very good . 5/5
5) sours - a variety of pickles - I loved the pickles tomatoes and the full-sour cucumbers . The half sour was so-so. 8$ for that is a little bit on the high side 4/5
6) the three of us shared a chocolate babka French toast for dessert - it was a good one , sufficient to split between us and the chocolate inside was quite generous , but the sour cream on the side ??? This one calls for a whipped cream . Definitely not sour.4/5
All in all it was about 105$, they also give you free seltzer and we ordered a coffee. little on The high side but a great experience overall . Service was exceptionally good 
Recommended !

Been wanting to try this breakfast/brunch spot for a while. Today was the day I went and waited the hour to get a table on the weekend. The good thing is they will take your number and you can walk around the neighborhood. The food is outstanding. I tried so much. The smoked salmon was so luxurious and melt in your mouth good. The farfel was butter good along with a side of potato latkas. I opted for the chicken soup to start. If I were to do it again I would skip that. Really good but too filling and there are so many other things to try. Finished the meal with some sweet noodle kuggel that was divine.  All in all an excellent meal with a staff that was friendly and attentive.

Below average tasting Bagels. The hype is real and while visiting NYC we decided to go out of our way and try it. It's a good tasting bagel with smoked salmon but we didn't think it was that good to wait in line for 30 min not to mentioned it's prices. We would pay even more if we were blown away by it but we had better bagels in many other places. 
Would not go back.

My friend recommended this place to me when I was in New York last December since I claimed to have never tried a New York-style bagel.

The entire experience was all I could ever ask of a bagel place which exceeded my expectations in EVERY way.

QUALITY. I ordered the salmon/sturgeon everything bagel with scallion cream cheese & brought back to my hotel to try. The quality of all parts of the bagel were regal and provide a perfect bite each time.

They're not shy with the amount of ingredients, and yet, all the flavors were perfectly balanced and never felt overwhelming.

That said, if you're not a huge eater, you can easily share this bagel with someone else or save the other half for the next meal.

This place was so good, that I had to order (& split) another similar (except one added fish - so there were 3 types of fish this time instead of 2) order the next day. 

This time, while just as delicious, it felt like a bit too much fish for me, so I would would prefer my first order going forward.

PLEASE do me a favor and try this place & make it your go-to regal bagel experience!

Went here on a Tuesday morning.   Seated at the counter after a 20 minute or so wait.  I got a molasses egg cream, yummy.  Husband got coffer soda.  It was so good we asked how to make it at home.   Shared a knish and a bialy platter.  The lightest bialy I every had.   Salmon was melt in your mouth.   Worth every penny.   Also tried the pickled herring trio, which looked so pretty, but we just could not stomach it.   Nothing bad about it,  just came  to the conclusion that pickled herring is not for us.  Got raspberry rugelach to go.   Can't wait to go back.

A great alternative to standing in line at the original Houston St. spot. You're going to pay a little more, and truth be told, a fancy board is not how I prefer my bagel sandwiches, but it's fun to feel a little fancy now and again, especially when the food is this good. The expanded menu is good too -- the latkes and matzo ball soup are great. And the desserts are not to be missed, especially the halva ice cream (the texture is a little weird, but I still like it).

Went to Russ and Daughters in New Years Eve with the Family...Being New Years Eve, I felt a bit celebratory and decided to go big and ordered the soft scrambled eggs with Caviar and Champagne.  Unbelievably delicious and worth every penny!  We'll be back!

I really enjoyed this place but it didn't quite live up to the hype for me. We got the classic and the potato latkes with salmon roe. The everything bagel was just alright -- I honestly didn't see anything special about it and it doesn't compare to the other iconic bagel places in NYC like Tompkins or Brooklyn Bagel. It went very well with the salmon and cream cheese though. The latkes were good, although I found them to be a little dry on their own. The salmon roe was delicious, and paired really well with the crème fraiche.

Great place for a satisfying breakfast, but I wouldn't rave about it.
The food was delicious. My first time there. New bar set and hoping to be able to enjoy this place again soon.

What a wonderful experience my buddy Stu and I had at Russ & Daughters Cafe. Never been to the restaurant only the Appetizing Store. We both ordered The board with nova and goat cheese cream cheese. Absolutely delicious. With tomatoes onions and capers. Our sever was a young woman who was phenomenal. They served us complimentary seltzer water. We both had a wonderful experience. Thank you so much Russ & Daughters

We came around 8:30AM and there was no wait. The service was great and our food came out within 10 minutes! The classic salmon board was really good and a must try if you come here! I didn't think I would like it but the smoked salmon/onion/tomato combo was perfect. I really liked being able to put together my bagel too. The green onion cream cheese spread made the bagel even better. I'd also recommend asking for pickled onions to add to your board. I did not enjoy the blintzes due to the cheese texture but my friends liked it. 

IG: tiffsfoodreview

The salmon was delish, the bagel was meh. More hype than it's worth. Glad to have tried it during brunch with a friend but 2 open face salmon bagels with coffee was $50 and way more than what it's worth. Nice atmosphere and really attentive staff. Note if you ask for extra cream cheese, they'll charge you.

The ambiance and the food itself are fantastic. Wish I could've had one of everything on the menu. It's not going to be your cheapest breakfast/brunch/etc., but that's to be expected with deli fare. To return for another meal!

I have gone to the original grab and go location and absolutely love the the quick service and awesome selection. The cafe unfortunately is a very different story. They miscalculated the wait- we were quoted an hour 15 minutes but texted an hour and a half wait. Ultimately we waited over 2 hours and were treated terribly by one of the hostess. Her attitude really put a damper on our day. Not only did they do a terrible job of ushering groups that have paid out but we're inconsiderate of the parties waiting. The hype is not worth it.
Delicious food. I had eggs, smoked salmom and potato latkes.... Yum! Elegant feeling with soothing jazz music playing. Don't judge this book by the neighborhood!

Visited Russ and Daughters after watching Somebody Feed Phil  

Got the egg cream, lox benedict, potato latkes with applesauce and sour cream, rugelach, and chocolate babka french toast. My favorite was the babka french toast (delicious!) followed by the latkes. The rest of the items I thought were ok.

Be prepared to put your name down and wait a good 45 minutes just fyi!
The best Nova Scotia anywhere, hands down. Also number one for bagels. Its small so expect some wait time.

Delicious salmon lox and great service! The salmon tasted very aromatic and the bagels tasted fresh. I highly recommend getting them toasted. 

The service was great. The check comes with a Russ & Daughters postcard, and when I took a picture of it, another waiter noticed and quickly gave us a couple more postcards. I also said the word "dessert" and my table's waiter immediately started pointing out the dessert options.

love their bagels and my friends love their bagels because it helps our jawline LOL I feel like their bagels are a little more chewy here but we like that experience and seek this location out when we feel that kind of vibe
Nice nostalgic taste of New York Style Jewish food. Everything was good. Not the best bagels but good enough. Fish was great and the babka French toast was really nice. Good service and very clean.

After 4 long years of waiting, was happy to be back for the best salmon bagel. Had it twice on this trip, and was happy that the quality and taste had not changed. My only issue was the salmon seemed to be less and less. It's paper thin and parceling it out on 2 slices of bagel was challenge. Also, not enough cream cheese.

If you do not like fish do not go here!

$123 for two salads, a dessert, and two cocktails. 

Uptown feel inside but still cozy. Food is meh.

Everything was delightful from start to finish.  Fun old time setting.  We sat at the bar after a 20 minute wait and had great service.  The match ball soup 2as delicious and beautifully presented.  The kashas were THE BEST version I gave ever had of kasha.  The whitefish salad was too mushy for my taste but tye presentation was beautiful.  The salmon was perfect.   Just a delight all around.

One of my favorite lox in the city! We had a group of 4 so we decided to share the Ida Platter and boy was it amazing. The pastrami cured salmon has to be the best there is! The spread is god level and while the menu mentions it feeds 3-4, I feel this could easily feed 6 people! With the amount of lox, bread, toppings, and everything we had plenty to take home. Surprisingly enough, the one can't miss attraction of Russ & Daughters is the matzo ball soup. It tastes like the cleanest, most chickeny broth you've ever had that I think it could possibly cure me of my mental illness LOL latkes never miss but be sure to stop by next time at the cafe.

Obviously the fish and the food are amazing. That goes without saying. I've been to this place multiple times and I cannot speak enough to the actual quality of the food. It's absurdly good. I actually came in with the intention of buying a few tins of caviar for a party after my meal but quickly changed my mind after a salty encounter with a waiter. The main thing that put me completely off was that I asked to taste a wine and the server said, "get the Albariño", my friend clarified and said, "she was asking if she could have a taste" to which he replied "no, she can taste it when she buys the glass". I understand it's no wine bar but literally waiters have let me taste wine at the Olive Garden. He had a salty attitude and there are so many other different ways to say it... "unfortunately we don't offer tastings but I think you might like this". His tone, words and body language just put me completely off. Didn't get my caviar because I was just over the whole experience. With that said, the service leaves MUCH to be desired.

What a gem! We came here for lunch after a tour at the Tentament Museum. Bagels, lox, matzo ball soup, latkes... everything was excellent. A lovely cafe with an interesting family legacy. Had a fancy diner diner vibe. Would highly recommend and will be back.

This is the elegant modern diner version of the original shop that's been a LES institution for over 100 years. A huge hit with our family and one of our favorite meals in Manhattan. Gaspe Nova salmon with cream cheese and caviar on a pumpernickel bagel is heaven in a bite...we also tried the pastrami cured salmon but their original Gaspe cure was our hands down favorite. We also had potato latkes with smoked salmon & salmon roe, matzo ball soup, pickled herring trio, chopped liver and chocolate babka French toast. Definitely not inexpensive @ almost $350 including tip, but worth every penny. Went to original store on Houston St to pickup box of chocolate rugelach and load of chocolate babka - huge hits!

My mom was friends with one the Russ daughters so this business is sorta in my blood.  Our family has been feasting on their supple lox and unctuous sable, babka and hopjes (Dutch coffee candies) for over a century.  Being able to lunch at this casual and comfy restaurant is a wonderful option.  Of course I order the bialy with cream cheese, capers and lox from the friendly server - when she gave us a few hopjes at the end my soul was full.  
It's a bright place, windows front and back, in a LES spot a brisk walk south of their store (a new branch is coming in Hudson Yards!).  Well worth the walk and I'm looking forward to a return visit for that sable.

Great breakfast/brunch spot! We were recommended by multiple people are live nearby that Russ and Daughters had some of the best lox bagels in New York so we had to give it a try. We ordered the classic board which came with a generous portion of toppings to build our bagel with. Lox was very fresh and flavorful. Latkes were crispy and well seasoned, paired well with the sauce. The pickled herring trio was incredibly tasty but more of an acquired taste if you are averse to pickled foods. Presentation on the board in particular was great as well and no complaints with the service. Nice decor, making this a suitable date spot as well.

The grab and go Russ and daughters spot was closed so we decided to come to this cute sit down spot to make sure we got our New York bagel! This place had a 30 minute wait but thankfully we were seated much faster which was nice. This is a spot where you can get a variety of breakfast brunch like food - we ended up ordering:

* lox bagel plate - this came with a pumpernickel bagel we chose and came with salmon, cream cheese, tomato, onions and dill. Everything was super fresh and went well together 

*latkas - these were really yummy - almost kindof like a super crispy hash brown with some onions inside as well and came with salmon roe and creme fraiche. Very flavorful and yummy to say the least

Overall, this is a nice solid spot if you are looking for some yummy breakfast food New York style!

came on a slow monday and there was a 45 minute wait. once we ordered, food came out pretty quick. staff was nice and made recommendations for us- it was our first time here. the classic is a MUST. saw photos on yelp and it lived up to the hype. staff recommended pastrami russ- surprisingly great choice. overall yummy and good midday snack.

You're coming here for the salmon and whitefish, not the bagels. The bagels are tough, and taste, smell, and have the texture of cardboard. 

This was validated by my Jewish friend. 

I sat next to someone who ordered the whitefish and witnessed them have a spiritual experience. I ordered the classic board which is their most popular item.

Despite not being a fan of uncooked salmon, the gaspe nova smoked salmon was phenomenal. It had a mild smoky flavor with a satiny texture.

TL;DR - solid bagel spot that lives up to its century old reputation. I'll make sure to come by their grab and go shop once it's done remodeling. 

Food - the whitefish chowder was very hearty with small cubes of carrots, celery, potato, and whitefish in a creamy broth. The cracker was very crispy and went well with the chowder. The classic bagel was also super tasty, and the smoked salmon was tender with a distinct salmon flavor without the fishiness. It went well with the everything bagel and fresh tomatoes, onions, capers, and cream cheese. The loaf cake with apple pie ice cream was the only thing that was meh. The cake wasn't very outstanding, and the apple pie ice cream was a bit icy, freezer burned, and too frozen to scoop. Overall, everything was excellent minus the dessert, so I'd still come back. 

Service - our server was very nice and friendly. It was a 30 minute wait to be seated (we came here for Monday lunch), and they don't allow to go orders so that's something to keep in mind. 

Ambiance - nice clean interior but a bit of a squeeze seating and spacing wise.

Great price point given the menu. The salmon and ingredients that came with my "Classic" tasted very refreshing. The presentation was humble but snazzy. Really enjoyed the food. Will definitely return. I like the little after mints they give too. Highly recommend.

I have always wanted to try Russ & Daughters and on this visit I finally did! 

First of all, the cafe is so cute- classic New York charm without feeling too cramped at all. Our service was excellent- friendly, helpful, professional.

I got a vanilla egg cream and my husband tried the house made cream soda. Why don't more places sell egg creams?! Yum! Then I got the smoked whitefish chowder and the "sours" (a bowl of house made pickled). The whitefish chowder was one of the most delicious things I've ever had in my life. Like last-meal on death row good! My husband went more traditional with "the classic" bagel and lox, and a bowl of matzoh ball soup. Everything was amazing!

I would have loved to try the babka but I was too full- next time!

This spot is so cute with a really fun menu. I love how they adapted their original concept to the cafe outpost. They did a great job with their offerings and made so many delicious new things, it was hard to decide what to get!

We loved their house-made sodas. I had the coffee version only because it sounded bad- I was curious- and it turned out to be so delightful! I had all of the usuals- lox platters, matzoh ball soup, bialeys, rugelach - the list goes on. All delicious. 

The only annoying thing is you can't order anything to-go. I understand they don't want to clog up the cafe with to-go orders as that's what their other location is for, but I just wanted a few pieces of dessert. I am not about to go blocks out of my way for it when I am sitting right here. It does get busy, so do be prepared for a wait, though the line does move quickly.
I was blown away by how cute the ambiance was! They were able to accommodate my big family despite us coming close to closing time. I loved my lox benedict

Had a truly great time here and will definitely be coming back. The servers were extremely friendly and attentive and the food was delicious. Just a little pricey! 

Latke: definitely worth getting! deliciously crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside. Only thing that would have made it better would be a little bit of seasoning. I chose the salmon roe and cream cheese which didn't add too much. So would opt for sour cream next time--cheaper and might have been more flavorful! 

White fish chowder: this was delicious! Got it after I saw yelp reviews that recommended it. They were right! It was creamy but not too thick. The fish chunks were meaty and not dry. And the seasoning added a nice tangy kick. 

Pickled herring platter: I love pickled food so I enjoyed this! The fish was meaty and well sliced. The curry was not quite my jam but still great.

Chocolate egg cream: this was the only thing that I wasn't super excited about! Got it because I've never had an egg cream before. But it is quite literally what it says it is--chocolate syrup with fizzy water. Nothing super special and also pricey at $6. Would definitely skip this is you are on a budget! 

Looking forward to coming back and trying other things in the menu!

Okay where to start with this review...

The restaurant...very cute and very Jewish, really liked the vibe

Service...good service, nice waiter 

Food...it was just okay. I've grown up on lox and bagels, so on my scale it was only about a 6/10. The bagel wasn't very doughy, it was toasted but wasn't that flavorful? Even though we got the everything, in my opinion it was a pretty dry bagel. The platter only came with 2 slices of tomato, a few red onion slices and capers w cream cheese. Overall it was okay. I ordered a coffee, a lox and bagel platter, with an extra bagel and cream cheese and that was it. My bill came out to be around $46 with tax and tip. I don't know how it possibly wound up being that much, but I wasn't happy about the price. Mistake? Inflation? I duno..does that amount sound right to you?

Hot saturday morning, I needed some coffee and walked into thr tiny take away next to the main restaurant. Server was so sweet and I had a cardamom rose water latte, which was delicious. I was sitting outside and enjoying my coffee but it was too hot ao I went back inside and asked for the girl to splash me with cold brew to make it a little colder and stronger. The manager said loudly: - Make sure to charge her again for an espesso shot. Lovely. I responded: -Sure, if I am paying for a full shot, please actually give me a shot. Manager tried to explain that a teaspoon of cold brew hassss to be charged no matter what, just making it more akward. It's not about paying for a $3 espresso shot, believe me. Anyway, all this review to say that Ella, the server, should be manager, and the other girl should be, well, not manager. And the coffee was insane good!

As a fellow jew this place hit the spot. It was so good. We put our name down and they said 40 minutes around 1 pm on a Sunday we ended up waiting almost an hour to sit at the bar. The white fish croquettes were amazing and so was the chopped liver. The pickles were so good too and the latkes. The only thing I was surprised was the lox was okay, not the best lox I've had. Orange juice was fresh which it should have been for 7 bucks lol. I want to come back next time I'm in town to try something else!

The quality of their product was exceptional, service was good however we had to ask for: pepper/salt, napkins & olive oil.  For the price we paid, attention to detail should have been "spot on". We choose the "Ida" platter ($110) which included 4 varieties of delicious fresh salmon, cream cheeses, a nice selection of bagels & breads, onions, capers,  and peppers. We added Potato Latkes with sour cream & applesauce! And if that wasn't enough, we tried the sesame ice cream with coffee.  Next time, we'll just do the individual platters, a much better choice.

Came here on a Saturday around 9ish and was seated immediately at the bar! For 2 people, we shared The Classic board with an everything bagel and Potato Latkes with salmon roe & crème fraiche. This was our first and only lox bagel on the trip (sad, I know) but it was the truly something!! Bagel was toasted perfectly and the salmon was nice and thin. The cream cheese was also easily spreadable, 10/10 bagel. This was my first time trying potato latkes and the potatoes were nicely seasoned and paired really well with the roe and crème fraiche! They were a nice balance to cut the heaviness of the fried potato patties. Pro tip: we put some of the salmon roe from the latkes on our bagel, so good!

Service was great, the woman working the bar was attentive and took care of us. We even got some delicious coffee candies at the end of our meal, I regret not buying any to take home with me. We noticed a line starting to form when we left around 9:40, so definitely try to come before 10.

Don't know how you would mess up a classic I definitely enjoyed it the staff where very nice and the cafe itself was definitely not your regular cafe,a little more pricey then your average bagel and in my words "fancy",A perfect start to celebrate any big day and get together with your friends,the only thing is how messy it got personally I prefer my bagel assembled but everything else made up for it,definitely would go back !!

Went at 1:30 on a Sunday and waiting for 90 minutes. It was nice that we can walk around and then got a text when the table was ready. 

The place is cute inside and they have nice big booths. Only two restrooms in the back. 

The food is all mainly breads like challah, bagel, rye and cured and smoked fish. So you got to be in the mood for that when you come. The eggs Benny was $26 and was a bit over priced for what it was. The challah was dry, there was t much flavor in the dish. Needed more hollandaise sauce. I barely tasted it. Eggs were poached well. The smoked salmon was fine, tasted good quality. I got a malted egg cream, it was decent. It's seltzer water with malt flavor and milk. It was good to have something sweet to pair with the salty fish. 

The waiters were nice but disorganized. They brought out our drink like 5-10 minutes after our food. And were also arguing on the side about our bill for some reason. 

I unfortunately wouldn't come here again. It's a cute place but long wait, high prices and average food. We split the bill and with each getting a meal and 1 drink it was over $50 a person with tip.
An iconic place for appetizers ie: chopped liver, kasha varnishkas, bagels and lox. The mushroom-barley soup was terrific! Not a long wait (15 minutes) at 1pm on a Wednesday.

the atmosphere is cute and our waitress was very sweet. i've been to the original russ and daughters takeaway location, but this was my first time at their sit down cafe. all in all, i much prefer the assembled bagel at their other location to this "bagel board". wish i would have tried some other things on their cafe menu instead.
Omg just get the lox and bagel. You won't regret it. Everyone else wanted mine :) the lox was so fresh and it was one of the best lox and bagels I've ever had. This ain't the spot for eggs.
Institution's sit down restaurant. What's not to love. Food is great. Service is quick. They have their act together.
Great quality comfort food. The Scottish lox on bagel was delicious and fresh. Great latkes.

Delicious and fancy. However, this is too overpriced for what you get. You can get a delicious salmon bagel with the works at other places for half the price. Love the style of the inside. Good service.

An iconic name and well-known spot that lived up to its reputation! 

I've known about Russ & Daughters for YEARS thanks to both Instagram and friends of mine talking about their delicious bagels, fish, and babka. The cafe is separate from the Russ & Daughters Appetizers counter shop which is about two blocks north of the cafe location. We arrived at about 8:15 to meet a friend, the cafe opens at 8:30 but we wanted to make sure we could get a seat; we were not formally "in-line" but happened to be the first to enter when the doors opened and the curtains rose. We were seated in a comfortable booth, though there is counter seating in lieu of a booth if you're ever dining solo. By the time we placed coffee orders the cafe was bustling, and it didn't take long for all booths to fill, so come early if you want a seat! 

I had iced coffee with oat milk and it was fresh and delicious and very strong. We decided to order a lot and share, which is definitely my recommendation at R&DC. In no particular order, we tried the pastrami Russ, the potato latkes with applesauce, sour cream, roe, and creme fresh, the classic board with a bagel, the plate of sours (pickles and pickled tomatoes), and the chocolate babka french toast. Everything was SO, SO DELICIOUS, and it was great to try bites of everything. That babka... it's out of this world. All the flavors were sharp and fresh and complementary in all dishes. 

Our server was SO attentive and kind, and there were so many little details that he maintained, including fresh silverware, whisking empty plates away, and checking on us in a warm and non-rushed way throughout the meal. Though the space was packed, it felt cozy and comfortable rather than claustrophobic. This place is so special and feels like an institution - which, with its namesake, it is. I recommend highly! I can't wait to come back and try all sorts of other goodies. PS: if you have time, walk the few blocks to check out the storefront, which is an entirely different (and very unique) experience.

This was my first time at the cafe, which opened up in 2014. The original store has been on Houston St. for over a century.  

The cafe's breakfast menu has many standouts.  The entrees are original.  You can't find most selections in any restaurant anywhere in the U.S. Check out the menu, which is also available online.  

Today I had some Gaspe Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese on a Pumpernickel bagel.   TIP:  mix some fresh dill into the cream cheese for a foodgasmic experience.

The rugelach is good, but I have had better elsewhere, like at Armin and Judy's in The Hamptons.  The raspberry at Russ and Daughter's is good, but the cinnamon raisin leaves a lot to be desired.  I wish they had apricot, which is my favorite rugelach flavor, but Russ and Daughters does not make it.  Armin and Judy's does.

The service in the cafe was terrific.  I sat at the bar.

The decor was sleek and modern.

I definitely will be back.

We arrived a few minutes before opening on the Friday after Turkey Day. Almost no line and the place never got crowded (a very off day).

Service is always good and the selections are huge. We had the omelette with veggies and "Lower Sunny Side" and 2 freshly brewed decafs.

A nice and tasty breakfast. Pete Wells was spot on this time.

Recommended!

Damages with tip for 2 was $70 - hey this is NYC!

Finally get the hype

RATING: 9.7/10 (for the lox sandwich) 

PRO TIP: yes the sandwich is pricey. Yes it is delicious.

LOX BAGEL SANDWICH
This place has so much hype around it and yes this sandwich is amazing. The high quality ingredients and their thoughtful proportions make for a DELICIOUS breakfast experience, beautifully, richly salty smoked salmon cuts through creamy, delectable cream cheese and capers/red onions add additional tartness and texture. My one area of improvement is that the bagel itself is easily not New York's best bagel, as it is soft but does fight you when you try to take bites off the bagel. However, that almost doesn't matter with how great the interior of the sandwich is.

FINAL RANKING: EXCELLENT
(terrible / bad / ok / good / great / EXCELLENT)

What an experience. You can't make reservations so we got there a little before they opened and was the second group in line. We ordered probably one of everything on the menu. Delicious. Bagels, lox, matzah ball soup, latkes, eggs, it was all seriously delicious. Bought the cookbook while we were there too.
The OG deli location, while not sit down, is sooooo much better.  The prepared food here just isn't that good. Service isn't very friendly and their cocktails are awful.  It's just not worth it

I preordered a bagel the night before thinking it would be busy on a saturday morning. The was a small line on opening. Bagel was done exactly on the time posted on my receipt. Got the lox. It was really flavorful. I didn't like that there was no option to toast it (well at least ordering online). The only thing bad about the bagel was the bread quality. Bread was tough. Cool spot but did not live up to the hype.

This was my first time ever having a lox bagel and I'm so glad I tried it here in ny! We ordered it with scallion cream cheese on a sesame bagel and it was the perfect combination of the flavors I enjoy! Looking forward to more lox bagels in the future as this was a great introductory experience!

No better time than the weekday to walk in and dine at russ and daughters than a weekday at 12pm

we started with the potato ladkes - they were juicy, crunchy, and full of flavor. reminded me of an indian pakora. we topped it with creme fraiche and salmon roe which IMO is the way to go. 

second was the salmon with an every bagel - super delicious and the salmon was insanely juicy and fresh. the everything bagel was a good call because it was doughy but also crunchy since we got it toasted! 

last and my fav was the challah bread pudding which was more on the pudding / squishy in texture side - super good and sweet if you like pudding. one of my favs from the meal.

overall good experience and service was quick. would def recommend and return!

Honestly a mixed experience for us.
It was a Saturday and it was very busy but the front of house host was lovely and helpful when adding us to a waitlist. I was advised the wait would be around 1 hour and 25mins for a party of 5 but that there were cancellations and others removing themselves from the waitlist so it might be sooner. I received a text about 45mins later saying our table was almost ready and to come back to the restaurant. We arrived back and were asked to wait again in their small waiting area near the door and the bar seats. We had to wait an additional 15 to 20mins until our table was actually ready. The waiting area is not big enough when there are multiple people waiting and you will end up very close to people eating at the bar. Understandably this isn't ideal however one member of staff was so incredibly passive aggressive and rude when asking waiting parties to move. The reality is there is no where to move if the restaurant is busy so honestly they should remove the bar seats that are directly beside the waiting area or find a way to expand the waiting area for everyone's comfort with the popularity of the restaurant. Or try to make sure tables are actually ready when calling people back to avoid waiting inside at all. 

However, despite a negative first impression it wasn't all bad. We had a table towards the back of the restaurant which was nice and less busy. Our server (who's name I've forgotten) was absolutely lovely, very friendly and engaging. We ordered the omelette with mushrooms, goats cheese, and spinach, the Matzo Ball soup, the classic board with a bagel, the shtetl board with bialy, and the Yum Kippered board with bialy. All of the bagel platters where delicious and came with plenty of the spread and fish, and the matzo ball soups was also great. The omelette left a bit to be desired as it was a little dense and rather than the mushrooms being mixed through the egg they were just sandwiched in the middle. There also wasn't really many mushrooms for a mushrooms omelette. We also ordered a tea, an orange juice and a beer. 
Overall, the experience wasn't particularly good or awful. It was simply alright and a bit overpriced. Personally I wouldn't go back.

Stopped in for a late morning bite. They don't take reservations, while it was busy my party of 2 was seated within 15 minutes. Started with the potato latkes with apple sauce and sour cream. Best latkes I've ever had. Ordered and shared the classic - smoked salmon with tomato onion capers cream cheese and choice of bagel - and the yum kippered - baked same otherwise the same as the classic. Both were amazing. Also ordered the pickle platter which was amazing. Finished with the bread pudding which was warm and delicious. Fun restaurant with great food and friendly staff. Has a bit of classic NYC LES deli feel to it. Also conveniently can stop at the Russ and daughters deli right near by.

Russ & Daughters Cafe was the first stop on my wife's birthday extravaganza. We'd been to the OG Russ & Daughter's shop. Good stuff but a lot of hype for bagels, spreads, and fish. I'm quite spoiled with having some great bagel and fish spots nearby, so treking out to the Soho?, Noho?, HoHo? area from Brooklyn or Queens is a big commitment.

When we walked in, immediately realized that it was going to be a great experience. Bar upfront with a limited but mindful selection of alcohol. They had Kings County, Blanton's, and Michter's all at reasonable prices. I opted for a spiked egg cream before following my heart to a pour of Kings County bourbon. Service at the bar was quick and attentive. 

Menu was super intriguing with sections dedicated to herring, caviar, smoked salmon, and Jewish classics. We ended up sharing a daily special - the potato "totkes" - , the white fish chowder, and the babka French toast. 

Totkes were great. Super crispy and came with a delicious Bloody Mary creme frachie. The smoked white fish chowder was creamy and savory. Tons of veggies and super hearty. Babka French toast is a dessert lover's treat for a meal.

Two gender neutral restrooms which were handicap accessible. One had a changing table. We were able to walk in on a weekday but I can imagine needing to get here earlier on the weekends.
Must visit, excellent Bagels and lox.  We did carry out from East Village location. The Classic was excellent.  Grab a number and be ready, it gets crowed but goes quickly.  Excellent service

Had a great brunchie vibe with my friends. Service was nice and the ambiance was very bright and clean. I shared my meal with a friend and it was a good amount of food (not too full, but not craving anything else.) I probably wouldn't return, but I enjoyed my meal.

Came by for breakfast the other day and it was a decent experience. Russ & Daughters is in the Lower East side and is featured in the Michelin guide as a Bib Gourmand.

The cafe was super clean and modern with elevated pricing. Staff wore a white Russ & Daughters lab coat as their front of the house uniform.

Ordered the smoked salmon eggs Benedict and it was decent. The bread was freshly cut and the smoked salmon was fragrant with the taste of preservatives. The actual poached egg was decent although I've had better. Their hollandaise sauce was good and not too heavy.

Service by the staff was quick and efficient.

$31/head for breakfast after tax and gratuity

Springfield Massachusetts misses you dearly..those delicious hot cross buns, delightful 7 inch chocolate chip cookies and the bread ooh la la
Since 1965 till you closed you will be missed...

Be prepared to wait BUT there are tons of coffee shops nearby and they'll text you when your tables ready. Sunday brunch at 11:30am PEAK time for Russ and Daughters but I put my name down met my friend at La Colombe had a coffee and about an hour later I got the text. We ordered latkes and a classic to share it was more food than we needed (bc we ordered an extra bagel on the side). The break fast martini was GREAT and on the stiffer side. Love sitting at the counter if it's just 2 of us, bartenders always great and the vibes are so classic New York.

I enjoyed my experience here, it was nice to have a place to sit and my bagel was SO FIRE! 
The service was also good.

Worth traveling across town for ! I actually found their other location first, which seemed more like a grab-and-go kind of place - it had a line out the door so I decided to pass. Then I found this location and I'm so glad I did ! (They're actually relatively close to each other which is awesome) 

Seating & wait time
I was alone and the wait was about 30ish minutes. However, I got a text from them maybe 10 minutes later that my seat was ready. Luckily I hadn't wandered too far ! They don't have much of a waiting area at the restaurant so I recommend walking around a bit
They have stool seating at the bar which is where I sat. Each spot does have hooks under the bar to hang your belongings. 
They also have table and booth seating further into the restaurant. 

Staff:
They have the most friendly and up beat staff I've ever seen! Everyone was very sweet and welcoming. They also joked around with each other and generally seemed to have a good time working there. 

Food:
I opted for the basic board with salmon. There were so many delicious looking options, but I felt (being alone) that a lot of the options would have been too much for me and better shared. That being said I definitely need to come back with a friend or two to experience more of the menu! 
Everything on my board was so fresh and flavorful! From the everything bagel to the onions to the salmon. Honestly it blew my mind how such a simple order could be so delicious 
I also ordered a tea and was given my own small pot. That was great with it being a cold & rainy day. 
When you sit down you're immediately given a whole bottle of still water which is nice too. 

Overall this place was amazing and I highly recommend it ! I can't wait to come back!

This is an excellent spot for amazing and flavorful food!

I'd been here before and it was nice to return and enjoy the great offerings. I went for the Classic Board and it did not disappoint - it included a fresh bagel and wonderful smoked salmon with all the accompaniments. Everything tasted great and one can tell that the quality is top-notch.

The setting is like a chic diner - it's a wonderful space to be in.

We experienced warm and friendly service...the host and server treated us very well and it helped to ensure a memorable experience.

This place is very popular, so make sure to plan accordingly; if you arrive at typical brunch times, expect a long wait.

i will still go back because i do enjoy this place. but wow. i was frankly blown away by the bafflingly low quality bagel i was served. excellent lox. but....
also abysmal borscht and BAD coffee! guys!?! get it together!

We were in town for Easter weekend. I got lazy so had it delivered to the hotel, I was worried about losing some of the quality but laziness won (it usually does ). We ordered a few Dr.Browns sodas and I got the classic which is an everything bagel/lox/capers/red onion/plain cream cheese . 
To say it was the best bagel I've ever had would be an understatement . It was also the best lox I've ever had. That bagel and that fish are perfect. There's nothing to change. Just enjoy !!

Before trekking on down here, you should know that about 80% of the menu items contain some kind of fish on them. Great for me, but my partner didn't feel great about his options. Luckily we found things to order we'd both enjoy... I had the eggs benny, which came with smoked salmon, poached egg and dreamy hollandaise on the perfect piece of challah bread. I thoroughly enjoyed each bite. My partner ordered the Latkes with apple sauce and it was the the light breakfast he was looking for. Somethings to know about the space, its bright and cute, but small... don't come here with a big party unless you're willing to wait 45-60 minutes. Can't wait to come back and try a few more things.

Superb service. Adorable space (I am reviewing the restaurant on Orchard). I ordered the shmaltz (chicken fat) cured herring and the chopped chicken liver.  I have no doubt the shmaltz herring was a perfectly fine version of that dish. So, I should say it was good. The ice cold vodka shot was a perfectly cleansing accompaniment.  I personally found the herring to be inedibly salty and I've not always experienced herring to be inedible. But again, I suspect people who love shmaltz herring will enjoy it. I liked that the chopped chicken liver had tiny bits instead of having been puréed. I will say, though, that it seemed to lack shmaltz. I thought the flavor lacked depth. The malt-flavored egg cream was delicious.  I gave three stars because the menu is fairly limited and also bec of the tumult and the wait for a table--those inconveniences were not, to my mind, worth suffering through.
Food are so yummy and love their bagel and also desserts are delicious. Must try!!! The restaurant so pretty too.

The cafe is the place to go. My dad and I went on a Friday at about 9:00 am and it was packed. People were there with their suitcases. We had to wait a little bit, but ended up getting two seats the bar top, which was cute. The inside of the cafe has great theming and decoration.

Concord Grape Soda ($8)
The drinks are pricey because they aren't can sodas, they are freshly made in the cafe. This one has jasmine, timut pepper, and lemon and obviously concord grapes. Their sodas are delicious and you have to be careful not to suck it down too quick!

The Classic Board ($22)
Nova smoked salmon, cream cheese, your choice of bagel, bialy, rye, or pumpernickel. I love this, it is simple, but delicious and hits every time. It is also very instagrammable the way they plate it. 

Overall really solid food, fun place to take people from out of town.

Excellent all around, everything bagel and eggs Benny were good. But the star of the show was the pickled herring. Generous portions and tasty pickled onions. Good service with refills on coffee. Good vibe, busy but not noisy.
Went for a work event overall wasn't super impressed with the bagels but it was my first time trying latkes and they were very good! Our lattes were good and the staff was super friendly
Perfect bagel! Perfect smoked salmon! Friendly staff, lovely ambiance, what more could we ask for?

My first upscale Jewish Diner experience and egg creme and shrub drink! Russ & Daugther now has several locations in NYC, and this one is lower east side, very close to the Russ & Daugther store and takeaway. This is sit down, and no reservations taken, we walked in and waited a 20 minutes before we sat down (we got a coffee at a different location to wait). 

The restaurant is immaculate with a super welcoming bar area and booths with tons of smoked fish, cured fish on the menu. The upscaleness comes from the caviar they sell. 
 
At Russ & Daughters with my Jewish friend, I got to try egg creme - which unlike it's name does not have egg or cream, it's a light chocolate milkshake think nesquick with soda water and it's delightful. I'd seen it a lot in the movies from the soda shop days and I've always wanted to try it. 

I also got a beet shrub: a drink made with a fruit-infused vinegar syrup and sparkling water. I'm a sucker for any beet juice drink. 

The food was lovely, very good Jewish deli food elevated - the portion sizes are controlled here, not like the old school delis where you meats are the size of your head. I rate this place 5 stars bc I think about that shrub. We did have a small tin of caviar, and it was a delightful experience. Would for sure come back and recommend to people who enjoy an upscale diner experience.

Came here after hearing and seeing so much hype. For all the chatter and rave reviews, the food was underwhelming to say the least.

Ordered a toasted bagel with Lox which came on a wooden platter with onions, capers and salmon. The bagel was NOT toasted as requested and there were a measly two slices of salmon and some tomatoes with cream cheese. They also forgot the egg i had asked for.

Also ordered hot coffee which was decent.

The ambience was as expected, that of an old school NY diner and it was definitely busy.

Service was average as got seating at the counter. The hostess was very kind and polite. 

I genuinely feel like several bodegas have bagel sandwiches that are SO much better than this place. The menu is overly pretentious and complicated (imho).

Paid $30 for the above... could have gotten a MUCH better meal with 1/4th the price at another 'no-frills' place and would have been much happier.

Feel like this is a tourist trap and most likely not come back again based on the experience...

Way too overpriced for the services and the food.   Got the classic.  Smallest amount of any lox served with a bagel and just salty.   Two thin slices! Making your own plate at home would have been more satisfying.   And on top of it they constantly interrupted you to clear your plates.   Almost felt like they were rushing you to turn the tables.   So sad!  I was really looking forward to enjoying my breakfast!
Food made me sick and I came here cause I was hungry and saw it was famous- the omelette was gross but the bread is good- there was no flavor in the salad either but the ambiance is cute

Every restaurant article points to Russ & Daughters - a must try. They did not disappoint! The latkes were my favorite!! They come with a few different toppings - roe and cream, apple sauce and sour cream.  Both are such good options. The apple sauce and sour cream are actually better than you would think. Nice surprise actually. I also really loved the babka French toast, perfect texture. 

We sat at the bar/counter. The waiter/bartender was super friendly and helpful. We had a great conversation with him! 

Really nice experience here and we will definitely come back!

Perfect NYC upscale sit-in deli atmosphere. Friendly service. Quick too but never felt rushed. And a seriously delicious bagel and smoked salmon board that got devoured. Recommend!! Close to Tenement museum too.
The line situation is kind of weird but the food was sooo good. I got the salmon lox I recommend. Also it was pretty expensive but worth it on special occasions.

Who knew I needed caviar on my bagel. Well new bar has been set on extravagant eating. 

Coffee selection is just drip but there's an espresso place really close if you are like me and need that. 

Service is great as you grab a number on way in and order when called. 

Highly recommend this place and can't wait to visit again

Famous for a reason. Enjoyed a delicious lox bagel and glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice. Admittedly on the pricier side, but enjoyed it nonetheless. The cafe itself is adorable, and the service was excellent.

This is a required stop whenever I visit New York City. I always bring home sable that is sliced so thin you can see through it! It melts in the mouth, has just the right amount of oiliness, and is bursting with flavor. This is exactly how sable should be. The counterman has the skill of a surgeon and the fish is placed on paper that makes it easy to lift off and it doesn't fall apart. Love it!

After visiting Russ & Daughters, we met a friend at the Russ & Daughters Café. It was worth it, but be prepared for a bit of a wait.

The café isn't large, but it's light, bright, and tidy.

I ordered The Classic: Gaspe Nova smoked salmon with cream cheese, red onion, capers, and tomatoes. They also ask for your choice of bagel--I had a plain one toasted. It was delicious and really hit the spot.

My husband ordered the Matzo Ball Soup, which was flavorful, with chicken and matzo balls--a comforting dish. He also had the pickled herring filet with pumpernickel, which he enjoyed (though it's not my favorite).

My friend had the Potato Latkes with wild salmon roe and crème fraîche, and she was also able to get applesauce and sour cream on the side, for a bit of both. They were delicious.

We ordered chocolate egg creams, and my husband had a house-made grape soda. If you're looking for Coke or Pepsi, they don't offer those, but I appreciated the unique house-made drinks.

Service was friendly and helpful.

It wasn't an inexpensive lunch, but it was worth it for the food and quality time with a dear friend. It was nice to be able to sit down comfortably and enjoy our meal.

The café is about a five-minute walk down Orchard Street from the original location.

Cheers!

Service was attentive and not overwhelming. The spot isn't huge so prepare for a wait that is most definitely worth it. Pickled herring trio is a great introduction to eating pickled herring. The sturgeon scramble was packed with fish and has a balanced flavor. I see why this historic place has withstood the tests of time.

PLEASE don't get discouraged by the wait time.  Waited an hour,  but took this opportunity to walk around and explore!
Food was absolutely perfect.  We ordered a little bit of everything.  Appetizer,  bagel board, mushroom omelet,  and French toast- cinnamon with two cocktails- Miriam s cup and break-fast martini.  FABULOUS!
SERVICE WAS GREAT AND QUICK!

Ambiance- great music,  great food,  ambiance was just right. 
Definitely will be returning next year!

Extraordinary experience with truly unique food. Impeccable drinks selection as well as an adorable atmosphere in the heart of midtown a nook in the wall leading to a beautiful experience of flavorful joy. 
The only down side would be the wait time on weekends but that just tells you even more how good of a place you are about to get into.

Came in on a Thursday at noon and there was a very short wait time. Lots of spacious seating with booths available. The server was very attentive and friendly, answering any questions we had. We ordered the Anne and it was delicious. All the smoked fish and accompaniments were amazing. The smoked salmon melted in your mouth with the butteriest feel. The sable was my second favorite with its satisfying chew. The bagels and bread basket were good, but not necessarily phenomenal. It may seem pricey at $120, but this satisfied four people, so it could be worth it as an occasional brunch spot. Haven't been here when it's super busy, though.

A true NYC classic, a must try!! I personally love Russ & Daughters Cafe and have been to it a few times over the years.

Service / Ambiance / Vibe:
- excellent service from the staff at large, when I went on 12/6 our waitress was very attentive and nice
- Cool to dine at the cafe of such a historic NYC business
- the decor and view of the kitchen really gives you that NY Diner feel

Food:
I love the food, the bagel - lox - cream cheese platter is fire. the SOUPS are incredible, menu at large is interesting and full of good food. As other reviewers have noted, it's a pricier option....if you just want a bagel sandwich at the best price - then yes obviously go to your local bodega and just get that. But if you want the full experience AND if I had to guess I'm sure the food quality and sourced ingredients are much better than a bodega....go to the cafe, have a seat and enjoy a great dining experience.

I love it here! I was told it would be a 30 minute wait and it ended up being a 6 minute wait so don't venture too far and don't hesitate to put your name on the list then bop around the neighborhood. From the hotel I was staying in, I walked past the R&D deli location en route to the cafe. The deli is your best bet for grab and go and a solid option for bagel sams eaten on the sidewalk. Besties, if you're looking for a more robust sit-down experience, ya gotta come here instead.

I love the special touches and the iconic New York experience-ness of it all. The drawings on the walls, the menu setup, all of it! None of that compares to the thinly slices, perfectly smoked lox. I also enjoyed the matzoh ball soup, chowder (sooo good), and a mimosa. This spot has booze! The classic board is a MUST and something I would order again and again.

Skip the cold and somewhat dense deviled eggs, otherwise have fun! Our server was fabulous and food comes out at a quick clip. If you're lucky, you'll get seated next to the magic (kitchen) and watch it all happen.

Still thinking about this place! Visited NYC and was on a mission for a good bagel with lox and this place did not disappoint. The cafe is a bit on the smaller side but it is warm and bright. This location does not serve the bagel sandwiches seen at other locations and instead has a few bagel board options. We had the Apple French toast as our sweet breakfast treat and it was also delicious. Highly recommend!

Russ and Daughters feels a bit like a time capsule when you walk in. The staff is friendly and efficient. Everything we ordered was delicious. The smoked salmon is top notch. If I were to go back I would order The Classic again. It was the perfect balance of smokey, fresh, and briney. So yummy!

The orange juice is fresh squeezed and the coffee was good.

Another FANTASTIC experience here. From the hostess, to our server, to the manager - everyone here is so nice. The hostess quoted us a 45 min wait when we arrived around 12:30pm for four people, but was able to seat us in half that time. Our waitress, Margot I believe was her name, was extremely understanding when two people in our party were pressed for time due to a show on the other side of time (our fault for getting here late) and made sure our food arrived very promptly. We got amazing suggestions for food from the manager and everything was spot on. 

We ordered the Ida board for four of us (the smoked salmon is like butter in your mouth!), potato latkes (some of the best I've EVER had), Super Heebster (wow), and the babka French toast for dessert (don't sleep on this one). It was the perfect amount of food for the four of us. 

I can't say enough good things about Russ and Daughters- one of my favorite spots in the city!

Can we give it 6 stars?  Only waited two minutes for a table which is unusual. Sam, our waiter, was super. We started with the Deviled Eggs with Smoked Trout which were creamy and delicious. Paired the eggs either a bowl of Smoked Whitefish Chowder that the kitchen split into two bowls for us. The chowder was our fondest memory from a previous visit and it didn't disappoint. Creamy but not too rich, flavorful but not too Smokey. Shared a classic nova board with an extra bagel. And, of course, a side of potato latkes. The nova was very mild and sliced paper thin. Very delicate. Wish there had been another slice or two but.... The latkes were thick, crispy on the outside and creamy inside. Had to try them; enjoyed them; might not do again. Finished with coffee (strong) and cinnamon Rugelach that were flaky and tasty. Everything we remembered and more. A really special brunch for us.

The service is great--so friendly and helpful. We love the bagels, shmears, bread, and baked goods. I wasn't overly crazy about the kasha varnishkes--to me it tasted like the barley was old, but it's not a dish that I have ever had before, so maybe that's just what it tastes like. Still, loved the experience.
Such a cute spot and I love the retro design, but my bagel was unfortunately hard and the disassembled aspect made it messy and difficult to eat.

Made a quick stop at Russ & Daughters this morning for a light breakfast. The Orchard Street location is really cool, it throws back to an old soda fountain/diner. Cool marble tiles and counter tops and great decor elsewhere, too. The couple staff I interacted with were smiley and kind.  I really enjoyed the whitefish croquettes and the rugelach.  The croquettes were piping hot and nested on a dill sauce. The rugelach were crispy and sweet.  Their menu is pretty expensive, too.
This place was so YUM! Very worth the 1 hour wait. I will forever be thinking about the latkes and salmon roe. I am also a salmon Benedict fan, and this one was scrumptious.
Great bagels. Great location. Great ambiance. Great staff. Three  of us ordered different items and all three loved what we got.

Service was top notch! Stopped in for brunch and had to try several
Items. The white fish chowder was delicious- maybe lacking some salt but very filling and comforting. The latkes were yummy, the bagel with horseradish cream cheese was delicious, and the chocolate egg cream while not something I'd order again, was unique. I was stuffed. It's pricey, but the ambiance and the service really make this place shine.

Great service with a clean, classic diner/deli vibe. We ordered The Classic Board with a plain bagel, Eggs Benny, and the yogurt, fruit, and granola. A must try if you're a fan of fresh, smoked salmon- my first time trying it and wasn't disappointed. If you're in the area, I highly recommend you try this 100+ year historical NYC staple.

When in the city I try to taste all of the best NYC has to offer.  And this is no exception. 

Service is on point.
